   On the event \(\bigcap_jH_j(p,q)\), choose one witnessing block symbol
   \(a_j\) for each \(j\), and put \(c=(a_1,\ldots,a_h)\).  Then
   \[
      S_P(p,c)=\sum_j\psi_j(p,a_j)\ge\sum_j\theta_{P,j}=\theta_P,
      \qquad
      S_Q(q,c)=\sum_j\phi_j(q,a_j)\ge\sum_j\theta_{Q,j}=\theta_Q .
   \]
   Hence the global hit event contains \(\bigcap_jH_j(p,q)\).  Independence
   gives \((BT4)\).  The final sentence is just the substitution of these
   factored estimates into \((PP1)\)--\((PP4)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Product-panel rate bookkeeping]
   \label{cor:product-panel-rate-bookkeeping}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:product-panel-tensorization}, and assume
   the number of blocks satisfies \(h\le\log^{O_c(1)}m\).  For every query
   \(q\), suppose there are deterministic block factors \(\mathfrak q_j(q)\)
   such that, for every realization of block \(j\),
   \[
      e^{-\beta\theta_{Q,j}}Z_j^Q(q)\le\mathfrak q_j(q),
      \qquad
      e^{\beta(M_j(q)-\theta_{Q,j})}\le\mathfrak q_j(q),
   \]
   and
   \[
      (1+D_j(q))e^{\beta(M_j(q)-\theta_{Q,j})}
      \le\mathfrak q_j(q).
   \]
   For data and far pairs put
   \[
      \mathfrak s_j(x)=
      \E\!\left[e^{-\alpha\theta_{P,j}}Z_j^P(x)\right],
      \qquad
      \mathfrak f_j(x,q)=
      \E\!\left[
      e^{-\alpha\theta_{P,j}-\beta\theta_{Q,j}}
      Z_j^{PQ}(x,q)
      \right],
   \]
   and for near pairs put
   \[
      \mathfrak h_j(p,q)=\Pr[H_j(p,q)].
   \]
   If
   \[
      \prod_{j=1}^h\mathfrak q_j(q)
      \le m^\rho\log^{O_c(1)}m
      \qquad\text{for every promised query }q,
      \tag{RB1}
   \]
   \[
      \prod_{j=1}^h\mathfrak s_j(x)
      \le m^\rho\log^{O_c(1)}m
      \qquad\text{for every data point }x,
      \tag{RB2}
   \]
   \[
      \prod_{j=1}^h\mathfrak f_j(x,q)
      \le m^{-(1-\rho)}\log^{O_c(1)}m
      \qquad
      \text{whenever }\|x-q\|>cr,
      \tag{RB3}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \prod_{j=1}^h\mathfrak h_j(p,q)
      \ge \log^{-O_c(1)}m
      \qquad
      \text{whenever }\|p-q\|\le r,
      \tag{RB4}
   \]
   then the product panel satisfies the certificates \((PP1)\)--\((PP4)\) of
   \cref{prop:product-panel-spectrum-compiler}, after increasing the
   polylogarithmic exponent.

   Equivalently, it is enough to prove one-block log-rate bounds
   \[
      \mathfrak q_j(q)\le m^{u_j},\qquad
      \mathfrak s_j(x)\le m^{v_j},\qquad
      \mathfrak f_j(x,q)\le m^{-w_j},\qquad
      \mathfrak h_j(p,q)\ge e^{-b_j},
   \]
   with
   \[
      \sum_j u_j\le\rho+O_c\!\left(\frac{\log\log m}{\log m}\right),
      \quad
      \sum_j v_j\le\rho+O_c\!\left(\frac{\log\log m}{\log m}\right),
   \]
   \[
      \sum_j w_j\ge1-\rho-O_c\!\left(\frac{\log\log m}{\log m}\right),
      \quad
      \sum_j b_j=O_c(\log\log m).
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \((BT1)\) and the definition of the factors \(\mathfrak q_j\), every
   prefix term in \(e^{-\beta\theta_Q}P_\beta(q)\) is at most
   \(\prod_j\mathfrak q_j(q)\).  There are \(h+1=\log^{O_c(1)}m\) terms, so
   \[
      e^{-\beta\theta_Q}P_\beta(q)
      \le
      (h+1)\prod_j\mathfrak q_j(q)
      \le m^\rho\log^{O_c(1)}m .
   \]
   The additive product-panel decoder with terminal prices \(Q_c=0\) therefore
   has work
   \[
      O\!\left(
      (m^\rho\log^{O_c(1)}m+1)\log(2+m^\rho\log^{O_c(1)}m)
      \right)
      =
      m^\rho\log^{O_c(1)}m,
   \]
   plus the explicit \(d\log^{O_c(1)}m\) work needed to compute the block
   query scores.  This is \((PP1)\).

   For storage, independence and \((BT2)\) give, for each fixed \(x\),
   \[
      \E e^{-\alpha\theta_P}\prod_j Z_j^P(x)
      =
      \prod_j\mathfrak s_j(x)
      \le m^\rho\log^{O_c(1)}m .
   \]
   Summing over the \(m\) data points gives \((PP2)\).  Similarly, for each far
   pair \((x,q)\), independence and \((BT3)\) give
   \[
      \E e^{-\alpha\theta_P-\beta\theta_Q}\prod_j Z_j^{PQ}(x,q)
      =
      \prod_j\mathfrak f_j(x,q)
      \le m^{-(1-\rho)}\log^{O_c(1)}m .
   \]
   Summing over at most \(m\) far points gives \((PP3)\).  Finally, \((BT4)\)
   and \((RB4)\) give \((PP4)\).

   The log-rate formulation is obtained by multiplying the displayed one-block
   bounds and using
   \[
      m^{O_c((\log\log m)/\log m)}=\log^{O_c(1)}m .
   \]
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Additive-IVF product-panel certificate]
   \label{cor:additive-ivf-product-panel}
   Let \(E_1,\ldots,E_h\) be mutually orthogonal subspaces of the local
   Euclidean space, let \(\Pi_j\) denote orthogonal projection to \(E_j\), and
   let \(\mathcal C_j\subset E_j\) be finite pivot codebooks.  For
   \(c=(c_1,\ldots,c_h)\in\prod_j\mathcal C_j\), write
   \[
      A(c)=\sum_{j=1}^h c_j
   \]
   for the additive pivot.  Define the block score
   \[
      \chi_j(y,c_j)=\ip{\Pi_jy}{c_j}-\frac12\|c_j\|^2 .
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \sum_{j=1}^h\chi_j(y,c_j)
      =
      \frac12\|\Pi_Ey\|^2
      -
      \frac12\|\Pi_Ey-A(c)\|^2,
      \qquad
      \Pi_E=\sum_j\Pi_j .
      \tag{AIVF}
   \]
   Consequently the following additive-IVF scheme is an instance of
   \cref{prop:product-panel-spectrum-compiler}: store \(x\) in tuple bucket
   \(c\) when
   \[
      \sum_j\chi_j(x,c_j)\ge\theta_P,
   \]
   and, on query \(q\), probe exactly the tuple buckets with
   \[
      \sum_j\chi_j(q,c_j)\ge\theta_Q
   \]
   using the product decoder of \cref{lem:additive-product-panel-decoder}.
   If the block factors of \cref{cor:product-panel-rate-bookkeeping}, with
   \(\psi_j=\phi_j=\chi_j\), satisfy \((RB1)\)--\((RB4)\), then
   \(O(\log^{O_c(1)}m)\) independent additive-IVF panels give terminal query
   work
   \[
      d\,m^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}m
   \]
   and space
   \[
      dm+m^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}m .
   \]

   For \(h=2\), the buckets are exactly pairs \((i_0,i_1)\) of pivots.  More
   generally, the retained family exposes \(\prod_j|\mathcal C_j|\) possible
   cells while the query pays only the output-sensitive prefix-list bound
   certified by \((RB1)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Orthogonality gives
   \[
      \|\Pi_Ey-A(c)\|^2
      =
      \sum_j\|\Pi_jy-c_j\|^2
      =
      \sum_j\|\Pi_jy\|^2
      -2\sum_j\ip{\Pi_jy}{c_j}
      +\sum_j\|c_j\|^2,
   \]
   which is \((AIVF)\).  On a fixed-norm localized shell, distance thresholding
   around the additive pivot is therefore literally score thresholding.  In
   general, the displayed score-threshold rules are the certified
   multi-assignment version of additive IVF, with \((AIVF)\) recording their
   relation to additive-pivot distance.  The storage rule, query-probe rule,
   decoder work, storage moment, far co-load moment, and near-hit condition are
   exactly the hypotheses of \cref{cor:product-panel-rate-bookkeeping} for the
   block scores \(\chi_j\).  Applying
   \cref{prop:product-panel-spectrum-compiler} gives the displayed resources.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Nonorthogonal additive quantization]
   \label{rem:nonorthogonal-additive-ivf}
   Full additive vector quantization uses codebooks in the same ambient space.
   In that case
   \[
      \ip{y}{A(c)}-\frac12\|A(c)\|^2
      =
      \sum_j\left(\ip{y}{c_j}-\frac12\|c_j\|^2\right)
      -
      \sum_{i<j}\ip{c_i}{c_j}.
      \tag{AQ1}
   \]
   Thus the only obstruction to the clean product proof is the
   query-independent interaction price
   \(\Pi(c)=\sum_{i<j}\ip{c_i}{c_j}\).  If the codebooks are constructed so
   that this price is \(O_c(\log\log m)\) on every tuple route that can be
   reported, it can be absorbed into the thresholds and contributes only a
   polylogarithmic slack to the product-panel rates.  Composite-quantization or
   approximately orthogonal codebooks are one way to aim for this condition.

   Without such a bound one should not pretend that \((AQ1)\) tensorizes.
   Instead the interaction must be part of the decoder certificate.  For
   \(h=2\), after choosing \(c_1\), the correct second-codebook score is
   \[
      \ip{y-c_1}{c_2}-\frac12\|c_2\|^2,
   \]
   so a certified reporter for the second pivot set may be run with shifted
   query \(y-c_1\).  This remains analyzable by the general
   Fano-biased/prefix-list framework, but the product rate identities
   \((BT1)\)--\((BT3)\) must be replaced by the corresponding prefix-moment
   bound for the priced pair decoder.  The useful theorem target for
   nonorthogonal additive IVF is therefore a compact priced-pair reporter whose
   prefix work, storage, far co-load, and near-hit spectrum pass the same
   \((PP1)\)--\((PP4)\) verifier; Lloyd or additive-quantization distortion
   alone is not the needed proof object.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[Rectangular interaction-cover additive-IVF compiler]
   \label{prop:rectangular-interaction-cover-aq}
   Fix a terminal localized ANN subproblem of size \(m\), approximation \(c\),
   and exponent \(\rho=\rho_c\).  Let \(L_m=\log^{A_c}m\).  A random
   nonorthogonal additive-IVF panel consists of finite ambient codebooks
   \(\mathcal C_1,\ldots,\mathcal C_h\), tuple score
   \[
      S_y(c_1,\ldots,c_h)
      =
      \ip{y}{\sum_jc_j}
      -\frac12\left\|\sum_jc_j\right\|^2,
   \]
   and thresholds \(\theta_P,\theta_Q\).  Write
   \[
      \chi_j(y,a)=\ip{y}{a}-\frac12\|a\|^2,
      \qquad
      \Pi(c)=\sum_{i<j}\ip{c_i}{c_j},
   \]
   so that \(S_y(c)=\sum_j\chi_j(y,c_j)-\Pi(c)\).  Suppose preprocessing also
   supplies a finite product-rectangle cover \(\mathcal B\) of the tuple
   universe.  Each \(B\in\mathcal B\) has the form
   \[
      B=\mathcal C_{B,1}\times\cdots\times\mathcal C_{B,h},
      \qquad \mathcal C_{B,j}\subseteq\mathcal C_j,
   \]
   and a certified lower interaction price
   \[
      \underline\Pi_B\le \Pi(c)\qquad(c\in B).
      \tag{RIC0}
   \]

   On query \(q\), for every rectangle \(B\), run the product decoder of
   \cref{lem:additive-product-panel-decoder} on the raw additive score
   \(\sum_j\chi_j(q,c_j)\) over \(B\) with threshold
   \(\theta_Q+\underline\Pi_B\), then exact-filter the emitted tuples by the
   true score \(S_q(c)\ge\theta_Q\).  Store a data point \(x\) in tuple bucket
   \(c\) when \(S_x(c)\ge\theta_P\).  Assume the one-panel expected reporter
   work of this rectangle decoder is
   \[
      \E W_{\rm rect}(q)\le dL_m+m^\rho L_m
      \qquad(q\in\mathcal Q).
      \tag{RIC1}
   \]
   Suppose further that there are \(\alpha,\beta>0\) such that
   \[
      \E
      \sum_{x\in P}\sum_{B\in\mathcal B}
      e^{-\alpha(\theta_P+\underline\Pi_B)}
      \prod_{j=1}^h
      \sum_{a\in\mathcal C_{B,j}}e^{\alpha\chi_j(x,a)}
      \le m^{1+\rho}L_m,
      \tag{RIC2}
   \]
   and, for every promised query \(q\),
   \[
      \E
      \sum_{\substack{x\in P\\ \|x-q\|>cr}}
      \sum_{B\in\mathcal B}
      e^{-\alpha(\theta_P+\underline\Pi_B)
        -\beta(\theta_Q+\underline\Pi_B)}
      \prod_{j=1}^h
      \sum_{a\in\mathcal C_{B,j}}
      e^{\alpha\chi_j(x,a)+\beta\chi_j(q,a)}
      \le m^\rho L_m .
      \tag{RIC3}
   \]
   Finally assume every near pair \((p,q)\), \(\|p-q\|\le r\), satisfies
   \[
      \Pr\!\left[
      \exists c\in\mathcal C_1\times\cdots\times\mathcal C_h:
      S_p(c)\ge\theta_P,\quad S_q(c)\ge\theta_Q
      \right]\ge L_m^{-1}.
      \tag{RIC4}
   \]
   Then \(O(L_m)\) independent rectangular interaction-cover panels give
   terminal query work
   \[
      d\,m^\rho\log^{O_c(1)}m
   \]
   and space
   \[
      dm+m^{1+\rho}\log^{O_c(1)}m ,
   \]
   with rectangle and decoder metadata charged to the displayed polylogarithmic
   factors.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
   Completeness of the query reporter follows from \((RIC0)\).  If
   \(S_q(c)\ge\theta_Q\) and \(c\in B\), then
   \[
      \sum_j\chi_j(q,c_j)=S_q(c)+\Pi(c)
      \ge \theta_Q+\underline\Pi_B,
   \]
   so the product decoder for \(B\) emits \(c\), and exact filtering keeps it.
   Thus the reporter lists every query-active tuple.  Its work is bounded by
   \((RIC1)\).

   The storage bound is charged to a rectangle cover.  If \(S_x(c)\ge
   \theta_P\) and \(c\in B\), then
   \[
      \sum_j\chi_j(x,c_j)\ge\theta_P+\underline\Pi_B.
   \]
   Since every tuple belongs to at least one rectangle, the number of stored
   point-tuple incidences is at most the rectangle-overcounted sum of these raw
   threshold events.  Applying
   \[
      \mathbf 1\!\left\{\sum_j\chi_j(x,c_j)\ge
      \theta_P+\underline\Pi_B\right\}
      \le
      e^{-\alpha(\theta_P+\underline\Pi_B)}
      \prod_j e^{\alpha\chi_j(x,c_j)}
   \]
   and summing over the product rectangle gives exactly the left side of
   \((RIC2)\).

   The same overcount bounds far scanned incidences.  If a far point \(x\) is
   stored in tuple \(c\) and query \(q\) reports \(c\), then for every rectangle
   \(B\ni c\) both raw inequalities
   \[
      \sum_j\chi_j(x,c_j)\ge\theta_P+\underline\Pi_B,
      \qquad
      \sum_j\chi_j(q,c_j)\ge\theta_Q+\underline\Pi_B
   \]
   hold.  The two exponential majorants with exponents \(\alpha,\beta\), summed
   over \(B\) and factored over its coordinates, give \((RIC3)\).

   On the near event in \((RIC4)\), choose a witnessing tuple \(c\) and any
   rectangle \(B\ni c\).  The previous completeness argument makes \(c\)
   reported by the query, while the storage rule stores \(p\) in that bucket.
   Therefore one panel succeeds with probability at least \(L_m^{-1}\).
   Repeating \(O(L_m)\) independent panels, verifying all emitted candidates in
   the original metric, and truncating the expected bounds as usual gives the
   displayed terminal resources.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[How to use the interaction-cover certificate]
   \label{rem:interaction-cover-certificate}
   \Cref{prop:rectangular-interaction-cover-aq} is the precise product-style
   version of the additive-quantization idea.  It is useful when preprocessing
   can cover the relevant tuple space by \(\log^{O_c(1)}m\) product rectangles
   on which the interaction price \(\Pi(c)\) has certified width
   \(O_c(\log\log m)\).  Then replacing \(\Pi(c)\) by the lower endpoint
   \(\underline\Pi_B\) loses only a polylogarithmic factor in the exponential
   query, storage, and far-load moments, while exact filtering preserves the
   true additive-vector-quantization buckets.  If such a low-entropy
   rectangular cover is unavailable, the prefix reporter of
   \cref{lem:priced-prefix-additive-ivf-reporter} and the generic scored-label
   certificate remain the appropriate theorem objects.
\end{remark}

\begin{lemma}[Two-stage priced-pair additive-IVF reporter]
   \label{lem:priced-pair-additive-ivf-reporter}
   Let \(\mathcal A,\mathcal B\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be two finite pivot
   codebooks.  Put
   \[
      \chi(y,a)=\ip{y}{a}-\frac12\|a\|^2,
      \qquad
      \zeta(z,b)=\ip{z}{b}-\frac12\|b\|^2 .
   \]
   For a pair \((a,b)\), define the full additive-quantization query score
   \[
      S_q(a,b)
      =
      \ip{q}{a+b}-\frac12\|a+b\|^2
      =
      \chi(q,a)+\zeta(q-a,b).
      \tag{PAIR}
   \]
   Let \(M(z)\ge\max_{b\in\mathcal B}\zeta(z,b)\).  Suppose there is a
   certified first-stage reporter which, for every \(q,\Theta\), lists all
   pivots \(a\in\mathcal A\) satisfying
   \[
      \chi(q,a)+M(q-a)\ge\Theta
      \tag{PPR0}
   \]
   in work \(D_0(q,\Theta)\) plus a constant per listed pivot.  Suppose also
   that the second codebook has a certified threshold reporter which, for every
   shifted query \(z\) and threshold \(\theta\), lists all
   \(b\in\mathcal B\) satisfying
   \[
      \zeta(z,b)\ge\theta
   \]
   in work \(D_1(z,\theta)\) plus a constant per listed pivot.

   The two-stage reporter first lists all first-stage pivots satisfying
   \((PPR0)\).  For each such \(a\), it runs the second reporter on
   \(z=q-a\) with threshold \(\Theta-\chi(q,a)\), and outputs the exact pairs
   that pass \(S_q(a,b)\ge\Theta\).  Then it outputs every pair whose
   additive-quantization score is at least \(\Theta\).

   Moreover, for every \(\beta>0\), its work is at most a logarithmic priority
   factor times
   \[
      D_0(q,\Theta)+1
      +
      e^{-\beta\Theta}P_\beta^{\rm pair}(q,\Theta),
      \tag{PPR1}
   \]
   where
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      P_\beta^{\rm pair}(q,\Theta)
      &=
      \sum_{a\in\mathcal A}
      e^{\beta(\chi(q,a)+M(q-a))}
      \\
      &\quad+
      \sum_{a\in\mathcal A}
      D_1(q-a,\Theta-\chi(q,a))
      e^{\beta(\chi(q,a)+M(q-a))}
      \\
      &\quad+
      \sum_{a\in\mathcal A}
      e^{\beta\chi(q,a)}
      \sum_{b\in\mathcal B}e^{\beta\zeta(q-a,b)} .
   \end{aligned}
   \tag{PPR2}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   If \(S_q(a,b)\ge\Theta\), then
   \[
      \chi(q,a)+M(q-a)
      \ge
      \chi(q,a)+\zeta(q-a,b)
      =
      S_q(a,b)
      \ge\Theta,
   \]
   so the first-stage reporter lists \(a\).  The second-stage threshold is
   exactly
   \[
      \zeta(q-a,b)\ge\Theta-\chi(q,a),
   \]
   hence it lists \(b\), and exact score filtering outputs the pair.

   The number of live first-stage pivots is bounded by the exponential
   majorant
   \[
      \sum_{a:\chi(q,a)+M(q-a)\ge\Theta}1
      \le
      e^{-\beta\Theta}
      \sum_a e^{\beta(\chi(q,a)+M(q-a))}.
   \]
   The fixed second-stage reporter costs are paid once for every live
   first-stage pivot, so the same majorant with the factor
   \(D_1(q-a,\Theta-\chi(q,a))\) gives the second sum in \((PPR2)\).  Finally,
   for each live \(a\), the number of reported second pivots is at most
   \[
      e^{-\beta(\Theta-\chi(q,a))}
      \sum_b e^{\beta\zeta(q-a,b)}.
   \]
   Summing over all \(a\) gives the third sum.  The stated work bound follows
   after adding the first-stage reporter cost and the standard priority-queue
   logarithm.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Priced-prefix additive-IVF reporter]
   \label{lem:priced-prefix-additive-ivf-reporter}
   Let \(\mathcal C_1,\ldots,\mathcal C_h\subset\mathbb R^d\) be finite
   codebooks in the same ambient space.  For a prefix
   \(u=(c_1,\ldots,c_j)\), write
   \[
      A(u)=\sum_{i=1}^j c_i,
      \qquad
      s_y(u)=\ip{y}{A(u)}-\frac12\|A(u)\|^2,
   \]
   with \(A(\varnothing)=0\) and \(s_y(\varnothing)=0\).  For a suffix
   \(v=(c_j,\ldots,c_h)\), define the suffix score
   \[
      S_z^{j:h}(v)=\ip{z}{A(v)}-\frac12\|A(v)\|^2 .
   \]
   Also set \(S_z^{h+1:h}(\varnothing)=0\).
   Then every complete tuple \(c=(c_1,\ldots,c_h)\) satisfies the exact
   shifted-prefix identity
   \[
      S_y^{1:h}(c)
      =
      s_y(c_1,\ldots,c_j)
      +
      S_{y-A(c_1,\ldots,c_j)}^{j+1:h}(c_{j+1},\ldots,c_h)
      \tag{PFX0}
   \]
   for all \(0\le j\le h\).  Equivalently, the incremental score of adding
   \(c_{j+1}\) after prefix \(u\) is
   \[
      s_y(uc_{j+1})-s_y(u)
      =
      \ip{y-A(u)}{c_{j+1}}-\frac12\|c_{j+1}\|^2 .
      \tag{PFX1}
   \]

   Suppose preprocessing supplies admissible suffix upper bounds
   \(M_j(z)\), \(1\le j\le h+1\), with \(M_{h+1}\equiv0\), such that
   \[
      M_j(z)\ge
      \max_{v\in\mathcal C_j\times\cdots\times\mathcal C_h}
      S_z^{j:h}(v).
      \tag{PFX2}
   \]
   For a prefix \(u\) of length \(j\), put
   \[
      U_q(u)=s_q(u)+M_{j+1}(q-A(u)).
      \tag{PFX3}
   \]
   Assume that, for every live prefix \(u\) of length \(j-1\), a certified
   one-step reporter lists all \(c\in\mathcal C_j\) satisfying
   \[
      U_q(uc)\ge\Theta
      \tag{PFX4}
   \]
   in work \(D_j(q,u,\Theta)\) plus a constant per listed child.

   The stack decoder that starts from \(\varnothing\), expands exactly prefixes
   with \(U_q(u)\ge\Theta\), and exact-filters terminal tuples outputs every
   tuple \(c\in\mathcal C_1\times\cdots\times\mathcal C_h\) with
   \(S_q^{1:h}(c)\ge\Theta\).  Moreover, for every \(\beta>0\), its work is at
   most
   \[
      1+
      e^{-\beta\Theta}
      \sum_{j=0}^{h-1}
      \sum_{u\in\mathcal C_1\times\cdots\times\mathcal C_j}
      D_{j+1}(q,u,\Theta)e^{\beta U_q(u)}
      +
      e^{-\beta\Theta}
      \sum_{j=1}^h
      \sum_{u\in\mathcal C_1\times\cdots\times\mathcal C_j}
      e^{\beta U_q(u)} .
      \tag{PFX5}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   The identity \((PFX1)\) follows from
   \[
      \|A(u)+c\|^2=\|A(u)\|^2+2\ip{A(u)}{c}+\|c\|^2.
   \]
   Summing these increments gives \((PFX0)\).  If a complete tuple \(c\)
   satisfies \(S_q^{1:h}(c)\ge\Theta\), then for every prefix \(u\) of \(c\),
   \((PFX0)\) and the admissibility of \(M\) give
   \[
      U_q(u)\ge S_q^{1:h}(c)\ge\Theta .
   \]
   Thus every prefix of \(c\) is live, so the stack decoder eventually reaches
   \(c\).  At depth \(h\), \(M_{h+1}=0\), hence \(U_q(c)=S_q^{1:h}(c)\), and
   exact filtering outputs \(c\).

   Let \(L_j=\{u\in\mathcal C_1\times\cdots\times\mathcal C_j:U_q(u)\ge
   \Theta\}\).  The fixed reporter cost is
   \[
      \sum_{j=0}^{h-1}\sum_{u\in L_j}D_{j+1}(q,u,\Theta),
   \]
   and the number of listed child prefixes is at most
   \[
      \sum_{j=1}^h |L_j|.
   \]
   For any nonnegative \(a(u)\),
   \[
      \sum_{u\in L_j}a(u)
      \le
      e^{-\beta\Theta}\sum_u a(u)e^{\beta U_q(u)}.
   \]
   Applying this with \(a=D_{j+1}\) and with \(a\equiv1\) proves \((PFX5)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Gibbs-prefix additive-IVF sampler]
   \label{lem:gibbs-prefix-additive-ivf-sampler}
   Let \(\mathcal C_1,\ldots,\mathcal C_h\subset\mathbb R^d\) be finite
   codebooks in the same ambient space, and use the additive suffix scores
   \(S_z^{j:h}\) from \cref{lem:priced-prefix-additive-ivf-reporter}.  Fix
   \(\beta>0\).  Define the exact suffix partition functions
   \[
      Z_{h+1}(z)=1,
      \qquad
      Z_j(z)=
      \sum_{v\in\mathcal C_j\times\cdots\times\mathcal C_h}
      \exp\!\left(\beta S_z^{j:h}(v)\right).
   \]
   Then
   \[
      Z_j(z)=
      \sum_{a\in\mathcal C_j}
      \exp\!\left(\beta\left(\ip{z}{a}-\frac12\|a\|^2\right)\right)
      Z_{j+1}(z-a).
      \tag{GPS1}
   \]
   The following sequential procedure samples a complete tuple
   \(c=(c_1,\ldots,c_h)\) from the exact Gibbs law
   \[
      \pi_q(c)=
      \frac{\exp(\beta S_q^{1:h}(c))}{Z_1(q)}.
      \tag{GPS2}
   \]
   Start with \(z_1=q\).  At step \(j\), choose \(c_j=a\in\mathcal C_j\) with
   probability proportional to
   \[
      \exp\!\left(\beta\left(\ip{z_j}{a}-\frac12\|a\|^2\right)\right)
      Z_{j+1}(z_j-a),
      \tag{GPS3}
   \]
   and set \(z_{j+1}=z_j-c_j\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   The shifted-prefix identity \((PFX0)\) gives, for
   \(v=(a,c_{j+1},\ldots,c_h)\),
   \[
      S_z^{j:h}(v)
      =
      \ip{z}{a}-\frac12\|a\|^2
      +
      S_{z-a}^{j+1:h}(c_{j+1},\ldots,c_h).
   \]
   Summing \(\exp(\beta S_z^{j:h})\) over all suffixes with first symbol
   \(a\), and then over \(a\), proves \((GPS1)\).

   By \((GPS1)\), the transition probabilities in \((GPS3)\) are normalized.
   The probability of outputting a fixed tuple \(c\) is the telescoping product
   \[
      \prod_{j=1}^h
      \frac{
         \exp\!\left(\beta(\ip{z_j}{c_j}-\|c_j\|^2/2)\right)
         Z_{j+1}(z_{j+1})
      }{
         Z_j(z_j)
      }
      =
      \frac{
         \exp(\beta S_q^{1:h}(c))
      }{
         Z_1(q)
      },
   \]
   because the additive score is the sum of the displayed residual increments.
   This is \((GPS2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Finite-state quotient sampler for additive IVF]
   \label{lem:gibbs-aq-state-quotient}
   Let
   \[
      \mathcal T=\mathcal C_1\times\cdots\times\mathcal C_h
   \]
   be a nonorthogonal additive-IVF tuple family with score
   \[
      S_q(a)=\ip{q}{\sum_ja_j}
      -\frac12\left\|\sum_ja_j\right\|^2 .
   \]
   Let \(\lambda:\mathcal T\to\Lambda\) map tuples to retained bucket labels.
   Suppose that, for every query \(q\), a finite acyclic state graph with
   source \(s\), terminals \(\mathcal T_{\rm out}\), terminal-label map
   \(\lambda_{\rm out}:\mathcal T_{\rm out}\to\Lambda\), and positive edge
   weights \(r_e(q)\) satisfies the exact aggregate identity
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{t\in\mathcal T_{\rm out}\\ \lambda_{\rm out}(t)=\ell}}
      \sum_{\pi:s\leadsto t}\prod_{e\in\pi}r_e(q)
      =
      \sum_{\substack{a\in\mathcal T\\ \lambda(a)=\ell}}
      e^{\beta S_q(a)}
      \qquad(\ell\in\Lambda).
      \tag{AQS1}
   \]
   Then the backward-partition sampler on this graph outputs label
   \(\ell\) with probability
   \[
      \Pi_q(\ell)=
      \frac{\sum_{a:\lambda(a)=\ell}e^{\beta S_q(a)}}
           {\sum_{a\in\mathcal T}e^{\beta S_q(a)}}.
      \tag{AQS2}
   \]
   Its arithmetic work is linear in the number of evaluated graph edges and
   states.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Define suffix partition functions by
   \[
      H_q(t)=1\quad(t\in\mathcal T_{\rm out}),
      \qquad
      H_q(u)=\sum_{(u,v)}r_{(u,v)}(q)H_q(v)
   \]
   at nonterminal states.  The top-down transition rule
   \[
      (u,v)\text{ is chosen with probability }
      \frac{r_{(u,v)}(q)H_q(v)}{H_q(u)}
   \]
   samples a terminal \(t\) with probability proportional to the aggregate
   weight of all paths from \(s\) to \(t\).  Summing over terminals with label
   \(\ell\) and using \((AQS1)\) gives \((AQS2)\).  The dynamic program
   evaluates each retained edge and state once.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite-state sampled additive-IVF quotient]
   \label{cor:finite-state-sampled-aq}
   Fix a terminal localized ANN subproblem of size \(m\), approximation \(c\),
   and exponent \(\rho=\rho_c\).  Let \(L_m=\log^{A_c}m\).  A random
   finite-state sampled additive-IVF panel consists of finite ambient codebooks,
   tuple score \(S_q(a)\) as in \cref{lem:gibbs-aq-state-quotient}, a
   tuple-to-label map \(\lambda:\mathcal T\to\Lambda\), stored bucket sets
   \(C_\ell\subseteq P\), and an exact state-quotient sampler satisfying
   \((AQS1)\) whose query work is \(d\log^{O_c(1)}m\).  Put \(\Pi_q\) for the
   induced law \((AQS2)\).  If
   \[
      \E\sum_{\ell\in\Lambda}|C_\ell|
      \le m^{1+\rho}L_m,
      \tag{FSA1}
   \]
   and, for every promised query \(q\),
   \[
      \E
      \sum_{\substack{x\in P\\ \|x-q\|>cr}}
      \sum_{\ell:\,x\in C_\ell}\Pi_q(\ell)
      \le m^\rho L_m,
      \tag{FSA2}
   \]
   while every near pair \((p,q)\), \(\|p-q\|\le r\), satisfies
   \[
      \E
      \sum_{\ell:\,p\in C_\ell}\Pi_q(\ell)
      \ge L_m^{-1},
      \tag{FSA3}
   \]
   then \(O(L_m)\) independent finite-state sampled additive-IVF panels give
   terminal query work
   \[
      d\,m^\rho\log^{O_c(1)}m
   \]
   and space
   \[
      dm+m^{1+\rho}\log^{O_c(1)}m .
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \cref{prop:sampled-structured-panel} with label set \(\Lambda\),
   predicates \(A_\ell(x)=\mathbf 1\{x\in C_\ell\}\), and query law \(\Pi_q\).
   The three hypotheses \((FSA1)\)--\((FSA3)\) are exactly
   \((SP1)\)--\((SP3)\), and the state-quotient sampler supplies the required
   per-trial sampling time.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Stable quotienting preserves sampled spectra]
   \label{lem:stable-quotient-sampled-spectrum}
   Work with a tuple family \(\mathcal T\), tuple storage predicates
   \(U_x(a)\in\{0,1\}\), a quotient map
   \(\lambda:\mathcal T\to\Lambda\), and quotient buckets
   \[
      C_\ell=\{x\in P:\exists a\in\mathcal T,\ \lambda(a)=\ell,\ U_x(a)=1\}.
   \]
   For a query \(q\), let
   \[
      \pi_q(a)=\frac{e^{\beta S_q(a)}}{\sum_b e^{\beta S_q(b)}},
      \qquad
      \Pi_q(\ell)=\sum_{a:\lambda(a)=\ell}\pi_q(a).
   \]
   Suppose the quotient satisfies the following \(K\)-stability certificate for
   the query/load pairs under consideration: for every such \(q,x,\ell\),
   \[
      \mathbf 1_{\{x\in C_\ell\}}
      \sum_{a:\lambda(a)=\ell}e^{\beta S_q(a)}
      \le
      K\sum_{\substack{a:\lambda(a)=\ell}}U_x(a)e^{\beta S_q(a)}.
      \tag{SQS0}
   \]
   Then, pointwise in the realized panel,
   \[
      \sum_{\ell\in\Lambda}|C_\ell|
      \le
      \sum_{x\in P}\sum_{a\in\mathcal T}U_x(a),
      \tag{SQS1}
   \]
   and every promised query \(q\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{x\in P\\ \|x-q\|>cr}}
      \sum_{\ell:\,x\in C_\ell}\Pi_q(\ell)
      \le
      K
      \sum_{\substack{x\in P\\ \|x-q\|>cr}}
      \sum_{a\in\mathcal T}\pi_q(a)U_x(a).
      \tag{SQS2}
   \]
   Finally, for every near pair \((p,q)\),
   \[
      \sum_{\ell:\,p\in C_\ell}\Pi_q(\ell)
      \ge
      \sum_{a\in\mathcal T}\pi_q(a)U_p(a).
      \tag{SQS3}
   \]
   Consequently, if this sufficient certificate holds with
   \(K\le\log^{O_c(1)}m\) and the unquotiented tuple panel has
   the sampled storage, far-load, and near-mass bounds of
   \cref{prop:sampled-structured-panel} with predicates \(U_x(a)\), then the
   quotient buckets satisfy \((FSA1)\)--\((FSA3)\) after increasing the
   polylogarithmic exponent.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   The storage inequality follows because
   \[
      \mathbf 1_{\{x\in C_\ell\}}
      \le
      \sum_{a:\lambda(a)=\ell}U_x(a),
   \]
   and summing over \(x,\ell\) gives \((SQS1)\).

   For far load, divide \((SQS0)\) by the global partition function
   \(\sum_b e^{\beta S_q(b)}\).  This gives, for each \(x,\ell\),
   \[
      \mathbf 1_{\{x\in C_\ell\}}\Pi_q(\ell)
      \le
      K\sum_{a:\lambda(a)=\ell}\pi_q(a)U_x(a).
   \]
   Summing over far \(x\) and over \(\ell\) proves \((SQS2)\).

   If \(U_p(a)=1\), then \(p\in C_{\lambda(a)}\).  Therefore
   \[
      \sum_{\ell:\,p\in C_\ell}\Pi_q(\ell)
      =
      \sum_a\pi_q(a)\mathbf 1_{\{p\in C_{\lambda(a)}\}}
      \ge
      \sum_a\pi_q(a)U_p(a),
   \]
   proving \((SQS3)\).  Taking expectations over the random panel and applying
   the unquotiented sampled-panel bounds gives the final statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Score-spread sufficient condition for quotient stability]
   \label{cor:score-spread-quotient-stability}
   In the setting of \cref{lem:stable-quotient-sampled-spectrum}, fix a query
   \(q\), a point \(x\), and a quotient class
   \(A_\ell=\{a:\lambda(a)=\ell\}\).  If either \(x\notin C_\ell\), or
   \[
      |A_\ell|\le B
      \quad\text{and}\quad
      \max_{a,b\in A_\ell}|S_q(a)-S_q(b)|\le\Delta,
      \tag{SSQ0}
   \]
   then \((SQS0)\) holds for this \(q,x,\ell\) with
   \[
      K=B e^{\beta\Delta}.
      \tag{SSQ1}
   \]
   Hence quotient classes of polylogarithmic size and query-score spread
   satisfying \(\beta\Delta=O_c(\log\log m)\) preserve the sampled spectra up
   to a polylogarithmic factor.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(x\notin C_\ell\), the left side of \((SQS0)\) is zero.  Otherwise
   choose \(a_*\in A_\ell\) with \(U_x(a_*)=1\).  Under \((SSQ0)\),
   \[
      \sum_{a\in A_\ell}e^{\beta S_q(a)}
      \le
      B e^{\beta\Delta}e^{\beta S_q(a_*)}
      \le
      B e^{\beta\Delta}
      \sum_{a\in A_\ell}U_x(a)e^{\beta S_q(a)}.
   \]
   This is \((SQS0)\).  The final sentence is the condition
   \(B e^{\beta\Delta}=\log^{O_c(1)}m\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Responsibility-thinned quotient reporting]
   \label{lem:responsibility-thinned-quotient}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:stable-quotient-sampled-spectrum}.  For
   \(A_\ell=\{a:\lambda(a)=\ell\}\), define the hidden loaded mass and the
   conditional responsibility of point \(x\) inside quotient class \(\ell\) by
   \[
      h_{q,x,\ell}
      =
      \sum_{a\in A_\ell}\pi_q(a)U_x(a),
      \qquad
      r_{q,x,\ell}
      =
      \begin{cases}
      h_{q,x,\ell}/\Pi_q(\ell), & \Pi_q(\ell)>0,\\
      0, & \Pi_q(\ell)=0 .
      \end{cases}
   \]
   Suppose that, after sampling \(\ell\sim\Pi_q\), the query uses an
   output-sensitive subbucket reporter.  Let
   \(\theta_{q,x,\ell}\in[0,1]\) be the conditional probability that this
   reporter emits \(x\).  If, for some \(K\ge1\),
   \[
      r_{q,x,\ell}
      \le
      \theta_{q,x,\ell}
      \le
      \min\{1,K r_{q,x,\ell}\}
      \tag{RTQ0}
   \]
   for every query/load pair under consideration, then every promised query
   satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{x\in P\\ \|x-q\|>cr}}
      \sum_{\ell\in\Lambda}\Pi_q(\ell)\theta_{q,x,\ell}
      \le
      K
      \sum_{\substack{x\in P\\ \|x-q\|>cr}}
      \sum_{a\in\mathcal T}\pi_q(a)U_x(a),
      \tag{RTQ1}
   \]
   while every near pair \((p,q)\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{\ell\in\Lambda}\Pi_q(\ell)\theta_{q,p,\ell}
      \ge
      \sum_{a\in\mathcal T}\pi_q(a)U_p(a).
      \tag{RTQ2}
   \]
   Thus responsibility thinning preserves the sampled near spectrum and
   inflates the sampled far spectrum by at most \(K\), without requiring the
   whole quotient class to be score-stable.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Since \(\Pi_q(\ell)r_{q,x,\ell}=h_{q,x,\ell}\), the upper inequality in
   \((RTQ0)\) gives
   \[
      \Pi_q(\ell)\theta_{q,x,\ell}
      \le
      K h_{q,x,\ell}
      =
      K\sum_{a\in A_\ell}\pi_q(a)U_x(a).
   \]
   Summing over far \(x\) and over \(\ell\) proves \((RTQ1)\).  Similarly, the
   lower inequality in \((RTQ0)\) gives
   \[
      \sum_\ell\Pi_q(\ell)\theta_{q,p,\ell}
      \ge
      \sum_\ell h_{q,p,\ell}
      =
      \sum_{a\in\mathcal T}\pi_q(a)U_p(a),
   \]
   which is \((RTQ2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Responsibility-thinned sampled additive-IVF quotient]
   \label{cor:responsibility-thinned-sampled-aq}
   Fix the terminal setting of \cref{cor:finite-state-sampled-aq}, but replace
   full scanning of \(C_\ell\) by responsibility-thinned subbucket reporters as
   in \cref{lem:responsibility-thinned-quotient}.  Suppose their retained
   metadata and the unquotiented tuple incidences satisfy
   \[
      \E\sum_{x\in P}\sum_{a\in\mathcal T}U_x(a)
      \le m^{1+\rho}L_m,
      \tag{RTA1}
   \]
   their expected auxiliary reporter work after \(\ell\sim\Pi_q\) is at most
   \(dL_m+m^\rho L_m\) for every promised query, and their output
   probabilities satisfy \((RTQ0)\) with \(K\le\log^{O_c(1)}m\).  If
   \[
      \E
      \sum_{\substack{x\in P\\ \|x-q\|>cr}}
      \sum_{a\in\mathcal T}\pi_q(a)U_x(a)
      \le m^\rho L_m
      \tag{RTA2}
   \]
   for every promised query \(q\), and
   \[
      \E\sum_{a\in\mathcal T}\pi_q(a)U_p(a)
      \ge L_m^{-1}
      \tag{RTA3}
   \]
   for every near pair \((p,q)\), then \(O(L_m)\) independent panels give the
   same terminal ANN bounds as \cref{cor:finite-state-sampled-aq}, after
   increasing the polylogarithmic exponent.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \cref{lem:responsibility-thinned-quotient}, \((RTA2)\) bounds the
   expected invalid emitted candidates by \(m^\rho\log^{O_c(1)}m\), while
   \((RTA3)\) gives inverse-polylogarithmic probability that one panel emits
   the true near point.  The auxiliary reporter work has the same bound by
   hypothesis, and \((RTA1)\) bounds retained incidences and metadata.  Repeating
   \(O(L_m)\) independent panels, verifying every emitted candidate in the
   original metric, and using the standard capped-expectation truncation gives
   the displayed terminal resources.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Ordinary quotient scanning is the stable special case]
   \label{rem:ordinary-quotient-scanning-stability}
   Full scanning of the merged bucket \(C_\ell\) corresponds to
   \[
      \theta_{q,x,\ell}=\mathbf 1_{\{x\in C_\ell\}}.
   \]
   The lower inequality in \((RTQ0)\) is then automatic, because
   \(r_{q,x,\ell}>0\) implies \(x\in C_\ell\).  The upper inequality in
   \((RTQ0)\) is exactly the stability condition \((SQS0)\), after multiplying
   by the global partition function.  Thus
   \cref{lem:stable-quotient-sampled-spectrum} analyzes ordinary IVF-style
   union scanning, while \cref{lem:responsibility-thinned-quotient} gives the
   lower-overhead target: report only the points carrying hidden Gibbs
   responsibility inside the sampled quotient class.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[Gibbs sampled additive-IVF spectrum compiler]
   \label{prop:gibbs-sampled-additive-ivf-compiler}
   Fix a terminal localized ANN subproblem of size \(m\), approximation \(c\),
   and exponent \(\rho=\rho_c\).  Let \(L_m=\log^{A_c}m\).  A random sampled
   additive-IVF panel consists of finite ambient codebooks
   \(\mathcal C_1,\ldots,\mathcal C_h\), the true nonorthogonal additive score
   \[
      S_y(c_1,\ldots,c_h)
      =
      \ip{y}{\sum_jc_j}
      -\frac12\left\|\sum_jc_j\right\|^2,
   \]
   a storage threshold \(\theta_P\), and a query Gibbs sampler
   \[
      \pi_q(c)=
      \frac{e^{\beta S_q(c)}}{Z_q},
      \qquad
      Z_q=\sum_{a\in\mathcal C_1\times\cdots\times\mathcal C_h}e^{\beta S_q(a)}.
      \tag{GSA0}
   \]
   In this proposition, every unqualified sum over \(a\) ranges over
   \(\mathcal C_1\times\cdots\times\mathcal C_h\).
   Assume the sampler is exact and runs in \(d\log^{O_c(1)}m\) time per trial;
   \cref{lem:gibbs-prefix-additive-ivf-sampler} is the singleton-label
   implementation when the suffix partition functions can be evaluated
   compactly, while \cref{lem:gibbs-aq-state-quotient} is the corresponding
   bucket-quotient implementation.

   Suppose that, for some \(\alpha,\beta>0\),
   \[
      \E
      \sum_{x\in P}
      e^{-\alpha\theta_P}
      \sum_{a\in\mathcal C_1\times\cdots\times\mathcal C_h}
      e^{\alpha S_x(a)}
      \le m^{1+\rho}L_m,
      \tag{GSA1}
   \]
   and, for every promised query \(q\),
   \[
      \E
      \sum_{\substack{x\in P\\ \|x-q\|>cr}}
      \frac{
         e^{-\alpha\theta_P}
         \sum_{a}
         e^{\alpha S_x(a)+\beta S_q(a)}
      }{Z_q}
      \le m^\rho L_m .
      \tag{GSA2}
   \]
   Finally assume that every near pair \((p,q)\), \(\|p-q\|\le r\), satisfies
   \[
      \E
      \frac{
         \sum_{a:\,S_p(a)\ge\theta_P}e^{\beta S_q(a)}
      }{Z_q}
      \ge L_m^{-1}.
      \tag{GSA3}
   \]
   Then \(O(L_m)\) independent sampled additive-IVF panels give terminal query
   work
   \[
      d\,m^\rho\log^{O_c(1)}m
   \]
   and space
   \[
      dm+m^{1+\rho}\log^{O_c(1)}m .
   \]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
   Use \cref{prop:sampled-structured-panel} with label set
   \(\mathcal L=\mathcal C_1\times\cdots\times\mathcal C_h\), predicate
   \(A_a(x)=\mathbf 1\{S_x(a)\ge\theta_P\}\), and query law \(\pi_q\) from
   \((GSA0)\).  The storage condition \((SP1)\) follows from
   \[
      A_a(x)\le e^{\alpha(S_x(a)-\theta_P)}
   \]
   and \((GSA1)\).  For a far point \(x\),
   \[
      \sum_a\pi_q(a)A_a(x)
      \le
      \frac{
         e^{-\alpha\theta_P}
         \sum_a e^{\alpha S_x(a)+\beta S_q(a)}
      }{Z_q},
   \]
   so \((GSA2)\) implies \((SP2)\).  The near sampled mass condition
   \((SP3)\) is exactly \((GSA3)\).  The sampled-panel compiler gives the
   claimed resources.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Sampled AQ avoids the interaction-cover tax]
   \label{rem:sampled-aq-interaction}
   The all-reporting route for nonorthogonal additive quantization needs
   either low-width interaction rectangles, as in
   \cref{prop:rectangular-interaction-cover-aq}, or admissible upper bounds
   for a prefix list, as in \cref{lem:priced-prefix-additive-ivf-reporter}.
   The sampled route is different: \cref{lem:gibbs-prefix-additive-ivf-sampler}
   uses the true residual partition functions, so the interaction term is
   handled exactly rather than lower-bounded and exact-filtered afterward.
   The finite-state form in \cref{lem:gibbs-aq-state-quotient} also separates
   tuple entropy from retained-bucket entropy: many tuples may contribute to
   one stored bucket label if the state graph can sample their aggregate tilted
   mass directly.  The remaining theorem is correspondingly sharper and more
   spectral: build codebooks, a trellis, or a lattice quotient whose suffix
   partition functions are compactly samplable and whose retained buckets
   satisfy either the tuple spectrum \((GSA1)\)--\((GSA3)\) or the quotient
   certificate \((FSA1)\)--\((FSA3)\).  Lloyd or AQ distortion can be a
   proposal heuristic for those panels, but the proof object is the sampled
   spectrum and exact partition sampler.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[Priced-pair additive-IVF spectrum compiler]
   \label{prop:priced-pair-additive-ivf-compiler}
   Fix a terminal localized ANN subproblem of size \(m\), approximation \(c\),
   and exponent \(\rho=\rho_c\).  Let \(L_m=\log^{A_c}m\).  A random
   priced-pair additive-IVF panel consists of two codebooks
   \(\mathcal A,\mathcal B\), the score \(S_y(a,b)\) from \((PAIR)\), and
   thresholds \(\theta_P,\theta_Q\).  Store \(x\) in tuple bucket \((a,b)\)
   when \(S_x(a,b)\ge\theta_P\), and on query \(q\) report all tuple buckets
   with \(S_q(a,b)\ge\theta_Q\) using a certified reporter such as
   \cref{lem:priced-pair-additive-ivf-reporter}.

   Suppose that, for every promised query \(q\), the one-panel expected
   reporter work is
   \[
      \E W_{\rm pair}(q)\le dL_m+m^\rho L_m .
      \tag{PAQ1}
   \]
   Suppose further that there are \(\alpha,\beta>0\) such that
   \[
      \E
      \sum_{x\in P}
      e^{-\alpha\theta_P}
      \sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\sum_{b\in\mathcal B}
      e^{\alpha S_x(a,b)}
      \le
      m^{1+\rho}L_m,
      \tag{PAQ2}
   \]
   and, for every promised query \(q\),
   \[
      \E
      \sum_{\substack{x\in P\\ \|x-q\|>cr}}
      e^{-\alpha\theta_P-\beta\theta_Q}
      \sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\sum_{b\in\mathcal B}
      e^{\alpha S_x(a,b)+\beta S_q(a,b)}
      \le
      m^\rho L_m .
      \tag{PAQ3}
   \]
   Finally assume every near pair \((p,q)\), \(\|p-q\|\le r\), satisfies
   \[
      \Pr\!\left[
      \exists(a,b):
      S_p(a,b)\ge\theta_P,\quad S_q(a,b)\ge\theta_Q
      \right]
      \ge L_m^{-1}.
      \tag{PAQ4}
   \]
   Then \(O(L_m)\) independent priced-pair additive-IVF panels give terminal
   query work
   \[
      d\,m^\rho\log^{O_c(1)}m
   \]
   and space
   \[
      dm+m^{1+\rho}\log^{O_c(1)}m .
   \]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
   The query reporter lists every bucket with \(S_q(a,b)\ge\theta_Q\), so
   \((PAQ1)\) gives the expected one-panel decoding work.  The expected number
   of stored point-bucket incidences is at most the left side of \((PAQ2)\),
   by the exponential majorant
   \[
      \mathbf 1\{S_x(a,b)\ge\theta_P\}
      \le e^{\alpha(S_x(a,b)-\theta_P)} .
   \]
   Similarly, the expected number of far point-bucket incidences scanned by a
   query \(q\) is at most the left side of \((PAQ3)\), using
   \[
      \mathbf 1\{S_x(a,b)\ge\theta_P\}
      \mathbf 1\{S_q(a,b)\ge\theta_Q\}
      \le
      e^{\alpha(S_x(a,b)-\theta_P)+\beta(S_q(a,b)-\theta_Q)} .
   \]
   Store \(B=\lceil C L_m\rceil\) independent panels.  By \((PAQ4)\), every
   true near pair misses all common tuple buckets with probability at most
   \((1-L_m^{-1})^B\le e^{-C}\).  Taking \(C\) large gives constant success.
   Multiplying the one-panel query, scan, and storage bounds by
   \(B=\log^{O_c(1)}m\), and verifying candidates in the original metric,
   proves the claimed terminal resources.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Priced-prefix additive-IVF spectrum compiler]
   \label{prop:priced-prefix-additive-ivf-compiler}
   Fix a terminal localized ANN subproblem of size \(m\), approximation \(c\),
   and exponent \(\rho=\rho_c\).  Let \(L_m=\log^{A_c}m\).  A random
   priced-prefix additive-IVF panel consists of finite codebooks
   \(\mathcal C_1,\ldots,\mathcal C_h\), the tuple score
   \[
      S_y(c_1,\ldots,c_h)
      =
      \ip{y}{\sum_jc_j}-\frac12\left\|\sum_jc_j\right\|^2,
      \tag{PFX6}
   \]
   thresholds \(\theta_P,\theta_Q\), and a certified query reporter, for
   example the reporter of
   \cref{lem:priced-prefix-additive-ivf-reporter}, which outputs every tuple
   satisfying \(S_q(c_1,\ldots,c_h)\ge\theta_Q\).  Store \(x\) in tuple bucket
   \(c=(c_1,\ldots,c_h)\) when \(S_x(c)\ge\theta_P\).

   Suppose that, for every promised query \(q\), the one-panel expected
   reporter work is
   \[
      \E W_{\rm prefix}(q)\le dL_m+m^\rho L_m .
      \tag{PFX7}
   \]
   Suppose further that there are \(\alpha,\beta>0\) such that
   \[
      \E
      \sum_{x\in P}
      e^{-\alpha\theta_P}
      \sum_{c\in\mathcal C_1\times\cdots\times\mathcal C_h}
      e^{\alpha S_x(c)}
      \le
      m^{1+\rho}L_m,
      \tag{PFX8}
   \]
   and, for every promised query \(q\),
   \[
      \E
      \sum_{\substack{x\in P\\ \|x-q\|>cr}}
      e^{-\alpha\theta_P-\beta\theta_Q}
      \sum_{c\in\mathcal C_1\times\cdots\times\mathcal C_h}
      e^{\alpha S_x(c)+\beta S_q(c)}
      \le
      m^\rho L_m .
      \tag{PFX9}
   \]
   Finally assume every near pair \((p,q)\), \(\|p-q\|\le r\), satisfies
   \[
      \Pr\!\left[
      \exists c\in\mathcal C_1\times\cdots\times\mathcal C_h:
      S_p(c)\ge\theta_P,\quad S_q(c)\ge\theta_Q
      \right]
      \ge L_m^{-1}.
      \tag{PFX10}
   \]
   Then \(O(L_m)\) independent priced-prefix additive-IVF panels give terminal
   query work
   \[
      d\,m^\rho\log^{O_c(1)}m
   \]
   and space
   \[
      dm+m^{1+\rho}\log^{O_c(1)}m .
   \]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
   The proof is the same as for
   \cref{prop:priced-pair-additive-ivf-compiler}, with the pair label
   \((a,b)\) replaced by the tuple label
   \(c\in\mathcal C_1\times\cdots\times\mathcal C_h\).  The reporter lists
   every query-active tuple, giving \((PFX7)\).  The storage and far scanned
   incidences are bounded by the exponential majorants
   \[
      \mathbf 1\{S_x(c)\ge\theta_P\}
      \le e^{\alpha(S_x(c)-\theta_P)}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \mathbf 1\{S_x(c)\ge\theta_P\}
      \mathbf 1\{S_q(c)\ge\theta_Q\}
      \le
      e^{\alpha(S_x(c)-\theta_P)+\beta(S_q(c)-\theta_Q)} ,
   \]
   which give \((PFX8)\) and \((PFX9)\).  Repeating \(O(L_m)\) independent
   panels amplifies the near hit in \((PFX10)\) to constant success
   probability.  Candidate verification in the original metric removes false
   positives, and the expected bounds are truncated as usual.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[What the priced-pair certificate buys]
   \label{rem:priced-pair-certificate-buys}
   \Cref{prop:priced-pair-additive-ivf-compiler} is the exact nonorthogonal
   analogue of \cref{cor:additive-ivf-product-panel}.  It does not assume that
   additive quantization minimizes distortion, nor that Lloyd iterations
   converge to useful cells.  The theorem object is instead the four
   verifiable spectra \((PAQ1)\)--\((PAQ4)\).  The two-stage reporter in
   \cref{lem:priced-pair-additive-ivf-reporter} shows how the interaction term
   \(\ip{a}{b}\) is decoded: after choosing \(a\), the second codebook sees the
   shifted query \(q-a\).  Thus a full additive-vector-quantizer index can be
   analyzed if preprocessing constructs codebooks for which the pair reporter
   has small partition work and the retained pair buckets pass the same
   storage, far co-load, and near-hit tests as the product-panel route.
   \Cref{lem:priced-prefix-additive-ivf-reporter} and
   \cref{prop:priced-prefix-additive-ivf-compiler} remove the two-codebook
   restriction: after each selected codeword, the next codebook sees the
   residual query \(q-\sum_i c_i\), and admissible suffix scores certify the
   output-sensitive prefix list.
\end{remark}

\begin{proposition}[Finite retained priced-pair certificate]
   \label{prop:finite-retained-priced-pair}
   Fix one terminal localized ANN subproblem \(P\) of size \(m\), and let
   \(\mathcal Q\) be the promised query domain.  Let
   \(\Sigma\) be a finite signature set with map
   \(\sigma:\mathcal Q\to\Sigma\).  For each signature \(\sigma_0\), let
   \(N_{\sigma_0}\subseteq P\) contain every possible near witness for queries
   of that signature:
   \[
      \{p\in P:\exists q\in\mathcal Q,\ \sigma(q)=\sigma_0,\ \|p-q\|\le r\}
      \subseteq N_{\sigma_0}.
      \tag{FRP0}
   \]
   Suppose preprocessing has retained a finite batch of priced-pair panels
   \(t\in\mathcal T\).  Panel \(t\) has codebooks
   \(\mathcal A_t,\mathcal B_t\), thresholds
   \(\theta_{P,t},\theta_{Q,t}\), pair score \(S_y^t(a,b)\) as in
   \((PAIR)\), and a certified query reporter \(R_t(q)\subseteq
   \mathcal A_t\times\mathcal B_t\) which outputs every pair satisfying
   \(S_q^t(a,b)\ge\theta_{Q,t}\).  Write
   \[
      U_t(x,a,b)=\mathbf 1\{S_x^t(a,b)\ge\theta_{P,t}\}.
   \]
   Assume preprocessing certifies finite envelopes \(D_{\sigma_0,t}\),
   \(C_{\sigma_0,t,x}\), and \(H_{\sigma_0,t,p}\in\{0,1\}\) such that, for
   every query \(q\) with signature \(\sigma_0\),
   \[
      \operatorname{work}(R_t(q))\le D_{\sigma_0,t},
      \tag{FRP1}
   \]
   \[
      \mathbf 1_{\{\|x-q\|>cr\}}
      \sum_{(a,b)\in R_t(q)}U_t(x,a,b)
      \le C_{\sigma_0,t,x}
      \qquad(x\in P),
      \tag{FRP2}
   \]
   and, whenever \(H_{\sigma_0,t,p}=1\) and
   \(q\) has signature \(\sigma_0\) with \(\|p-q\|\le r\), there exists a
   reported stored pair:
   \[
      \exists(a,b)\in R_t(q)\quad U_t(p,a,b)=1.
      \tag{FRP3}
   \]
   Assume also that the retained batch satisfies the global storage envelope
   \[
      \sum_{t\in\mathcal T}\sum_{x\in P}
      \sum_{(a,b)\in\mathcal A_t\times\mathcal B_t}U_t(x,a,b)
      \le m^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}m,
      \tag{FRP5}
   \]
   If, for every signature \(\sigma_0\),
   \[
      \sum_{t\in\mathcal T}D_{\sigma_0,t}
      \le d\log^{O_c(1)}m+m^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}m,
      \tag{FRP4}
   \]
   \[
      \sum_{t\in\mathcal T}\sum_{x\in P}C_{\sigma_0,t,x}
      \le m^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}m,
      \tag{FRP6}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \sum_{t\in\mathcal T}H_{\sigma_0,t,p}\ge1
      \qquad(p\in N_{\sigma_0}),
      \tag{FRP7}
   \]
   then the retained batch is a deterministic terminal ANN structure with
   query work
   \[
      d\,m^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}m
   \]
   and space
   \[
      dm+m^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}m .
   \]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
   On query \(q\), run the reporters \(R_t(q)\), expose the reported pair
   buckets in any fixed order, verify each exposed point in the original
   metric, and stop at the first verified \(cr\)-neighbor.  The reporter work
   is bounded by \((FRP4)\).  The retained point-bucket incidences are exactly
   the left side of \((FRP5)\), giving the stated storage.

   Fix a query \(q\) of signature \(\sigma_0\).  The number of scanned far
   point incidences is at most
   \[
      \sum_{t\in\mathcal T}
      \sum_{\substack{x\in P\\ \|x-q\|>cr}}
      \sum_{(a,b)\in R_t(q)}U_t(x,a,b),
   \]
   which is at most the left side of \((FRP6)\) by \((FRP2)\).  Before the
   stopping time every rejected candidate is far, and the stopping candidate
   contributes at most one additional metric verification.  Hence the
   candidate-verification work is \(d\,m^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}m\), up to the
   harmless final valid check.

   If \(q\) has a near witness \(p\), then \(p\in N_{\sigma_0}\) by
   \((FRP0)\).  By \((FRP7)\), choose \(t\) with
   \(H_{\sigma_0,t,p}=1\).  Then \((FRP3)\) says that \(p\) is stored in a pair
   reported by \(R_t(q)\).  Therefore either the query has already accepted
   another \(cr\)-neighbor, or it eventually scans \(p\) and accepts.  Thus the
   structure is deterministic on the promised query domain, with the displayed
   resources.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Finite retained scored-label certificate]
   \label{prop:finite-retained-scored-label}
   Fix one terminal localized ANN subproblem \(P\) of size \(m\), and let
   \(\mathcal Q\) be the promised query domain.  Let
   \(\sigma:\mathcal Q\to\Sigma\) be a finite signature map, and for each
   \(\sigma_0\in\Sigma\) let \(N_{\sigma_0}\subseteq P\) contain every
   possible near witness for queries of that signature:
   \[
      \{p\in P:\exists q\in\mathcal Q,\ \sigma(q)=\sigma_0,\ \|p-q\|\le r\}
      \subseteq N_{\sigma_0}.
      \tag{FSL0}
   \]
   Suppose preprocessing has retained a finite batch of scored-label panels
   \(t\in\mathcal T\).  Panel \(t\) has a finite label set
   \(\mathcal L_t\), a certified query reporter
   \(R_t(q)\subseteq\mathcal L_t\), and a storage predicate
   \[
      U_t(x,\ell)\in\{0,1\}
      \qquad(x\in P,\ \ell\in\mathcal L_t).
   \]
   Assume preprocessing certifies finite envelopes \(D_{\sigma_0,t}\),
   \(C_{\sigma_0,t,x}\), and \(H_{\sigma_0,t,p}\in\{0,1\}\) such that, for
   every query \(q\) with signature \(\sigma_0\),
   \[
      \operatorname{work}(R_t(q))\le D_{\sigma_0,t},
      \tag{FSL1}
   \]
   \[
      \mathbf 1_{\{\|x-q\|>cr\}}
      \sum_{\ell\in R_t(q)}U_t(x,\ell)
      \le C_{\sigma_0,t,x}
      \qquad(x\in P),
      \tag{FSL2}
   \]
   and, whenever \(H_{\sigma_0,t,p}=1\) and
   \(q\) has signature \(\sigma_0\) with \(\|p-q\|\le r\), there exists a
   reported stored label:
   \[
      \exists \ell\in R_t(q)\quad U_t(p,\ell)=1.
      \tag{FSL3}
   \]
   Assume also the global storage envelope
   \[
      \sum_{t\in\mathcal T}\sum_{x\in P}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal L_t}
      U_t(x,\ell)
      \le m^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}m.
      \tag{FSL4}
   \]
   If, for every signature \(\sigma_0\),
   \[
      \sum_{t\in\mathcal T}D_{\sigma_0,t}
      \le d\log^{O_c(1)}m+m^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}m,
      \tag{FSL5}
   \]
   \[
      \sum_{t\in\mathcal T}\sum_{x\in P}C_{\sigma_0,t,x}
      \le m^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}m,
      \tag{FSL6}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \sum_{t\in\mathcal T}H_{\sigma_0,t,p}\ge1
      \qquad(p\in N_{\sigma_0}),
      \tag{FSL7}
   \]
   then the retained batch is a deterministic terminal ANN structure with
   query work
   \[
      d\,m^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}m
   \]
   and space
   \[
      dm+m^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}m .
   \]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
   On query \(q\), run the reporters \(R_t(q)\), expose the reported label
   buckets in any fixed order, verify each exposed point in the original
   metric, and stop at the first verified \(cr\)-neighbor.  The reporter work
   is bounded by \((FSL5)\), and \((FSL4)\) is exactly the retained
   point-label storage.

   Fix \(q\) with signature \(\sigma_0\).  Before the stopping time every
   rejected candidate is far, so the number of rejected point-label incidences
   is at most
   \[
      \sum_{t\in\mathcal T}
      \sum_{\substack{x\in P\\ \|x-q\|>cr}}
      \sum_{\ell\in R_t(q)}U_t(x,\ell),
   \]
   which is at most the left side of \((FSL6)\) by \((FSL2)\).  The final
   accepted candidate contributes at most one extra metric verification.
   Thus the candidate-verification work is
   \(d\,m^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}m\), up to the harmless final valid check.

   If \(q\) has a near witness \(p\), then \(p\in N_{\sigma_0}\) by
   \((FSL0)\).  By \((FSL7)\), choose \(t\) with
   \(H_{\sigma_0,t,p}=1\).  Then \((FSL3)\) says that \(p\) is stored in a
   reported label.  Therefore the query either has already accepted another
   \(cr\)-neighbor or eventually scans \(p\) and accepts.  The structure is
   deterministic on the promised query domain.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Build-time search versus retained proof]
   \label{rem:priced-pair-retained-proof}
   \Cref{prop:finite-retained-priced-pair} is the Las Vegas build-time form of
   the additive-IVF idea.  Preprocessing may generate candidate codebooks by
   \(k\)-means++, random centroids, additive quantization, column generation,
   or a list-decoding proposal routine.  None of those heuristics is trusted by
   the proof.  The retained index is accepted only after the finite reporter
   work, stored-incidence, far-load, and near-coverage envelopes
   \((FRP1)\)--\((FRP7)\) have been checked.  For a continuous query domain the
   hard part is now explicit: construct compact signatures whose envelopes
   certify \((FRP2)\) and \((FRP3)\) without a metric net of superpolynomial
   size.  For finite workloads or finite decoder transcripts, the certificate
   is directly checkable.  \Cref{prop:finite-retained-scored-label} is the same
   retained proof after forgetting the internal representation of a label, so
   pair buckets, prefix tuples, codewords, trellis terminals, and lattice
   residues can share the same final verifier.
\end{remark}

\begin{lemma}[Finite priced-pair LP dual]
   \label{lem:finite-priced-pair-lp-dual}
   Work in the setting of \cref{prop:finite-retained-priced-pair}, but replace
   the retained batch by a finite proposal universe \(\mathcal U\) of
   certified priced-pair panels.  For \(t\in\mathcal U\), let
   \(D_{\sigma,t}\), \(C_{\sigma,t,x}\), and \(H_{\sigma,t,p}\) be certified
   envelopes of the form \((FRP1)\)--\((FRP3)\), and define
   \[
      F_{\sigma,t}=\sum_{x\in P}C_{\sigma,t,x},
      \qquad
      S_t=
      \sum_{x\in P}
      \sum_{(a,b)\in\mathcal A_t\times\mathcal B_t}U_t(x,a,b).
   \]
   Fix budgets \(L_D,L_F,L_S>0\) and a coverage target \(h>0\).  Consider the
   fractional pair-panel feasibility problem
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \text{\rm find} & z_t\ge0\qquad(t\in\mathcal U)\\[0.3em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & \displaystyle \sum_tz_tD_{\sigma,t}\le L_D
        \qquad(\sigma\in\Sigma),\\[0.8em]
      & \displaystyle \sum_tz_tF_{\sigma,t}\le L_F
        \qquad(\sigma\in\Sigma),\\[0.8em]
      & \displaystyle \sum_tz_tS_t\le L_S,\\[0.8em]
      & \displaystyle \sum_tz_tH_{\sigma,t,p}\ge h
        \qquad(\sigma\in\Sigma,\ p\in N_\sigma).
   \end{array}
   \tag{\(\mathsf{PPLP}\)}
   \]
   This program is infeasible if and only if there are nonnegative prices
   \[
      \lambda_\sigma,\ \phi_\sigma,\ \psi,\ \mu_{\sigma,p}
   \]
   with strict surplus
   \[
      h\sum_{\sigma}\sum_{p\in N_\sigma}\mu_{\sigma,p}
      >
      L_D\sum_\sigma\lambda_\sigma
      +
      L_F\sum_\sigma\phi_\sigma
      +
      L_S\psi,
      \tag{PPLP1}
   \]
   such that every proposed panel has nonpositive reduced gain,
   \[
      \sum_\sigma\sum_{p\in N_\sigma}
      \mu_{\sigma,p}H_{\sigma,t,p}
      \le
      \sum_\sigma\lambda_\sigma D_{\sigma,t}
      +
      \sum_\sigma\phi_\sigma F_{\sigma,t}
      +
      \psi S_t
      \qquad(t\in\mathcal U).
      \tag{PPLP2}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   The converse is immediate.  If \(z\) were feasible, multiplying
   \((PPLP2)\) by \(z_t\), summing over \(t\), and using the constraints of
   \(\mathsf{PPLP}\) would give
   \[
      h\sum_{\sigma,p}\mu_{\sigma,p}
      \le
      L_D\sum_\sigma\lambda_\sigma
      +
      L_F\sum_\sigma\phi_\sigma
      +
      L_S\psi,
   \]
   contradicting \((PPLP1)\).

   For the forward implication, apply the finite-dimensional separating
   hyperplane theorem, equivalently Farkas' lemma, to the polyhedron
   \(\mathsf{PPLP}\).  The upper-bound constraints contribute the nonnegative
   multipliers \(\lambda,\phi,\psi\), and the lower-bound coverage constraints
   contribute the nonnegative multipliers \(\mu\).  Separating infeasibility
   gives a strict positive right-hand-side surplus and a nonpositive
   coefficient on every variable \(z_t\), which are exactly \((PPLP1)\) and
   \((PPLP2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Finite scored-label LP dual]
   \label{lem:finite-scored-label-lp-dual}
   Work in the setting of \cref{prop:finite-retained-scored-label}, but start
   from a finite proposal universe \(\mathcal U\) of certified scored-label
   panels.  For \(t\in\mathcal U\), define
   \[
      F_{\sigma,t}=\sum_{x\in P}C_{\sigma,t,x},
      \qquad
      S_t=\sum_{x\in P}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal L_t}U_t(x,\ell).
   \]
   Fix budgets \(L_D,L_F,L_S>0\) and a coverage target \(h>0\).  Consider the
   fractional scored-label feasibility problem
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \text{\rm find} & z_t\ge0\qquad(t\in\mathcal U)\\[0.3em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & \displaystyle \sum_tz_tD_{\sigma,t}\le L_D
        \qquad(\sigma\in\Sigma),\\[0.8em]
      & \displaystyle \sum_tz_tF_{\sigma,t}\le L_F
        \qquad(\sigma\in\Sigma),\\[0.8em]
      & \displaystyle \sum_tz_tS_t\le L_S,\\[0.8em]
      & \displaystyle \sum_tz_tH_{\sigma,t,p}\ge h
        \qquad(\sigma\in\Sigma,\ p\in N_\sigma).
   \end{array}
   \tag{\(\mathsf{FSLP}\)}
   \]
   This program is infeasible if and only if there are nonnegative prices
   \[
      \lambda_\sigma,\ \phi_\sigma,\ \psi,\ \mu_{\sigma,p}
   \]
   with strict surplus
   \[
      h\sum_{\sigma}\sum_{p\in N_\sigma}\mu_{\sigma,p}
      >
      L_D\sum_\sigma\lambda_\sigma
      +
      L_F\sum_\sigma\phi_\sigma
      +
      L_S\psi,
      \tag{FSLD1}
   \]
   such that every proposed scored-label panel has nonpositive reduced gain,
   \[
      \sum_\sigma\sum_{p\in N_\sigma}
      \mu_{\sigma,p}H_{\sigma,t,p}
      \le
      \sum_\sigma\lambda_\sigma D_{\sigma,t}
      +
      \sum_\sigma\phi_\sigma F_{\sigma,t}
      +
      \psi S_t
      \qquad(t\in\mathcal U).
      \tag{FSLD2}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   The proof is the same Farkas separation as
   \cref{lem:finite-priced-pair-lp-dual}.  If \(z\) is feasible and
   \((FSLD2)\) holds for every \(t\), multiplying by \(z_t\) and summing gives
   the opposite of the strict surplus \((FSLD1)\).

   Conversely, if \(\mathsf{FSLP}\) is infeasible, separate its finite
   constraint polyhedron from the nonnegative orthant.  Upper-bound constraints
   contribute the nonnegative prices \(\lambda,\phi,\psi\), and lower-bound
   witness constraints contribute the nonnegative prices \(\mu\).  The
   separated right-hand side is the strict surplus \((FSLD1)\), while the
   nonpositive coefficient of each variable \(z_t\) is exactly \((FSLD2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Scored-label column generation]
   \label{cor:scored-label-column-generation}
   Work with the finite proposal universe and budgets of
   \cref{lem:finite-scored-label-lp-dual}.  Assume that the full program
   \(\mathsf{FSLP}\) is feasible, and that preprocessing has an exact
   reduced-gain separator for \(\mathcal U\): given nonnegative prices
   \(\lambda,\phi,\psi,\mu\), it either returns a panel \(t\in\mathcal U\)
   with
   \[
      \sum_\sigma\sum_{p\in N_\sigma}\mu_{\sigma,p}H_{\sigma,t,p}
      >
      \sum_\sigma\lambda_\sigma D_{\sigma,t}
      +
      \sum_\sigma\phi_\sigma F_{\sigma,t}
      +
      \psi S_t
      \tag{FSLG}
   \]
   or certifies that none exists.  Then uncharged preprocessing can find
   feasible weights supported on at most
   \[
      2|\Sigma|+1+\sum_\sigma|N_\sigma|
   \]
   scored-label panels.  Consequently, under the atom, entropy, and
   polylogarithmic budget hypotheses of
   \cref{cor:fractional-scored-label-terminal}, exact column generation plus
   materialization produces the terminal retained index of that corollary.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Start from any finite restricted pool \(\mathcal V\subseteq\mathcal U\).
   If the restricted version of \(\mathsf{FSLP}\) over \(\mathcal V\) is
   feasible, minimize \(\sum_{t\in\mathcal V}z_t\) over the restricted
   feasible region.  The optimum is attained inside the compact sublevel set
   cut out by any feasible solution.  Choose an optimal basic feasible solution
   after adding slack variables.  There are
   \(2|\Sigma|+1+\sum_\sigma|N_\sigma|\) nontrivial constraints, so the
   support of the panel variables can be bounded by that number.

   If the restricted program is infeasible, apply
   \cref{lem:finite-scored-label-lp-dual} to \(\mathcal V\).  The resulting
   prices have strict surplus and nonpositive reduced gain on every panel in
   \(\mathcal V\).  Since the full program over \(\mathcal U\) is feasible,
   the same prices cannot have nonpositive reduced gain on all of
   \(\mathcal U\).  The exact separator therefore returns a positive-gain
   panel, and it is not already in \(\mathcal V\).  Add it and repeat.  The
   universe is finite, so the process terminates at a feasible restricted
   program, and the support reduction above gives the claimed bound.  The last
   sentence is \cref{cor:fractional-scored-label-terminal}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Fractional priced-pair materialization]
   \label{lem:fractional-priced-pair-materialization}
   Suppose \(\mathsf{PPLP}\) is feasible with \(0<h\le1\), and suppose every
   proposed panel satisfies the atom bounds
   \[
      D_{\sigma,t}\le L_D,\qquad
      F_{\sigma,t}\le L_F,\qquad
      S_t\le L_S
      \qquad(\sigma\in\Sigma,\ t\in\mathcal U).
      \tag{PPM0}
   \]
   Put
   \[
      M=1+2|\Sigma|+\sum_{\sigma\in\Sigma}|N_\sigma|
   \]
   and let
   \[
      B\ge \max\{1,\log(4M)\}.
   \]
   Then there is an integral retained subfamily
   \(\mathcal T\subseteq\mathcal U\) such that, for every signature
   \(\sigma\),
   \[
      \sum_{t\in\mathcal T}D_{\sigma,t}
      \le 6Bh^{-1}L_D,
      \tag{PPM1}
   \]
   \[
      \sum_{t\in\mathcal T}F_{\sigma,t}
      \le 6Bh^{-1}L_F,
      \tag{PPM2}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \sum_{t\in\mathcal T}H_{\sigma,t,p}\ge1
      \qquad(p\in N_\sigma),
      \tag{PPM3}
   \]
   while the global storage incidence satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{t\in\mathcal T}S_t\le6Bh^{-1}L_S.
      \tag{PPM4}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Let \(z\) be a feasible fractional solution.  Independently retain each
   panel \(t\) with probability
   \[
      p_t=\min\{1,Bz_t/h\}.
   \]
   Fix \(\sigma\) and \(p\in N_\sigma\).  If some panel with
   \(H_{\sigma,t,p}=1\) has \(p_t=1\), then \(p\) is certainly covered.
   Otherwise,
   \[
      \Pr\left[\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}H_{\sigma,t,p}=0\right]
      \le
      \exp\left(-\sum_t p_tH_{\sigma,t,p}\right)
      \le
      \exp\left(-Bh^{-1}\sum_tz_tH_{\sigma,t,p}\right)
      \le e^{-B}.
      \tag{PPM5}
   \]

   For a fixed signature \(\sigma\), the normalized reporter load
   \[
      X_\sigma=L_D^{-1}\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}D_{\sigma,t}
   \]
   is a sum of independent \([0,1]\)-valued random variables by \((PPM0)\),
   and
   \[
      \E X_\sigma
      \le
      Bh^{-1}L_D^{-1}\sum_tz_tD_{\sigma,t}
      \le Bh^{-1}.
   \]
   The elementary Chernoff bound
   \[
      \Pr[X_\sigma>6Bh^{-1}]\le e^{-Bh^{-1}}\le e^{-B}
   \]
   gives \((PPM1)\) except with probability at most \(e^{-B}\).  The same
   argument applied to \(L_F^{-1}\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}F_{\sigma,t}\) and to
   \(L_S^{-1}\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}S_t\) gives \((PPM2)\) and \((PPM4)\) with
   the same failure probability.

   There are at most \(M\) events to check: all witness-cover events, all
   reporter-work events, all far-load events, and the one storage event.  Since
   \(B\ge\log(4M)\), the union bound shows that all desired inequalities hold
   simultaneously with positive probability.  Hence such a retained subfamily
   exists.  Uncharged preprocessing may find it by repeated randomized
   materialization followed by the deterministic checks \((PPM1)\)--\((PPM4)\),
   or by exhaustive search over subfamilies.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Fractional priced-pair terminal compiler]
   \label{cor:fractional-priced-pair-terminal}
   Let \(L_m=\log^{A_c}m\).  Suppose the finite proposal universe in
   \cref{lem:finite-priced-pair-lp-dual} admits a fractional solution with
   \[
      h\ge L_m^{-1},
      \qquad
      L_D\le dL_m+m^{\rho_c}L_m,
      \qquad
      L_F\le m^{\rho_c}L_m,
      \qquad
      L_S\le m^{1+\rho_c}L_m,
   \]
   and suppose the atom bounds \((PPM0)\) hold.  If the finite constraint
   entropy satisfies
   \[
      \log\left(4+8|\Sigma|+4\sum_\sigma|N_\sigma|\right)
      \le L_m,
   \]
   then uncharged preprocessing can retain a priced-pair additive-IVF index
   with terminal query work
   \[
      d\,m^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}m
   \]
   and space
   \[
      dm+m^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}m .
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \cref{lem:fractional-priced-pair-materialization}.  Since
   \(Bh^{-1}\le\log^{O_c(1)}m\), the rounded family satisfies
   \[
      \sum_tD_{\sigma,t}
      \le d\log^{O_c(1)}m+m^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}m,
   \]
   \[
      \sum_tF_{\sigma,t}\le m^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}m,
      \qquad
      \sum_tS_t\le m^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}m,
   \]
   and covers every possible near witness.  These are exactly
   \((FRP4)\), \((FRP6)\), \((FRP5)\), and \((FRP7)\) for
   \cref{prop:finite-retained-priced-pair}.  That proposition gives the
   displayed terminal ANN resources.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Fractional scored-label terminal compiler]
   \label{cor:fractional-scored-label-terminal}
   Work in the setting of \cref{prop:finite-retained-scored-label}, but start
   from a finite proposal universe \(\mathcal U\) of certified scored-label
   panels.  For \(t\in\mathcal U\), define
   \[
      F_{\sigma,t}=\sum_{x\in P}C_{\sigma,t,x},
      \qquad
      S_t=\sum_{x\in P}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal L_t}U_t(x,\ell).
   \]
   Let \(L_m=\log^{A_c}m\).  Suppose there are nonnegative weights \(z_t\)
   satisfying
   \[
      \sum_tz_tD_{\sigma,t}\le L_D,
      \qquad
      \sum_tz_tF_{\sigma,t}\le L_F
      \qquad(\sigma\in\Sigma),
      \tag{FSLP1}
   \]
   \[
      \sum_tz_tS_t\le L_S,
      \qquad
      \sum_tz_tH_{\sigma,t,p}\ge h
      \qquad(\sigma\in\Sigma,\ p\in N_\sigma),
      \tag{FSLP2}
   \]
   with
   \[
      h\ge L_m^{-1},
      \qquad
      L_D\le dL_m+m^{\rho_c}L_m,
      \qquad
      L_F\le m^{\rho_c}L_m,
      \qquad
      L_S\le m^{1+\rho_c}L_m.
      \tag{FSLP3}
   \]
   Assume the atom bounds
   \[
      D_{\sigma,t}\le L_D,\qquad
      F_{\sigma,t}\le L_F,\qquad
      S_t\le L_S
      \qquad(\sigma\in\Sigma,\ t\in\mathcal U),
      \tag{FSLP4}
   \]
   and the finite constraint entropy bound
   \[
      \log\left(4+8|\Sigma|+4\sum_\sigma|N_\sigma|\right)
      \le L_m.
      \tag{FSLP5}
   \]
   Then uncharged preprocessing can retain an integral scored-label index with
   terminal query work
   \[
      d\,m^{\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}m
   \]
   and space
   \[
      dm+m^{1+\rho_c}\log^{O_c(1)}m .
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If necessary, replace \(h\) by \(\min\{h,1\}\); the hypotheses remain true
   and \(h^{-1}\) only changes by a constant factor.
   The proof of \cref{lem:fractional-priced-pair-materialization} uses only
   the four nonnegative column quantities \(D_{\sigma,t}\), \(F_{\sigma,t}\),
   \(S_t\), and \(H_{\sigma,t,p}\).  It does not use the fact that a label is
   a pair.  Applying the same independent rounding with probabilities
   \[
      p_t=\min\{1,Bz_t/h\},
      \qquad
      B\ge\max\left\{1,\log\left(4+8|\Sigma|+4\sum_\sigma|N_\sigma|\right)\right\},
   \]
   gives, with positive probability, an integral retained family satisfying
   \[
      \sum_tD_{\sigma,t}\le6Bh^{-1}L_D,\qquad
      \sum_tF_{\sigma,t}\le6Bh^{-1}L_F,
   \]
   \[
      \sum_tS_t\le6Bh^{-1}L_S,
      \qquad
      \sum_tH_{\sigma,t,p}\ge1 .
   \]
   By \((FSLP3)\)--\((FSLP5)\), these are precisely
   \((FSL4)\)--\((FSL7)\) after increasing the polylogarithmic exponent.
   Applying \cref{prop:finite-retained-scored-label} gives the displayed
   resources.  Preprocessing may repeat the rounding until the deterministic
   certificate passes.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[What this asks of \(k\)-means++ or AQ proposals]
   \label{rem:kmeans-pair-panel-dual}
   \Cref{lem:finite-scored-label-lp-dual} is the theory-facing replacement for
   a Lloyd or distortion objective.  If the current proposal pool is not
   fractionally sufficient, the dual prices assign value to uncovered
   signature--witness pairs and prices to reporter work, far scans, and stored
   incidences.  A build-time generator is useful exactly when, against every
   surplus dual price system, it proposes a panel whose near-witness gain
   exceeds those three costs.  Thus \(k\)-means++, residual \(D^2\) sampling,
   additive quantization training, learned pivots, or list-decoding proposals
   can all be used as separators in
   \cref{cor:scored-label-column-generation}.  The charged theorem is then the
   fractional LP plus the retained integral certificate of
   \cref{cor:fractional-scored-label-terminal}; no part of the argument is
   tied to pair labels.  In the recursive fractional-cover layer this same
   principle appears as \cref{lem:proposal-law-filter-separator}: the panel
   generator only has to prove positive expected reduced gain, or the equivalent
   marginal incidence inequality, against the current filter-cover dual.  Thus
   an additive-IVF or \(k\)-means++ panel is not a separate algorithmic case; it
   is a proposal law whose accepted outputs become ordinary filter columns.
\end{remark}

\begin{corollary}[Superset product-panel rate bookkeeping]
   \label{cor:superset-product-panel-rate-bookkeeping}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:product-panel-tensorization}, but use the
   superset block reporters of \cref{lem:superset-product-panel-decoder}.  Thus
   block \(j\)'s candidate work satisfies \((SR1)\) with functions
   \(A_j(q)\) and \(B_j(q)\).  For every query \(q\), suppose there are
   deterministic block factors \(\widehat{\mathfrak q}_j(q)\) such that, for
   every realization of block \(j\),
   \[
      e^{-\beta\theta_{Q,j}}Z_j^Q(q)
      \le\widehat{\mathfrak q}_j(q),
      \qquad
      e^{\beta(M_j(q)-\theta_{Q,j})}
      \le\widehat{\mathfrak q}_j(q),
      \tag{SRB1}
   \]
   \[
      A_j(q)e^{\beta(M_j(q)-\theta_{Q,j})}
      \le\widehat{\mathfrak q}_j(q),
      \qquad
      B_j(q)e^{-\beta\theta_{Q,j}}
      \le\widehat{\mathfrak q}_j(q).
      \tag{SRB2}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \prod_{j=1}^h\widehat{\mathfrak q}_j(q)
      \le m^\rho\log^{O_c(1)}m
      \qquad\text{for every promised query }q,
      \tag{SRB3}
   \]
   then the superset product decoder has one-panel query work
   \(m^\rho\log^{O_c(1)}m\), up to the explicit block score-evaluation
   preprocessing already included in \(A_j,B_j\).

   In particular, for the OSD block reporter of
   \cref{cor:osd-superset-block-reporter}, where
   \(B_j(q)=\exp(\beta M_j(q)+\Lambda_j(q))\), it is enough to choose
   \(\widehat{\mathfrak q}_j(q)\) satisfying
   \[
      e^{-\beta\theta_{Q,j}}Z_j^Q(q)
      \le\widehat{\mathfrak q}_j(q),
      \qquad
      \bigl(1+A_j(q)+e^{\Lambda_j(q)}\bigr)
      e^{\beta(M_j(q)-\theta_{Q,j})}
      \le\widehat{\mathfrak q}_j(q).
      \tag{SRB4}
   \]
   Thus the OSD query-rate penalty is exactly the entropy multiplier
   \(e^{\Lambda_j(q)}\) at the decoded block, plus the chart-construction term
   \(A_j(q)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   We bound \(e^{-\beta\theta_Q}\widehat P_\beta(q)\).  The first sum in
   \(\widehat P_\beta\) is the live-prefix sum from \((BT1)\) with coefficient
   \(1\), so every term is bounded by
   \(\prod_j\widehat{\mathfrak q}_j(q)\) using \((SRB1)\).

   For the fixed reporter-work term at level \(\ell\), let \(r=\ell+1\).
   After multiplying by \(e^{-\beta\theta_Q}\), the term factors as
   \[
      A_r(q)
      \prod_{j<r}\left(e^{-\beta\theta_{Q,j}}Z_j^Q(q)\right)
      e^{\beta(M_r(q)-\theta_{Q,r})}
      \prod_{j>r}e^{\beta(M_j(q)-\theta_{Q,j})}.
   \]
   This is at most \(\prod_j\widehat{\mathfrak q}_j(q)\) by \((SRB1)\) and
   the first inequality in \((SRB2)\).

   For the threshold-dependent candidate term at level \(\ell\), again put
   \(r=\ell+1\).  Multiplication by \(e^{-\beta\theta_Q}\) gives
   \[
      B_r(q)e^{-\beta\theta_{Q,r}}
      \prod_{j<r}\left(e^{-\beta\theta_{Q,j}}Z_j^Q(q)\right)
      \prod_{j>r}e^{\beta(M_j(q)-\theta_{Q,j})},
   \]
   which is also at most the product of the
   \(\widehat{\mathfrak q}_j(q)\)'s.  There are \(2h+1=\log^{O_c(1)}m\) sums,
   so \((SRB3)\) gives
   \[
      e^{-\beta\theta_Q}\widehat P_\beta(q)
      \le m^\rho\log^{O_c(1)}m .
   \]
   Substituting this into \cref{lem:superset-product-panel-decoder}, with
   terminal prices \(Q_c=0\), proves the query-work claim.

   For an OSD block,
   \[
      B_j(q)e^{-\beta\theta_{Q,j}}
      =
      e^{\Lambda_j(q)}e^{\beta(M_j(q)-\theta_{Q,j})}.
   \]
   Combining this with the live-prefix and fixed-work requirements gives
   \((SRB4)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Soft list-recovery blocks are threshold reporters]
   \label{lem:soft-list-recovery-reporter}
   Fix one product block \(j\).  Let
   \(\mathcal C_j\subseteq\Sigma_j^{b_j}\) be a code, and suppose the query
   score decomposes coordinatewise:
   \[
      \phi_j(q,c)=\sum_{i=1}^{b_j}\omega_{j,i}(q,c_i)
      \qquad(c=(c_1,\ldots,c_{b_j})\in\mathcal C_j).
   \]
   Suppose there is a certified soft list-recovery decoder which, for every
   query \(q\) and threshold \(\theta\), returns exactly
   \[
      \mathsf L_j(q,\theta)
      =
      \left\{
      c\in\mathcal C_j:
      \sum_{i=1}^{b_j}\omega_{j,i}(q,c_i)\ge\theta
      \right\}
   \]
   in work \(D_j(q)+O(|\mathsf L_j(q,\theta)|)\).  Then block \(j\) supplies
   the threshold reporter required by
   \cref{lem:additive-product-panel-decoder}.  Consequently, any
   code or lattice family with such certified soft reporters and with the
   one-block rate bounds of \cref{cor:product-panel-rate-bookkeeping}
   implements the product-panel terminal engine.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   The threshold reporter in \cref{lem:additive-product-panel-decoder} is
   precisely the map \((q,\theta)\mapsto\mathsf L_j(q,\theta)\).  Substituting
   the certified work bound for \(D_j(q)\) gives the decoder work estimate.
   The final statement is the composition with
   \cref{lem:additive-product-panel-decoder},
   \cref{prop:product-panel-spectrum-compiler}, and
   \cref{cor:product-panel-rate-bookkeeping}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Euclidean list decoders are soft-score reporters]
   \label{cor:euclidean-list-decoder-reporter}
   Let a block code \(\mathcal C\subseteq\Sigma^h\) have symbol embeddings
   \(a\mapsto v_i(a)\in\mathbb R^{d_i}\).  For a query block
   \(y=(y_1,\ldots,y_h)\), define the Euclidean score
   \[
      S_y(c)
      =
      \sum_{i=1}^h
      \left(\ip{y_i}{v_i(c_i)}-\frac12\|v_i(c_i)\|^2\right).
   \]
   Suppose a certified Euclidean list decoder for the embedded code
   \(V(c)=(v_1(c_1),\ldots,v_h(c_h))\) returns, for every radius \(R\), every
   codeword satisfying
   \[
      \sum_{i=1}^h\|y_i-v_i(c_i)\|^2\le R^2
   \]
   in work \(D_{\rm Euc}(y,R)+O(|L(y,R)|)\).  Then, for every threshold
   \(\theta\), calling this decoder with
   \[
      R^2=\sum_{i=1}^h\|y_i\|^2-2\theta
   \]
   gives a certified threshold reporter for
   \[
      \{c\in\mathcal C:\ S_y(c)\ge\theta\}.
   \]
   Consequently, Euclidean Reed--Solomon, Barnes--Sloane, Construction-A, or
   lattice quotient decoders can be used directly as block reporters whenever
   their list-size and work certificates match the product-panel rates.  No
   repeated-coordinate discretization is needed for scores of this form.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For every codeword \(c\),
   \[
      S_y(c)
      =
      \frac12\sum_{i=1}^h\|y_i\|^2
      -
      \frac12\sum_{i=1}^h\|y_i-v_i(c_i)\|^2 .
   \]
   Thus \(S_y(c)\ge\theta\) is exactly the displayed Euclidean-radius
   condition with \(R^2=\sum_i\|y_i\|^2-2\theta\).  The work statement is the
   assumed certified decoder work, and the composition with the product-panel
   framework is the same as in \cref{lem:soft-list-recovery-reporter}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Hard list-recovery lift for soft scores]
   \label{lem:hard-list-recovery-lift}
   Let \(\mathcal C\subseteq\Sigma^h\) be a code and let a query \(q\)
   assign bounded nonnegative symbol scores
   \[
      0\le\omega_i(q,a)\le M
      \qquad(i\in[h],\ a\in\Sigma).
   \]
   For \(c\in\mathcal C\), put
   \[
      S_q(c)=\sum_{i=1}^h\omega_i(q,c_i).
   \]
   Fix a mesh \(\Delta>0\), let \(L=\lceil M/\Delta\rceil\), and define
   threshold lists
   \[
      \Gamma_{i,\ell}(q)=
      \{a\in\Sigma:\ \omega_i(q,a)\ge \ell\Delta\},
      \qquad i\in[h],\ \ell\in[L].
   \]
   Suppose there is a certified list-recovery oracle for the repeated-coordinate
   lift of \(\mathcal C\) which, for any integer \(A\), returns a superset of
   \[
      \left\{
      c\in\mathcal C:\
      \sum_{i=1}^h\sum_{\ell=1}^{L}
      \mathbf 1\{c_i\in\Gamma_{i,\ell}(q)\}\ge A
      \right\}
   \]
   and includes every codeword in this set, in work
   \(D_{\rm LR}(q,A)+O(|\mathsf O|h)\), where \(\mathsf O\) is the returned
   output list.  Then, for every score threshold \(\Theta\), running the oracle
   with
   \[
      A=\max\left\{0,\left\lceil \frac{\Theta}{\Delta}-h\right\rceil\right\}
   \]
   and filtering the returned codewords by the exact score \(S_q(c)\ge\Theta\)
   gives a certified threshold reporter for
   \[
      \{c\in\mathcal C:\ S_q(c)\ge\Theta\}.
   \]
   Its work is \(D_{\rm LR}(q,A)+O(|\mathsf O|h)\), plus the work needed to
   build the lists \(\Gamma_{i,\ell}(q)\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   For a fixed coordinate with score \(w=\omega_i(q,c_i)\),
   \[
      \sum_{\ell=1}^{L}\mathbf 1\{w\ge \ell\Delta\}
      =
      \left\lfloor \frac{w}{\Delta}\right\rfloor
      \ge
      \frac{w}{\Delta}-1 .
   \]
