   single class \(\mathcal N_j\); exact verification against the original prices
   then certifies \((CQ1)\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   The identity \((DUQ2)\) follows by expanding
   \[
      \sum_G\frac{\lambda_G}{b_G}
      \sum_{(z,q)\in\mathcal I_G}A_{z,q}
   \]
   and collecting the coefficient of each demand pair.  By \((DUQ3)\),
   \[
      \mathsf A_\lambda
      \le
      2\sum_{j=1}^J\mathsf A_{\lambda,j}.
   \]
   If \((DUQ5)\) holds, then
   \[
      \sum_{j=1}^J\mathsf A_{\lambda,j}
      >
      J
      \sum_G\lambda_G
      \left[
         T_G\sum_q\tau_qa_G(q)+\sigma S_G
      \right].
   \]
   One layer must therefore satisfy \((DUQ6)\).  Since every pair in
   \(\mathcal N_j\) has original price at least \(\theta_j\), the original conic
   demand contributed by that layer is at least \(\mathsf A_{\lambda,j}\).  Thus
   \((DUQ6)\) implies the strict conic inequality \((CQ1)\), and
   \cref{cor:conic-quotient-packing} exposes a positive-gain quotient.
\end{proof}

The factor \(J\) is only a build-time search loss: after a candidate layer and
quotient packing are proposed, the verifier evaluates the original weighted
objective \((CQ1)\).  If the relevant dual prices lie in a polynomial window then
\(J=O(\log n)\); if not, preprocessing may still enumerate more classes without
changing the retained query or storage certificate.

\begin{corollary}[Unweighted quotient coverage screen]
   \label{cor:unweighted-quotient-coverage-screen}
   Fix one dyadic class \(\mathcal N_j\) from
   \cref{lem:dyadic-quotient-packing}.  For a quotient \(G\), define its
   de-duplicated unweighted layer coverage by
   \[
      C_j(G)
      =
      \frac1{b_G}
      \sum_{(z,q)\in\mathcal I_G}
      \left|
         \{p\in V_{z,q}:(p,q)\in\mathcal N_j\}
      \right|
      \tag{UQ1}
   \]
   and its dual price by
   \[
      P(G)=T_G\sum_q\tau_qa_G(q)+\sigma S_G.
      \tag{UQ2}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \theta_j C_j(G)>P(G),
      \tag{UQ3}
   \]
   then \(G\) has positive reduced gain.  Conversely, if a conic layer witness
   satisfies \((DUQ6)\), then some quotient \(G\) in its support satisfies
   \((UQ3)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Since every demand pair in \(\mathcal N_j\) has original price at least
   \(\theta_j\), the true captured demand of \(G\) is at least
   \(\theta_j C_j(G)\).  Thus \((UQ3)\) implies true captured demand greater than
   \(P(G)\), which is positive reduced gain.

   For the converse, write \((DUQ6)\) for the conic intensities as
   \[
      \sum_G\lambda_G\theta_j C_j(G)>
      \sum_G\lambda_GP(G).
   \]
   If every \(G\) in the support had \(\theta_jC_j(G)\le P(G)\), the displayed
   strict inequality would be impossible.  Hence some support quotient satisfies
   \((UQ3)\).
\end{proof}

Thus after dyadic unweighting, quotient generation is an ordinary unweighted
coverage problem with a priced threshold \(P(G)/\theta_j\).  A proposal routine
may list quotients with large \(C_j(G)\), but every returned quotient is still
checked against the exact weighted reduced-gain inequality before it is retained.

\begin{lemma}[Captured-demand dyadic layer]
   \label{lem:captured-demand-dyadic-layer}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:high-correlation-dense-slice-separator}.
   Assume every demanded pair satisfies \(p\in H(q)\), and let
   \(\mathcal N_1,\ldots,\mathcal N_J\) be dyadic classes of the positive demand
   prices as in \cref{lem:dyadic-quotient-packing}.  Define the unweighted
   captured layer mass
   \[
      B_j
      =
      \theta_j\,
      \E_{Z\sim\Pi}
      \sum_q
      \left|
         \{p\in V_{Z,q}:(p,q)\in\mathcal N_j\}
      \right|.
      \tag{CDL1}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \sum_{j=1}^JB_j
      \ge
      \frac12
      \E_{Z\sim\Pi}\sum_qA_{Z,q}
      \ge
      \frac{\pi_1}{2}A_\alpha .
      \tag{CDL2}
   \]
   Consequently some dyadic layer satisfies
   \[
      B_j\ge \frac{\pi_1}{2J}A_\alpha .
      \tag{CDL3}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   By the dyadic definition, every pair in \(\mathcal N_j\) has
   \(\alpha_{p,q}<2\theta_j\).  Therefore
   \[
      \E_Z\sum_qA_{Z,q}
      \le
      2\sum_{j=1}^JB_j,
   \]
   which gives the first inequality in \((CDL2)\).  For the second, expand the
   captured demand:
   \[
      \E_Z\sum_qA_{Z,q}
      =
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}
      \alpha_{p,q}\Pr_Z[p\in U_Z\cap H(q)].
   \]
   Since every demand has \(p\in H(q)\), the probability on the right is at
   least \(\Pr_Z[p\in U_Z,\chi_Z(q)=1]\), which is at least \(\pi_1\) by
   \((WS1)\).  This proves \((CDL2)\).  The pigeonhole principle gives
   \((CDL3)\).
\end{proof}

\Cref{lem:captured-demand-dyadic-layer} identifies the layer that a quotient
separator should try to compress.  The loss \(J\) belongs to build-time layer
search and to proof bookkeeping; after a quotient is proposed, the retained
certificate still checks the original weighted reduced gain.

\begin{lemma}[Hinge form of query-side quotient activation]
   \label{lem:hinge-quotient-activation}
   Fix a dyadic layer \(\mathcal N_j\) and a quotient \(G\) as in
   \cref{cor:unweighted-quotient-coverage-screen}.  Define its query-local
   de-duplicated layer coverage by
   \[
      C_j(G;q)
      =
      \frac1{b_G}
      \sum_{\substack{z:(z,q)\in\mathcal I_G}}
      \left|
         \{p\in V_{z,q}:(p,q)\in\mathcal N_j\}
      \right|.
      \tag{HQ1}
   \]
   Thus \(C_j(G)=\sum_qC_j(G;q)\).  Suppose the quotient universe is closed under
   activation restriction: for every subset \(Q'\subseteq\{q:a_G(q)=1\}\), it
   contains the restricted quotient \(G|Q'\) with the same update side and
   certified prices \(T_G,S_G\), activation only on \(Q'\), and assigned
   primitive slices \(\{(z,q)\in\mathcal I_G:q\in Q'\}\).

   If \(G\) satisfies the layer screen
   \[
      \theta_jC_j(G)>T_G\sum_q\tau_qa_G(q)+\sigma S_G,
      \tag{HQ2}
   \]
   then the positive-margin restriction
   \[
      Q^+(G)=
      \{q:a_G(q)=1,\ \theta_jC_j(G;q)>T_G\tau_q\}
   \]
   also satisfies the layer screen.  Equivalently, under activation-restriction
   closure, a positive layer quotient exists if and only if some quotient core
   satisfies the hinge inequality
   \[
      \sum_q
      \bigl(\theta_jC_j(G;q)-T_G\tau_q\bigr)_+
      >
      \sigma S_G .
      \tag{HQ3}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Put
   \[
      d_q=\theta_jC_j(G;q)-T_G\tau_q
   \]
   for active queries and \(d_q=0\) otherwise.  The layer surplus of \(G\) is
   \[
      \sum_qd_q-\sigma S_G.
   \]
   If this is positive, then \(\sum_q(d_q)_+>\sigma S_G\), so \(Q^+(G)\) is
   nonempty.  The restricted quotient has the same storage price, no larger
   query-price term, and duplicate factor at most \(b_G\).  Therefore its true
   de-duplicated coverage is at least the sum of the old \(C_j(G;q)\) over
   \(Q^+(G)\).  Its layer surplus is at least
   \[
      \sum_q(d_q)_+-\sigma S_G>0,
   \]
   proving the first claim.

   If a quotient satisfies \((HQ3)\), then restricting it to the positive-margin
   queries gives a quotient satisfying \((HQ2)\), hence a positive layer
   quotient by \cref{cor:unweighted-quotient-coverage-screen}.  Conversely, any
   quotient satisfying \((HQ2)\) has \(\sum_q(d_q)_+>\sigma S_G\), which is
   \((HQ3)\).
\end{proof}

\Cref{lem:hinge-quotient-activation} removes another artificial choice from the
dense side.  A proposal routine may search only for an update-side quotient core
and its primitive incidences.  The query side is then determined by the dual
prices: activate exactly those queries whose layer coverage beats their local
query charge, and test whether the remaining positive margins pay the one-time
storage price.  This is the fractional analogue of merging many dense children:
overlap at a query is not forbidden, it is bought only when its local margin is
positive.

\begin{lemma}[Dyadic query-margin layer]
   \label{lem:dyadic-query-margin-layer}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:hinge-quotient-activation}.  For a quotient
   core \(G\), write its positive query margins as
   \[
      d_q(G)=
      \bigl(\theta_jC_j(G;q)-T_G\tau_q\bigr)_+ .
   \]
   Partition the positive margins into dyadic classes
   \(\mathcal Q_1,\ldots,\mathcal Q_K\), where
   \[
      \Delta_\ell\le d_q(G)<2\Delta_\ell
      \qquad(q\in\mathcal Q_\ell).
      \tag{DQM1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \sum_qd_q(G)>2K\,\sigma S_G,
      \tag{DQM2}
   \]
   then some margin class \(\mathcal Q_\ell\) satisfies
   \[
      \Delta_\ell|\mathcal Q_\ell|>\sigma S_G
      \tag{DQM3}
   \]
   and hence
   \[
      \sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_\ell}
      \bigl(\theta_jC_j(G;q)-T_G\tau_q\bigr)
      >
      \sigma S_G .
      \tag{DQM4}
   \]
   Consequently, under activation-restriction closure, the quotient restricted
   to this single dyadic query-margin layer has positive reduced gain.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   If every class had
   \[
      \Delta_\ell|\mathcal Q_\ell|\le\sigma S_G,
   \]
   then by the upper half of \((DQM1)\),
   \[
      \sum_qd_q(G)
      <
      2\sum_{\ell=1}^K\Delta_\ell|\mathcal Q_\ell|
      \le
      2K\sigma S_G,
   \]
   contradicting \((DQM2)\).  Thus some class satisfies \((DQM3)\).  On that
   class all margins are at least \(\Delta_\ell\), so
   \[
      \sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_\ell}d_q(G)
      \ge
      \Delta_\ell|\mathcal Q_\ell|
      >
      \sigma S_G,
   \]
   which is \((DQM4)\).  Restricting the quotient activation to
   \(\mathcal Q_\ell\) gives
   layer surplus greater than the storage price, and
   \cref{lem:hinge-quotient-activation} then gives positive reduced gain.
\end{proof}

\Cref{lem:dyadic-query-margin-layer} is a build-time simplification.  If a core
has hinge surplus with logarithmic slack, preprocessing may search one
uniform-margin query layer at a time.  The exact verifier still tests the
original weighted reduced gain, so the dyadic query-margin loss is proof/search
bookkeeping rather than a stored-index overhead.

\begin{lemma}[Atomized quotient reduced-gain test]
   \label{lem:atomized-quotient-reduced-gain}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:unweighted-quotient-coverage-screen}.  Let
   \(G\) be a certified quotient filter with update side \(U_G\), activation
   predicate \(a_G\), and prices \(T_G,S_G\).  Instead of assigning whole
   primitive slices to \(G\), assign a finite set of primitive atoms
   \[
      \mathcal A_G
      \subseteq
      \{(z,q,p): (p,q)\in\mathcal N,\ p\in V_{z,q}\cap U_G,\ a_G(q)=1\}.
   \]
   Put
   \[
      b_G^{\rm at}
      =
      \max\left\{
         1,\;
         \max_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}
         |\{z:(z,q,p)\in\mathcal A_G\}|
      \right\},
      \tag{AQ1}
   \]
   and, for a dyadic demand layer \(\mathcal N_j\),
   \[
      C_j^{\rm at}(G;q)
      =
      \frac1{b_G^{\rm at}}
      |\{(z,q,p)\in\mathcal A_G:(p,q)\in\mathcal N_j\}|.
      \tag{AQ2}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \theta_j\sum_qC_j^{\rm at}(G;q)
      >
      T_G\sum_q\tau_qa_G(q)+\sigma S_G,
      \tag{AQ3}
   \]
   then \(G\) has positive reduced gain in the original filter-cover dual.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   The true demand captured by \(G\) is
   \[
      A_G=
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}
      \alpha_{p,q}\mathbf 1\{p\in U_G\}a_G(q).
   \]
   Expanding the atomized layer count and using \((AQ1)\),
   \[
      \sum_qC_j^{\rm at}(G;q)
      \le
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N_j}
      \mathbf 1\{p\in U_G\}a_G(q).
   \]
   Every pair in \(\mathcal N_j\) has \(\alpha_{p,q}\ge\theta_j\), hence
   \[
      A_G\ge
      \theta_j\sum_qC_j^{\rm at}(G;q).
   \]
   Combining this with \((AQ3)\) gives
   \[
      A_G>
      T_G\sum_q\tau_qa_G(q)+\sigma S_G,
   \]
   which is exactly positive reduced gain.
\end{proof}

\Cref{lem:atomized-quotient-reduced-gain} lets the quotient separator merge
selected incidences, not only whole primitive slices.  This is useful for dense
cores whose profitable part is a common prefix, superlevel, or decoded list
inside many high-correlation slices.  The retained child is still the ordinary
filter \(G=(U_G,a_G,T_G,S_G)\); the atom set is only a certificate proving that
its true captured demand exceeds its query and storage price.

\begin{lemma}[Atom de-duplication normal form]
   \label{lem:atom-deduplication-normal-form}
   Fix a container \(W\subseteq P\), a query set \(Q'\subseteq\mathcal Q\), a
   price factor \(\psi>0\), and an exponent \(0\le\rho_D\le1\).  Put
   \[
      \mathsf T(Q')=\sum_{q\in Q'}\tau_q .
   \]
   Let
   \[
      \mathcal A\subseteq
      \{(z,q,p):p\in W,\ q\in Q',\ p\in V_{z,q},\ (p,q)\in\mathcal N_j\}
   \]
   be any finite atom family, and suppose
   \[
      |\{z:(z,q,p)\in\mathcal A\}|\le b
      \qquad((p,q)\in\mathcal N_j).
      \tag{AD0}
   \]
   Then there is a subfamily \(\mathcal A^\sharp\subseteq\mathcal A\) with
   duplicate bound \(1\) such that, for every \(U\subseteq W\),
   \[
      |\{(z,q,p)\in\mathcal A^\sharp:p\in U\}|
      \ge
      \frac1b|\{(z,q,p)\in\mathcal A:p\in U\}|.
      \tag{AD1}
   \]
   Consequently, if a \(k\)-point update side \(U\) satisfies
   \[
      \frac{\theta_j}{b}
      |\{(z,q,p)\in\mathcal A:p\in U\}|
      >
      \psi\bigl(\mathsf T(Q')k^{\rho_D}
      +\sigma k^{1+\rho_D}\bigr),
      \tag{AD2}
   \]
   then the same \(U\) satisfies the duplicate-free atomized inequality
   \[
      \theta_j|\{(z,q,p)\in\mathcal A^\sharp:p\in U\}|
      >
      \psi\bigl(\mathsf T(Q')k^{\rho_D}
      +\sigma k^{1+\rho_D}\bigr).
      \tag{AD3}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   For each pair \((p,q)\) for which some atom \((z,q,p)\in\mathcal A\) exists,
   choose one such atom and put it in \(\mathcal A^\sharp\).  Then no pair
   \((p,q)\) appears more than once in \(\mathcal A^\sharp\), so the duplicate
   bound is \(1\).  For a fixed \(U\subseteq W\), write
   \[
      t_{p,q}=|\{z:(z,q,p)\in\mathcal A\}|.
   \]
   On the pairs with \(p\in U\), each nonzero \(t_{p,q}\) is at most \(b\), hence
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{(p,q):p\in U\\t_{p,q}>0}}1
      \ge
      \frac1b\sum_{\substack{(p,q):p\in U}}t_{p,q}.
   \]
   The left-hand side is exactly the number of atoms of
   \(\mathcal A^\sharp\) with point in \(U\), while the right-hand side is
   \(b^{-1}\) times the corresponding count for \(\mathcal A\).  This proves
   \((AD1)\), and \((AD3)\) follows immediately from \((AD1)\) and \((AD2)\).
\end{proof}

\Cref{lem:atom-deduplication-normal-form} removes the duplicate factor from the
atomized part of the separator.  Duplicate factors are still useful when a
quotient is certified by whole primitive slices, but once individual
point-slice incidences are available, the certificate should keep one witness
slice per covered near pair.  The degree used by the atomized prefix search can
therefore be read as a pair-support degree,
\[
   d^\sharp(p)=|\{q:\exists z\ (z,q,p)\in\mathcal A,\ (p,q)\in\mathcal N_j\}|,
\]
and the subsequent top-degree, envelope, and dyadic-cardinality reductions may
be applied in the duplicate-free case \(b=1\).

\begin{lemma}[Pair-support saturation for atomized cores]
   \label{lem:pair-support-saturation-atomized}
   Fix a container \(W\subseteq P\), a query set \(Q'\subseteq\mathcal Q\), a
   price factor \(\psi>0\), and an exponent \(0\le\rho_D\le1\).  Put
   \[
      \mathsf T(Q')=\sum_{q\in Q'}\tau_q .
   \]
   For every pair \((p,q)\in\mathcal N_j\) with \(p\in W\), \(q\in Q'\), and
   \(p\in V_{z,q}\) for at least one \(z\), choose one witness
   \(z^\star(p,q)\), and define the saturated duplicate-free atom family
   \[
      \mathcal A^\star(W,Q')
      =
      \{(z^\star(p,q),q,p):p\in W,\ q\in Q',
      (p,q)\in\mathcal N_j,\ p\in V_{z^\star(p,q),q}\}.
   \]
   Let
   \[
      d^\star(p)=|\{q:(z^\star(p,q),q,p)\in\mathcal A^\star(W,Q')\}|
   \]
   and order \(W=\{p_1^\star,\ldots,p_M^\star\}\) so that
   \(d^\star(p_1^\star)\ge\cdots\ge d^\star(p_M^\star)\).  For \(k\le M\), put
   \(U_k^\star=\{p_1^\star,\ldots,p_k^\star\}\).

   Suppose there is a duplicate-free atom family
   \[
      \mathcal A\subseteq
      \{(z,q,p):p\in W,\ q\in Q',\ p\in V_{z,q},\ (p,q)\in\mathcal N_j\}
   \]
   and a \(k\)-point update side \(U\subseteq W\) such that
   \[
      \theta_j|\{(z,q,p)\in\mathcal A:p\in U\}|
      >
      \psi\bigl(\mathsf T(Q')k^{\rho_D}
      +\sigma k^{1+\rho_D}\bigr).
      \tag{PS1}
   \]
   Then the saturated top-degree prefix satisfies
   \[
      \theta_j|\{(z,q,p)\in\mathcal A^\star(W,Q'):p\in U_k^\star\}|
      >
      \psi\bigl(\mathsf T(Q')k^{\rho_D}
      +\sigma k^{1+\rho_D}\bigr).
      \tag{PS2}
   \]
   Consequently, after \cref{lem:atom-deduplication-normal-form}, any positive
   atomized quotient inside the fixed container and query layer is witnessed by
   the saturated pair-support prefix \(U_k^\star\) for the same cardinality.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Since \(\mathcal A\) is duplicate-free, for each pair \((p,q)\) it contains
   at most one witness.  Whenever \((z,q,p)\in\mathcal A\), the pair \((p,q)\)
   is feasible for the saturated family, so
   \[
      d^\star(p)\ge |\{(z,q,p)\in\mathcal A\}|
      \qquad(p\in W).
   \]
   Therefore, for the \(k\)-set \(U\),
   \[
      \sum_{i\le k}d^\star(p_i^\star)
      \ge
      \sum_{p\in U}d^\star(p)
      \ge
      |\{(z,q,p)\in\mathcal A:p\in U\}|.
   \]
   The left-hand side is exactly the number of saturated atoms whose point lies
   in \(U_k^\star\).  Combining this inequality with \((PS1)\) gives
   \((PS2)\).

   For the final statement, first apply
   \cref{lem:atom-deduplication-normal-form} to pass to a duplicate-free
   atomized certificate with no loss in normalized coverage, then apply the
   first part of this lemma and finally
   \cref{lem:atomized-quotient-reduced-gain}.
\end{proof}

\Cref{lem:pair-support-saturation-atomized} removes the atom-family choice from
the atomized separator.  Once \(W\) and \(Q'\) are fixed, preprocessing should
use the whole pair-support relation between \(W\) and \(Q'\) induced by the
primitive slices, then sort points by the saturated support degree \(d^\star\).
Thus the residual atomized search has only three discrete choices left:
certified container, query layer, and prefix cardinality.

\begin{lemma}[Top-degree update prefix for atomized cores]
   \label{lem:top-degree-atomized-prefix}
   Fix a certified container \(W\subseteq P\), a query set
   \(Q'\subseteq\mathcal Q\), a duplicate parameter \(b\ge1\), a price factor
   \(\psi>0\), and an exponent \(0\le\rho_D\le1\).  Let
   \[
      \mathcal A\subseteq
      \{(z,q,p):p\in W,\ q\in Q',\ p\in V_{z,q},\ (p,q)\in\mathcal N_j\}
   \]
   be a finite atom family, and define the point degree
   \[
      d_{\mathcal A}(p)=|\{(z,q,p)\in\mathcal A\}|.
   \]
   Assume \(b\) upper-bounds duplicate incidence:
   \[
      \max_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N_j}
      |\{z:(z,q,p)\in\mathcal A\}|
      \le b .
      \tag{TDA0}
   \]
   Order \(W=\{p_1,\ldots,p_M\}\) so that
   \[
      d_{\mathcal A}(p_1)\ge d_{\mathcal A}(p_2)\ge\cdots\ge d_{\mathcal A}(p_M).
   \]
   For \(k\le M\), let \(U_k=\{p_1,\ldots,p_k\}\), and price every
   \(k\)-point child inside \(W\) by
   \[
      T(k)=\psi k^{\rho_D},
      \qquad
      S(k)=\psi k^{1+\rho_D}.
      \tag{TDA1}
   \]
   If some \(U\subseteq W\) with \(|U|=k\) satisfies
   \[
      \frac{\theta_j}{b}
      |\{(z,q,p)\in\mathcal A:p\in U\}|
      >
      T(k)\sum_{q\in Q'}\tau_q+\sigma S(k),
      \tag{TDA2}
   \]
   then the top-degree prefix \(U_k\) satisfies the same strict inequality.
   Consequently, if the quotient universe contains the certified prefixes
   \((U_k,Q')\) for all atom-safe \(k\), any positive atomized quotient inside
   this fixed container and query layer is witnessed by one of those prefixes.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Among all \(k\)-subsets of \(W\), the prefix \(U_k\) maximizes
   \[
      \sum_{p\in U}d_{\mathcal A}(p)
      =
      |\{(z,q,p)\in\mathcal A:p\in U\}|.
   \]
   The right-hand side of \((TDA2)\) depends only on \(k\), not on the identity
   of the selected points.  Therefore if some \(k\)-set satisfies \((TDA2)\),
   the top-degree \(k\)-set also satisfies it.

   For the final statement, take \(\mathcal A_G\) to be the atoms of
   \(\mathcal A\) whose point lies in \(U_k\), set \(a_G=\mathbf 1_{Q'}\), and
   use \(b_G^{\rm at}\le b\).  The strict inequality for \(U_k\) implies
   \((AQ3)\), so \cref{lem:atomized-quotient-reduced-gain} gives positive
   reduced gain.
\end{proof}

\Cref{lem:top-degree-atomized-prefix} removes the update-side combinatorial
choice inside a fixed geometric container and query layer.
\Cref{lem:pair-support-saturation-atomized} removes the atom-family choice in
the duplicate-free normal form.  The offline separator only has to choose the
container, the query-margin layer, and a cardinality \(k\); the best \(k\)-point
update side is the degree-sorted prefix of the saturated pair-support relation.
This is the quotient analogue of the dense-slice prefix lemma, but it applies
after merging incidences from many slices.

\begin{lemma}[Atomized prefix-density envelope]
   \label{lem:atomized-prefix-density-envelope}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:top-degree-atomized-prefix}.  Put
   \[
      D_k=\sum_{i\le k}d_{\mathcal A}(p_i),
      \qquad
      \mathsf T(Q')=\sum_{q\in Q'}\tau_q .
   \]
   Suppose that no atom-safe top-degree prefix has positive atomized gain, that
   is, for every atom-safe \(k\),
   \[
      \frac{\theta_j}{b}D_k
      \le
      \psi\bigl(\mathsf T(Q')k^{\rho_D}
      +\sigma k^{1+\rho_D}\bigr).
      \tag{APE1}
   \]
   Then every atom-safe \(k\) satisfies the average-degree envelope
   \[
      \frac{D_k}{k}
      \le
      \frac{b\psi}{\theta_j}
      \bigl(\mathsf T(Q')k^{\rho_D-1}
      +\sigma k^{\rho_D}\bigr).
      \tag{APE2}
   \]
   Consequently, for every degree level \(\delta>0\), if
   \[
      h_\delta=
      |\{p\in W:d_{\mathcal A}(p)\ge\delta\}|
   \]
   is atom-safe and nonzero, then
   \[
      \delta
      \le
      \frac{b\psi}{\theta_j}
      \bigl(\mathsf T(Q')h_\delta^{\rho_D-1}
      +\sigma h_\delta^{\rho_D}\bigr).
      \tag{APE3}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Dividing \((APE1)\) by \(k\) gives \((APE2)\).  For the degree-level form,
   let \(h=h_\delta\).  The top \(h\) points all have degree at least
   \(\delta\), hence \(D_h\ge\delta h\).  If \((APE3)\) failed, then
   \((APE2)\) would fail at \(k=h\), and the corresponding top-degree prefix
   would have positive atomized gain by \cref{lem:top-degree-atomized-prefix}.
   This contradiction proves \((APE3)\).
\end{proof}

\Cref{lem:atomized-prefix-density-envelope} is the residual form of the
atomized separator.  After fixing a container and a query-margin layer, failure
of every prefix does not leave an arbitrary obstruction: every degree superlevel
must lie below the displayed Rényi envelope.  The remaining geometric theorem
can therefore be phrased as a packing statement saying that the heavy dyadic
demand layer and query-margin layer cannot satisfy all such envelopes in every
certified container.

\begin{lemma}[Dyadic cardinality screen for atomized prefixes]
   \label{lem:dyadic-atomized-prefix-screen}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:atomized-prefix-density-envelope}, and
   assume the atom-safe cardinalities are downward closed: if \(k\) is
   atom-safe, then every \(1\le h\le k\) is atom-safe.  Let
   \[
      \mathcal K_2=\{2^\ell:0\le\ell\le \lfloor\log_2M\rfloor\}.
   \]
   If some atom-safe \(k\) satisfies the constant-slack prefix inequality
   \[
      \frac{\theta_j}{b}D_k
      >
      2\psi\bigl(\mathsf T(Q')k^{\rho_D}
      +\sigma k^{1+\rho_D}\bigr),
      \tag{DAP1}
   \]
   then some dyadic atom-safe \(h\in\mathcal K_2\) satisfies
   \[
      \frac{\theta_j}{b}D_h
      >
      \psi\bigl(\mathsf T(Q')h^{\rho_D}
      +\sigma h^{1+\rho_D}\bigr).
      \tag{DAP2}
   \]
   Consequently, if no dyadic atom-safe prefix has positive atomized gain, then
   every atom-safe \(k\) satisfies
   \[
      \frac{\theta_j}{b}D_k
      \le
      2\psi\bigl(\mathsf T(Q')k^{\rho_D}
      +\sigma k^{1+\rho_D}\bigr),
      \tag{DAP3}
   \]
   and the average-degree and degree-superlevel envelopes
   \((APE2)\)--\((APE3)\) hold with their right-hand sides multiplied by \(2\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Let \(h=2^{\lfloor\log_2k\rfloor}\).  Then \(h\le k<2h\), and \(h\) is
   atom-safe by downward closure.  Since the degrees are sorted in nonincreasing
   order,
   \[
      \frac{D_h}{h}\ge \frac{D_k}{k},
   \]
   so \(D_h\ge (h/k)D_k>D_k/2\).  If \((DAP1)\) holds, then
   \[
      \frac{\theta_j}{b}D_h
      >
      \psi\bigl(\mathsf T(Q')k^{\rho_D}
      +\sigma k^{1+\rho_D}\bigr)
      \ge
      \psi\bigl(\mathsf T(Q')h^{\rho_D}
      +\sigma h^{1+\rho_D}\bigr),
   \]
   because \(0\le\rho_D\le1\) and \(h\le k\).  This is \((DAP2)\).

   The contrapositive gives \((DAP3)\).  Dividing \((DAP3)\) by \(k\) gives the
   factor-\(2\) version of \((APE2)\), and the same level-set argument as in
   \cref{lem:atomized-prefix-density-envelope} gives the factor-\(2\) version
   of \((APE3)\).
\end{proof}

\Cref{lem:dyadic-atomized-prefix-screen} makes the cardinality part of the
separator logarithmic whenever the proposed atomized core has constant slack.
The build stage may search powers of two in each certified container and
query-margin layer, then run the exact reduced-gain verifier on any returned
prefix.  The dyadic loss is therefore a proposal-generation slack, not a charge
that has to remain in the final retained index.

\begin{corollary}[Saturated pair-support envelope test]
   \label{cor:saturated-pair-support-envelope}
   Fix a certified container \(W\subseteq P\), a query set
   \(Q'\subseteq\mathcal Q\), a price factor \(\psi>0\), and an exponent
   \(0\le\rho_D\le1\).  Let \(\mathcal A^\star(W,Q')\), \(d^\star\), and
   \(U_k^\star\) be the saturated duplicate-free atom family, degrees, and
   prefixes from \cref{lem:pair-support-saturation-atomized}.  Put
   \[
      D_k^\star=\sum_{p\in U_k^\star}d^\star(p),
      \qquad
      \mathsf T(Q')=\sum_{q\in Q'}\tau_q .
   \]
   If an atom-safe \(k\) satisfies
   \[
      \theta_jD_k^\star
      >
      \psi\bigl(\mathsf T(Q')k^{\rho_D}
      +\sigma k^{1+\rho_D}\bigr),
      \tag{SPE1}
   \]
   then the saturated prefix \((U_k^\star,Q')\) has positive reduced gain.
   Therefore, if no saturated atom-safe prefix inside \(W,Q'\) has positive
   reduced gain, every atom-safe \(k\) satisfies
   \[
      \frac{D_k^\star}{k}
      \le
      \frac{\psi}{\theta_j}
      \bigl(\mathsf T(Q')k^{\rho_D-1}
      +\sigma k^{\rho_D}\bigr),
      \tag{SPE2}
   \]
   and every atom-safe degree superlevel
   \[
      h_\delta^\star=|\{p\in W:d^\star(p)\ge\delta\}|
   \]
   that is nonzero satisfies
   \[
      \delta
      \le
      \frac{\psi}{\theta_j}
      \bigl(\mathsf T(Q')(h_\delta^\star)^{\rho_D-1}
      +\sigma (h_\delta^\star)^{\rho_D}\bigr).
      \tag{SPE3}
   \]
   If the atom-safe cardinalities are downward closed and only dyadic
   cardinalities are searched, then absence of positive dyadic saturated
   prefixes implies the same two envelopes with the right-hand sides multiplied
   by \(2\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The family \(\mathcal A^\star(W,Q')\) is duplicate-free, so applying
   \cref{lem:atomized-quotient-reduced-gain} to the prefix \(U_k^\star\), with
   \(a_G=\mathbf 1_{Q'}\), \(T_G=\psi k^{\rho_D}\), and
   \(S_G=\psi k^{1+\rho_D}\), shows that \((SPE1)\) gives positive reduced gain.

   If no saturated atom-safe prefix has positive reduced gain, the contrapositive
   gives
   \[
      \theta_jD_k^\star
      \le
      \psi\bigl(\mathsf T(Q')k^{\rho_D}
      +\sigma k^{1+\rho_D}\bigr)
   \]
   for every atom-safe \(k\).  Dividing by \(k\) gives \((SPE2)\).  For the
   superlevel form, take \(h=h_\delta^\star\).  The top \(h\) saturated-degree
   points all have degree at least \(\delta\), hence \(D_h^\star\ge\delta h\).
   Combining this with \((SPE2)\) gives \((SPE3)\).

   The dyadic statement is exactly \cref{lem:dyadic-atomized-prefix-screen}
   applied to the saturated family with duplicate factor \(b=1\).
\end{proof}

\Cref{cor:saturated-pair-support-envelope} is the current residual target in its
most concrete form.  After fixing a dyadic demand layer and a dyadic
query-margin layer, the build-time separator only has to find a certified
container \(W\) whose saturated pair-support degree sequence violates
\((SPE2)\) or \((SPE3)\) at some atom-safe scale.  If every certified container
obeys these envelopes, the unresolved obstruction is no longer a branching or
quotient-accounting issue; it is a pure geometric packing statement about
saturated pair-support degrees.

\begin{lemma}[Saturated container-packing separator]
   \label{lem:saturated-container-packing-separator}
   Fix a dyadic demand layer \(\mathcal N_j\).  Let \(\mathcal C\) be a finite
   family of certified container records.  A record
   \(C\in\mathcal C\) consists of a container \(W_C\subseteq P\), a query layer
   \(Q_C\subseteq\mathcal Q\), a price factor \(\psi_C>0\), an exponent
   \(0\le\rho_C\le1\), and a finite atom-safe cardinality set
   \(\mathcal K_C\).  For each \(C\), form the saturated pair-support relation
   \(\mathcal A^\star(W_C,Q_C)\) from
   \cref{lem:pair-support-saturation-atomized}; let
   \(D_{C,k}^\star\) be the total saturated degree of its top \(k\) points.
   Put
   \[
      \mathsf T_C=\sum_{q\in Q_C}\tau_q,
      \qquad
      B_C(k)=\theta_jD_{C,k}^\star,
   \]
   and
   \[
      P_C(k)
      =
      \psi_C\bigl(\mathsf T_Ck^{\rho_C}
      +\sigma k^{1+\rho_C}\bigr).
   \]
   Suppose the filter universe contains, for every \(C\) and every
   \(k\in\mathcal K_C\), the saturated prefix filter
   \[
      (U_{C,k}^\star,Q_C)
   \]
   with prices
   \[
      T_{C,k}=\psi_Ck^{\rho_C},
      \qquad
      S_{C,k}=\psi_Ck^{1+\rho_C}.
   \]
   If there are nonnegative intensities \(\lambda_{C,k}\), not all zero, such
   that
   \[
      \sum_{C\in\mathcal C}\sum_{k\in\mathcal K_C}
      \lambda_{C,k} B_C(k)
      >
      \sum_{C\in\mathcal C}\sum_{k\in\mathcal K_C}
      \lambda_{C,k} P_C(k),
      \tag{SCP1}
   \]
   then some saturated prefix filter has positive reduced gain.  Conversely, if
   no saturated prefix filter has positive reduced gain, then \((SCP1)\) fails
   for every nonnegative intensity vector.

   If, for every \(C\), the atom-safe cardinalities are downward closed, then a
   factor-two conic violation
   \[
      \sum_{C,k}\lambda_{C,k} B_C(k)
      >
      2\sum_{C,k}\lambda_{C,k} P_C(k)
      \tag{SCP2}
   \]
   already implies that a dyadic atom-safe prefix in one of the containers has
   positive reduced gain.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   For a fixed pair \((C,k)\), \cref{cor:saturated-pair-support-envelope} says
   exactly that \(B_C(k)>P_C(k)\) implies positive reduced gain of the prefix
   \((U_{C,k}^\star,Q_C)\).  If \((SCP1)\) holds, some term in the support must
   have \(B_C(k)>P_C(k)\); otherwise the two sums would satisfy the opposite
   inequality.  This gives the first claim.  The converse is the same argument
   read backward: if no prefix has positive gain, then
   \(B_C(k)\le P_C(k)\) for every prefix, and summing with nonnegative
   coefficients rules out \((SCP1)\).

   For the dyadic statement, \((SCP2)\) implies that some support term has
   \(B_C(k)>2P_C(k)\).  Under downward closure,
   \cref{cor:saturated-pair-support-envelope} and
   \cref{lem:dyadic-atomized-prefix-screen} imply that this constant-slack
   violation exposes a positive-gain dyadic prefix in the same container.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Saturated container packing implies local cover]
   \label{cor:saturated-container-packing-local-cover}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:residual-separator-local-cover}.  Enlarge
   the finite filter universe by the following closure.  For each subset
   \(\mathcal L\subseteq\mathcal N\) that may appear as a dyadic demand layer,
   include a finite family \(\mathcal C(\mathcal L)\) of certified container
   records as in \cref{lem:saturated-container-packing-separator}, formed with
   \(\mathcal N_j=\mathcal L\), and include all their atom-safe saturated prefix
   filters with the displayed certified prices.  This closure is finite because
   \(\mathcal N\) is finite.

   Suppose that every surplus dual price system \((\alpha,\tau,\sigma)\)
   satisfying \((RS1)\) and having nonpositive reduced gain on the spherical
   buckets, whole high-correlation dense slices, and atom-safe primitive dense
   prefixes has the following property: after dyadically partitioning its
   positive demand prices, some layer \(\mathcal L\) admits nonnegative
   intensities on \(\mathcal C(\mathcal L)\) satisfying \((SCP1)\).  Then the
   finite filter-cover LP \((\mathsf{FC}_{\mathcal N})\) is feasible with query
   budget \(L\) and storage budget \(S\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If the finite filter-cover LP were infeasible, then
   \cref{lem:finite-filter-cover-dual} would give a surplus dual price system
   with nonpositive reduced gain on every column of the enlarged universe.  In
   particular, it has nonpositive gain on the spherical buckets, whole dense
   slices, and primitive dense prefixes, so the hypothesis supplies a dyadic
   layer and a saturated container-packing witness satisfying \((SCP1)\).
   \Cref{lem:saturated-container-packing-separator} then exposes a saturated
   prefix filter with positive reduced gain.  This filter is a column of the
   enlarged universe, contradicting the dual certificate.
\end{proof}

\Cref{lem:saturated-container-packing-separator} is the fully fractional form of
the dense-container search.  The proof no longer asks preprocessing to commit to
a clever disjoint or greedy set of dense clusters.  It may instead construct any
conic certificate over containers, query layers, and prefix sizes whose
total saturated pair-support benefit exceeds its recursive query and storage
price.  A \(k\)-means++, additive-quantization, range-reporting, or
list-recovery routine is useful only as a separator for this positive reduced
cost condition; the retained index still keeps just the verified prefix filters
accepted by the finite cover LP.

\begin{lemma}[Saturated query-hinge normal form]
   \label{lem:saturated-query-hinge-normal-form}
   Fix a dyadic demand layer \(\mathcal N_j\), a certified container
   \(W\subseteq P\), an update set \(U\subseteq W\) of size \(k\), a price
   factor \(\psi>0\), and an exponent \(0\le\rho\le1\).  For each query
   \(q\in\mathcal Q\), define the saturated query degree of \(U\) by
   \[
      c_U(q)
      =
      |\{p\in U:(p,q)\in\mathcal N_j
      \text{ and }\exists z\in\mathcal Z:\ p\in V_{z,q}\}|.
   \]
   Put
   \[
      T_U=\psi k^\rho,\qquad S_U=\psi k^{1+\rho},
   \]
   and
   \[
      d_q(U)=\bigl(\theta_jc_U(q)-T_U\tau_q\bigr)_+ .
   \]
   If
   \[
      \sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}d_q(U)>\sigma S_U,
      \tag{SQH1}
   \]
   and \(k\) is atom-safe for the query set
   \[
      Q^+(U)=\{q:\theta_jc_U(q)>T_U\tau_q\},
   \]
   then the saturated top-degree \(k\)-prefix inside \(W,Q^+(U)\) has positive
   reduced gain.

   Conversely, if no atom-safe saturated \(k\)-prefix inside \(W,Q'\) has
   positive reduced gain for any \(Q'\subseteq\mathcal Q\), then every
   \(k\)-set \(U\subseteq W\) for which \(Q^+(U)\) is atom-safe satisfies
   \[
      \sum_qd_q(U)\le\sigma S_U .
      \tag{SQH2}
   \]

   Finally, partition the positive margins \(d_q(U)\) into dyadic classes
   \(\mathcal Q_1,\ldots,\mathcal Q_K\), where
   \[
      \Delta_\ell\le d_q(U)<2\Delta_\ell
      \qquad(q\in\mathcal Q_\ell).
   \]
   If
   \[
      \sum_qd_q(U)>2K\,\sigma S_U,
      \tag{SQH3}
   \]
   then some dyadic margin class \(\mathcal Q_\ell\) has the property that the
   saturated top-degree \(k\)-prefix inside \(W,\mathcal Q_\ell\) has positive
   reduced gain, provided \(k\) is atom-safe for that layer.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   For each pair \((p,q)\) counted by \(c_U(q)\), choose one witness
   \(z^\star(p,q)\) with \(p\in V_{z^\star(p,q),q}\).  This gives a
   duplicate-free atom family inside \(W,Q^+(U)\).  By the definition of
   \(Q^+(U)\),
   \[
      \theta_j\sum_{q\in Q^+(U)}c_U(q)
      -
      T_U\sum_{q\in Q^+(U)}\tau_q
      =
      \sum_qd_q(U).
   \]
   Thus \((SQH1)\) implies
   \[
      \theta_j
      |\{(z^\star(p,q),q,p):p\in U,\ q\in Q^+(U)\}|
      >
      T_U\sum_{q\in Q^+(U)}\tau_q+\sigma S_U .
   \]
   Apply \cref{lem:pair-support-saturation-atomized} with
   \(Q'=Q^+(U)\): the saturated top-degree \(k\)-prefix has at least this many
   feasible pair-support atoms.  Then
   \cref{lem:atomized-quotient-reduced-gain} gives positive reduced gain with
   prices \(T_U,S_U\).

   The converse is the contrapositive of the first claim.

   For the dyadic statement, if every margin class satisfied
   \(\Delta_\ell|\mathcal Q_\ell|\le\sigma S_U\), then
   \[
      \sum_qd_q(U)
      <
      2\sum_{\ell=1}^K\Delta_\ell|\mathcal Q_\ell|
      \le
      2K\,\sigma S_U,
   \]
   contradicting \((SQH3)\).  Hence some class has
   \(\Delta_\ell|\mathcal Q_\ell|>\sigma S_U\), and on this class
   \[
      \sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_\ell}
      \bigl(\theta_jc_U(q)-T_U\tau_q\bigr)
      \ge
      \Delta_\ell|\mathcal Q_\ell|
      >
      \sigma S_U .
   \]
   Repeating the first part with \(Q'=\mathcal Q_\ell\) gives a positive-gain
   saturated prefix for that layer.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Hinge container separator implies local cover]
   \label{cor:hinge-container-separator-local-cover}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:residual-separator-local-cover}.  Enlarge
   the finite filter universe so that, for every finite dyadic demand layer
   \(\mathcal L\subseteq\mathcal N\), every certified container \(W\) in a
   finite container family, every query set \(Q'\subseteq\mathcal Q\), and every
   atom-safe cardinality \(k\), it contains the saturated top-degree
   \(k\)-prefix filter inside \(W,Q'\) with the certified prices
   \(T=\psi_Wk^{\rho_W}\) and \(S=\psi_Wk^{1+\rho_W}\).

   Suppose that every surplus dual price system \((\alpha,\tau,\sigma)\)
   satisfying \((RS1)\) and having nonpositive reduced gain on the spherical
   buckets, whole high-correlation dense slices, and atom-safe primitive dense
   prefixes has the following property: after dyadically partitioning its
   positive demand prices, some layer \(\mathcal L\), certified container
   \(W\), and update set \(U\subseteq W\) satisfy \((SQH1)\) with the price
   parameters of \(W\), and the induced positive query layer \(Q^+(U)\) is
   atom-safe for \(k=|U|\).  Then the finite filter-cover LP
   \((\mathsf{FC}_{\mathcal N})\) is feasible with query budget \(L\) and
   storage budget \(S\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If the LP were infeasible, \cref{lem:finite-filter-cover-dual} would give a
   surplus dual certificate with nonpositive reduced gain on every column of the
   enlarged universe.  The hypothesis supplies a dyadic layer, container, and
   update set satisfying \((SQH1)\).  By
   \cref{lem:saturated-query-hinge-normal-form}, some saturated top-degree
   prefix filter in the enlarged universe has positive reduced gain, a
   contradiction.
\end{proof}

\Cref{lem:saturated-query-hinge-normal-form} removes the query-side choice from
the saturated container target.  For a proposed update core \(U\), the best query
activation is not a clustering decision: keep exactly those query signatures for
which the layer support count \(\theta_jc_U(q)\) exceeds the local query charge
\(T_U\tau_q\), and ask whether the positive margins pay storage.  Thus the
remaining geometric statement may be phrased as a priced bipartite
support-density problem between data points and query signatures.  The
build-time separator can search arbitrary containers and update cores, but every
accepted object still reduces to a saturated prefix column verified by the
finite filter-cover dual.

\begin{lemma}[Fractional query-weight degree normal form]
   \label{lem:fractional-query-weight-degree-normal-form}
   Work with the bipartite support relation from
   \cref{lem:saturated-query-hinge-normal-form}.  For a query weight vector
   \(0\le y_q\le1\), define the weighted support degree
   \[
      d_y(p)
      =
      \sum_{\substack{q\in\mathcal Q:\\
         (p,q)\in\mathcal N_j,\ \exists z\in\mathcal Z:\ p\in V_{z,q}}}
      y_q ,
   \]
   and let \(D_y(k)\) be the sum of the largest \(k\) values of \(d_y(p)\) over
   \(p\in W\).  With
   \[
      T(k)=\psi k^\rho,\qquad S(k)=\psi k^{1+\rho},
   \]
   define
   \[
      f_k(y)=\theta_jD_y(k)-T(k)\sum_q\tau_qy_q-\sigma S(k).
   \]
   Then the optimal hinge surplus over \(k\)-point update cores is exactly
   \[
      \max_{\substack{U\subseteq W\\ |U|=k}}
      \left[
         \sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}
         \bigl(\theta_jc_U(q)-T(k)\tau_q\bigr)_+
         -\sigma S(k)
      \right]
      =
      \max_{0\le y\le1}
      \left[
         \theta_jD_y(k)-T(k)\sum_q\tau_qy_q-\sigma S(k)
      \right].
      \tag{FQW1}
   \]
   Consequently, if the left-hand side of \((FQW1)\) is positive, then some
   integral query set \(Q'\subseteq\mathcal Q\) satisfies \(f_k(\mathbf 1_{Q'})>0\).
   If \(k\) is atom-safe for this \(Q'\), the saturated top-degree \(k\)-prefix
   inside \(W,Q'\) has positive reduced gain.

   More generally, let \(\mathcal Q_k^{\rm safe}\) be any family of query sets for which
   \(k\) is atom-safe.  If no saturated \(k\)-prefix inside \(W,Q'\) has positive
   reduced gain for any \(Q'\in\mathcal Q_k^{\rm safe}\), then every
   \(y\in\operatorname{conv}\{\mathbf 1_{Q'}:Q'\in\mathcal Q_k^{\rm safe}\}\) satisfies
   \[
      \theta_jD_y(k)
      \le
      T(k)\sum_q\tau_qy_q+\sigma S(k).
      \tag{FQW2}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   For a fixed update core \(U\), use
   \[
      (x)_+=\max_{0\le y\le1}yx
   \]
   independently for each query.  This gives
   \[
      \sum_q(\theta_jc_U(q)-T(k)\tau_q)_+
      =
      \max_{0\le y\le1}
      \left[
         \theta_j\sum_qy_qc_U(q)-T(k)\sum_q\tau_qy_q
      \right].
   \]
   Since all sets are finite, the maxima over \(U\) and \(y\) commute.  For fixed
   \(y\),
   \[
      \sum_qy_qc_U(q)=\sum_{p\in U}d_y(p),
   \]
   and the best \(k\)-point set \(U\) is the top-\(k\) weighted-degree prefix,
   whose value is \(D_y(k)\).  This proves \((FQW1)\).

   The function \(f_k\) is convex, because \(D_y(k)\) is a maximum of finitely
   many linear functions and the remaining terms are linear or constant.
   A convex function on the cube \([0,1]^{\mathcal Q}\) attains its maximum at an
   extreme point.  Thus a positive right-hand side in \((FQW1)\) is witnessed by
   an integral vector \(y=\mathbf 1_{Q'}\).  The top-\(k\) weighted-degree prefix
   for this \(Q'\) is exactly the saturated top-degree prefix inside \(W,Q'\).
   When \(k\) is atom-safe for \(Q'\), the strict inequality is the positive
   reduced-gain condition from \cref{cor:saturated-pair-support-envelope}.

   For the final statement, write
   \(y=\sum_i\lambda_i\mathbf 1_{Q_i}\) with \(Q_i\in\mathcal Q_k^{\rm safe}\),
   \(\lambda_i\ge0\), and \(\sum_i\lambda_i=1\).  Convexity gives
   \[
      f_k(y)\le\sum_i\lambda_if_k(\mathbf 1_{Q_i}).
   \]
   If \(f_k(y)>0\), then some \(Q_i\) has \(f_k(\mathbf 1_{Q_i})>0\), hence a
   positive-gain atom-safe saturated prefix.  The contrapositive is \((FQW2)\).
\end{proof}

\Cref{lem:fractional-query-weight-degree-normal-form} is the cleanest residual
form of the saturated dense separator.  After fixing a certified container and a
cardinality \(k\), failure of every atom-safe query-side prefix implies the
weighted top-\(k\) degree inequality \((FQW2)\) for every fractional query
weighting generated by atom-safe query sets; when all query subsets are
atom-safe, this is an exact reformulation of the hinge target.  This is a more
convenient target for geometry than the set-valued hinge: it says that no
probability or price distribution on query signatures can concentrate too much
support on a \(k\)-point core inside the container unless the recursive query
price or storage price pays for it.

\begin{lemma}[Layer-cake query-threshold separator]
   \label{lem:layer-cake-query-threshold-separator}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{lem:fractional-query-weight-degree-normal-form}.  Fix
   \(0\le y_q\le1\) and, for \(t\in(0,1]\), put
   \[
      Q_t(y)=\{q\in\mathcal Q:y_q\ge t\}.
   \]
   For \(U\subseteq W\), define
   \[
      E_t(U)
      =
      |\{(p,q):p\in U,\ q\in Q_t(y),\
      (p,q)\in\mathcal N_j,\ \exists z\in\mathcal Z:\ p\in V_{z,q}\}|.
   \]
   Let \(\tau(Q_t)=\sum_{q\in Q_t(y)}\tau_q\) and
   \(L_y=\sum_q\tau_qy_q\).  Fix \(h\) and assume \(h\) is atom-safe for every
   threshold set \(Q_t(y)\).  If some \(h\)-point set \(U\subseteq W\) satisfies
   \[
      \theta_j\sum_{p\in U}d_y(p)
      >
      \psi\bigl(L_yh^\rho+\sigma h^{1+\rho}\bigr),
      \tag{LCQ1}
   \]
   then there is a threshold \(t\in(0,1]\) such that the saturated top-degree
   \(h\)-prefix inside \(W,Q_t(y)\) has positive reduced gain with prices
   \[
      T=\psi h^\rho,\qquad S=\psi h^{1+\rho}.
   \]
   Consequently, if no threshold query set \(Q_t(y)\) exposes a positive
   saturated \(h\)-prefix, then every \(h\)-point set \(U\subseteq W\) satisfies
   the reverse inequality in \((LCQ1)\).  In particular,
   \[
      \theta_jD_y(h)
      \le
      \psi\bigl(L_yh^\rho+\sigma h^{1+\rho}\bigr).
      \tag{LCQ2}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   The layer-cake identities give
   \[
      \sum_{p\in U}d_y(p)=\int_0^1E_t(U)\,dt,
      \qquad
      L_y=\int_0^1\tau(Q_t)\,dt .
   \]
   Thus \((LCQ1)\) is equivalent to
   \[
      \int_0^1
      \left[
         \theta_jE_t(U)-\psi h^\rho\tau(Q_t)
      \right]dt
      >
      \psi\sigma h^{1+\rho}.
   \]
   Since the interval has length one, some threshold \(t\) satisfies
   \[
      \theta_jE_t(U)-\psi h^\rho\tau(Q_t)
      >
      \psi\sigma h^{1+\rho}.
   \]
   For this \(t\), the saturated top-degree \(h\)-prefix inside \(W,Q_t(y)\)
   has at least \(E_t(U)\) feasible pair-support incidences.  Therefore
   \[
      \theta_jD_t^\star(h)
      >
      \psi\bigl(\tau(Q_t)h^\rho+\sigma h^{1+\rho}\bigr),
   \]
   where \(D_t^\star(h)\) is the saturated prefix degree for \(Q_t(y)\).  By
   \cref{cor:saturated-pair-support-envelope}, this prefix has positive reduced
   gain.  The converse statement is the contrapositive, and taking \(U\) to be
   the top \(h\) points for the weighted degrees \(d_y\) gives \((LCQ2)\).
\end{proof}

\Cref{lem:layer-cake-query-threshold-separator} removes the last fractional
artifact from the query side when threshold sets are allowed: every violation of
the weighted degree envelope is witnessed by an ordinary query layer
\(Q_t(y)\).  Thus a geometric separator may work with finite threshold layers
sorted by a dual query weighting, and the retained column is still an integral
saturated prefix filter.  Fractional query weights remain useful only as a
dual-analysis certificate for finding which threshold layer must exist.

\begin{lemma}[Fractional threshold-container packing separator]
   \label{lem:fractional-threshold-container-packing}
   Fix a dyadic demand layer \(\mathcal N_j\).  Let \(\mathcal C\) be a finite
   family of query-weighted certified container records.  A record
   \(C\in\mathcal C\) consists of a container \(W_C\subseteq P\), a price factor
   \(\psi_C>0\), an exponent \(0\le\rho_C\le1\), a finite atom-safe cardinality
   set \(\mathcal K_C\), and query weights \(0\le y_q^C\le1\).  Put
   \[
      Q_t^C=\{q\in\mathcal Q:y_q^C\ge t\},
      \qquad
      L_C=\sum_q\tau_qy_q^C ,
   \]
   and assume that every \(h\in\mathcal K_C\) is atom-safe for every threshold
   set \(Q_t^C\).  Define the weighted saturated support degree in \(W_C\) by
   \[
      d_C(p)=
      \sum_{\substack{q\in\mathcal Q:\\
         (p,q)\in\mathcal N_j,\ \exists z\in\mathcal Z:\ p\in V_{z,q}}}
      y_q^C ,
   \]
   and let \(D_C(h)\) be the sum of the largest \(h\) values of \(d_C(p)\) over
   \(p\in W_C\).  Finally set
   \[
      B_C(h)=\theta_jD_C(h),
      \qquad
      P_C(h)=\psi_C\bigl(L_Ch^{\rho_C}+\sigma h^{1+\rho_C}\bigr).
   \]
   Suppose the filter universe contains, for every \(C\), every
   \(h\in\mathcal K_C\), and every distinct threshold set \(Q_t^C\), the
   saturated top-degree \(h\)-prefix inside \(W_C,Q_t^C\) with prices
   \[
      T=\psi_Ch^{\rho_C},
      \qquad
      S=\psi_Ch^{1+\rho_C}.
   \]
   If there are nonnegative intensities \(\lambda_{C,h}\), not all zero, such
   that
   \[
      \sum_{C\in\mathcal C}\sum_{h\in\mathcal K_C}
      \lambda_{C,h}B_C(h)
      >
      \sum_{C\in\mathcal C}\sum_{h\in\mathcal K_C}
      \lambda_{C,h}P_C(h),
      \tag{FTCP1}
   \]
   then some retained threshold-prefix filter has positive reduced gain.
   Conversely, if no such threshold-prefix filter has positive reduced gain,
   then \((FTCP1)\) fails for every nonnegative intensity vector.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   If \((FTCP1)\) holds, some term in the support of \(\lambda\) satisfies
   \(B_C(h)>P_C(h)\).  Let \(U\) be the \(h\)-point top-degree set in \(W_C\) for
   the weights \(d_C\).  The inequality \(B_C(h)>P_C(h)\) is exactly
   \[
      \theta_j\sum_{p\in U}d_C(p)
      >
      \psi_C\bigl(L_Ch^{\rho_C}+\sigma h^{1+\rho_C}\bigr).
   \]
   Applying \cref{lem:layer-cake-query-threshold-separator} with
   \(W=W_C\), \(y=y^C\), \(\psi=\psi_C\), and \(\rho=\rho_C\) gives a threshold
   \(t\) for which the saturated top-degree \(h\)-prefix inside
   \(W_C,Q_t^C\) has positive reduced gain.  This prefix is one of the retained
   filters by assumption.

   Conversely, if no retained threshold-prefix filter has positive reduced
   gain, then the same layer-cake lemma implies \(B_C(h)\le P_C(h)\) for every
   \(C\) and \(h\in\mathcal K_C\).  Summing these inequalities with arbitrary
   nonnegative coefficients rules out \((FTCP1)\).
\end{proof}

\Cref{lem:fractional-threshold-container-packing} is the fully fractional
container-search form.  A separator no longer has to guess a query layer before
it knows the dual prices; it may propose a container together with a fractional
query weighting and a prefix scale.  The verifier then performs only the
canonical layer-cake conversion and keeps one ordinary threshold query layer
with a saturated top-degree update prefix.  Thus LP range-reporting,
additive-quantization, list-decoding, or learned proposal routines may optimize
a continuous reduced-cost surrogate during preprocessing, while the retained
proof object remains an integral filter-cover column.

\begin{corollary}[Fractional threshold-container packing implies local cover]
   \label{cor:fractional-threshold-container-local-cover}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:residual-separator-local-cover}.  Enlarge
   the finite filter universe as follows.  For each subset
   \(\mathcal L\subseteq\mathcal N\) that may appear as a dyadic demand layer,
   include a finite family \(\mathcal C_{\rm th}(\mathcal L)\) of
   query-weighted certified container records as in
   \cref{lem:fractional-threshold-container-packing}, formed with
   \(\mathcal N_j=\mathcal L\), and include all of their atom-safe threshold
   prefix filters with the displayed certified prices.

   Suppose that every surplus dual price system \((\alpha,\tau,\sigma)\)
   satisfying \((RS1)\) and having nonpositive reduced gain on the spherical
   buckets, whole high-correlation dense slices, and atom-safe primitive dense
   prefixes has the following property: after dyadically partitioning its
   positive demand prices, some layer \(\mathcal L\) admits nonnegative
   intensities on \(\mathcal C_{\rm th}(\mathcal L)\) satisfying \((FTCP1)\).
   Then the finite filter-cover LP \((\mathsf{FC}_{\mathcal N})\) is feasible
   with query budget \(L\) and storage budget \(S\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If the LP were infeasible, \cref{lem:finite-filter-cover-dual} would give a
   surplus dual price system with nonpositive reduced gain on every column of
   the enlarged universe.  The hypothesis supplies a dyadic layer and a
   fractional threshold-container packing witness satisfying \((FTCP1)\).
   By \cref{lem:fractional-threshold-container-packing}, some threshold-prefix
   filter in the enlarged universe has positive reduced gain, contradicting the
   dual certificate.  Therefore the LP is feasible.
\end{proof}

\Cref{cor:fractional-threshold-container-local-cover} is the exact replacement
for a hard dense branching theorem.  The build stage may search for fractional
query-weighted container packings, but the final contradiction always produces
one ordinary filter-cover column.  Therefore proving a geometric separator in
this fractional language is already enough for the recursive polylog accounting
of \cref{prop:fractional-filter-cover-polylog}.

\begin{lemma}[A posteriori pricing of threshold prefixes]
   \label{lem:threshold-prefix-pareto-pricing}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{lem:fractional-threshold-container-packing}.  Suppose that whenever a
   threshold-prefix filter \(A=(U,Q')\) is produced from a record \(C\) and
   cardinality \(h=|U|\), the offline verifier may replace the search price
   factor \(\psi_C\) by any certified descendant price pair
   \[
      \widehat T_A\le \psi_Ch^{\rho_C},
      \qquad
      \widehat S_A\le \psi_Ch^{1+\rho_C}.
      \tag{TPP1}
   \]
   Then every positive threshold-prefix filter exposed by
   \cref{lem:fractional-threshold-container-packing} remains positive after
   this replacement.  In particular, if \(U\) is certified inside a smaller
   ball, or if an already-built child index gives a better Pareto price than the
   closed-form surrogate, the retained filter-cover LP may charge
   \((\widehat T_A,\widehat S_A)\) instead of
   \((\psi_Ch^{\rho_C},\psi_Ch^{1+\rho_C})\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Let \(A=(U,Q')\) be the threshold-prefix filter found by
   \cref{lem:fractional-threshold-container-packing}.  Its positive reduced gain
   with the search prices is
   \[
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\alpha_{p,q}\mathbf 1\{p\in U,\ q\in Q'\}
      -
      \psi_Ch^{\rho_C}\sum_{q\in Q'}\tau_q
      -
      \sigma\psi_Ch^{1+\rho_C}
      >0 .
   \]
   Replacing the query and storage prices by \(\widehat T_A,\widehat S_A\)
   changes only the two negative terms, and \((TPP1)\) can only decrease them.
   The reduced gain therefore stays positive.  The final statement is just the
   priced-cover convention of \cref{lem:priced-cover-compiler} and
   \cref{cor:offline-recursive-pareto-pricing}: any certified descendant
   query-storage pair may be used as the retained column price.
\end{proof}

\Cref{lem:threshold-prefix-pareto-pricing} is important for overhead.  The
fractional separator may use a simple closed-form cost such as
\(|U|^\rho\Psi(R)\) to find a violation, but the retained index is charged by
the best certified price of the actual prefix that layer-cake exposes.  Thus the
standard certified ball recursion, dense score filters, residual scans, and
terminal smooth product filters remain parts of one Pareto-priced cover rather
than separate algorithmic cases.

\begin{lemma}[Pareto-priced dense-core layer-cake]
   \label{lem:pareto-dense-core-layercake}
   Fix a dyadic demand layer \(\mathcal N_j\), query weights \(0\le y_q\le1\),
   and a set \(U\subseteq P\).  Define
   \[
      d_y(p)=
      \sum_{\substack{q\in\mathcal Q:\\
         (p,q)\in\mathcal N_j,\ \exists z\in\mathcal Z:\ p\in V_{z,q}}}
      y_q ,
      \qquad
      L_y=\sum_q\tau_qy_q ,
   \]
   and, for \(t\in(0,1]\),
   \[
      Q_t(y)=\{q:y_q\ge t\},
      \qquad
      E_t(U)=|\{(p,q):p\in U,\ q\in Q_t(y),\
      (p,q)\in\mathcal N_j,\ \exists z\in\mathcal Z:\ p\in V_{z,q}\}|.
   \]
   Suppose \(U\) has certified descendant prices \(T_U,S_U\), and the filter
   universe contains the threshold filters \((U,Q_t(y))\), for all distinct
   threshold sets, with those prices.  If
   \[
      \theta_j\sum_{p\in U}d_y(p)>T_UL_y+\sigma S_U,
      \tag{PDL1}
   \]
   then some threshold filter \((U,Q_t(y))\) has positive reduced gain.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   The layer-cake identities give
   \[
      \sum_{p\in U}d_y(p)=\int_0^1E_t(U)\,dt,
      \qquad
      L_y=\int_0^1\sum_{q\in Q_t(y)}\tau_q\,dt .
   \]
   Hence \((PDL1)\) implies
   \[
      \int_0^1
      \left[
         \theta_jE_t(U)-T_U\sum_{q\in Q_t(y)}\tau_q
      \right]dt
      >
      \sigma S_U .
   \]
   For some threshold \(t\),
   \[
      \theta_jE_t(U)
      >
      T_U\sum_{q\in Q_t(y)}\tau_q+\sigma S_U .
   \]
   Every incidence counted by \(E_t(U)\) is a demand pair in the dyadic layer,
   and therefore has original demand price at least \(\theta_j\).  Thus the
   true demand captured by the filter \((U,Q_t(y))\) is at least
   \(\theta_jE_t(U)\), while its query and storage charges are exactly the two
   terms on the right.  Its reduced gain is positive.
\end{proof}

\Cref{lem:pareto-dense-core-layercake} is the smallest dense-overlap target.
The geometric theorem may search directly for a set \(U\) of small certified
radius or low descendant Pareto price; it only has to beat the weighted support
objective in \((PDL1)\).  The query side is then forced by thresholding the dual
query weights.  This is the fractional analogue of ordinary dense ball
recursion: choose a smaller certified child because its near-pair support value
justifies its true recursive query and storage price.

\begin{corollary}[Pareto dense-core residual envelope]
   \label{cor:pareto-dense-core-envelope}
   Fix a dyadic demand layer \(\mathcal N_j\) and a finite family of certified
   cores
   \[
      \mathcal U=\{(U,T_U,S_U):U\subseteq P\}.
   \]
   Suppose the filter universe contains, for every \(U\in\mathcal U\) and every
   subset \(Q'\subseteq\mathcal Q\), the filter \((U,Q')\) with certified
   prices \(T_U,S_U\).  For \(0\le y_q\le1\), define \(d_y\) and \(L_y\) as in
   \cref{lem:pareto-dense-core-layercake}.  If no filter generated by
   \(\mathcal U\) has positive reduced gain, then every core and every
   fractional query weighting satisfy
   \[
      \theta_j\sum_{p\in U}d_y(p)
      \le
      T_UL_y+\sigma S_U .
      \tag{PDCE1}
   \]
   Conversely, any violation of \((PDCE1)\) exposes a positive-gain threshold
   activation of the same core.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((PDCE1)\) fails for some \(U\) and \(y\), then
   \cref{lem:pareto-dense-core-layercake} gives a threshold set \(Q_t(y)\) such
   that \((U,Q_t(y))\) has positive reduced gain.  This filter is in the
   universe by hypothesis.  The contrapositive gives the envelope when no
   generated filter has positive gain.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Core-envelope separator implies local cover]
   \label{cor:core-envelope-local-cover}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:residual-separator-local-cover}.  Enlarge
   the finite filter universe so that, for every finite dyadic demand layer
   \(\mathcal L\subseteq\mathcal N\), it contains all threshold activations of
   a finite Pareto-priced core family \(\mathcal U(\mathcal L)\) as in
   \cref{cor:pareto-dense-core-envelope}.

   Suppose that every surplus dual price system \((\alpha,\tau,\sigma)\)
   satisfying \((RS1)\) and having nonpositive reduced gain on the spherical
   buckets, whole high-correlation dense slices, and atom-safe primitive dense
   prefixes has the following property: after dyadically partitioning its
   positive demand prices, some layer \(\mathcal L\), core
   \((U,T_U,S_U)\in\mathcal U(\mathcal L)\), and fractional query weighting
   \(0\le y\le1\) violate \((PDCE1)\).  Then the finite filter-cover LP
   \((\mathsf{FC}_{\mathcal N})\) is feasible with query budget \(L\) and
   storage budget \(S\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If the LP were infeasible, \cref{lem:finite-filter-cover-dual} would give a
   surplus dual certificate with nonpositive reduced gain on every column in the
   enlarged universe.  The assumed separator supplies a dyadic layer, a core,
   and query weights violating \((PDCE1)\).  By
   \cref{cor:pareto-dense-core-envelope}, some threshold activation of that core
   has positive reduced gain.  This threshold activation is a column of the
   enlarged universe, contradicting the dual certificate.
\end{proof}

\Cref{cor:pareto-dense-core-envelope} and
\cref{cor:core-envelope-local-cover} are the precise min-max form of the
remaining dense theorem.  A failed cover supplies dual prices; a successful
geometric separator must find a Pareto-priced core whose weighted support
violates \((PDCE1)\).  If no such core exists, then the residual is
``pseudo-random'' exactly in the sense that every certified smaller-radius child
has support bounded by its true query and storage price.  This is the statement
that has to be contradicted using the spherical high-correlation co-load, or
accepted as the condition under which the spherical reduced-gain test already
wins.

\begin{lemma}[Pareto core hinge normal form]
   \label{lem:pareto-core-hinge-normal-form}
   Fix a dyadic demand layer \(\mathcal N_j\) and a certified core
   \((U,T_U,S_U)\).  Define its saturated layer support at a query by
   \[
      c_U(q)
      =
      |\{p\in U:(p,q)\in\mathcal N_j,\
      \exists z\in\mathcal Z:\ p\in V_{z,q}\}|.
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \max_{0\le y\le1}
      \left[
         \theta_j\sum_{p\in U}d_y(p)-T_U\sum_q\tau_qy_q-\sigma S_U
      \right]
      =
      \sum_q(\theta_jc_U(q)-T_U\tau_q)_+-\sigma S_U .
      \tag{PCH1}
   \]
   Consequently, the following are equivalent.
   First, the core violates the residual envelope \((PDCE1)\) for some
   fractional query weighting.  Second,
   \[
      \sum_q(\theta_jc_U(q)-T_U\tau_q)_+>\sigma S_U .
      \tag{PCH2}
   \]
   Third, the positive-margin query set
   \[
      Q^+(U)=\{q:\theta_jc_U(q)>T_U\tau_q\}
   \]
   makes the threshold filter \((U,Q^+(U))\) have positive reduced gain.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Since
   \[
      \sum_{p\in U}d_y(p)=\sum_qy_qc_U(q),
   \]
   the expression inside the maximum is
   \[
      \sum_qy_q(\theta_jc_U(q)-T_U\tau_q)-\sigma S_U .
   \]
   Maximizing independently over \(0\le y_q\le1\) gives \((PCH1)\).
   Thus some fractional weighting violates \((PDCE1)\) if and only if
   \((PCH2)\) holds.

   For \(Q^+(U)\), the captured demand in the dyadic layer is at least
   \[
      \theta_j\sum_{q\in Q^+(U)}c_U(q).
   \]
   Therefore the reduced gain of \((U,Q^+(U))\) is at least
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q^+(U)}(\theta_jc_U(q)-T_U\tau_q)-\sigma S_U
      =
      \sum_q(\theta_jc_U(q)-T_U\tau_q)_+-\sigma S_U .
   \]
   Hence \((PCH2)\) implies positive reduced gain.  Conversely, if some query
   set \(Q'\) gives positive reduced gain, then the same lower-bound expression
   over \(Q'\) is positive after discarding nonpositive margins, so
   \((PCH2)\) holds.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Dyadic Pareto-core margin screen]
   \label{cor:dyadic-pareto-core-margin-screen}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:pareto-core-hinge-normal-form}.  Partition
   the positive margins
   \[
      d_q(U)=(\theta_jc_U(q)-T_U\tau_q)_+
   \]
   into dyadic classes \(\mathcal Q_1,\ldots,\mathcal Q_K\), where
   \[
      \Delta_\ell\le d_q(U)<2\Delta_\ell
      \qquad(q\in\mathcal Q_\ell).
   \]
   If
   \[
      \sum_qd_q(U)>2K\,\sigma S_U,
      \tag{PCM1}
   \]
   then some margin class \(\mathcal Q_\ell\) makes the restricted filter
   \((U,\mathcal Q_\ell)\) have positive reduced gain.  Conversely, if no
   dyadic margin class of \(U\) has positive reduced gain, then
   \[
      \sum_qd_q(U)\le2K\,\sigma S_U .
      \tag{PCM2}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If every class satisfied
   \[
      \Delta_\ell|\mathcal Q_\ell|\le\sigma S_U,
   \]
   then
   \[
      \sum_qd_q(U)
      <
      2\sum_{\ell=1}^K\Delta_\ell|\mathcal Q_\ell|
      \le
      2K\sigma S_U,
   \]
   contradicting \((PCM1)\).  Hence some class has
   \(\Delta_\ell|\mathcal Q_\ell|>\sigma S_U\).  On this class,
   \[
      \sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_\ell}
      (\theta_jc_U(q)-T_U\tau_q)
      \ge
      \Delta_\ell|\mathcal Q_\ell|
      >
      \sigma S_U .
   \]
   The reduced gain of \((U,\mathcal Q_\ell)\) is positive by the same dyadic
   layer lower bound used in \cref{lem:pareto-core-hinge-normal-form}.  The
   converse is the contrapositive.
\end{proof}

\Cref{lem:pareto-core-hinge-normal-form} removes fractional query weights from
the verification of a proposed core.  The only remaining choices are the
update-side certified core and, up to the logarithmic search slack in
\cref{cor:dyadic-pareto-core-margin-screen}, one ordinary query-margin layer.
Thus the geometric separator can focus on producing a smaller-radius or cheaper
Pareto core with large positive support-minus-load margin; the query side is
canonical.

\begin{lemma}[Fractional Pareto-core packing separator]
   \label{lem:fractional-pareto-core-packing-separator}
   Fix a dyadic demand layer \(\mathcal N_j\) and a finite family of certified
   cores \(\mathcal U\).  For \(U\in\mathcal U\), let \(c_U(q)\) be its
   saturated layer support from \cref{lem:pareto-core-hinge-normal-form}.  Let
   \(\Lambda\) be any finite nonnegative measure on records \((U,y)\), where
   \(U\in\mathcal U\) and \(0\le y_q\le1\).  If
   \[
      \sum_{(U,y)}\Lambda_{U,y}
      \left[
         \theta_j\sum_qy_qc_U(q)
         -
         T_U\sum_q\tau_qy_q
         -
         \sigma S_U
      \right]
      >
      0,
      \tag{FPC1}
   \]
   then some threshold activation of a core in \(\mathcal U\) has positive
   reduced gain.

   Conversely, if no threshold activation of any core in \(\mathcal U\) has
   positive reduced gain, then \((FPC1)\) fails for every such nonnegative
   measure \(\Lambda\).  Equivalently, after optimizing out the fractional query
   weights, the same condition is
   \[
      \sum_{U\in\mathcal U}\lambda_U
      \left[
         \sum_q(\theta_jc_U(q)-T_U\tau_q)_+
         -
         \sigma S_U
      \right]
      \le
      0
      \tag{FPC2}
   \]
   for every nonnegative vector \(\lambda_U\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   If \((FPC1)\) holds, then at least one record \((U,y)\) in the support of
   \(\Lambda\) has
   \[
      \theta_j\sum_qy_qc_U(q)
      >
      T_U\sum_q\tau_qy_q+\sigma S_U .
   \]
   Since
   \[
      \sum_qy_qc_U(q)=\sum_{p\in U}d_y(p),
   \]
   this is exactly the hypothesis \((PDL1)\) of
   \cref{lem:pareto-dense-core-layercake}.  Hence some threshold activation of
   \(U\) has positive reduced gain.

   For the converse, if no threshold activation has positive reduced gain, then
   \cref{cor:pareto-dense-core-envelope} gives \((PDCE1)\) for every \(U\) and
   \(y\).  Multiplying these inequalities by \(\Lambda_{U,y}\) and summing
   proves that the left-hand side of \((FPC1)\) is nonpositive.

   Finally, for a fixed \(U\), maximizing the bracketed expression in
   \((FPC1)\) over \(0\le y\le1\) gives
   \[
      \sum_q(\theta_jc_U(q)-T_U\tau_q)_+-\sigma S_U
   \]
   by \cref{lem:pareto-core-hinge-normal-form}.  Therefore the query-weighted
   conic form \((FPC1)\) is equivalent to the optimized core form \((FPC2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Fractional Pareto-core packing implies local cover]
   \label{cor:fractional-pareto-core-packing-local-cover}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:core-envelope-local-cover}.  Suppose that
   every surplus dual price system \((\alpha,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying
   \((RS1)\), after dyadically partitioning its positive demand prices, admits
   some layer \(\mathcal L\) and a nonnegative measure on query-weighted records
   \[
      (U,y),
      \qquad
      (U,T_U,S_U)\in\mathcal U(\mathcal L),
      \qquad
      0\le y\le1,
   \]
   satisfying \((FPC1)\).  Then the finite filter-cover LP
   \((\mathsf{FC}_{\mathcal N})\) is feasible with query budget \(L\) and
   storage budget \(S\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If the LP were infeasible, \cref{lem:finite-filter-cover-dual} would give a
   surplus dual certificate with nonpositive reduced gain on every retained
   column.  By hypothesis, one dyadic layer admits a fractional Pareto-core
   packing satisfying \((FPC1)\).  Then
   \cref{lem:fractional-pareto-core-packing-separator} exposes a positive-gain
   threshold activation of a core in the enlarged universe, contradicting the
   dual certificate.  Hence the cover LP is feasible.
\end{proof}

This is the fully fractional dense-overlap search problem in its most compact
form.  A proposal mechanism does not have to choose disjoint clusters, Lloyd
centers, or even integral query sides.  It may output any conic combination of
certified cores and fractional query weights.  The verifier reduces positive
total reduced cost to one ordinary retained filter, and
\cref{lem:pareto-core-hinge-normal-form} says that the exact core oracle is the
hinge maximization
\[
   \max_{(U,T_U,S_U)\in\mathcal U}
   \left\{
      \sum_q(\theta_jc_U(q)-T_U\tau_q)_+-\sigma S_U
   \right\}.
\]
Thus \(k\)-means++, additive vector quantization, list decoding, range-reporting
violator search, or learned proposals are useful only insofar as they find
positive reduced-cost cores for this objective.  If every such conic packing has
nonpositive value, the inequalities \((FPC1)\)--\((FPC2)\) are the explicit
weighted pseudo-randomness certificate that must be fed back into the spherical
analysis.

\begin{lemma}[Weighted Pareto-core hinge separator]
   \label{lem:weighted-pareto-core-hinge-separator}
   Work with the original finite demand set \(\mathcal N\) and dual demand
   prices \(\alpha_{p,q}\), without first dyadically unweighting them.  For a
   certified core \((U,T_U,S_U)\), define its exact priced support at query \(q\)
   by
   \[
      a_U(q)
      =
      \sum_{\substack{p\in U:\\
         (p,q)\in\mathcal N,\,
         \exists z\in\mathcal Z:\ p\in V_{z,q}}}
      \alpha_{p,q}.
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \max_{0\le y\le1}
      \left[
         \sum_qy_qa_U(q)
         -
         T_U\sum_q\tau_qy_q
         -
         \sigma S_U
      \right]
      =
      \sum_q(a_U(q)-T_U\tau_q)_+-\sigma S_U .
      \tag{WPC1}
   \]
   Consequently, if
   \[
      \sum_q(a_U(q)-T_U\tau_q)_+>\sigma S_U,
      \tag{WPC2}
   \]
   then the positive-margin activation
   \[
      Q_\alpha^+(U)=\{q:a_U(q)>T_U\tau_q\}
   \]
   makes the filter \((U,Q_\alpha^+(U))\) have positive reduced gain.  Conversely,
   if no threshold activation of \(U\) has positive reduced gain, then
   \((WPC2)\) fails.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   The expression inside the maximum is
   \[
      \sum_qy_q(a_U(q)-T_U\tau_q)-\sigma S_U .
   \]
   Since the coordinates \(y_q\in[0,1]\) are independent, the maximum is attained
   by taking \(y_q=1\) exactly on the positive margins.  This gives \((WPC1)\).

   The reduced gain of \((U,Q_\alpha^+(U))\) is exactly
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q_\alpha^+(U)}a_U(q)
      -
      T_U\sum_{q\in Q_\alpha^+(U)}\tau_q
      -
      \sigma S_U
      =
      \sum_q(a_U(q)-T_U\tau_q)_+-\sigma S_U,
   \]
   so \((WPC2)\) gives positive gain.  Conversely, for any query set \(Q'\), the
   reduced gain of \((U,Q')\) is bounded above by the same positive-part sum
   minus \(\sigma S_U\), because discarding nonpositive margins can only improve
   the value.  Hence a positive-gain activation would imply \((WPC2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Weighted Pareto-core law separator]
   \label{cor:weighted-pareto-core-law-separator}
   Let \(\mathcal U\) be a finite family of certified cores, and let \(\Lambda\)
   be any finite nonnegative measure on records \((U,y)\), where
   \(U\in\mathcal U\) and \(0\le y_q\le1\).  If
   \[
      \sum_{(U,y)}\Lambda_{U,y}
      \left[
         \sum_qy_qa_U(q)
         -
         T_U\sum_q\tau_qy_q
         -
         \sigma S_U
      \right]
      >
      0,
      \tag{WCL1}
   \]
   then some threshold activation of a core in \(\mathcal U\) has positive
   reduced gain.  Equivalently, if no such activation has positive gain, then
   every nonnegative vector \(\lambda_U\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{U\in\mathcal U}\lambda_U
      \left[
         \sum_q(a_U(q)-T_U\tau_q)_+
         -
         \sigma S_U
      \right]
      \le0 .
      \tag{WCL2}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((WCL1)\) holds, one record in the support of \(\Lambda\) has a positive
   bracketed value.  For that core, the maximum in \((WPC1)\) is positive, so
   \cref{lem:weighted-pareto-core-hinge-separator} gives a positive-gain
   activation.

   If no activation has positive gain, then each core has nonpositive optimized
   hinge by \cref{lem:weighted-pareto-core-hinge-separator}; summing those
   inequalities with coefficients \(\lambda_U\) gives \((WCL2)\).  Conversely,
   if \((WCL2)\) fails for some \(\lambda\), then the same lemma exposes a
   positive-gain activation from one core in the support.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Weighted Pareto-core law implies local cover]
   \label{cor:weighted-pareto-core-law-local-cover}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:residual-separator-local-cover}.  Enlarge
   the finite filter universe so that it contains every threshold activation of
   a finite Pareto-priced core family \(\mathcal U_{\rm wt}\), each charged by
   its certified price pair \((T_U,S_U)\).  Suppose that every surplus dual price
   system \((\alpha,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying \((RS1)\) and having nonpositive
   reduced gain on the spherical buckets, whole high-correlation dense slices,
   and atom-safe primitive dense prefixes admits a nonnegative measure on
   query-weighted records
   \[
      (U,y),
      \qquad
      (U,T_U,S_U)\in\mathcal U_{\rm wt},
      \qquad
      0\le y\le1,
   \]
   satisfying \((WCL1)\), with \(a_U(q)\) formed from the original dual prices
   \(\alpha_{p,q}\).  Then the finite filter-cover LP
   \((\mathsf{FC}_{\mathcal N})\) is feasible with query budget \(L\) and
   storage budget \(S\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If the LP were infeasible, \cref{lem:finite-filter-cover-dual} would give a
   surplus dual certificate with nonpositive reduced gain on every column in the
   enlarged universe.  The hypothesis supplies a weighted Pareto-core law
   satisfying \((WCL1)\).  By
   \cref{cor:weighted-pareto-core-law-separator}, some threshold activation of a
   core in \(\mathcal U_{\rm wt}\) has positive reduced gain, contradicting the
   dual certificate.  Thus the cover LP is feasible.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Slice-to-core domination certificate]
   \label{lem:slice-to-core-domination}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:high-correlation-dense-slice-separator}, and
   let \(\mathcal U\) be a finite Pareto-priced core family.  Define the average
   primitive high-correlation captured demand
   \[
      \mathsf A_{\rm hc}
      =
      \E_{Z\sim\Pi}\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}A_{Z,q}
      =
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}
      \alpha_{p,q}\Pr_{Z\sim\Pi}[p\in V_{Z,q}].
      \tag{SCD0}
   \]
   Suppose there is a finite nonnegative measure \(\Lambda\) on records
   \[
      (U,y),
      \qquad
      (U,T_U,S_U)\in\mathcal U,
      \qquad
      0\le y\le1,
   \]
   satisfying the pairwise domination inequalities
   \[
      \sum_{(U,y)}\Lambda_{U,y}y_q
      \mathbf 1\{p\in U,\ \exists z\in\mathcal Z:\ p\in V_{z,q}\}
      \ge
      \Pr_{Z\sim\Pi}[p\in V_{Z,q}]
      \qquad((p,q)\in\mathcal N),
      \tag{SCD1}
   \]
   and the strict price inequality
   \[
      \sum_{(U,y)}\Lambda_{U,y}
      \left[
         T_U\sum_q\tau_qy_q+\sigma S_U
      \right]
      <
      \mathsf A_{\rm hc}.
      \tag{SCD2}
   \]
   Then some threshold activation of a core in \(\mathcal U\) has positive
   reduced gain.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Using the definition of \(a_U(q)\) from
   \cref{lem:weighted-pareto-core-hinge-separator}, the demand side of the
   weighted core law is
   \[
      \sum_{(U,y)}\Lambda_{U,y}\sum_qy_qa_U(q)
      =
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}
      \alpha_{p,q}
      \sum_{(U,y)}\Lambda_{U,y}y_q
      \mathbf 1\{p\in U,\ \exists z\in\mathcal Z:\ p\in V_{z,q}\}.
   \]
   By \((SCD1)\), this is at least \(\mathsf A_{\rm hc}\).  Subtracting the
   price side and using \((SCD2)\) gives \((WCL1)\).  The conclusion follows
   from \cref{cor:weighted-pareto-core-law-separator}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Dominating slice compression implies local cover]
   \label{cor:slice-core-compression-local-cover}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:residual-separator-local-cover}.  Enlarge
   the finite filter universe by threshold activations of a finite Pareto-priced
   core family \(\mathcal U_{\rm sc}\).  Suppose that every surplus dual price
   system \((\alpha,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying \((RS1)\) and having nonpositive
   reduced gain on the spherical buckets, whole high-correlation dense slices,
   and atom-safe primitive dense prefixes admits a measure \(\Lambda\) on
   \(\mathcal U_{\rm sc}\) satisfying \((SCD1)\)--\((SCD2)\).  Then the finite
   filter-cover LP \((\mathsf{FC}_{\mathcal N})\) is feasible with query budget
   \(L\) and storage budget \(S\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If the cover LP were infeasible, \cref{lem:finite-filter-cover-dual} would
   give a surplus dual certificate with nonpositive reduced gain on every
   retained column.  The assumed slice-to-core domination certificate and
   \cref{lem:slice-to-core-domination} then expose a positive-gain threshold
   activation from the enlarged universe, a contradiction.
\end{proof}

The domination certificate is the precise compression version of dense merging.
If the records \((U,y)\) are the singleton slices
\((V_{z,q},\mathbf 1_{\{q\}})\) with intensity \(\Pi(z)\) for every query \(q\),
then \((SCD1)\) is equality and \((SCD2)\) is exactly the sharp average
dense-slice test \((DS2)\); the displayed condition \((DS3)\) is its
\((WS1)\)-based lower-bound sufficient form.  A nontrivial quotient, cap net,
facility bucket, additive quantization cell, or list-decoded region is useful
only when it preserves the same pair-incidence profile while reducing the
Pareto price in \((SCD2)\).
Thus the remaining geometric theorem can be stated without algorithmic
branching language: every residual spherical obstruction must admit a
radius-contracting core domination of the primitive high-correlation slice law
whose price is below its captured dual mass.

\begin{lemma}[Dual obstruction to slice-to-core compression]
   \label{lem:slice-core-compression-dual}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:slice-to-core-domination}, and fix a finite
   family \(\mathcal R\) of query-weighted core records
   \[
      R=(U_R,y^R,T_R,S_R),
      \qquad 0\le y^R\le1.
   \]
   Put
   \[
      r_{p,q}=\Pr_{Z\sim\Pi}[p\in V_{Z,q}],
   \]
   \[
      b_R(p,q)=
      y_q^R\mathbf 1\{p\in U_R,\ \exists z\in\mathcal Z:\ p\in V_{z,q}\},
   \]
   and
   \[
      P_R=T_R\sum_q\tau_qy_q^R+\sigma S_R .
   \]
   Consider the finite compression LP
   \[
      \min_{\lambda_R\ge0}
      \sum_{R\in\mathcal R}\lambda_RP_R
      \qquad\text{subject to}\qquad
      \sum_{R\in\mathcal R}\lambda_Rb_R(p,q)\ge r_{p,q}
      \quad((p,q)\in\mathcal N).
      \tag{SCD-LP}
   \]
   Its dual is
   \[
      \max_{\beta_{p,q}\ge0}
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\beta_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      \qquad\text{subject to}\qquad
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\beta_{p,q}b_R(p,q)\le P_R
      \quad(R\in\mathcal R).
      \tag{SCD-D}
   \]
   Therefore exactly one of the following two alternatives holds:
   \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
      \item there is a slice-to-core domination certificate supported on
      \(\mathcal R\) with price \(<\mathsf A_{\rm hc}\), and hence a positive
      reduced-gain core activation;
      \item there is a nonnegative pair potential \(\beta\) satisfying all dual
      constraints in \((SCD-D)\) and
      \[
         \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\beta_{p,q}r_{p,q}
         \ge
         \mathsf A_{\rm hc}.
         \tag{SCDD1}
      \]
   \end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
