   The displayed primal and dual are a finite covering LP pair.  Weak duality is
   immediate:
   \[
      \sum_{p,q}\beta_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      \le
      \sum_{p,q}\beta_{p,q}\sum_R\lambda_Rb_R(p,q)
      =
      \sum_R\lambda_R\sum_{p,q}\beta_{p,q}b_R(p,q)
      \le
      \sum_R\lambda_RP_R .
   \]
   Finite-dimensional LP duality, equivalently the Farkas separation argument of
   \cref{lem:finite-filter-cover-dual} applied to these inequalities, gives
   equality of the primal and dual optima whenever the primal is feasible.  If
   the primal is infeasible, the same Farkas alternative gives a nonnegative
   dual ray with positive \(r\)-objective and nonpositive \(b_R\)-incidence for
   every \(R\); after scaling it satisfies \((SCDD1)\).  Thus, if the primal has
   value \(<\mathsf A_{\rm hc}\), its optimizer is the desired domination
   certificate and \cref{lem:slice-to-core-domination} gives a positive
   reduced-gain core activation.  In all other cases, a feasible dual obstruction
   satisfies \((SCDD1)\).
\end{proof}

Thus failure of slice-to-core compression has an exact residual meaning.  There
is a new pair potential \(\beta\), supported on the same primitive
high-correlation slice profile \(r_{p,q}\), such that every retained core record
has \(\beta\)-incidence at most its Pareto query/storage price.  This is the
dual weighted pseudo-randomness condition that remains to be contradicted by
geometry, by enriching \(\mathcal R\), or by showing that the spherical bucket
law already has positive reduced gain.

\begin{lemma}[Compression-dual hinge normal form]
   \label{lem:compression-dual-hinge-normal-form}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:slice-core-compression-dual}.  Let
   \(\mathcal U\) be a finite family of Pareto-priced cores
   \((U,T_U,S_U)\).  For \(U\in\mathcal U\) and a nonnegative pair potential
   \(\beta\), define the primitive-visible support at query \(q\) by
   \[
      a_U^\beta(q)
      =
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}
      \beta_{p,q}\mathbf 1\{p\in U,\ \exists z\in\mathcal Z:\ p\in V_{z,q}\}.
      \tag{CDH1}
   \]
   Let \(\mathcal R_{\rm bool}(\mathcal U)\) contain, for every
   \(U\in\mathcal U\) and every query subset \(Q'\subseteq\mathcal Q\), the
   record
   \[
      R=(U,\mathbf 1_{Q'},T_U,S_U).
   \]
   Then \(\beta\) satisfies all dual constraints \((SCD\text{-}D)\) for
   \(\mathcal R_{\rm bool}(\mathcal U)\) if and only if every
   \(U\in\mathcal U\) satisfies the hinge envelope
   \[
      \sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}\bigl(a_U^\beta(q)-T_U\tau_q\bigr)_+
      \le
      \sigma S_U .
      \tag{CDH2}
   \]
   Equivalently, any violation of \((CDH2)\) is witnessed by the single Boolean
   record whose query side is
   \[
      Q_\beta^+(U)=\{q:a_U^\beta(q)>T_U\tau_q\}.
      \tag{CDH3}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   For the Boolean record \(R=(U,\mathbf 1_{Q'},T_U,S_U)\), the dual constraint
   is
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q'}a_U^\beta(q)
      \le
      T_U\sum_{q\in Q'}\tau_q+\sigma S_U .
   \]
   Thus all Boolean constraints for a fixed \(U\) hold if and only if
   \[
      \max_{Q'\subseteq\mathcal Q}
      \sum_{q\in Q'}\bigl(a_U^\beta(q)-T_U\tau_q\bigr)
      \le
      \sigma S_U .
   \]
   The maximum is attained by taking exactly the positive-margin coordinates,
   giving \((CDH2)\) and the witness set \((CDH3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Two-potential residual normal form]
   \label{cor:two-potential-residual-normal-form}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:residual-separator-local-cover}.  Enlarge
   the finite filter universe by all threshold activations of a finite
   Pareto-priced core family \(\mathcal U\), and form the Boolean
   query-record family \(\mathcal R_{\rm bool}(\mathcal U)\) above.

   If the finite filter-cover LP over this enlarged universe is infeasible, then
   there exist nonnegative prices \((\alpha,\tau,\sigma)\) and a nonnegative
   pair potential \(\beta\) such that:
   \[
      A_\alpha>L\sum_q\tau_q+\sigma S,
      \tag{TPR1}
   \]
   every spherical bucket, whole high-correlation dense slice, atom-safe
   primitive dense prefix, and threshold activation of a core in \(\mathcal U\)
   has nonpositive \(\alpha\)-reduced gain;
   \[
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\beta_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      \ge
      \mathsf A_{\rm hc};
      \tag{TPR2}
   \]
   and every \(U\in\mathcal U\) satisfies the \(\beta\)-hinge envelope
   \[
      \sum_q\bigl(a_U^\beta(q)-T_U\tau_q\bigr)_+
      \le
      \sigma S_U .
      \tag{TPR3}
   \]
   Consequently, ruling out all tuples
   \((\alpha,\tau,\sigma,\beta)\) satisfying \((TPR1)\)--\((TPR3)\) proves the
   finite local filter-cover LP feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If the enlarged cover LP is infeasible, \cref{lem:finite-filter-cover-dual}
   gives a surplus dual system \((\alpha,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying \((TPR1)\)
   and having nonpositive reduced gain on every retained column, including the
   listed spherical, primitive dense, and core-threshold columns.  If a
   slice-to-core domination certificate supported on
   \(\mathcal R_{\rm bool}(\mathcal U)\) had price
   \(<\mathsf A_{\rm hc}\), then \cref{lem:slice-to-core-domination} would
   expose a positive-gain threshold activation of a core in \(\mathcal U\),
   contradicting the dual certificate.  Hence alternative \textup{(i)} of
   \cref{lem:slice-core-compression-dual} is impossible, so alternative
   \textup{(ii)} gives a feasible compression dual \(\beta\) satisfying
   \((TPR2)\).  Applying
   \cref{lem:compression-dual-hinge-normal-form} to the Boolean record family
   gives \((TPR3)\).

   The final statement is the contrapositive of the first statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Balanced residual segment]
   \label{cor:balanced-residual-segment}
   In \cref{cor:two-potential-residual-normal-form}, the compression potential
   \(\beta\) may be chosen so that
   \[
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\beta_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      =
      \mathsf A_{\rm hc}
      =
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\alpha_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
      \tag{BRS1}
   \]
   Moreover, for every \(0\le\theta\le1\), the interpolated potential
   \[
      \gamma^\theta=(1-\theta)\alpha+\theta\beta
      \tag{BRS2}
   \]
   has the same primitive captured mass and satisfies the same Pareto-core
   hinge envelope:
   \[
      \sum_q\bigl(a_U^{\gamma^\theta}(q)-T_U\tau_q\bigr)_+
      \le
      \sigma S_U
      \qquad(U\in\mathcal U).
      \tag{BRS3}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If the \(\beta\) supplied by
   \cref{cor:two-potential-residual-normal-form} has primitive captured mass
   larger than \(\mathsf A_{\rm hc}\), scale it down by the factor
   \[
      \frac{\mathsf A_{\rm hc}}
      {\sum_{(p,q)}\beta_{p,q}r_{p,q}} .
   \]
   The dual constraints and the hinge envelopes are monotone under this scaling,
   so feasibility is preserved and \((BRS1)\) holds.  The equality with the
   \(\alpha\)-mass is the definition \((SCD0)\).

   It remains to prove the hinge bound along the segment.  Since every threshold
   activation of every core in \(\mathcal U\) has nonpositive
   \(\alpha\)-reduced gain, the same maximization argument used in
   \cref{lem:compression-dual-hinge-normal-form} gives
   \[
      \sum_q(a_U^\alpha(q)-T_U\tau_q)_+\le\sigma S_U
      \qquad(U\in\mathcal U).
   \]
   The scaled \(\beta\) satisfies the identical bound by \((TPR3)\).  For fixed
   \(U\), the map
   \[
      \gamma\mapsto
      \sum_q(a_U^\gamma(q)-T_U\tau_q)_+
   \]
   is convex because \(a_U^\gamma(q)\) is linear in \(\gamma\) and
   \(x\mapsto x_+\) is convex.  Applying convexity to
   \(\gamma^\theta=(1-\theta)\alpha+\theta\beta\) proves \((BRS3)\).  The
   captured-mass equality along the segment follows linearly from \((BRS1)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{assumption}[One-potential captured-mass core separator]
   \label{asm:one-potential-core-separator}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:high-correlation-dense-slice-separator},
   and assume the budgeted spherical family satisfies \((WS1)\).  Let
   \(\mathcal U\) be a finite Pareto-priced core family.  For every nonnegative
   pair potential \(\gamma\), put
   \[
      \mathsf M(\gamma)
      =
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q},
      \qquad
      r_{p,q}=\Pr_{Z\sim\Pi}[p\in V_{Z,q}].
      \tag{OPC1}
   \]
   The family \(\mathcal U\) is one-potential separating if, for every
   \(\tau_q\ge0\), \(\sigma\ge0\), and nonnegative \(\gamma\) satisfying
   \[
      \mathsf M(\gamma)>
      \pi_1\left(L\sum_q\tau_q+\sigma S\right),
      \tag{OPC2}
   \]
   some \(U\in\mathcal U\) violates the core hinge envelope
   \[
      \sum_q\bigl(a_U^\gamma(q)-T_U\tau_q\bigr)_+
      >
      \sigma S_U .
      \tag{OPC3}
   \]
\end{assumption}

\begin{corollary}[One-potential separation implies local cover]
   \label{cor:one-potential-local-cover}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:residual-separator-local-cover}.  Enlarge
   the finite filter universe by all threshold activations of a finite
   Pareto-priced core family \(\mathcal U\), and assume that
   \(\mathcal U\) is one-potential separating in the sense of
   \cref{asm:one-potential-core-separator}.  Then the finite filter-cover LP
   \((\mathsf{FC}_{\mathcal N})\) is feasible with query budget \(L\) and
   storage budget \(S\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Suppose the enlarged filter-cover LP were infeasible.  Apply
   \cref{cor:two-potential-residual-normal-form} and
   \cref{cor:balanced-residual-segment}, and take any interpolated potential
   \(\gamma^\theta\) from \((BRS2)\).  By \((BRS1)\) and \((SCD0)\),
   \[
      \mathsf M(\gamma^\theta)=\mathsf A_{\rm hc}.
   \]
   Since \(r_{p,q}\ge\pi_1\) for every demanded pair by \((WS1)\) and
   \(p\in H(q)\), while the residual dual has surplus \((TPR1)\),
   \[
      \mathsf A_{\rm hc}
      =
      \sum_{(p,q)}\alpha_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      \ge
      \pi_1A_\alpha
      >
      \pi_1\left(L\sum_q\tau_q+\sigma S\right).
   \]
   Thus \(\gamma^\theta\) satisfies \((OPC2)\).  The one-potential separator
   gives a core \(U\) violating \((OPC3)\), but \((BRS3)\) says every core
   satisfies the opposite inequality along the entire residual segment.  This
   contradiction proves the finite cover LP feasible.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Normalized one-potential obstruction]
   \label{cor:normalized-one-potential-obstruction}
   Failure of \cref{asm:one-potential-core-separator} is equivalent to the
   existence of nonnegative \(\gamma,\tau,\sigma\) such that
   \[
      \mathsf M(\gamma)=1,
      \qquad
      L\sum_q\tau_q+\sigma S<\frac1{\pi_1},
      \tag{NOP1}
   \]
   and every core \(U\in\mathcal U\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_q\bigl(a_U^\gamma(q)-T_U\tau_q\bigr)_+
      \le
      \sigma S_U .
      \tag{NOP2}
   \]
   Equivalently, the one-potential separator is the scale-free statement that
   every unit primitive captured-mass potential has Pareto-core hinge price at
   least \(1/\pi_1\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If the separator fails, there are nonnegative
   \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying \((OPC2)\) while every core satisfies the
   non-strict opposite of \((OPC3)\).  Since \((OPC2)\) makes
   \(\mathsf M(\gamma)>0\), divide \(\gamma,\tau,\sigma\) by
   \(\mathsf M(\gamma)\).  The captured mass becomes \(1\), the price inequality
   becomes the strict inequality in \((NOP1)\), and \((NOP2)\) is preserved
   because both \(a_U^\gamma\) and \(T_U\tau_q\) scale by the same factor and
   the positive part is homogeneous.

   Conversely, multiplying a normalized witness by any positive scalar preserves
   \((NOP2)\) and gives \((OPC2)\).  Thus a normalized witness is exactly a
   scale-fixed failure of \cref{asm:one-potential-core-separator}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Guarded normalized residual segment]
   \label{cor:guarded-normalized-residual-segment}
   Work in the local-cover setting of
   \cref{cor:one-potential-local-cover}, and assume the spherical bucket law
   satisfies \((WS1)\)--\((WS3)\) and \((WS6)\).  Put
   \[
      a_q=\Pr_{Z\sim\Pi}[\chi_Z(q)=1].
   \]
   If the enlarged finite filter-cover LP is infeasible, then there are a
   number \(\kappa\in[1,\pi_1^{-1}]\), nonnegative prices
   \(\bar\tau_q,\bar\sigma\), and a segment of nonnegative pair potentials
   \(\bar\gamma^\theta\), \(0\le\theta\le1\), such that, for every
   \(\theta\),
   \[
      \mathsf M(\bar\gamma^\theta)=1,
      \tag{GNR1}
   \]
   \[
      L\sum_q\bar\tau_q+\bar\sigma S<\kappa,
      \tag{GNR2}
   \]
   and every core \(U\in\mathcal U\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_q\bigl(a_U^{\bar\gamma^\theta}(q)-T_U\bar\tau_q\bigr)_+
      \le
      \bar\sigma S_U .
      \tag{GNR3}
   \]
   Moreover the same normalized residual has large activation-weighted
   high-correlation guard mass:
   \[
      \sum_q\bar\tau_q a_q |H(q)|
      >
      \frac{\pi_1\kappa}{2}.
      \tag{GNR4}
   \]
   Consequently, if all query constraints lie in a low-guard domain
   \(\Omega_{\rm low}=\{q:|P\cap B(q,cr)|<\gamma_0|P|\}\) and
   \(H(q)\subseteq P\cap B(q,cr)\) for every \(q\), then
   \[
      \gamma_0|P|\sum_q\bar\tau_q a_q
      >
      \frac{\pi_1\kappa}{2}.
      \tag{GNR5}
   \]
   In particular no such residual exists when
   \[
      \gamma_0|P|\max_q a_q\le\frac{\pi_1L}{2}.
      \tag{GNR6}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \cref{cor:two-potential-residual-normal-form} and
   \cref{cor:balanced-residual-segment} to the infeasible enlarged LP.  Let
   \[
      M=\mathsf A_{\rm hc}
      =
      \sum_{(p,q)}\alpha_{p,q}r_{p,q},
      \qquad
      \kappa=\frac{A_\alpha}{M}.
   \]
   By \((WS1)\), \(r_{p,q}\ge\pi_1\) on demanded pairs, while
   \(r_{p,q}\le1\) because it is a probability.  Hence
   \[
      \pi_1A_\alpha\le M\le A_\alpha,
      \qquad
      1\le\kappa\le\pi_1^{-1}.
   \]
   Define
   \[
      \bar\gamma^\theta=\gamma^\theta/M,
      \qquad
      \bar\tau=\tau/M,
      \qquad
      \bar\sigma=\sigma/M .
   \]
   The captured-mass equality in \cref{cor:balanced-residual-segment} gives
   \((GNR1)\).  Dividing the surplus inequality
   \(A_\alpha>L\sum_q\tau_q+\sigma S\) by \(M\) gives \((GNR2)\).  Dividing
   \((BRS3)\) by \(M\) gives \((GNR3)\), using homogeneity of the positive
   part.

   Since the infeasible LP's dual has nonpositive reduced gain on every
   spherical bucket, \cref{cor:dual-weighted-guard-spherical-reduced-gain}
   implies the strict failure of \((DWG1)\):
   \[
      \sum_q\tau_q a_q|H(q)|>\frac{\pi_1}{2}A_\alpha .
   \]
   Dividing by \(M\) gives \((GNR4)\).

   Under the low-guard containment hypotheses, \(|H(q)|<\gamma_0|P|\), so
   \((GNR4)\) implies \((GNR5)\).  If \((GNR6)\) also held, then \((GNR2)\)
   would give
   \[
      \gamma_0|P|\sum_q\bar\tau_qa_q
      \le
      \gamma_0|P|\max_q a_q\sum_q\bar\tau_q
      <
      \frac{\pi_1L}{2}\frac{\kappa}{L}
      =
      \frac{\pi_1\kappa}{2},
   \]
   contradicting \((GNR5)\).  Therefore no infeasible residual can exist under
   \((GNR6)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Guard-leakage residual dichotomy]
   \label{cor:guard-leakage-residual-dichotomy}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:guarded-normalized-residual-segment}.  Assume all query
   constraints lie in the low-guard domain
   \[
      \Omega_{\rm low}
      =
      \{q:|P\cap B(q,cr)|<\gamma_0|P|\}.
   \]
   For each query write
   \[
      H_{\rm in}(q)=H(q)\cap B(q,cr),
      \qquad
      H_{\rm out}(q)=H(q)\setminus B(q,cr).
   \]
   If the activation-weighted guard budget satisfies, for some
   \(0\le\eta<1/2\),
   \[
      \gamma_0|P|\max_q a_q\le \eta\,\pi_1L,
      \tag{GLD1}
   \]
   then every guarded normalized residual from
   \cref{cor:guarded-normalized-residual-segment} satisfies
   \[
      \sum_q\bar\tau_q a_q |H_{\rm out}(q)|
      >
      \left(\frac12-\eta\right)\pi_1\kappa .
      \tag{GLD2}
   \]
   Thus, under the budget-compatible low-guard choice, any residual high
   correlation that is not already separated by spherical buckets must appear
   as annular high-correlation leakage outside the resident \(cr\)-guard ball.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Since \(q\in\Omega_{\rm low}\),
   \[
      |H_{\rm in}(q)|
      \le |P\cap B(q,cr)|
      < \gamma_0|P| .
   \]
   Therefore, using \((GNR2)\),
   \[
      \sum_q\bar\tau_q a_q|H_{\rm in}(q)|
      \le
      \gamma_0|P|\max_q a_q\sum_q\bar\tau_q
      <
      \eta\pi_1L\cdot \frac{\kappa}{L}
      =
      \eta\pi_1\kappa .
   \]
   On the other hand, \((GNR4)\) gives
   \[
      \sum_q\bar\tau_q a_q
      \bigl(|H_{\rm in}(q)|+|H_{\rm out}(q)|\bigr)
      >
      \frac{\pi_1\kappa}{2}.
   \]
   Subtracting the inside bound proves \((GLD2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Thresholded annular collision residual]
   \label{cor:thresholded-annular-collision-residual}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:guarded-normalized-residual-segment}.  For the spherical bucket
   law define the point-query collision profile
   \[
      c_q(x)=\Pr_{Z\sim\Pi}[x\in U_Z,\ \chi_Z(q)=1],
      \qquad
      a_q=\Pr_{Z\sim\Pi}[\chi_Z(q)=1].
   \]
   Fix a far threshold \(\pi_2>0\), and suppose every demanded pair satisfies
   \(\|p-q\|\le r\).  For each query put
   \[
      A_{\pi_2}(q)
      =
      \{x\in P:\|x-q\|>cr,\ c_q(x)>\pi_2\},
      \tag{TAC1}
   \]
   and choose the high-correlation set
   \[
      H_{\pi_2}(q)=\bigl(P\cap B(q,cr)\bigr)\cup A_{\pi_2}(q).
      \tag{TAC2}
   \]
   Assume the near-hit and update bounds \((WS1)\), \((WS3)\), and the budget
   inequalities
   \[
      \pi_2|P|\le\frac{\pi_1L}{4},
      \qquad
      \pi_u|P|\le\frac{\pi_1S}{4}.
      \tag{TAC3}
   \]
   Also assume all query constraints lie in
   \[
      \Omega_{\rm low}=\{q:|P\cap B(q,cr)|<\gamma_0|P|\},
   \]
   and that, for some \(0\le\eta<1/2\),
   \[
      \gamma_0|P|\max_q a_q\le\eta\,\pi_1L .
      \tag{TAC4}
   \]
   If the enlarged local filter-cover LP is infeasible, then the guarded
   normalized residual produced using \(H_{\pi_2}\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_q\bar\tau_q a_q |A_{\pi_2}(q)|
      >
      \left(\frac12-\eta\right)\pi_1\kappa .
      \tag{TAC5}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The choice \(H_{\pi_2}\) contains every demanded near point because
   \(\|p-q\|\le r<cr\).  If \(x\notin H_{\pi_2}(q)\), then either
   \(x\notin P\cap B(q,cr)\) and \(x\notin A_{\pi_2}(q)\), or \(x\notin P\).
   For resident points this gives \(c_q(x)\le\pi_2\), which is exactly
   \((WS2)\) for the high-correlation set \(H_{\pi_2}\).  Together with
   \((WS1)\), \((WS3)\), and \((TAC3)\), the hypotheses of
   \cref{cor:guarded-normalized-residual-segment} hold for this choice of
   \(H\).  Moreover
   \[
      H_{\pi_2}(q)\setminus B(q,cr)=A_{\pi_2}(q).
   \]
   Applying \cref{cor:guard-leakage-residual-dichotomy} with
   \((TAC4)\) gives \((TAC5)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Annular active-collision residual]
   \label{cor:annular-active-collision-residual}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:thresholded-annular-collision-residual}.  If the enlarged local
   filter-cover LP is infeasible, then the guarded normalized residual satisfies
   the far active-collision lower bound
   \[
      \sum_q\bar\tau_q
      \sum_{\substack{x\in P\\ \|x-q\|>cr}}
      c_q(x)
      >
      \pi_2\left(\frac12-\eta\right)\pi_1\kappa .
      \tag{AAC1}
   \]
   Consequently, a proof that every normalized residual satisfying the core
   hinge envelopes has the opposite upper bound on the left side of
   \((AAC1)\) rules out local infeasibility.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For \(x\in A_{\pi_2}(q)\), \(c_q(x)>\pi_2\).  Also
   \(0\le a_q\le1\).  Hence
   \[
      \sum_{\|x-q\|>cr}c_q(x)
      \ge
      \sum_{x\in A_{\pi_2}(q)}c_q(x)
      >
      \pi_2|A_{\pi_2}(q)|
      \ge
      \pi_2a_q|A_{\pi_2}(q)|.
   \]
   Multiplying by \(\bar\tau_q\), summing over \(q\), and applying
   \((TAC5)\) gives \((AAC1)\).

   The final statement is the contrapositive: by
   \cref{cor:thresholded-annular-collision-residual}, any infeasible local cover
   produces a normalized residual satisfying \((AAC1)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Activation-relative annular collision residual]
   \label{cor:relative-annular-active-collision-residual}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:guarded-normalized-residual-segment}.  For the spherical bucket law
   define
   \[
      c_q(x)=\Pr_{Z\sim\Pi}[x\in U_Z,\ \chi_Z(q)=1],
      \qquad
      a_q=\Pr_{Z\sim\Pi}[\chi_Z(q)=1],
      \qquad
      a_*=\max_q a_q .
   \]
   Fix \(0<\beta\le1\), and suppose every demanded pair satisfies
   \(\|p-q\|\le r\).  For each query put
   \[
      A_\beta(q)
      =
      \{x\in P:\|x-q\|>cr,\ c_q(x)>\beta a_q\},
      \tag{RAC1}
   \]
   and
   \[
      H_\beta(q)=\bigl(P\cap B(q,cr)\bigr)\cup A_\beta(q).
      \tag{RAC2}
   \]
   Assume the near-hit and update bounds \((WS1)\), \((WS3)\), and the budget
   inequalities
   \[
      \beta a_*|P|\le\frac{\pi_1L}{4},
      \qquad
      \pi_u|P|\le\frac{\pi_1S}{4}.
      \tag{RAC3}
   \]
   Also assume all query constraints lie in
   \[
      \Omega_{\rm low}=\{q:|P\cap B(q,cr)|<\gamma_0|P|\},
   \]
   and that, for some \(0\le\eta<1/2\),
   \[
      \gamma_0|P|a_*\le\eta\,\pi_1L .
      \tag{RAC4}
   \]
   If the enlarged local filter-cover LP is infeasible, then the guarded
   normalized residual produced using \(H_\beta\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_q\bar\tau_q a_q |A_\beta(q)|
      >
      \left(\frac12-\eta\right)\pi_1\kappa ,
      \tag{RAC5}
   \]
   and therefore
   \[
      \sum_q\bar\tau_q
      \sum_{\substack{x\in P\\ \|x-q\|>cr}}
      c_q(x)
      >
      \beta\left(\frac12-\eta\right)\pi_1\kappa .
      \tag{RAC6}
   \]
   Consequently, a proof that every normalized residual satisfying the core
   hinge envelopes has the opposite upper bound on the left side of \((RAC6)\)
   rules out local infeasibility in this activation-relative branch.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The set \(H_\beta(q)\) contains every demanded near point because
   \(\|p-q\|\le r<cr\).  If \(x\in P\setminus H_\beta(q)\), then
   \(x\notin P\cap B(q,cr)\), so \(\|x-q\|>cr\), and also
   \(x\notin A_\beta(q)\).  Thus every resident point outside \(H_\beta(q)\)
   satisfies
   \[
      c_q(x)\le \beta a_q\le \beta a_* .
   \]
   Hence \((WS2)\) holds for this \(H_\beta\) with far parameter
   \(\pi_2=\beta a_*\), and \((RAC3)\) gives the spherical budget condition
   \((WS6)\).  Applying
   \cref{cor:guarded-normalized-residual-segment} and then
   \cref{cor:guard-leakage-residual-dichotomy} with \((RAC4)\) yields
   \((RAC5)\), since
   \(H_\beta(q)\setminus B(q,cr)=A_\beta(q)\).

   For \(x\in A_\beta(q)\), \(c_q(x)>\beta a_q\).  Therefore
   \[
      \sum_{\|x-q\|>cr}c_q(x)
      \ge
      \sum_{x\in A_\beta(q)}c_q(x)
      >
      \beta a_q|A_\beta(q)|.
   \]
   Multiplying by \(\bar\tau_q\), summing over \(q\), and using \((RAC5)\) gives
   \((RAC6)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Far active-load spherical fallback]
   \label{cor:far-active-load-spherical-fallback}
   Work in the setting and under the hypotheses of
   \cref{cor:relative-annular-active-collision-residual}.  Suppose in addition
   that every query has budget-compatible far active load:
   \[
      F_q^{\rm far}
      :=
      \sum_{\substack{x\in P\\ \|x-q\|>cr}}c_q(x)
      \le
      \beta\left(\frac12-\eta\right)\pi_1L
      \qquad(q\in\mathcal Q).
      \tag{FAL1}
   \]
   Then the enlarged local filter-cover LP is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If the LP were infeasible, then
   \cref{cor:relative-annular-active-collision-residual} would produce a guarded
   normalized residual satisfying \((RAC6)\).  On the other hand, \((FAL1)\) and
   the normalized price bound \((GNR2)\) give
   \[
      \sum_q\bar\tau_qF_q^{\rm far}
      \le
      \beta\left(\frac12-\eta\right)\pi_1L\sum_q\bar\tau_q
      <
      \beta\left(\frac12-\eta\right)\pi_1\kappa ,
   \]
   since \(\bar\sigma S\ge0\).  This contradicts \((RAC6)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Dyadic relative-load superlevel]
   \label{lem:dyadic-relative-load-superlevel}
   Fix a query \(q\), and use the notation of
   \cref{cor:relative-annular-active-collision-residual}.  For an integer
   \(J\ge1\), let
   \[
      \mathcal B_J=\{2^{-j}:1\le j\le J\},
   \]
   and, for \(\beta\in\mathcal B_J\), put
   \[
      A_\beta(q)=
      \{x\in P:\|x-q\|>cr,\ c_q(x)>\beta a_q\}.
   \]
   Then
   \[
      F_q^{\rm far}
      :=
      \sum_{\substack{x\in P\\ \|x-q\|>cr}}c_q(x)
      \le
      a_q|P|2^{-J}
      +
      2\sum_{\beta\in\mathcal B_J}\beta a_q |A_\beta(q)|.
      \tag{DRL1}
   \]
   Consequently, if \(F_q^{\rm far}>a_q|P|2^{-J}\), then some
   \(\beta\in\mathcal B_J\) satisfies
   \[
      \beta a_q |A_\beta(q)|
      \ge
      \frac{F_q^{\rm far}-a_q|P|2^{-J}}{2J}.
      \tag{DRL2}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   If \(a_q=0\), then \(c_q(x)\le a_q=0\) for every \(x\), so the claim is
   trivial.  Otherwise put \(s_x=c_q(x)/a_q\in[0,1]\) for far points
   \(\|x-q\|>cr\).  For every \(s\in[0,1]\),
   \[
      s\le 2^{-J}+2\sum_{j=1}^J2^{-j}\mathbf 1\{s>2^{-j}\}.
   \]
   Summing this inequality over far points and multiplying by \(a_q\) gives
   \((DRL1)\).  If every dyadic level were strictly smaller than the right side
   of \((DRL2)\), then \((DRL1)\) would make \(F_q^{\rm far}\) strictly smaller
   than itself.  Hence at least one level satisfies \((DRL2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Weighted dyadic annular load]
   \label{lem:weighted-dyadic-annular-load}
   In the setting of \cref{lem:dyadic-relative-load-superlevel}, let
   \(\omega_q\ge0\) be arbitrary query weights, and put
   \[
      M_{\rm far}(\omega)
      =
      \sum_q\omega_q
      \sum_{\substack{x\in P\\ \|x-q\|>cr}}c_q(x).
   \]
   Then
   \[
      M_{\rm far}(\omega)
      \le
      2^{-J}|P|\sum_q\omega_qa_q
      +
      2\sum_{\beta\in\mathcal B_J}
      \beta\sum_q\omega_qa_q|A_\beta(q)|.
      \tag{WDL1}
   \]
   Consequently, if
   \[
      M_{\rm far}(\omega)>2^{-J}|P|\sum_q\omega_qa_q,
   \]
   then some \(\beta\in\mathcal B_J\) satisfies
   \[
      \beta\sum_q\omega_qa_q|A_\beta(q)|
      \ge
      \frac{
         M_{\rm far}(\omega)-2^{-J}|P|\sum_q\omega_qa_q
      }{2J}.
      \tag{WDL2}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Multiply \((DRL1)\) by \(\omega_q\) and sum over \(q\).  This proves
   \((WDL1)\).  If every dyadic level were strictly smaller than the right side
   of \((WDL2)\), then \((WDL1)\) would contradict the assumed strict lower
   bound on \(M_{\rm far}(\omega)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Dyadic annular residual witness]
   \label{cor:dyadic-annular-residual-witness}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:relative-annular-active-collision-residual}, but denote its
   relative threshold by \(\beta_0\).  Let
   \(C_\eta=\frac12-\eta\), and let \(J\ge1\).  Suppose the enlarged local
   filter-cover LP is infeasible, and let
   \((\bar\tau,\bar\sigma,\bar\gamma^\theta,\kappa)\) be the guarded normalized
   residual produced by that corollary.  If, for some \(0\le\xi<1\),
   \[
      2^{-J}a_*|P|\le \xi\,\beta_0 C_\eta\pi_1L,
      \tag{DAR1}
   \]
   then some dyadic level \(\beta\in\mathcal B_J\) satisfies
   \[
      \beta\sum_q\bar\tau_q a_q |A_\beta(q)|
      >
      \frac{(1-\xi)\beta_0 C_\eta\pi_1\kappa}{2J}.
      \tag{DAR2}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \cref{lem:weighted-dyadic-annular-load} with
   \(\omega_q=\bar\tau_q\).  The far-load term is strictly larger than
   \(\beta_0C_\eta\pi_1\kappa\) by \((RAC6)\).  The tail term is bounded using
   \((GNR2)\):
   \[
      2^{-J}|P|\sum_q\bar\tau_qa_q
      \le
      2^{-J}a_*|P|\sum_q\bar\tau_q
      <
      2^{-J}a_*|P|\,\frac{\kappa}{L}
      \le
      \xi\,\beta_0C_\eta\pi_1\kappa .
   \]
   Therefore the numerator in \((WDL2)\) is strictly larger than
   \((1-\xi)\beta_0C_\eta\pi_1\kappa\), which gives \((DAR2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Primitive lift of annular superlevels]
   \label{lem:primitive-annular-superlevel-lift}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:weighted-dyadic-annular-load}, and write
   \[
      c_q(x)=\Pr_{Z\sim\Pi}[x\in U_Z,\ \chi_Z(q)=1],
      \qquad
      a_q=\Pr_{Z\sim\Pi}[\chi_Z(q)=1].
   \]
   For \(\beta\in\mathcal B_J\), set
   \[
      B_{z,\beta}(q)=U_z\cap A_\beta(q),
      \qquad
      A_\beta(q)=\{x\in P:\|x-q\|>cr,\ c_q(x)>\beta a_q\}.
   \]
   Then every nonnegative query weighting \(\omega_q\) satisfies
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \E_{Z\sim\Pi}\sum_q\omega_q\chi_Z(q)|B_{Z,\beta}(q)|
      &=
      \sum_q\omega_q\sum_{x\in A_\beta(q)}c_q(x)\\
      &>
      \beta\sum_q\omega_qa_q|A_\beta(q)|.
   \end{aligned}
      \tag{PAS1}
   \]
   Consequently, in the setting of
   \cref{cor:dyadic-annular-residual-witness}, the dyadic level supplied by
   \((DAR2)\) also satisfies
   \[
      \E_{Z\sim\Pi}\sum_q\bar\tau_q\chi_Z(q)|B_{Z,\beta}(q)|
      >
      \frac{(1-\xi)\beta_0C_\eta\pi_1\kappa}{2J}.
      \tag{PAS2}
   \]
   If the primitive law has finite support, then some seed \(z\) in that support
   has
   \[
      \sum_q\bar\tau_q\chi_z(q)|B_{z,\beta}(q)|
      >
      \frac{(1-\xi)\beta_0C_\eta\pi_1\kappa}{2J}.
      \tag{PAS3}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Expand the expectation and exchange the finite sums:
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \E_Z\sum_q\omega_q\chi_Z(q)|B_{Z,\beta}(q)|
      &=
      \sum_q\omega_q
      \sum_{x\in A_\beta(q)}
      \Pr_Z[x\in U_Z,\ \chi_Z(q)=1]\\
      &=
      \sum_q\omega_q\sum_{x\in A_\beta(q)}c_q(x).
   \end{aligned}
   \]
   For every \(x\in A_\beta(q)\), the defining inequality gives
   \(c_q(x)>\beta a_q\).  This proves \((PAS1)\).  Combining \((PAS1)\) with
   \((DAR2)\), using \(\omega=\bar\tau\), gives \((PAS2)\).  The finite-support
   statement is averaging: if every seed had value at most the right side of
   \((PAS3)\), then the expectation in \((PAS2)\) would also be at most that
   value.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Single-seed annular query layer]
   \label{cor:single-seed-annular-query-layer}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:dyadic-annular-residual-witness}, and assume the primitive law has
   finite support.  Let \(m=|P|\ge1\),
   \[
      K_m=1+\lceil\log_2 m\rceil,
      \qquad
      \mathcal D_m=\{2^\ell:0\le\ell\le\lceil\log_2 m\rceil\}.
   \]
   If the local LP is infeasible and the tail condition \((DAR1)\) holds, then
   for the dyadic collision level \(\beta\) from
   \cref{cor:dyadic-annular-residual-witness} there are a seed \(z\) and a
   size level \(\Delta\in\mathcal D_m\) such that the Boolean query layer
   \[
      Q_{z,\beta,\Delta}
      =
      \{q:\chi_z(q)=1,\ |B_{z,\beta}(q)|\ge\Delta\}
      \tag{SAQ1}
   \]
   satisfies
   \[
      \Delta\sum_{q\in Q_{z,\beta,\Delta}}\bar\tau_q
      >
      \frac{(1-\xi)\beta_0C_\eta\pi_1\kappa}{4JK_m}.
      \tag{SAQ2}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \cref{lem:primitive-annular-superlevel-lift}, some seed \(z\) satisfies
   \((PAS3)\).  Put
   \[
      h_q=\chi_z(q)|B_{z,\beta}(q)|.
   \]
   For every integer \(0\le h\le m\),
   \[
      h\le2\sum_{\Delta\in\mathcal D_m}\Delta\mathbf 1\{h\ge\Delta\}.
   \]
   Multiplying by \(\bar\tau_q\), summing over \(q\), and using \((PAS3)\)
   gives
   \[
      2\sum_{\Delta\in\mathcal D_m}
      \Delta\sum_{q:h_q\ge\Delta}\bar\tau_q
      >
      \frac{(1-\xi)\beta_0C_\eta\pi_1\kappa}{2J}.
   \]
   Since \(|\mathcal D_m|=K_m\), one level \(\Delta\) satisfies \((SAQ2)\).
   The set \(\{q:h_q\ge\Delta\}\) is exactly \(Q_{z,\beta,\Delta}\).
\end{proof}

\begin{assumption}[Weighted annular-to-scalar reporter]
   \label{asm:weighted-annular-scalar-reporter}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:dyadic-annular-residual-witness}, and let
   the retained scalar prefix pool be the one used in
   \cref{cor:certified-scalar-superlevel-reporter}.  Fix the residual threshold
   \(\beta_0\), the dyadic depth \(J\), the tail parameter \(\xi\), and
   \(C_\eta=\frac12-\eta\).  The primitive law and retained pool are
   annular-reporting complete if the following implication holds.

   Whenever a guarded normalized residual
   \((\bar\tau,\bar\sigma,\bar\gamma^\theta,\kappa)\) satisfies
   \((GNR1)\)--\((GNR3)\) and, for some \(\beta\in\mathcal B_J\),
   \[
      \beta\sum_q\bar\tau_q a_q |A_\beta(q)|
      >
      \frac{(1-\xi)\beta_0 C_\eta\pi_1\kappa}{2J},
      \tag{ASR1}
   \]
   there are a parameter \(\theta\in[0,1]\), a retained container \(W\), and a
   finite law \(\nu\) on scalar total-degree levels such that the one-sided
   certificates \(X_\delta,K_\delta\) of
   \cref{cor:certified-scalar-superlevel-reporter}, computed for the scalar
   degree
   \[
      d^{\bar\gamma^\theta}(p)
      =
      \sum_{q:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\bar\gamma^\theta_{p,q}r_{p,q},
   \]
   satisfy \((CSR0)\) and either \((CSR1)\) or its capped form \((CSR2)\), with
   query and storage prices \((\bar\tau,\bar\sigma)\).
\end{assumption}

\begin{corollary}[Primitive annular panel reporter suffices]
   \label{cor:primitive-annular-panel-reporter-suffices}
   In the setting of \cref{asm:weighted-annular-scalar-reporter}, it is enough
   to prove the following primitive-panel reporter statement.  Whenever a
   guarded normalized residual satisfies \((GNR1)\)--\((GNR3)\) and, for some
   \(\beta\in\mathcal B_J\), with \(B_{z,\beta}(q)\) as in
   \cref{lem:primitive-annular-superlevel-lift},
   \[
      \E_{Z\sim\Pi}\sum_q\bar\tau_q\chi_Z(q)|B_{Z,\beta}(q)|
      >
      \frac{(1-\xi)\beta_0C_\eta\pi_1\kappa}{2J},
      \tag{PAPR1}
   \]
   the primitive annular panel \(B_{z,\beta}(q)\) yields the one-sided scalar
   reporter required in
   \cref{asm:weighted-annular-scalar-reporter}.  Under this primitive-panel
   reporter statement, the local-cover conclusion of
   \cref{cor:annular-reporter-local-cover} follows.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If a guarded normalized residual satisfies \((ASR1)\), then
   \cref{lem:primitive-annular-superlevel-lift} gives \((PAPR1)\).  The assumed
   primitive-panel reporter therefore supplies the same certified scalar
   superlevel panel demanded by \cref{asm:weighted-annular-scalar-reporter}.
   Hence the weighted annular-to-scalar reporter assumption holds, and
   \cref{cor:annular-reporter-local-cover} gives local feasibility.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Single-seed query-layer reporter suffices]
   \label{cor:single-seed-query-layer-reporter-suffices}
   Work under the hypotheses of \cref{cor:annular-reporter-local-cover}, and
   assume the primitive law has finite support.  It is enough to prove the
   primitive-panel reporter only for panels that contain a seed \(z\), dyadic
   collision level \(\beta\), and size level \(\Delta\in\mathcal D_{|P|}\)
   satisfying \((SAQ1)\)--\((SAQ2)\).  More explicitly, if every such
   single-seed annular query layer yields the one-sided scalar reporter required
   in \cref{asm:weighted-annular-scalar-reporter}, then the enlarged local
   filter-cover LP is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Infeasibility plus \((DAR1)\) gives a layer
   \(Q_{z,\beta,\Delta}\) satisfying \((SAQ1)\)--\((SAQ2)\) by
   \cref{cor:single-seed-annular-query-layer}.  The assumed single-seed
   query-layer reporter supplies the one-sided scalar panel required in
   \cref{asm:weighted-annular-scalar-reporter} for this residual.  Thus every
   residual produced by local infeasibility satisfies the weighted
   annular-to-scalar reporter condition, and
   \cref{cor:annular-reporter-local-cover} gives the local-cover conclusion.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Annular scalar-reporter record]
   \label{def:annular-scalar-reporter-record}
   Fix a guarded normalized residual
   \((\bar\tau,\bar\sigma,\bar\gamma^\theta,\kappa)\).  An annular
   scalar-reporter record is a tuple
   \[
      R=(\theta_R,W_R,\nu_R,X^R,K^R)
   \]
   where \(0\le\theta_R\le1\), \(W_R\) is a retained container, \(\nu_R\) is a
   finite probability law on positive scalar levels, and \(X^R_\delta,K^R_\delta\)
   are one-sided certificates for the scalar degree
   \[
      d_R(p)=
      \sum_{q:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}
      \bar\gamma^{\theta_R}_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
   \]
   The constants in the surplus test below are the scalar-prefix constants used
   in \cref{cor:certified-scalar-superlevel-reporter}.
   Thus, writing
   \[
      H^R_\delta=
      |\{p\in W_R:d_R(p)\ge\delta\}|,
   \]
   the record must certify
   \[
      0\le X^R_\delta\le\delta H^R_\delta,
      \qquad
      H^R_\delta\le K^R_\delta
      \tag{ARR0}
   \]
   for every reported level.  Its certified surplus is
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \Phi(R)
      &=
      \E_{\nu_R}X^R_\delta\\
      &\quad-
      \frac{b\,\psi_{W_R}}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{\rho_{W_R}}
               (\E_{\nu_R}K^R_\delta)^{\rho_{W_R}}}{L}
         +
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{1+\rho_{W_R}}
               \E_{\nu_R}(K^R_\delta)^{1+\rho_{W_R}}}{S}
      \right).
   \end{aligned}
      \tag{ARR1}
   \]
   If the record also certifies a cap \(K^R_\delta\le H_R\) on the support of
   \(\nu_R\), its capped surplus is
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \Phi_{\rm cap}(R)
      &=
      \E_{\nu_R}X^R_\delta\\
      &\quad-
      \frac{b\,\psi_{W_R}}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{\rho_{W_R}}
               (\E_{\nu_R}K^R_\delta)^{\rho_{W_R}}}{L}
         +
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{1+\rho_{W_R}}
               H_R^{\rho_{W_R}}\E_{\nu_R}K^R_\delta}{S}
      \right).
   \end{aligned}
      \tag{ARR2}
   \]
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Single-seed reporter proposal criterion]
   \label{cor:single-seed-reporter-proposal-criterion}
   Work under the hypotheses of
   \cref{cor:single-seed-query-layer-reporter-suffices}.  Fix any guarded
   normalized residual and any single-seed annular query layer
   \(Q_{z,\beta,\Delta}\) satisfying \((SAQ1)\)--\((SAQ2)\).  Suppose a finite
   proposal law over annular scalar-reporter records, possibly depending on
   this layer, satisfies
   \[
      \E_R\Phi(R)>0
      \tag{SRP1}
   \]
   or satisfies the capped analogue
   \[
      \E_R\Phi_{\rm cap}(R)>0 .
      \tag{SRP2}
   \]
   Then this single-seed layer yields the one-sided scalar reporter required in
   \cref{asm:weighted-annular-scalar-reporter}.  Consequently, if every
   single-seed annular query layer produced by
   \cref{cor:single-seed-annular-query-layer} admits such a finite proposal
   law, then the enlarged local filter-cover LP is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((SRP1)\) holds, some record \(R\) has \(\Phi(R)>0\).  In particular
   \(\E_{\nu_R}X^R_\delta>0\), because the price terms in \((ARR1)\) are
   nonnegative.  The certificates \((ARR0)\) are exactly \((CSR0)\) for the
   residual potential \(\bar\gamma^{\theta_R}\), the retained container
   \(W_R\), and the level law \(\nu_R\).  The inequality \(\Phi(R)>0\) is
   strictly stronger than \((CSR1)\).  Hence this record is a valid scalar
   reporter for the fixed single-seed layer.  The capped case is identical,
   using \((ARR2)\) to get \((CSR2)\).

   If every layer satisfying \((SAQ1)\)--\((SAQ2)\) has such a proposal law,
   then every layer supplied by
   \cref{cor:single-seed-annular-query-layer} yields the reporter demanded in
   \cref{cor:single-seed-query-layer-reporter-suffices}.  That corollary gives
   local feasibility of the enlarged filter-cover LP.
\end{proof}

The criterion above is the fully fractional dense-overlap interface at the
current annular endpoint.  A \(k\)-means++ panel, additive-quantization panel,
lattice list-decoder, or range-reporting routine is useful only through a
finite law over certified records with positive expected surplus
\((SRP1)\) or \((SRP2)\).  The annular far points remain proposal evidence; they
are not themselves cover columns.  The retained object is the deterministic
record exposed by averaging, which is then verified against the scalar
near-pair degree and charged by the ordinary filter-cover LP.

\begin{corollary}[Near-shadow mass certificate for annular reporters]
   \label{cor:annular-near-shadow-mass-reporter}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:single-seed-reporter-proposal-criterion}.  Fix a guarded
   normalized residual, a parameter \(0\le\theta\le1\), a query layer
   \(Q'\subseteq\mathcal Q\), and a retained container \(W\).  Put
   \[
      d^\theta(p)
      =
      \sum_{q:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}
      \bar\gamma^\theta_{p,q}r_{p,q},
      \qquad
      d_{Q'}^\theta(p)
      =
      \sum_{\substack{q\in Q'\\(p,q)\in\mathcal N}}
      \bar\gamma^\theta_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
   \]
   Suppose a proposal routine certifies numbers \(K\ge1\) and \(V>0\) such that
   \[
      |W|\le K,
      \qquad
      V\le\sum_{p\in W}d_{Q'}^\theta(p).
      \tag{ANS1}
   \]
   Let
   \[
      J_{K,V}=1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{2K}{V}\right\rceil .
   \]
   If
   \[
      \frac{V}{4J_{K,V}}
      >
      \frac{b\,\psi_W}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{\rho_W}K^{\rho_W}}{L}
         +
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{1+\rho_W}K^{1+\rho_W}}{S}
      \right),
      \tag{ANS2}
   \]
   then the proposal routine can materialize an annular scalar-reporter record
   with positive certified surplus \(\Phi(R)>0\).  Consequently this
   single-seed annular layer satisfies the reporter hypothesis of
   \cref{cor:single-seed-reporter-proposal-criterion}.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Since \(d_{Q'}^\theta(p)\le d^\theta(p)\), \((ANS1)\) gives
   \[
      V\le M:=\sum_{p\in W}d^\theta(p).
   \]
   By \((GNR1)\), the total mass of \(d^\theta\) over \(P\) is one, so every
   value \(d^\theta(p)\) lies in \([0,1]\).  For
   \(1\le j\le J_{K,V}\), put \(\delta_j=2^{-j}\) and
   \[
      H_j=\left|\{p\in W:d^\theta(p)\ge\delta_j\}\right|.
   \]
   The elementary dyadic layer-cake bound gives
   \[
      M
      \le
      2^{-J_{K,V}}K
      +
      2\sum_{j=1}^{J_{K,V}}\delta_jH_j .
   \]
   The choice of \(J_{K,V}\) makes \(2^{-J_{K,V}}K\le V/4\).  Therefore
   \[
      2\sum_{j=1}^{J_{K,V}}\delta_jH_j
      \ge M-\frac V4
      \ge \frac{3V}{4},
   \]
   so some \(j\) satisfies
   \[
      \delta_jH_j>\frac{V}{4J_{K,V}}.
      \tag{ANS3}
   \]
   Form the point-mass reporter record \(R\) with \(\theta_R=\theta\),
   \(W_R=W\), \(\nu_R=\delta_{\delta_j}\), exact lower hit certificate
   \(X^R_{\delta_j}=\delta_jH_j\), and exact size certificate
   \(K^R_{\delta_j}=H_j\).  This satisfies \((ARR0)\).  Since \(H_j\le |W|\le K\),
   the price side in \((ARR1)\) is at most the right side of \((ANS2)\).  By
   \((ANS2)\) and \((ANS3)\), \(\Phi(R)>0\).  The final statement is
   \cref{cor:single-seed-reporter-proposal-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Near-shadow prefix separator]
   \label{cor:annular-near-shadow-prefix-separator}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:annular-near-shadow-mass-reporter}.  Fix a retained certified
   container \(W_0\), and assume that every top-degree subset of \(W_0\) may be
   materialized as a retained subcontainer with the same price factor
   \(\psi_{W_0}\) and exponent \(\rho_{W_0}\).  Order the points of \(W_0\) by
   decreasing near-shadow degree \(d_{Q'}^\theta(p)\), and let
   \(W_K\) be the first \(K\) points.  Put
   \[
      V_K=
      \sum_{p\in W_K}d_{Q'}^\theta(p),
      \qquad
      J_K=1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{2K}{V_K}\right\rceil
      \quad(V_K>0).
   \]
   If, for some \(1\le K\le |W_0|\) with \(V_K>0\),
   \[
      \frac{V_K}{4J_K}
      >
      \frac{b\,\psi_{W_0}}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{\rho_{W_0}}K^{\rho_{W_0}}}{L}
         +
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{1+\rho_{W_0}}K^{1+\rho_{W_0}}}{S}
      \right),
      \tag{NSP1}
   \]
   then the single-seed annular layer yields the scalar reporter required by
   \cref{asm:weighted-annular-scalar-reporter}.

   Conversely, if no retained subcontainer obtained this way yields such a
   reporter through \cref{cor:annular-near-shadow-mass-reporter}, then every
   retained container \(W_0\) and every \(K\) with \(V_K>0\) satisfies the
   reverse inequality
   \[
      \frac{V_K}{4J_K}
      \le
      \frac{b\,\psi_{W_0}}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{\rho_{W_0}}K^{\rho_{W_0}}}{L}
         +
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{1+\rho_{W_0}}K^{1+\rho_{W_0}}}{S}
      \right).
      \tag{NSP2}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((NSP1)\) holds, apply
   \cref{cor:annular-near-shadow-mass-reporter} to the retained subcontainer
   \(W_K\), with \(K\) as its certified size bound and \(V=V_K\).  The
   certified mass condition \((ANS1)\) holds by definition of \(V_K\), and
   \((ANS2)\) is exactly \((NSP1)\).  Hence a positive scalar-reporter record
   exists, and
   \cref{cor:single-seed-reporter-proposal-criterion} supplies the required
   annular-to-scalar reporter.

   The converse is just the contrapositive of the first statement, applied to
   every retained container and every available prefix size.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Query-layer near-shadow hinge envelope]
   \label{lem:query-layer-near-shadow-hinge}
   Work with a guarded normalized residual satisfying \((GNR3)\).  Let
   \(Q'\subseteq\mathcal Q\), \(0\le\theta\le1\), and let
   \(U\in\mathcal U\) be a retained core with certified prices \(T_U,S_U\).
   Define
   \[
      d_{Q'}^\theta(p)
      =
      \sum_{\substack{q\in Q'\\(p,q)\in\mathcal N}}
      \bar\gamma^\theta_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \sum_{p\in U}d_{Q'}^\theta(p)
      \le
      T_U\sum_{q\in Q'}\bar\tau_q+\bar\sigma S_U .
      \tag{QNH1}
   \]
   In particular, if a prefix core \(U\) has price
   \(T_U=\psi K^\rho\), \(S_U=\psi K^{1+\rho}\), then
   \[
      \sum_{p\in U}d_{Q'}^\theta(p)
      \le
      \psi K^\rho\sum_{q\in Q'}\bar\tau_q
      +\bar\sigma\psi K^{1+\rho}.
      \tag{QNH2}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   By definition of the primitive-visible support,
   \[
      a_U^{\bar\gamma^\theta}(q)
      =
      \sum_{\substack{p\in U\\(p,q)\in\mathcal N}}
      \bar\gamma^\theta_{p,q}
      \mathbf 1\{\exists z\in\mathcal Z:\ p\in V_{z,q}\}.
   \]
   Since \(0\le r_{p,q}=\Pr_Z[p\in V_{Z,q}]\le1\), and \(r_{p,q}>0\) implies
   \(\exists z\) with \(p\in V_{z,q}\),
   \[
      \sum_{p\in U}d_{Q'}^\theta(p)
      \le
      \sum_{q\in Q'}a_U^{\bar\gamma^\theta}(q).
   \]
   For each \(q\),
   \[
      a_U^{\bar\gamma^\theta}(q)
      \le
      \bigl(a_U^{\bar\gamma^\theta}(q)-T_U\bar\tau_q\bigr)_+
      +T_U\bar\tau_q .
   \]
   Summing over \(q\in Q'\) and then using \((GNR3)\) gives
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q'}a_U^{\bar\gamma^\theta}(q)
      \le
      \sum_q
      \bigl(a_U^{\bar\gamma^\theta}(q)-T_U\bar\tau_q\bigr)_+
      +T_U\sum_{q\in Q'}\bar\tau_q
      \le
      \bar\sigma S_U+T_U\sum_{q\in Q'}\bar\tau_q .
   \]
   This proves \((QNH1)\), and \((QNH2)\) is the stated price specialization.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Single-seed near-shadow prefix obstruction]
   \label{cor:single-seed-near-shadow-prefix-obstruction}
   Work under the hypotheses of \cref{cor:annular-reporter-local-cover}, assume
   the primitive law has finite support, and suppose the retained container
   family is prefix-closed in the sense of
   \cref{cor:annular-near-shadow-prefix-separator}.  If the enlarged local
   filter-cover LP is infeasible and the tail condition \((DAR1)\) holds, then
   there are a guarded normalized residual
   \((\bar\tau,\bar\sigma,\bar\gamma^\theta,\kappa)\), a seed \(z\), a dyadic
   collision level \(\beta\), a dyadic size level
   \(\Delta\in\mathcal D_{|P|}\), and the query layer
   \[
      Q'=Q_{z,\beta,\Delta}
   \]
   satisfying the annular lower bound
   \[
      \Delta\sum_{q\in Q'}\bar\tau_q
      >
      \frac{(1-\xi)\beta_0C_\eta\pi_1\kappa}{4J K_{|P|}},
      \tag{SPO1}
   \]
   while every \(0\le\theta\le1\), every retained container \(W_0\), and every
   \(K\) with
   \[
      V_K^\theta=
      \sum_{p\in W_K}d_{Q'}^\theta(p)>0
   \]
   obey
   \[
      \frac{V_K^\theta}{4J_K^\theta}
      \le
      \frac{b\,\psi_{W_0}}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{\rho_{W_0}}K^{\rho_{W_0}}}{L}
         +
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{1+\rho_{W_0}}K^{1+\rho_{W_0}}}{S}
      \right),
      \tag{SPO2}
   \]
   and also the query-local hinge envelope
   \[
      V_K^\theta
      \le
      \psi_{W_0}K^{\rho_{W_0}}
      \sum_{q\in Q'}\bar\tau_q
      +
      \bar\sigma\psi_{W_0}K^{1+\rho_{W_0}},
      \tag{SPO3}
   \]
   where \(W_K\) is the top-\(K\) prefix of \(W_0\) by
   \(d_{Q'}^\theta\), and
   \(J_K^\theta=1+\lceil\log_2(2K/V_K^\theta)\rceil\).

   Consequently, to prove local feasibility it is enough to prove the geometric
   statement that no guarded normalized residual can satisfy both the annular
   lower bound \((SPO1)\), the prefix envelope \((SPO2)\), and the
   query-local envelope \((SPO3)\) for all retained containers and all
   \(\theta\in[0,1]\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Infeasibility and \((DAR1)\) give the guarded normalized residual and the
   layer \(Q'=Q_{z,\beta,\Delta}\) satisfying \((SAQ1)\)--\((SAQ2)\) by
   \cref{cor:single-seed-annular-query-layer}; \((SPO1)\) is exactly
   \((SAQ2)\).

   If some \(\theta,W_0,K\) violate \((NSP2)\), then they satisfy the strict
   prefix inequality \((NSP1)\).  By
   \cref{cor:annular-near-shadow-prefix-separator}, this single-seed annular
   layer yields the one-sided scalar reporter required in
   \cref{asm:weighted-annular-scalar-reporter}.  Then
   \cref{cor:single-seed-query-layer-reporter-suffices} gives the local-cover
   conclusion, contradicting the assumed infeasible residual.  Therefore any
   infeasible residual must satisfy the reverse inequality for every
   \(\theta,W_0,K\), which is \((SPO2)\).

   The same prefix \(W_K\) is a retained core by prefix-closure, with certified
   prices
   \(T_{W_K}=\psi_{W_0}K^{\rho_{W_0}}\) and
   \(S_{W_K}=\psi_{W_0}K^{1+\rho_{W_0}}\).  Applying
   \cref{lem:query-layer-near-shadow-hinge} to \(U=W_K\) gives \((SPO3)\).

   The final claim is the contrapositive: if the displayed simultaneous
   obstruction is geometrically impossible, every infeasible residual exposes a
   prefix violation and hence a valid reporter, so
   \cref{cor:annular-reporter-local-cover} rules out local infeasibility.
\end{proof}

Thus the single-seed annular reporter theorem can be attacked through a simpler
range-reporting certificate.  For the layer \(Q_{z,\beta,\Delta}\), it is enough
to output one retained container with a certified lower bound on the true
near-shadow mass \(\sum_{p\in W}d_{Q_{z,\beta,\Delta}}^\theta(p)\) and a
certified size upper bound \(K\) satisfying \((ANS2)\).  The dyadic loss
\(J_{K,V}\) is logarithmic once the certificate has positive margin.  This is a
more concrete target for \(k\)-means++ panels, additive-quantization buckets,
lattice/list decoders, and LP range-reporting routines than directly producing
a scalar level panel.  By \cref{cor:annular-near-shadow-prefix-separator}, the
canonical search problem is a top-\(K\) near-shadow prefix query inside retained
certified containers; if every such prefix obeys \((NSP2)\), that explicit
weak-type envelope is the remaining pseudo-random obstruction.
\Cref{cor:single-seed-near-shadow-prefix-obstruction} packages the exact
counterexample: a query-price-heavy annular layer \((SPO1)\) coexists with the
near-shadow prefix envelope \((SPO2)\) for every retained container and every
point on the residual segment.  The original Pareto-core hinge envelope also
gives the query-local bound \((SPO3)\), so the remaining obstruction is not just
globally diffuse; it is diffuse even relative to the same query-price mass that
makes the annular layer heavy.  This is now the concrete geometric theorem left
for LP range reporting, list recovery, additive quantization, or a
success-normalized bucket-net argument.

\begin{definition}[Annular-to-shadow transport]
   \label{def:annular-shadow-transport}
   Fix a guarded normalized residual, a parameter \(0\le\theta\le1\), a query
   layer \(Q'\subseteq\mathcal Q\), annular witness sets \(B(q)\subseteq P\) for
   \(q\in Q'\), and a retained container \(W\).  A \(C\)-congested
   \(\theta\)-shadow transport of mass \(M\) from the annular witnesses into
   \(W\) consists of numbers
   \[
      \pi_{q,x,p}\ge0
      \qquad(q\in Q',\ x\in B(q),\ p\in W)
   \]
   and shipped amounts \(0\le s_{q,x}\le1\) such that
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{p\in W:\\ (p,q)\in\mathcal N}}\pi_{q,x,p}
      =
      s_{q,x}
      \qquad(q\in Q',\ x\in B(q)),
      \tag{AST1}
   \]
   \[
      M=
      \sum_{q\in Q'}\bar\tau_q
      \sum_{x\in B(q)}s_{q,x},
      \tag{AST2}
   \]
   and, for every \(p\in W\),
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q'}\bar\tau_q
      \sum_{x\in B(q)}\pi_{q,x,p}
      \le
      C\,d_{Q'}^\theta(p),
      \tag{AST3}
   \]
   where
   \[
      d_{Q'}^\theta(p)=
      \sum_{\substack{q\in Q'\\(p,q)\in\mathcal N}}
      \bar\gamma^\theta_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
   \]
   The weighted-unit case has \(s_{q,x}=1\) for every annular incidence with
   \(\bar\tau_q>0\); zero-price incidences carry no mass and may be ignored.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Transport certificate for annular reporters]
   \label{lem:annular-shadow-transport-reporter}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:annular-near-shadow-mass-reporter}.  Suppose the annular witness
   family \(B(q)\) admits a \(C\)-congested \(\theta\)-shadow transport of mass
   \(M>0\) into a retained container \(W\), and suppose \(|W|\le K\).  Put
   \[
      V=\frac{M}{C},
      \qquad
      J_{K,V}=1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{2K}{V}\right\rceil .
   \]
   If
   \[
      \frac{M}{4C J_{K,V}}
      >
      \frac{b\,\psi_W}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{\rho_W}K^{\rho_W}}{L}
         +
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{1+\rho_W}K^{1+\rho_W}}{S}
      \right),
      \tag{AST4}
   \]
   then the single-seed annular layer yields the scalar reporter required by
   \cref{asm:weighted-annular-scalar-reporter}.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Summing \((AST3)\) over \(p\in W\) and using \((AST1)\)--\((AST2)\) gives
   \[
      M
      \le
      C\sum_{p\in W}d_{Q'}^\theta(p).
   \]
   Hence \(V=M/C\) is a certified lower bound on the near-shadow mass in \(W\).
   The assumptions \(|W|\le K\) and \((AST4)\) are exactly \((ANS1)\) and
   \((ANS2)\) of \cref{cor:annular-near-shadow-mass-reporter}, with this value
   of \(V\).  That corollary materializes a positive annular scalar-reporter
   record, which is the reporter demanded by
   \cref{asm:weighted-annular-scalar-reporter}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Transport obstruction for a surviving annular layer]
   \label{cor:annular-shadow-transport-obstruction}
   Work under the hypotheses of
   \cref{cor:single-seed-near-shadow-prefix-obstruction}.  Let
   \(Q'=Q_{z,\beta,\Delta}\) be the single-seed annular query layer, and take
   \(B(q)=B_{z,\beta}(q)\).  If the local filter-cover LP is infeasible, then
   every \(C\)-congested \(\theta\)-shadow transport of mass \(M>0\) into every
   retained container \(W\) with \(|W|\le K\) satisfies the reverse inequality
   \[
      \frac{M}{4C J_{K,M/C}}
      \le
      \frac{b\,\psi_W}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{\rho_W}K^{\rho_W}}{L}
         +
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{1+\rho_W}K^{1+\rho_W}}{S}
      \right).
      \tag{AST5}
   \]
   In particular, any weighted-unit transport into \(W\) obeys
   \[
      \frac{
         \sum_{q\in Q'}\bar\tau_q |B_{z,\beta}(q)|
      }{
         4C J_{K,M/C}
      }
      \le
      \frac{b\,\psi_W}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{\rho_W}K^{\rho_W}}{L}
         +
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{1+\rho_W}K^{1+\rho_W}}{S}
      \right),
      \tag{AST6}
   \]
   with \(M=\sum_{q\in Q'}\bar\tau_q |B_{z,\beta}(q)|\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((AST5)\) failed for some transport, then
   \cref{lem:annular-shadow-transport-reporter} would produce the scalar
   reporter required by \cref{asm:weighted-annular-scalar-reporter} for this
   guarded residual and this single-seed layer.  As in the proof of
   \cref{cor:annular-reporter-local-cover}, that reporter materializes a
   positive reduced-gain retained prefix/core and contradicts the hinge
   envelope \((GNR3)\) of the surviving residual.  Hence no such transport can
   exist under local infeasibility.  The weighted-unit statement is the
   specialization \(s_{q,x}=1\), for which the mass identity \((AST2)\) gives
   the displayed value of \(M\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Query-local congestion lower bound]
   \label{cor:annular-shadow-congestion-lower-bound}
   Work with a guarded normalized residual satisfying \((GNR3)\).  Let
   \(Q'\subseteq\mathcal Q\), let \(W\) be a retained core with prices
   \(T_W,S_W\), and suppose a \(C\)-congested \(\theta\)-shadow transport of
   mass \(M\) enters \(W\).  Then
   \[
      M
      \le
      C\left(
         T_W\sum_{q\in Q'}\bar\tau_q+\bar\sigma S_W
      \right).
      \tag{AST7}
   \]
   Therefore, for the single-seed layer with \(|B_{z,\beta}(q)|\ge\Delta\) on
   \(Q'\), any weighted-unit transport into a \(K\)-point prefix core of price
   \(T_W=\psi K^\rho\), \(S_W=\psi K^{1+\rho}\) must have
   \[
      C
      \ge
      \frac{\Delta\sum_{q\in Q'}\bar\tau_q}
      {\psi K^\rho\sum_{q\in Q'}\bar\tau_q
       +\bar\sigma\psi K^{1+\rho}} .
      \tag{AST8}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Summing the congestion bound \((AST3)\) gives
   \(M\le C\sum_{p\in W}d_{Q'}^\theta(p)\).  Applying
   \cref{lem:query-layer-near-shadow-hinge} to \(W\) gives \((AST7)\).  In the
   unit single-seed case,
   \[
      M=\sum_{q\in Q'}\bar\tau_q|B_{z,\beta}(q)|
      \ge
      \Delta\sum_{q\in Q'}\bar\tau_q,
   \]
   and substituting the prefix prices into \((AST7)\) gives \((AST8)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Annular-shadow cut normal form]
   \label{lem:annular-shadow-cut-normal-form}
   Work in the setting of \cref{def:annular-shadow-transport}.  Put
   \[
      b_q=\bar\tau_q|B(q)|,
      \qquad
      B_{\rm tot}=\sum_{q\in Q'}b_q,
   \]
   and, for \(Y\subseteq Q'\),
   \[
      N_W(Y)=\{p\in W:\exists q\in Y,\ (p,q)\in\mathcal N\},
      \qquad
      D_W^\theta(Y)=\sum_{p\in N_W(Y)}d_{Q'}^\theta(p).
   \]
   Let \(\Phi_C^\theta(W)\) be the largest mass \(M\) for which a
   \(C\)-congested \(\theta\)-shadow transport into \(W\) exists.  Then
   \[
      \Phi_C^\theta(W)
      =
      \min_{Y\subseteq Q'}
      \left\{
         \sum_{q\in Q'\setminus Y}b_q
         +C D_W^\theta(Y)
      \right\}
      =
      B_{\rm tot}
      -
      \max_{Y\subseteq Q'}
      \left\{
         \sum_{q\in Y}b_q-CD_W^\theta(Y)
      \right\}.
      \tag{ASC1}
   \]
   Consequently, for \(0\le M_0\le B_{\rm tot}\), a transport of mass at least
   \(M_0\) exists if and only if every \(Y\subseteq Q'\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Y}b_q
      \le
      C D_W^\theta(Y)+B_{\rm tot}-M_0 .
      \tag{ASC2}
   \]
   In particular, a weighted-unit transport of all positive-price annular
   incidences exists if and only if
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Y}b_q\le C D_W^\theta(Y)
      \qquad(Y\subseteq Q').
      \tag{ASC3}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Aggregate the transport variables by query and point.  A transport of mass
   \(M\) is equivalent to nonnegative variables \(f_{q,p}\), supported on
   \(p\in W\) with \((p,q)\in\mathcal N\), such that
   \[
      \sum_{p\in N_W(\{q\})}f_{q,p}\le b_q,
      \qquad
      \sum_{\substack{q\in Q':\\(p,q)\in\mathcal N}}f_{q,p}
      \le C d_{Q'}^\theta(p),
      \qquad
      \sum_{q,p}f_{q,p}=M .
   \]
   The equivalence follows by setting
   \(f_{q,p}=\bar\tau_q\sum_{x\in B(q)}\pi_{q,x,p}\).  Conversely, because
   \(\sum_pf_{q,p}\le\bar\tau_q|B(q)|\), the normalized amount
   \(\bar\tau_q^{-1}f_{q,p}\) can be distributed fractionally among the
   \(|B(q)|\) incidences when \(\bar\tau_q>0\); queries with
   \(\bar\tau_q=0\) carry no mass.

   Thus \(\Phi_C^\theta(W)\) is the optimum of the finite fractional flow LP
   that maximizes \(\sum_{q,p}f_{q,p}\) subject to the two displayed capacity
   constraints.  Its dual is
   \[
      \min
      \left\{
         \sum_qb_qu_q+C\sum_{p\in W}d_{Q'}^\theta(p)v_p:
         u_q+v_p\ge1\ \text{whenever }(p,q)\in\mathcal N,\quad
         u_q,v_p\ge0
      \right\}.
      \tag{ASC4}
   \]
   Strong duality holds because the finite primal is feasible and bounded.

   For any \(Y\subseteq Q'\), the Boolean dual
   \[
      u_q=\mathbf 1\{q\notin Y\},
      \qquad
      v_p=\mathbf 1\{p\in N_W(Y)\}
   \]
   is feasible and has value
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q'\setminus Y}b_q+CD_W^\theta(Y).
   \]
   Therefore the dual optimum is at most the right side of \((ASC1)\).

   Conversely, take any feasible dual \((u,v)\) and truncate it to
   \(0\le u_q,v_p\le1\), which cannot increase the objective or destroy the
   constraints.  For \(t\in(0,1]\), let
   \[
      Y_t=\{q:u_q<t\},
      \qquad
      P_t=\{p:v_p\ge1-t\}.
   \]
   If \(q\in Y_t\) and \((p,q)\in\mathcal N\), then
   \(v_p\ge1-u_q>1-t\), so \(N_W(Y_t)\subseteq P_t\).  Hence
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \sum_qb_qu_q+C\sum_pd_{Q'}^\theta(p)v_p
      &=
      \int_0^1
      \left(
         \sum_{q:u_q\ge t}b_q
         +C\sum_{p:v_p\ge1-t}d_{Q'}^\theta(p)
      \right)dt\\
      &\ge
      \int_0^1
      \left(
         \sum_{q\in Q'\setminus Y_t}b_q
         +C D_W^\theta(Y_t)
      \right)dt\\
      &\ge
      \min_{Y\subseteq Q'}
      \left\{
         \sum_{q\in Q'\setminus Y}b_q
         +C D_W^\theta(Y)
      \right\}.
   \end{aligned}
   \]
   This proves the cut formula \((ASC1)\).  Rewriting
   \(\Phi_C^\theta(W)\ge M_0\) using the second form of \((ASC1)\) gives
   \((ASC2)\), and \(M_0=B_{\rm tot}\) gives \((ASC3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cut-certified annular reporter]
   \label{cor:cut-certified-annular-reporter}
   Work under the hypotheses of
   \cref{cor:single-seed-near-shadow-prefix-obstruction}.  Let
   \(Q'=Q_{z,\beta,\Delta}\), \(B(q)=B_{z,\beta}(q)\), and define
   \(b_q,B_{\rm tot},D_W^\theta\) as in
   \cref{lem:annular-shadow-cut-normal-form}.  Suppose there are a retained
   container \(W\), a size certificate \(|W|\le K\), a congestion parameter
   \(C>0\), a segment point \(0\le\theta\le1\), and a target mass
   \(0<M_0\le B_{\rm tot}\) such that every query sublayer \(Y\subseteq Q'\)
   satisfies the cut inequalities
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Y}b_q
      \le
      C D_W^\theta(Y)+B_{\rm tot}-M_0,
      \tag{CCR1}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \frac{M_0}{4C J_{K,M_0/C}}
      >
      \frac{b\,\psi_W}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{\rho_W}K^{\rho_W}}{L}
         +
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{1+\rho_W}K^{1+\rho_W}}{S}
      \right).
      \tag{CCR2}
   \]
   Then this single-seed annular layer yields the scalar reporter required by
   \cref{asm:weighted-annular-scalar-reporter}.

   Conversely, if the local filter-cover LP is infeasible, then for every
   choice of \(W,K,C,\theta,M_0\) satisfying \((CCR2)\) there is a query
   sublayer \(Y\subseteq Q'\) with
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Y}b_q
      >
      C D_W^\theta(Y)+B_{\rm tot}-M_0 .
      \tag{CCR3}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \cref{lem:annular-shadow-cut-normal-form}, the cut inequalities
   \((CCR1)\) are equivalent to the existence of a
   \(C\)-congested \(\theta\)-shadow transport of mass at least \(M_0\) into
   \(W\).  With \((CCR2)\), \cref{lem:annular-shadow-transport-reporter}
   produces the required scalar reporter.

   For the converse, if no violating sublayer existed, then \((CCR1)\) would
   hold and the first part would produce the reporter.  As in
   \cref{cor:annular-shadow-transport-obstruction}, that reporter contradicts
   the surviving residual's hinge envelope under local infeasibility.  Hence
   some cut violation \((CCR3)\) must exist.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Half-mass excess-cut obstruction]
   \label{cor:half-mass-excess-cut-obstruction}
   Work under the hypotheses of
   \cref{cor:single-seed-near-shadow-prefix-obstruction}, and keep the notation
   \(Q'\), \(B(q)\), \(b_q\), \(B_{\rm tot}\), and \(D_W^\theta\) from
   \cref{cor:cut-certified-annular-reporter}.  Fix a retained container \(W\),
   a size certificate \(|W|\le K\), a congestion parameter \(C>0\), and
   \(0\le\theta\le1\).  Assume \(B_{\rm tot}>0\), and suppose
   \[
      \frac{B_{\rm tot}}
      {8C\,J_{K,B_{\rm tot}/(2C)}}
      >
      \frac{b\,\psi_W}{\pi_1}
      \left(
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{\rho_W}K^{\rho_W}}{L}
         +
         \frac{(\chi\beta b_0)^{1+\rho_W}K^{1+\rho_W}}{S}
      \right).
      \tag{HMC1}
   \]
   If the local filter-cover LP is infeasible, then there is a query sublayer
   \(Y\subseteq Q'\) satisfying
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Y}b_q-C D_W^\theta(Y)>\frac{B_{\rm tot}}2 .
      \tag{HMC2}
   \]
   In particular,
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Y}b_q>\frac{B_{\rm tot}}2,
      \qquad
      D_W^\theta(Y)
      <
      \frac1C
      \left(\sum_{q\in Y}b_q-\frac{B_{\rm tot}}2\right)
      \le \frac1C\sum_{q\in Y}b_q .
      \tag{HMC3}
   \]
   Conversely, if for some \(W,K,C,\theta\) satisfying \((HMC1)\) every query
   sublayer obeys
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Y}b_q-C D_W^\theta(Y)\le\frac{B_{\rm tot}}2,
      \tag{HMC4}
   \]
   then the single-seed annular layer yields the scalar reporter required by
   \cref{asm:weighted-annular-scalar-reporter}.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \cref{cor:cut-certified-annular-reporter} with
   \(M_0=B_{\rm tot}/2\).  The affordability condition \((CCR2)\) becomes
   exactly \((HMC1)\), and the cut violation \((CCR3)\) becomes \((HMC2)\).
   The two inequalities in \((HMC3)\) are immediate from \((HMC2)\) and
   nonnegativity of \(D_W^\theta(Y)\).

   For the converse, \((HMC4)\) is exactly the cut condition \((CCR1)\) with
   \(M_0=B_{\rm tot}/2\).  Together with \((HMC1)\), the first part of
   \cref{cor:cut-certified-annular-reporter} gives the reporter.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Cut-recycled annular sublayer]
   \label{lem:cut-recycled-annular-sublayer}
   Work under the hypotheses of
   \cref{cor:half-mass-excess-cut-obstruction}, and suppose a query sublayer
   \(Y\subseteq Q'\) satisfies the excess-cut conclusion \((HMC2)\).  Let
   \(m=|P|\), write \(Q'=Q_{z,\beta,\Delta}\), and put
   \[
      \mathcal D_m=\{2^\ell:0\le\ell\le\lceil\log_2m\rceil\},
      \qquad
      \mathcal D_m(\Delta)
      =
      \{\Delta'\in\mathcal D_m:\Delta\le\Delta'\le m\},
      \qquad
      H_m(\Delta)=|\mathcal D_m(\Delta)|.
   \]
   If \(B_Y=\sum_{q\in Y}b_q\), then there are a dyadic level
   \(\Delta'\in\mathcal D_m(\Delta)\) and a cut-restricted annular layer
   \[
      Y'=\{q\in Y: |B(q)|\ge\Delta'\}
      \tag{CRA1}
   \]
   such that
   \[
      \Delta'\sum_{q\in Y'}\bar\tau_q
      \ge
      \frac{B_Y}{2H_m(\Delta)}
      >
      \frac{B_{\rm tot}}{4H_m(\Delta)} .
      \tag{CRA2}
   \]
   Define the near-shadow capacity restricted to \(Y'\) by
   \[
      D_{W,Y'}^\theta(Y')
      =
      \sum_{p\in N_W(Y')}
      \sum_{\substack{q\in Y'\\(p,q)\in\mathcal N}}
      \bar\gamma^\theta_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
   \]
   Then
   \[
      D_{W,Y'}^\theta(Y')
      \le
      D_W^\theta(Y)
      <
      \frac{B_Y-B_{\rm tot}/2}{C}
      \le
      \frac{B_Y}{C}
      \le
      \frac{2H_m(\Delta)}{C}\,
      \Delta'\sum_{q\in Y'}\bar\tau_q .
      \tag{CRA3}
   \]
   In particular, if \(Y\) comes from an infeasible local cover through
   \cref{cor:single-seed-near-shadow-prefix-obstruction}, then
   \[
      \Delta'\sum_{q\in Y'}\bar\tau_q
      >
      \frac{(1-\xi)\beta_0C_\eta\pi_1\kappa}
      {16J K_{|P|}H_m(\Delta)} .
      \tag{CRA4}
   \]
   Here \(K_{|P|}=1+\lceil\log_2|P|\rceil\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   For \(q\in Y\subseteq Q_{z,\beta,\Delta}\), the integer
   \(h_q=|B(q)|\) is at least \(\Delta\).  Since \(\Delta\) and the levels in
   \(\mathcal D_m\) are dyadic,
   \[
      h_q
      \le
      2\sum_{\Delta'\in\mathcal D_m(\Delta)}
      \Delta'\mathbf 1\{h_q\ge\Delta'\}.
   \]
   Multiplying by \(\bar\tau_q\), summing over \(Y\), and using
   \(b_q=\bar\tau_qh_q\) gives
   \[
      B_Y
      \le
      2\sum_{\Delta'\in\mathcal D_m(\Delta)}
      \Delta'\sum_{\substack{q\in Y:\\ |B(q)|\ge\Delta'}}\bar\tau_q .
   \]
   Averaging over the \(H_m(\Delta)\) levels gives a level \(\Delta'\) satisfying
   the first inequality in \((CRA2)\).  The second inequality is \((HMC2)\), since
   \(D_W^\theta(Y)\ge0\).

   The capacity comparison follows from monotonicity: \(Y'\subseteq Y\), so
   \(N_W(Y')\subseteq N_W(Y)\), and the degree restricted to \(Y'\) is bounded by
   the degree restricted to \(Q'\).  Therefore
   \(D_{W,Y'}^\theta(Y')\le D_W^\theta(Y)\).  The strict middle inequality is
   \((HMC2)\), and the final inequality is the rearranged lower bound in
   \((CRA2)\).

   Finally, \((SPO1)\) gives
   \(B_{\rm tot}\ge\Delta\sum_{q\in Q'}\bar\tau_q
   >(1-\xi)\beta_0C_\eta\pi_1\kappa/(4JK_{|P|})\).  Combining this with
   \((CRA2)\) gives \((CRA4)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Recycled-sublayer separator suffices]
   \label{cor:recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices}
   Work under the hypotheses of \cref{cor:annular-reporter-local-cover}, assume
   the primitive law has finite support, and assume the retained container family
   is prefix-closed as in
   \cref{cor:single-seed-near-shadow-prefix-obstruction}.  Suppose the following
   separator property holds for every guarded normalized residual and every
   single-seed annular query layer \(Q'=Q_{z,\beta,\Delta}\) satisfying
   \((SAQ1)\)--\((SAQ2)\).  There are a retained container \(W\), a size
   certificate \(|W|\le K\), a congestion parameter \(C>0\), and
   \(0\le\theta\le1\) satisfying the affordability inequality \((HMC1)\), such
   that, with
   \[
      m=|P|,
      \qquad
      \mathcal D_m=\{2^\ell:0\le\ell\le\lceil\log_2m\rceil\},
      \qquad
      H_m(\Delta)
      =
      |\{\Delta'\in\mathcal D_m:\Delta\le\Delta'\le m\}|,
   \]
   every dyadic level \(\Delta'\in\mathcal D_m\) with \(\Delta'\ge\Delta\) and
   every cut-restricted layer
   \[
      Y'\subseteq\{q\in Q': |B_{z,\beta}(q)|\ge\Delta'\}
   \]
   with
   \[
      \Delta'\sum_{q\in Y'}\bar\tau_q
      >
      \frac{(1-\xi)\beta_0C_\eta\pi_1\kappa}
      {16J K_{|P|}H_m(\Delta)}
      \tag{RSS1}
   \]
   satisfies the near-shadow lower bound
   \[
      D_{W,Y'}^\theta(Y')
      >
      \frac{2H_m(\Delta)}{C}\,
      \Delta'\sum_{q\in Y'}\bar\tau_q .
      \tag{RSS2}
   \]
   where \(D_{W,Y'}^\theta(Y')\) is the restricted near-shadow capacity from
   \cref{lem:cut-recycled-annular-sublayer}.
   Then the enlarged local filter-cover LP is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Suppose the enlarged local LP were infeasible.  By
   \cref{cor:single-seed-near-shadow-prefix-obstruction}, there is a guarded
   normalized residual and a single-seed annular query layer
   \(Q'=Q_{z,\beta,\Delta}\) satisfying \((SAQ1)\)--\((SAQ2)\) and \((SPO1)\).
   Apply the assumed separator property to this layer and obtain
   \(W,K,C,\theta\) satisfying \((HMC1)\).

   Since the local LP is infeasible, \cref{cor:half-mass-excess-cut-obstruction}
   gives a half-mass excess cut \(Y\subseteq Q'\).  Applying
   \cref{lem:cut-recycled-annular-sublayer} to this cut produces a dyadic
   \(\Delta'\) and a cut-restricted layer \(Y'\).  The load lower bound
   \((CRA4)\) is exactly \((RSS1)\), while \((CRA3)\) gives the opposite of
   \((RSS2)\).  This contradiction rules out local infeasibility.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Lagrange screen for recycled sublayers]
   \label{lem:lagrange-recycled-sublayer-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices}, and fix
   \(W,C,\theta,\Delta'\).  Put
   \[
      Q_{\Delta'}=\{q\in Q': |B_{z,\beta}(q)|\ge\Delta'\},
      \qquad
      \ell_q=\Delta'\bar\tau_q ,
   \]
   \[
      s_q=s_{W,\theta}(q)
      =
      \sum_{\substack{p\in W\\(p,q)\in\mathcal N}}
      \bar\gamma^\theta_{p,q}r_{p,q},
      \qquad
      A=\frac{2H_m(\Delta)}{C},
   \]
   and let \(\Lambda>0\).  If there is a number \(\lambda>0\) such that
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}}
      \bigl((A+\lambda)\ell_q-s_q\bigr)_+
      \le
      \lambda\Lambda ,
      \tag{LRS1}
   \]
   then every subset \(Y'\subseteq Q_{\Delta'}\) with
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Y'}\ell_q>\Lambda
      \tag{LRS2}
   \]
   satisfies
   \[
      D_{W,Y'}^\theta(Y')
      >
      A\sum_{q\in Y'}\ell_q .
      \tag{LRS3}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   For \(Y'\subseteq Q_{\Delta'}\), the restricted near-shadow capacity is
   additive in the selected queries:
   \[
      D_{W,Y'}^\theta(Y')
      =
      \sum_{q\in Y'}s_q .
   \]
   If \((LRS3)\) failed for some \(Y'\) satisfying \((LRS2)\), then
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}}
      \bigl((A+\lambda)\ell_q-s_q\bigr)_+
      &\ge
      \sum_{q\in Y'}\bigl((A+\lambda)\ell_q-s_q\bigr)\\
      &=
      A\sum_{q\in Y'}\ell_q-D_{W,Y'}^\theta(Y')
      +\lambda\sum_{q\in Y'}\ell_q\\
      &\ge
      \lambda\sum_{q\in Y'}\ell_q\\
      &>
      \lambda\Lambda ,
   \end{aligned}
   \]
   contradicting \((LRS1)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Fractional recycled-layer dual normal form]
   \label{lem:fractional-recycled-layer-dual-normal-form}
   Work in the notation of \cref{lem:lagrange-recycled-sublayer-screen}.
   With the convention that the maximum over an empty feasible set is
   \(-\infty\), define the fractional bad-layer value
   \[
      \Phi_{\Delta'}(W,\theta)
      =
      \max
      \left\{
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}} y_q(A\ell_q-s_q):
      0\le y_q\le1,\quad
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}}y_q\ell_q\ge\Lambda
      \right\}.
      \tag{FRD1}
   \]
   Then, in the same extended-real convention,
   \[
      \Phi_{\Delta'}(W,\theta)
      =
      \inf_{\lambda\ge0}
      \left\{
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}}
      \bigl((A+\lambda)\ell_q-s_q\bigr)_+
      -
      \lambda\Lambda
      \right\}.
      \tag{FRD2}
   \]
   Moreover, for every \(\lambda>0\) and every vector
   \(0\le y_q\le1\),
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}}y_q(A\ell_q-s_q)
      \le
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}}
      \bigl((A+\lambda)\ell_q-s_q\bigr)_+
      -
      \lambda\Lambda
      -
      \lambda
      \left(
         \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}}y_q\ell_q-\Lambda
      \right).
      \tag{FRD3}
   \]
   Consequently, if the dual expression in \((FRD2)\) is at most \(0\) for
   some positive \(\lambda\), then every fractional sublayer \(y\) with
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}}y_q\ell_q>\Lambda
   \]
   satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}}y_qs_q
      >
      A\sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}}y_q\ell_q .
      \tag{FRD4}
   \]
   In particular every integral sublayer \(Y'\subseteq Q_{\Delta'}\) with
   load above \(\Lambda\) satisfies \((LRS3)\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   The inequality \((FRD3)\) is the pointwise Lagrange upper bound.  Indeed,
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      &\sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}}y_q(A\ell_q-s_q)
      +
      \lambda
      \left(
         \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}}y_q\ell_q-\Lambda
      \right)\\
      &\qquad =
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}}
      y_q\bigl((A+\lambda)\ell_q-s_q\bigr)
      -
      \lambda\Lambda\\
      &\qquad \le
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}}
      \bigl((A+\lambda)\ell_q-s_q\bigr)_+
      -
      \lambda\Lambda .
   \end{aligned}
   \]
   Rearranging gives \((FRD3)\).  If the displayed dual expression is at most
   zero and \(\sum_qy_q\ell_q>\Lambda\), then \((FRD3)\) gives
   \[
      \sum_qy_q(A\ell_q-s_q)<0,
   \]
   which is \((FRD4)\).  Taking \(y_q=\mathbf 1_{\{q\in Y'\}}\) gives the
   asserted integral consequence.

   It remains only to identify the exact fractional value.  If
   \(\sum_q\ell_q<\Lambda\), the feasible set in \((FRD1)\) is empty, while
   the right-hand side of \((FRD2)\) tends to \(-\infty\) as
   \(\lambda\to\infty\).  Otherwise \((FRD1)\) is the finite linear program
   \[
      \max\ c^\top y
      \quad\text{subject to}\quad
      -\ell^\top y\le-\Lambda,\quad
      y\le\mathbf 1,\quad
      -y\le0,
   \]
   where \(c_q=A\ell_q-s_q\).  Its dual is
   \[
      \min_{\lambda,u,v\ge0}
      -\lambda\Lambda+\sum_qu_q
      \quad\text{subject to}\quad
      -\lambda\ell_q+u_q-v_q\ge c_q\quad(q\in Q_{\Delta'}).
   \]
   For fixed \(\lambda\), minimizing over \(u_q,v_q\) gives
   \(u_q=(c_q+\lambda\ell_q)_+\).  Thus the dual objective is exactly the
   right-hand side of \((FRD2)\), and finite-dimensional LP duality proves
   equality.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Threshold form of recycled bad layers]
   \label{lem:threshold-recycled-bad-layers}
   Work in the notation of
   \cref{lem:fractional-recycled-layer-dual-normal-form}, and put
   \[
      Q^+=\{q\in Q_{\Delta'}:\ell_q>0\},
      \qquad
      \sigma_q=\frac{s_q}{\ell_q}\quad(q\in Q^+).
   \]
   For \(t>A\), define the low-efficiency prefix statistics
   \[
      L(t)=\sum_{\substack{q\in Q^+\\ \sigma_q\le t}}\ell_q,
      \qquad
      S(t)=\sum_{\substack{q\in Q^+\\ \sigma_q\le t}}s_q,
   \]
   and
   \[
      G(t)=tL(t)-S(t)-(t-A)\Lambda .
      \tag{TRB1}
   \]
   Then the Lagrange screen with multiplier \(\lambda=t-A\) is equivalent
   to
   \[
      G(t)\le0 .
      \tag{TRB2}
   \]
   Moreover, if the fractional bad-layer problem \((FRD1)\) is feasible, it
   has an optimizer \(y\) of the following threshold form.  There is a level
   \(t_*\ge A\) such that
   \[
      y_q=1\quad(\sigma_q<t_*),
      \qquad
      y_q=0\quad(\sigma_q>t_*),
      \tag{TRB3}
   \]
   with arbitrary coefficients \(0\le y_q\le1\) only on the boundary
   \(\sigma_q=t_*\).  Queries with \(\ell_q=0\) may be assigned \(y_q=0\).
   Consequently, if a fractional sublayer of load \(>\Lambda\) and capacity at
   most \(A\) times its load exists, then such a threshold sublayer exists with
   load at least \(\Lambda\) and capacity at most \(A\) times its load.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   For \(t=A+\lambda\), the positive part in \((LRS1)\) is nonzero exactly
   when \(\sigma_q\le t\), up to zero-valued boundary terms.  Hence
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}}
      \bigl((A+\lambda)\ell_q-s_q\bigr)_+
      =
      tL(t)-S(t),
   \]
   and \((LRS1)\) is precisely \((TRB2)\).

   It remains to record the standard fractional-knapsack structure of
   \((FRD1)\).  Terms with \(\ell_q=0\) have coefficient \(-s_q\le0\) and do
   not help meet the load constraint, so an optimizer may set them to zero.
   Since
   \[
      A\ell_q-s_q=(A-\sigma_q)\ell_q\qquad(q\in Q^+),
   \]
   every query with \(\sigma_q<A\) has positive profit per unit load and may be
   included fully in an optimizer.  Queries with \(\sigma_q=A\) have zero
   profit per unit load and can be used only to meet the load constraint.
   After those levels are fixed, the remaining task, if any load is still
   needed, is to minimize \(\sum_qy_q(\sigma_q-A)\ell_q\) over
   \(\sigma_q>A\) subject to a lower load constraint.  The fractional
   knapsack exchange argument sorts by increasing \(\sigma_q\): if
   \(\sigma_i<\sigma_j\), \(y_i<1\), and \(y_j>0\), moving an equal amount of
   load from \(j\) to \(i\) does not reduce feasibility and strictly improves
   the objective.  Thus an optimizer has the threshold form \((TRB3)\), with
   at most one boundary level partially used.

   If a fractional sublayer has load \(>\Lambda\) and
   \(\sum_qy_qs_q\le A\sum_qy_q\ell_q\), then its objective in \((FRD1)\) is
   nonnegative.  Replacing it by an optimizer preserves nonnegative objective
   and feasibility, and the optimizer has the threshold form just proved.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Finite prefix screen for recycled thresholds]
   \label{lem:finite-prefix-recycled-threshold-screen}
   Work in the notation of \cref{lem:threshold-recycled-bad-layers}.  Let
   \(a_1<\cdots<a_k\) be the distinct values of \(\sigma_q\) that are larger
   than \(A\).  Put \(a_0=A\), and define
   \[
      L_i=\sum_{\substack{q\in Q^+\\ \sigma_q\le a_i}}\ell_q,
      \qquad
      S_i=\sum_{\substack{q\in Q^+\\ \sigma_q\le a_i}}s_q
      \qquad(0\le i\le k),
   \]
   with \(L_\infty=\sum_{q\in Q^+}\ell_q\).  The threshold screen
   \[
      \exists t>A:
      \qquad
      tL(t)-S(t)\le(t-A)\Lambda
      \tag{FPS1}
   \]
   holds if and only if at least one of the following finite alternatives
