   holds:
   \[
      A L_0-S_0=0
      \quad\text{and}\quad
      L_0\le\Lambda ,
      \tag{FPS2}
   \]
   \[
      \exists i\in\{1,\ldots,k\}:
      \qquad
      a_iL_i-S_i\le(a_i-A)\Lambda ,
      \tag{FPS3}
   \]
   or
   \[
      L_\infty<\Lambda .
      \tag{FPS4}
   \]
   Thus a threshold certificate can be searched by sorting the finitely many
   efficiencies \(\sigma_q\) and scanning prefix sums.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Let
   \[
      G(t)=tL(t)-S(t)-(t-A)\Lambda .
   \]
   The function \(G\) is continuous and affine on each interval
   \((a_i,a_{i+1})\), with slope \(L_i-\Lambda\).  It is continuous at each
   breakpoint because the newly added queries have \(s_q=a_i\ell_q\).  On the
   last interval \((a_k,\infty)\) its slope is \(L_\infty-\Lambda\).

   The three displayed alternatives are sufficient.  If \((FPS2)\) holds, then
   either \(G(t)=0\) for all sufficiently small \(t>A\) or \(G(t)<0\) for all
   sufficiently small \(t>A\).  If \((FPS3)\) holds, choose \(t=a_i\).  If
   \((FPS4)\) holds, then \(G(t)\to-\infty\) as \(t\to\infty\).

   Conversely suppose \(G(t)\le0\) for some \(t>A\).  If \(t=a_i\) for a
   breakpoint \(i\ge1\), then \((FPS3)\) holds.  If \(t\in(a_i,a_{i+1})\),
   then \(G\) is affine on that interval.  When its slope is nonnegative,
   moving left cannot increase \(G\); if \(i\ge1\) this gives \((FPS3)\).  If
   \(i=0\), then \(G(A)=A L_0-S_0\le0\).  Since every included query has
   \(\sigma_q\le A\), also \(G(A)\ge0\).  Thus \(G(A)=0\), and the fact that
   \(G(t)\le0\) with nonnegative slope forces \(L_0-\Lambda=0\), giving
   \((FPS2)\).  When the slope is negative, moving right cannot increase
   \(G\); if \(i<k\) this gives \((FPS3)\), while if \(i=k\) it gives
   \(L_\infty<\Lambda\).

   It remains to handle \(t>a_k\), including the case \(k=0\).  On
   \((a_k,\infty)\), if the slope \(L_\infty-\Lambda\) is negative then
   \((FPS4)\) holds.  If the slope is nonnegative and \(k\ge1\), moving left to
   \(a_k\) gives \((FPS3)\).  If the slope is nonnegative and \(k=0\), the
   same argument at \(A\) gives \(G(A)=0\), and nonnegative slope plus
   \(G(t)\le0\) again forces \(L_0=\Lambda\), hence \((FPS2)\).  These cases
   exhaust all \(t>A\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Lagrange recycled-sublayer separator suffices]
   \label{cor:lagrange-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices}
   Work under the hypotheses of \cref{cor:annular-reporter-local-cover}, assume
   finite primitive support and prefix-closed retained containers as in
   \cref{cor:recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices}.  Suppose the following
   positive-part screen holds for every guarded normalized residual and every
   single-seed annular query layer \(Q'=Q_{z,\beta,\Delta}\) satisfying
   \((SAQ1)\)--\((SAQ2)\).  There are a retained container \(W\), a size
   certificate \(|W|\le K\), a congestion parameter \(C>0\), and
   \(0\le\theta\le1\) satisfying \((HMC1)\).  Put
   \[
      m=|P|,
      \qquad
      \mathcal D_m=\{2^\ell:0\le\ell\le\lceil\log_2m\rceil\},
      \qquad
      H_m(\Delta)=|\{\Delta''\in\mathcal D_m:\Delta\le\Delta''\le m\}|.
   \]
   Suppose that for every dyadic \(\Delta'\in\mathcal D_m\) with
   \(\Delta'\ge\Delta\) there is \(\lambda_{\Delta'}>0\) with
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}}
      \left(
         \left(\frac{2H_m(\Delta)}{C}+\lambda_{\Delta'}\right)
         \Delta'\bar\tau_q
         -
         s_{W,\theta}(q)
      \right)_+
      \le
      \lambda_{\Delta'}\,
      \frac{(1-\xi)\beta_0C_\eta\pi_1\kappa}
      {16J K_{|P|}H_m(\Delta)} .
      \tag{LRS4}
   \]
   Here \(Q_{\Delta'}=\{q\in Q':|B_{z,\beta}(q)|\ge\Delta'\}\),
   and \(s_{W,\theta}(q)\) is the query-wise near-shadow mass from
   \cref{lem:lagrange-recycled-sublayer-screen}.  Then the enlarged local
   filter-cover LP is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \cref{lem:lagrange-recycled-sublayer-screen} at each dyadic
   \(\Delta'\), with
   \[
      \Lambda=
      \frac{(1-\xi)\beta_0C_\eta\pi_1\kappa}
      {16J K_{|P|}H_m(\Delta)} .
   \]
   The screen \((LRS4)\) gives exactly \((RSS2)\) for every layer satisfying
   \((RSS1)\).  Thus the separator property of
   \cref{cor:recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices} holds, and that corollary
   proves local filter-cover feasibility.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Threshold recycled-sublayer separator suffices]
   \label{cor:threshold-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices}
   Work under the hypotheses of \cref{cor:annular-reporter-local-cover}, assume
   finite primitive support and prefix-closed retained containers as in
   \cref{cor:recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices}.  Suppose the following
   threshold screen holds for every guarded normalized residual and every
   single-seed annular query layer \(Q'=Q_{z,\beta,\Delta}\) satisfying
   \((SAQ1)\)--\((SAQ2)\).  There are a retained container \(W\), a size
   certificate \(|W|\le K\), a congestion parameter \(C>0\), and
   \(0\le\theta\le1\) satisfying \((HMC1)\).  Put
   \[
      m=|P|,
      \qquad
      \mathcal D_m=\{2^\ell:0\le\ell\le\lceil\log_2m\rceil\},
      \qquad
      H_m(\Delta)=|\{\Delta''\in\mathcal D_m:\Delta\le\Delta''\le m\}|,
   \]
   and
   \[
      A=\frac{2H_m(\Delta)}{C},
      \qquad
      \Lambda=
      \frac{(1-\xi)\beta_0C_\eta\pi_1\kappa}
      {16J K_{|P|}H_m(\Delta)} .
   \]
   For each dyadic \(\Delta'\in\mathcal D_m\) with \(\Delta'\ge\Delta\), define
   \[
      Q_{\Delta'}=\{q\in Q':|B_{z,\beta}(q)|\ge\Delta'\},
      \qquad
      \ell_q=\Delta'\bar\tau_q,
      \qquad
      s_q=s_{W,\theta}(q),
   \]
   and, for \(t>A\),
   \[
      L_{\Delta'}(t)
      =
      \sum_{\substack{q\in Q_{\Delta'}\\ \ell_q>0\\ s_q/\ell_q\le t}}
      \ell_q,
      \qquad
      S_{\Delta'}(t)
      =
      \sum_{\substack{q\in Q_{\Delta'}\\ \ell_q>0\\ s_q/\ell_q\le t}}
      s_q .
   \]
   If for every such \(\Delta'\) there exists a threshold \(t_{\Delta'}>A\)
   such that
   \[
      t_{\Delta'}L_{\Delta'}(t_{\Delta'})
      -
      S_{\Delta'}(t_{\Delta'})
      \le
      (t_{\Delta'}-A)\Lambda ,
      \tag{TRS1}
   \]
   then the enlarged local filter-cover LP is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a dyadic \(\Delta'\).  Applying
   \cref{lem:threshold-recycled-bad-layers} with \(t=t_{\Delta'}\) shows that
   \((TRS1)\) is exactly the positive-part Lagrange screen \((LRS4)\), with
   multiplier \(\lambda_{\Delta'}=t_{\Delta'}-A>0\).  Since this holds for
   every dyadic level, \cref{cor:lagrange-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices}
   proves local feasibility.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite-prefix recycled-sublayer separator suffices]
   \label{cor:finite-prefix-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices}
   In \cref{cor:threshold-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices}, the threshold
   condition \((TRS1)\) may be replaced by the following finite prefix
   condition at each dyadic \(\Delta'\).  Let \(a_1<\cdots<a_k\) be the
   distinct values larger than \(A\) of
   \(s_{W,\theta}(q)/(\Delta'\bar\tau_q)\) over queries
   \(q\in Q_{\Delta'}\) with \(\bar\tau_q>0\).  Set \(a_0=A\), and define
   \[
      L_i=\sum_{\substack{q\in Q_{\Delta'}\\
                  \bar\tau_q>0\\
                  s_{W,\theta}(q)/(\Delta'\bar\tau_q)\le a_i}}
            \Delta'\bar\tau_q,
      \qquad
      S_i=\sum_{\substack{q\in Q_{\Delta'}\\
                  \bar\tau_q>0\\
                  s_{W,\theta}(q)/(\Delta'\bar\tau_q)\le a_i}}
            s_{W,\theta}(q).
   \]
   If, for every \(\Delta'\), at least one of
   \[
      A L_0-S_0=0\quad\text{and}\quad L_0\le\Lambda ,
      \tag{FPR1}
   \]
   \[
      \exists i\in\{1,\ldots,k\}:
      \qquad
      a_iL_i-S_i\le(a_i-A)\Lambda ,
      \tag{FPR2}
   \]
   or
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{q\in Q_{\Delta'}\\ \bar\tau_q>0}}
      \Delta'\bar\tau_q
      <\Lambda
      \tag{FPR3}
   \]
   holds, then the enlarged local filter-cover LP is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For each fixed dyadic \(\Delta'\), this is exactly
   \cref{lem:finite-prefix-recycled-threshold-screen} applied with
   \(\ell_q=\Delta'\bar\tau_q\) and \(s_q=s_{W,\theta}(q)\).  Hence the
   threshold condition of
   \cref{cor:threshold-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices} holds at every
   dyadic level, and that corollary proves feasibility.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Load-quantile recycled threshold screen]
   \label{lem:load-quantile-recycled-threshold-screen}
   Work in the notation of
   \cref{lem:finite-prefix-recycled-threshold-screen}.  The threshold screen
   \((FPS1)\) holds if and only if at least one of the following alternatives
   holds:
   \[
      A L_0-S_0=0
      \quad\text{and}\quad
      L_0\le\Lambda ,
      \tag{LQS1}
   \]
   \[
      L_\infty<\Lambda ,
      \tag{LQS2}
   \]
   or
   \[
      L_0<\Lambda\le L_\infty,
      \quad
      a_jL_j-S_j\le(a_j-A)\Lambda ,
      \tag{LQS3}
   \]
   where
   \[
      j=\min\{i\in\{1,\ldots,k\}: L_i\ge\Lambda\}.
      \tag{LQS4}
   \]
   Thus, after sorting the efficiencies, the continuous threshold search reduces
   to the \(A\)-boundary, the terminal load test, and one weighted
   \(\Lambda\)-quantile breakpoint.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Let
   \[
      G(t)=tL(t)-S(t)-(t-A)\Lambda .
   \]
   As in the proof of \cref{lem:finite-prefix-recycled-threshold-screen}, \(G\)
   is continuous and piecewise affine, and on the interval after breakpoint
   \(a_i\) its slope is \(L_i-\Lambda\).  These slopes are nondecreasing in
   \(i\).

   The alternatives are sufficient: \((LQS1)\) is exactly the boundary
   alternative \((FPS2)\), \((LQS2)\) is \((FPS4)\), and \((LQS3)\) is the
   breakpoint alternative \((FPS3)\) at the first load-crossing index \(j\).

   Conversely suppose \((FPS1)\) holds.  If \(L_\infty<\Lambda\), then
   \((LQS2)\) holds.  Hence assume \(L_\infty\ge\Lambda\).  If \(L_0\ge\Lambda\),
   every right slope is nonnegative, so \(G(t)\ge G(A)\) for all \(t>A\).  Since
   \(G(A)=A L_0-S_0\ge0\), the only way some \(t>A\) can satisfy \(G(t)\le0\) is
   \(G(A)=0\) and \(L_0=\Lambda\), which is \((LQS1)\).  If \(L_0<\Lambda\),
   then the index \(j\) in \((LQS4)\) exists.  For \(i<j\) the slope
   \(L_i-\Lambda\) is negative, and for \(i\ge j\) it is nonnegative.  Therefore
   \(G\) attains its global minimum at \(a_j\).  Since \((FPS1)\) holds,
   \(G(a_j)\le0\), which is \((LQS3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Exact-load recycled quantile screen]
   \label{lem:exact-load-recycled-quantile-screen}
   Work in the notation of
   \cref{lem:finite-prefix-recycled-threshold-screen}, and assume
   \(L_0<\Lambda\le L_\infty\).  Let
   \[
      j=\min\{i\in\{1,\ldots,k\}:L_i\ge\Lambda\},
      \qquad
      \alpha=\frac{\Lambda-L_{j-1}}{L_j-L_{j-1}} .
      \tag{ELQ1}
   \]
   Define the fractional \(\Lambda\)-load quantile capacity
   \[
      \widehat S_\Lambda
      =
      S_{j-1}+\alpha(S_j-S_{j-1}) .
      \tag{ELQ2}
   \]
   Then the quantile breakpoint condition in \((LQS3)\) is equivalent to
   \[
      \widehat S_\Lambda\ge A\Lambda .
      \tag{ELQ3}
   \]
   Equivalently, in the non-boundary regime \(L_0<\Lambda\le L_\infty\), the
   threshold screen holds if and only if the lowest-efficiency fractional prefix
   of exact load \(\Lambda\) has average capacity at least \(A\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   All mass added between \(L_{j-1}\) and \(L_j\) has efficiency \(a_j\).  Hence
   \[
      S_j-S_{j-1}=a_j(L_j-L_{j-1}),
   \]
   and therefore
   \[
      \widehat S_\Lambda
      =
      S_j-a_j(L_j-\Lambda).
   \]
   The inequality \(\widehat S_\Lambda\ge A\Lambda\) is exactly
   \(a_jL_j-S_j\le(a_j-A)\Lambda\), which is the quantile condition in
   \((LQS3)\).  The final sentence follows from
   \cref{lem:load-quantile-recycled-threshold-screen} under the standing
   assumption \(L_0<\Lambda\le L_\infty\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Variational exact-load recycled screen]
   \label{lem:variational-exact-load-recycled-screen}
   Work in the notation of
   \cref{lem:exact-load-recycled-quantile-screen}.  Define
   \[
      V_\Lambda
      =
      \min
      \left\{
      \sum_{q\in Q^+}y_qs_q:
      0\le y_q\le1,\quad
      \sum_{q\in Q^+}y_q\ell_q=\Lambda
      \right\}.
      \tag{VEL1}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      V_\Lambda=\widehat S_\Lambda .
      \tag{VEL2}
   \]
   Consequently, in the non-boundary regime \(L_0<\Lambda\le L_\infty\), the
   threshold screen holds if and only if
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q^+}y_qs_q\ge A\Lambda
      \tag{VEL3}
   \]
   for every fractional sublayer \(0\le y_q\le1\) of exact load
   \(\sum_qy_q\ell_q=\Lambda\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   This is the fractional-knapsack minimum.  If
   \(\sigma_q<\sigma_{q'}\), \(y_q<1\), and \(y_{q'}>0\), choose
   \[
      0<\delta\le\min\{(1-y_q)\ell_q,\ y_{q'}\ell_{q'}\}.
   \]
   Replacing \(y_q\) by \(y_q+\delta/\ell_q\) and \(y_{q'}\) by
   \(y_{q'}-\delta/\ell_{q'}\) preserves the exact load and changes the
   capacity by
   \[
      \delta(\sigma_q-\sigma_{q'})<0 .
   \]
   Hence an optimizer is a lowest-efficiency fractional prefix.  Since
   \(L_0<\Lambda\), every level with \(\sigma_q\le A\) is fully included, and the
   only fractional boundary can occur at the first level \(a_j\) for which
   \(L_j\ge\Lambda\).  Its value is exactly \(\widehat S_\Lambda\).

   Therefore the minimum value of the left side of \((VEL3)\) over exact-load
   fractional sublayers is \(\widehat S_\Lambda\).  The final equivalence follows
   from \cref{lem:exact-load-recycled-quantile-screen}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Exact-load margin extension]
   \label{lem:exact-load-margin-extension}
   Work in the notation of \cref{lem:exact-load-recycled-quantile-screen}, and
   assume
   \[
      \widehat S_\Lambda\ge A\Lambda .
      \tag{ELM1}
   \]
   For \(H\in(\Lambda,L_\infty]\), define
   \[
      V_H=
      \min
      \left\{
      \sum_{q\in Q^+}y_qs_q:
      0\le y_q\le1,\quad
      \sum_{q\in Q^+}y_q\ell_q=H
      \right\}.
      \tag{ELM2}
   \]
   Then, with \(j\) from \((ELQ1)\),
   \[
      V_H
      \ge
      AH+(a_j-A)(H-\Lambda)
      >
      AH .
      \tag{ELM3}
   \]
   Consequently every fractional sublayer \(0\le y_q\le1\) with load
   \(\sum_qy_q\ell_q>\Lambda\) has capacity strictly larger than \(A\) times its
   load.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   By the same fractional-knapsack exchange used in
   \cref{lem:variational-exact-load-recycled-screen}, \(V_H\) is obtained by the
   lowest-efficiency fractional prefix of load \(H\).  Since \(H>\Lambda\), this
   prefix contains the exact \(\Lambda\)-load prefix and then adds only mass with
   efficiency at least \(a_j\).  Therefore
   \[
      V_H\ge \widehat S_\Lambda+a_j(H-\Lambda).
   \]
   Using \((ELM1)\) gives the first inequality in \((ELM3)\).  The second is
   strict because \(L_0<\Lambda\) in the standing hypotheses of
   \cref{lem:exact-load-recycled-quantile-screen}, so the first crossing level
   satisfies \(a_j>A\).  Any fractional sublayer of load \(H\) has capacity at
   least \(V_H\), giving the consequence.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Dominated-load recycled screen]
   \label{lem:dominated-load-recycled-screen}
   Work in the notation of \cref{lem:exact-load-recycled-quantile-screen}.  In
   the non-boundary regime \(L_0<\Lambda\le L_\infty\), the threshold screen
   holds if and only if every probability vector \(\nu\) on \(Q^+\) satisfying
   \[
      0\le\nu_q\le\frac{\ell_q}{\Lambda},
      \qquad
      \sum_{q\in Q^+}\nu_q=1
      \tag{DLR1}
   \]
   has average efficiency at least \(A\):
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q^+}\nu_q\sigma_q\ge A .
      \tag{DLR2}
   \]
   Failure of the threshold screen in this regime is equivalently the existence
   of such a dominated probability vector with average efficiency \(<A\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Exact-load fractional layers \(y\) are in bijection with vectors \(\nu\)
   satisfying \((DLR1)\) by
   \[
      \nu_q=\frac{y_q\ell_q}{\Lambda},
      \qquad
      y_q=\frac{\Lambda\nu_q}{\ell_q}
      \quad(q\in Q^+).
   \]
   Under this change of variables,
   \[
      \frac1\Lambda\sum_{q\in Q^+}y_qs_q
      =
      \sum_{q\in Q^+}\nu_q\frac{s_q}{\ell_q}
      =
      \sum_{q\in Q^+}\nu_q\sigma_q .
   \]
   The claim is therefore exactly
   \cref{lem:variational-exact-load-recycled-screen} divided by \(\Lambda\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Load-quantile recycled-sublayer separator suffices]
   \label{cor:load-quantile-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices}
   In \cref{cor:finite-prefix-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices}, the finite
   prefix condition may be replaced by the following load-quantile condition at
   each dyadic \(\Delta'\).  With \(a_i,L_i,S_i,L_\infty,A,\Lambda\) as there,
   at least one of
   \[
      A L_0-S_0=0
      \quad\text{and}\quad
      L_0\le\Lambda ,
      \tag{LQR1}
   \]
   \[
      L_\infty<\Lambda ,
      \tag{LQR2}
   \]
   or
   \[
      L_0<\Lambda\le L_\infty,
      \quad
      a_jL_j-S_j\le(a_j-A)\Lambda ,
      \qquad
      j=\min\{i\ge1:L_i\ge\Lambda\}
      \tag{LQR3}
   \]
   holds.  Then the enlarged local filter-cover LP is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \cref{lem:load-quantile-recycled-threshold-screen} at each dyadic
   level.  The resulting threshold screen is precisely the hypothesis needed by
   \cref{cor:threshold-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exact-load recycled-sublayer separator suffices]
   \label{cor:exact-load-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices}
   In \cref{cor:finite-prefix-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices}, the finite
   prefix condition may be replaced by the following exact-load quantile
   condition at each dyadic \(\Delta'\).  With \(a_i,L_i,S_i,L_\infty,A,\Lambda\)
   as there, at least one of
   \[
      A L_0-S_0=0
      \quad\text{and}\quad
      L_0\le\Lambda ,
      \tag{ELR1}
   \]
   \[
      L_\infty<\Lambda ,
      \tag{ELR2}
   \]
   or
   \[
      L_0<\Lambda\le L_\infty
      \quad\text{and}\quad
      \widehat S_\Lambda\ge A\Lambda ,
      \tag{ELR3}
   \]
   holds, where \(\widehat S_\Lambda\) is the fractional quantile capacity from
   \cref{lem:exact-load-recycled-quantile-screen}.  Then the enlarged local
   filter-cover LP is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   In the third alternative,
   \cref{lem:exact-load-recycled-quantile-screen} gives exactly the quantile
   breakpoint condition \((LQR3)\).  The first two alternatives are \((LQR1)\)
   and \((LQR2)\).  Hence
   \cref{cor:load-quantile-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices} applies.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Variational exact-load recycled separator suffices]
   \label{cor:variational-exact-load-recycled-separator-suffices}
   In \cref{cor:finite-prefix-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices}, the finite
   prefix condition may be replaced by the following variational condition at
   each dyadic \(\Delta'\).  With \(L_0,S_0,L_\infty,A,\Lambda\) as there, at
   least one of
   \[
      A L_0-S_0=0
      \quad\text{and}\quad
      L_0\le\Lambda ,
      \tag{VER1}
   \]
   \[
      L_\infty<\Lambda ,
      \tag{VER2}
   \]
   or
   \[
      L_0<\Lambda\le L_\infty
      \quad\text{and}\quad
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}}y_qs_{W,\theta}(q)\ge A\Lambda
      \tag{VER3}
   \]
   for every \(0\le y_q\le1\) satisfying
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}} y_q\,\Delta'\bar\tau_q=\Lambda
      \tag{VER4}
   \]
   holds.  Then the enlarged local filter-cover LP is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   In the third case, apply
   \cref{lem:variational-exact-load-recycled-screen} with
   \(\ell_q=\Delta'\bar\tau_q\) and \(s_q=s_{W,\theta}(q)\).  The variational
   inequality \((VER3)\)--\((VER4)\) is equivalent to
   \(\widehat S_\Lambda\ge A\Lambda\).  Hence
   \cref{cor:exact-load-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices} applies.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Dominated-load recycled separator suffices]
   \label{cor:dominated-load-recycled-separator-suffices}
   In \cref{cor:finite-prefix-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices}, the finite
   prefix condition may be replaced by the following dominated-load condition at
   each dyadic \(\Delta'\).  With \(L_0,S_0,L_\infty,A,\Lambda\) as there, at
   least one of
   \[
      A L_0-S_0=0
      \quad\text{and}\quad
      L_0\le\Lambda ,
      \tag{DLR3}
   \]
   \[
      L_\infty<\Lambda ,
      \tag{DLR4}
   \]
   or
   \[
      L_0<\Lambda\le L_\infty
      \quad\text{and}\quad
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}}\nu_q
      \frac{s_{W,\theta}(q)}{\Delta'\bar\tau_q}
      \ge A
      \tag{DLR5}
   \]
   for every probability vector \(\nu\) supported on queries with
   \(\bar\tau_q>0\) and satisfying
   \[
      0\le\nu_q\le\frac{\Delta'\bar\tau_q}{\Lambda},
      \qquad
      \sum_q\nu_q=1
      \tag{DLR6}
   \]
   holds.  Then the enlarged local filter-cover LP is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   In the third case, apply \cref{lem:dominated-load-recycled-screen} with
   \(\ell_q=\Delta'\bar\tau_q\) and \(s_q=s_{W,\theta}(q)\).  The dominated-load
   inequality \((DLR5)\)--\((DLR6)\) is equivalent to the variational
   exact-load condition, so
   \cref{cor:variational-exact-load-recycled-separator-suffices} applies.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Dominated-load recycled local-cover endpoint]
   \label{cor:dominated-load-recycled-local-cover-endpoint}
   Work under the hypotheses of \cref{cor:annular-reporter-local-cover}, assume
   finite primitive support and prefix-closed retained containers as in
   \cref{cor:recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices}.  Suppose the following
   dominated-load separator holds for every guarded normalized residual and
   every single-seed annular query layer \(Q'=Q_{z,\beta,\Delta}\) satisfying
   \((SAQ1)\)--\((SAQ2)\).  There are a retained container \(W\), a size
   certificate \(|W|\le K\), a congestion parameter \(C>0\), and
   \(0\le\theta\le1\) satisfying \((HMC1)\).  Put
   \[
      m=|P|,
      \qquad
      \mathcal D_m=\{2^\ell:0\le\ell\le\lceil\log_2m\rceil\},
      \qquad
      H_m(\Delta)=|\{\Delta''\in\mathcal D_m:\Delta\le\Delta''\le m\}|,
   \]
   \[
      A=\frac{2H_m(\Delta)}{C},
      \qquad
      \Lambda=
      \frac{(1-\xi)\beta_0C_\eta\pi_1\kappa}
      {16J K_{|P|}H_m(\Delta)} .
      \tag{DLE1}
   \]
   For every dyadic \(\Delta'\in\mathcal D_m\) with \(\Delta'\ge\Delta\), define
   \[
      Q_{\Delta'}=\{q\in Q': |B_{z,\beta}(q)|\ge\Delta'\},
      \qquad
      \ell_q=\Delta'\bar\tau_q,
      \qquad
      s_q=s_{W,\theta}(q).
   \]
   Let \(Q_{\Delta'}^+=\{q\in Q_{\Delta'}:\ell_q>0\}\), put
   \[
      \sigma_q=\frac{s_q}{\ell_q}\qquad(q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+),
   \]
   and define
   \[
      L_0=\sum_{\substack{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+\\ \sigma_q\le A}}\ell_q,
      \qquad
      S_0=\sum_{\substack{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+\\ \sigma_q\le A}}s_q,
      \qquad
      L_\infty=\sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+}\ell_q .
   \]
   Assume that at least one of the following holds for each \(\Delta'\):
   \[
      A L_0-S_0=0
      \quad\text{and}\quad
      L_0\le\Lambda ,
      \tag{DLE2}
   \]
   \[
      L_\infty<\Lambda ,
      \tag{DLE3}
   \]
   or
   \[
      L_0<\Lambda\le L_\infty
      \quad\text{and}\quad
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+}\nu_q\sigma_q\ge A
      \tag{DLE4}
   \]
   for every probability vector \(\nu\) on \(Q_{\Delta'}^+\) satisfying
   \[
      0\le\nu_q\le\frac{\ell_q}{\Lambda},
      \qquad
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+}\nu_q=1 .
      \tag{DLE5}
   \]
   Then the enlarged local filter-cover LP is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The alternatives \((DLE2)\)--\((DLE5)\) are exactly the dominated-load
   condition of \cref{cor:dominated-load-recycled-separator-suffices} at each
   dyadic level, with the constants from
   \cref{cor:threshold-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices}.  Hence the finite
   prefix condition holds at every dyadic level, and
   \cref{cor:finite-prefix-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices} proves local
   filter-cover feasibility.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Finite dominated-load proposal game]
   \label{lem:finite-dominated-load-proposal-game}
   Fix the guarded residual and single-seed annular query layer in
   \cref{cor:dominated-load-recycled-local-cover-endpoint}.  Fix also one
   congestion stratum \(C\), and put \(A=2H_m(\Delta)/C\) and \(\Lambda\) as in
   \((DLE1)\).  Let
   \[
      \mathcal I\subseteq
      \{\Delta'\in\mathcal D_m:\Delta'\ge\Delta\}
   \]
   be a nonempty set of active dyadic levels for which
   \[
      Q_{\Delta'}^+=
      \{q\in Q': |B_{z,\beta}(q)|\ge\Delta',\ \Delta'\bar\tau_q>0\}
   \]
   has total load at least \(\Lambda\).  For \(\Delta'\in\mathcal I\), define
   \[
      \mathcal V_{\Delta'}
      =
      \left\{
      \nu\in\R_+^{Q_{\Delta'}^+}:
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+}\nu_q=1,\quad
      \nu_q\le\frac{\Delta'\bar\tau_q}{\Lambda}
      \right\}.
      \tag{DPG1}
   \]
   Let \(\mathcal R\) be a finite family of affordable candidate records
   \(R=(W_R,K_R,\theta_R)\) such that \(W_R,K_R,C,\theta_R\) satisfy
   \((HMC1)\).  For \(R\in\mathcal R\), \(\Delta'\in\mathcal I\), and
   \(\nu\in\mathcal V_{\Delta'}\), write
   \[
      s_R^{\Delta'}(q)=s_{W_R,\theta_R}(q),
      \qquad
      \sigma_R^{\Delta'}(q)=
      \frac{s_R^{\Delta'}(q)}{\Delta'\bar\tau_q},
   \]
   and define the dominated-load margin
   \[
      M(R,\Delta',\nu)
      =
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+}\nu_q\sigma_R^{\Delta'}(q)-A .
   \]
   Then
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      &\max_{\omega\in\Delta_{\mathcal R}}
      \min_{\Delta'\in\mathcal I}
      \min_{\nu\in\mathcal V_{\Delta'}}
      \sum_{R\in\mathcal R}\omega_R M(R,\Delta',\nu)\\
      &\qquad =
      \min_{\substack{\alpha\in\Delta_{\mathcal I}\\
                      \nu^{\Delta'}\in\mathcal V_{\Delta'}}}
      \max_{R\in\mathcal R}
      \sum_{\Delta'\in\mathcal I}
      \alpha_{\Delta'}M(R,\Delta',\nu^{\Delta'}).
   \end{aligned}
      \tag{DPG2}
   \]
   Consequently, there is a proposal law \(\omega\) whose averaged candidate
   passes every dominated-load test,
   \[
      \sum_{R\in\mathcal R}\omega_R
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+}\nu_q\sigma_R^{\Delta'}(q)
      \ge A
      \qquad
      (\Delta'\in\mathcal I,\ \nu\in\mathcal V_{\Delta'}),
      \tag{DPG3}
   \]
   if and only if no level-weighted dominated residual
   \((\alpha,\{\nu^{\Delta'}\})\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{\Delta'\in\mathcal I}
      \alpha_{\Delta'}
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+}
      \nu_q^{\Delta'}\sigma_R^{\Delta'}(q)
      < A
      \qquad(R\in\mathcal R).
      \tag{DPG4}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Each \(\mathcal V_{\Delta'}\) is a nonempty finite-dimensional polytope, and
   the margin is linear in \(\nu\).  Hence the inner minimum over
   \(\mathcal V_{\Delta'}\) is attained at an extreme point.  Let
   \[
      \mathcal E=
      \{(\Delta',e):\Delta'\in\mathcal I,
        e\in\operatorname{Ext}(\mathcal V_{\Delta'})\}.
   \]
   This set is finite.  The left side of \((DPG2)\) is the value of the finite
   matrix game
   \[
      \max_{\omega\in\Delta_{\mathcal R}}
      \min_{(\Delta',e)\in\mathcal E}
      \sum_R\omega_RM(R,\Delta',e).
   \]
   Write this value as the linear program
   \[
      \max v
      \quad\text{subject to}\quad
      \sum_R\omega_RM(R,\Delta',e)\ge v\ ((\Delta',e)\in\mathcal E),
      \quad
      \omega\in\Delta_{\mathcal R}.
   \]
   Its finite LP dual is
   \[
      \min z
      \quad\text{subject to}\quad
      \sum_{(\Delta',e)\in\mathcal E}\alpha_{\Delta',e}M(R,\Delta',e)\le z
      \ (R\in\mathcal R),
      \quad
      \alpha\in\Delta_{\mathcal E}.
   \]
   Strong duality gives equality of the two displayed values.  Finally collapse
   the dual distribution over extreme points inside each dyadic level.  Put
   \(\alpha_{\Delta'}=\sum_e\alpha_{\Delta',e}\); if
   \(\alpha_{\Delta'}>0\), define
   \[
      \nu^{\Delta'}
      =
      \alpha_{\Delta'}^{-1}
      \sum_e\alpha_{\Delta',e}e\in\mathcal V_{\Delta'}.
   \]
   Levels with \(\alpha_{\Delta'}=0\) may choose any point of
   \(\mathcal V_{\Delta'}\).  This gives the right side of \((DPG2)\), and the
   converse expansion of each \(\nu^{\Delta'}\) into extreme points gives the
   reverse inequality.

   The final statement is just the sign form of \((DPG2)\).  The compact maxima
   and minima are attained, so failure of \((DPG3)\) is equivalent to the value
   in \((DPG2)\) being strictly negative, which is exactly the existence of
   \((DPG4)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exact-load form of the dominated proposal obstruction]
   \label{cor:exact-load-dominated-proposal-obstruction}
   In the setting of \cref{lem:finite-dominated-load-proposal-game}, failure of
   the averaged dominated-load test \((DPG3)\) is equivalent to the existence of
   level weights \(\alpha\in\Delta_{\mathcal I}\) and, for each
   \(\Delta'\in\mathcal I\), a fractional exact-load cohort
   \(0\le y_q^{\Delta'}\le1\) on \(Q_{\Delta'}^+\) satisfying
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+}
      y_q^{\Delta'}\,\Delta'\bar\tau_q
      =
      \Lambda ,
      \tag{EDP1}
   \]
   such that every affordable record \(R\in\mathcal R\) has deficient averaged
   near-shadow capacity
   \[
      \sum_{\Delta'\in\mathcal I}
      \alpha_{\Delta'}
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+}
      y_q^{\Delta'}s_R^{\Delta'}(q)
      <
      A\Lambda .
      \tag{EDP2}
   \]
   Moreover each cohort \(y^{\Delta'}\) decomposes into extreme exact-load
   cohorts.  Equivalently, the same obstruction may be represented by a
   probability law \(\eta\) on pairs \((\Delta',e)\), where \(e\) is an
   exact-load cohort at level \(\Delta'\) with all but at most one coordinate in
   \(\{0,1\}\), such that
   \[
      \E_{(\Delta',e)\sim\eta}
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+}e_qs_R^{\Delta'}(q)
      <
      A\Lambda
      \qquad(R\in\mathcal R).
      \tag{EDP3}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Starting from the dominated residual \((\alpha,\nu^{\Delta'})\) in
   \((DPG4)\), set
   \[
      y_q^{\Delta'}
      =
      \frac{\Lambda\nu_q^{\Delta'}}{\Delta'\bar\tau_q}.
   \]
   The cap in \((DPG1)\) gives \(0\le y_q^{\Delta'}\le1\), and
   \(\sum_q\nu_q^{\Delta'}=1\) gives \((EDP1)\).  Also
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+}
      \nu_q^{\Delta'}\sigma_R^{\Delta'}(q)
      =
      \frac1\Lambda
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+}
      y_q^{\Delta'}s_R^{\Delta'}(q),
   \]
   so \((DPG4)\) is exactly \((EDP2)\) after multiplying by \(\Lambda\).
   The converse change of variables is identical:
   \[
      \nu_q^{\Delta'}
      =
      \frac{y_q^{\Delta'}\,\Delta'\bar\tau_q}{\Lambda}.
   \]

   The exact-load feasible region
   \[
      \{0\le y\le1:\sum_qy_q\Delta'\bar\tau_q=\Lambda\}
   \]
   is a bounded polytope, so each \(y^{\Delta'}\) is a convex combination of its
   extreme points.  Expanding these combinations and absorbing the level weight
   \(\alpha_{\Delta'}\) into the coefficients gives the law \(\eta\) and preserves
   the strict inequalities in \((EDP2)\) by linearity, giving \((EDP3)\).

   It remains only to identify the extreme points.  If two coordinates \(i,j\)
   are both strictly between \(0\) and \(1\), moving a small amount of load from
   \(i\) to \(j\) or from \(j\) to \(i\) preserves \((EDP1)\) and remains
   feasible, so the point is not extreme.  Hence an extreme point has at most one
   fractional coordinate.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exact-load cohort-law separator]
   \label{cor:exact-load-cohort-law-separator}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:finite-dominated-load-proposal-game}.  Let
   \(\mathcal E_{\rm load}\) be the finite family of pairs \((\Delta',e)\) where
   \(\Delta'\in\mathcal I\) and \(e\) is an extreme exact-load cohort at that
   level:
   \[
      0\le e_q\le1,\qquad
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+}e_q\,\Delta'\bar\tau_q=\Lambda,
      \qquad
      e_q=0\text{ for }q\notin Q_{\Delta'}^+ .
   \]
   Suppose that every probability law \(\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}\)
   admits an affordable record \(R\in\mathcal R\) with
   \[
      \E_{(\Delta',e)\sim\eta}
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+}e_qs_R^{\Delta'}(q)
      \ge A\Lambda .
      \tag{CLS1}
   \]
   Then there is a proposal law \(\omega\in\Delta_{\mathcal R}\) satisfying the
   averaged dominated-load certificate \((DPG3)\).

   Conversely, if no such proposal law exists, then there is a cohort law
   \(\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}\) such that every affordable record
   violates \((CLS1)\) strictly.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   This is the contrapositive of
   \cref{cor:exact-load-dominated-proposal-obstruction}.  If \((DPG3)\) fails,
   that corollary gives a law \(\eta\) over extreme exact-load cohorts satisfying
   \((EDP3)\), which is the strict failure of \((CLS1)\) for every
   \(R\in\mathcal R\).  Therefore, if every cohort law has some record satisfying
   \((CLS1)\), \((DPG3)\) cannot fail.  The converse is exactly the same
   implication read forward.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cohort-law scalar prefix normal form]
   \label{cor:cohort-law-scalar-prefix-normal-form}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:exact-load-cohort-law-separator}.  For a
   cohort law \(\eta\) and a segment parameter \(0\le\theta\le1\), define the
   cohort scalar degree
   \[
      d_\eta^\theta(p)
      =
      \E_{(\Delta',e)\sim\eta}
      \sum_{\substack{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+\\(p,q)\in\mathcal N}}
      e_q\,\bar\gamma^\theta_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
      \tag{CSP1}
   \]
   For a retained parent container \(W_0\), an integer \(1\le K\le |W_0|\), and
   \(\theta\), let
   \[
      D_\eta^\theta(W_0,K)
      =
      \max_{\substack{U\subseteq W_0\\ |U|=K}}
      \sum_{p\in U}d_\eta^\theta(p).
      \tag{CSP2}
   \]
   Assume that every maximizing subset \(U\) in \((CSP2)\) can be materialized as
   an affordable record \((U,K,\theta)\in\mathcal R\) whenever
   \(U,K,C,\theta\) satisfy \((HMC1)\).  If every cohort law \(\eta\) admits
   \(W_0,K,\theta\) satisfying \((HMC1)\) and
   \[
      D_\eta^\theta(W_0,K)\ge A\Lambda ,
      \tag{CSP3}
   \]
   then the averaged dominated-load certificate \((DPG3)\) holds.

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then there is a cohort law \(\eta\) such that
   every materializable affordable prefix template satisfies the strict prefix
   envelope
   \[
      D_\eta^\theta(W_0,K)< A\Lambda .
      \tag{CSP4}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For any retained record \(R=(U,K,\theta)\), Fubini's theorem and the
   definition of \(s_R^{\Delta'}\) give
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \E_{(\Delta',e)\sim\eta}
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+}e_qs_R^{\Delta'}(q)
      &=
      \E_{(\Delta',e)\sim\eta}
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+}
      e_q
      \sum_{\substack{p\in U\\(p,q)\in\mathcal N}}
      \bar\gamma^\theta_{p,q}r_{p,q}\\
      &=
      \sum_{p\in U}d_\eta^\theta(p).
   \end{aligned}
      \tag{CSP5}
   \]
   Thus, if \(U\) is a maximizing \(K\)-subset of \(W_0\) and \((CSP3)\) holds,
   the materialized record satisfies \((CLS1)\).  Applying
   \cref{cor:exact-load-cohort-law-separator} gives \((DPG3)\).

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, the same corollary gives a cohort law
   \(\eta\) for which every affordable record has strict capacity \(<A\Lambda\).
   Applying \((CSP5)\) to the materialized top-\(K\) records gives \((CSP4)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cohort-law weak-type superlevel normal form]
   \label{cor:cohort-law-weak-type-superlevel}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:cohort-law-scalar-prefix-normal-form}.  For a cohort law \(\eta\),
   a segment parameter \(\theta\), a retained parent container \(W_0\), and a
   level \(\delta>0\), put
   \[
      U_{\eta,\theta,\delta}(W_0)
      =
      \{p\in W_0:d_\eta^\theta(p)\ge\delta\},
      \qquad
      h_{\eta,\theta,\delta}(W_0)=|U_{\eta,\theta,\delta}(W_0)|.
      \tag{CWS1}
   \]
   Assume that every nonempty set \(U_{\eta,\theta,\delta}(W_0)\) can be
   materialized as an affordable record
   \[
      (U_{\eta,\theta,\delta}(W_0),
       h_{\eta,\theta,\delta}(W_0),\theta)\in\mathcal R
   \]
   whenever its size certificate and \(\theta\) satisfy \((HMC1)\).  If every
   cohort law \(\eta\) admits \(W_0,\theta,\delta\) with
   \(h=h_{\eta,\theta,\delta}(W_0)>0\), such that the superlevel record
   \((U_{\eta,\theta,\delta}(W_0),h,\theta)\) satisfies \((HMC1)\), and
   \[
      \delta h\ge A\Lambda ,
      \tag{CWS2}
   \]
   then the averaged dominated-load certificate \((DPG3)\) holds.

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then there is a cohort law \(\eta\) such that
   every materializable affordable superlevel satisfies the strict weak-type
   envelope
   \[
      \delta\,h_{\eta,\theta,\delta}(W_0)<A\Lambda .
      \tag{CWS3}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((CWS2)\) holds, then the materialized superlevel record \(R=(U,h,\theta)\)
   has capacity, by \((CSP5)\),
   \[
      \E_{(\Delta',e)\sim\eta}
      \sum_{q\in Q_{\Delta'}^+}e_qs_R^{\Delta'}(q)
      =
      \sum_{p\in U}d_\eta^\theta(p)
      \ge
      \delta h
      \ge
      A\Lambda .
   \]
   Hence \((CLS1)\) holds for this cohort law, and
   \cref{cor:exact-load-cohort-law-separator} gives \((DPG3)\).

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then
   \cref{cor:cohort-law-scalar-prefix-normal-form} gives a cohort law satisfying
   the strict prefix envelope \((CSP4)\).  For a materializable affordable
   superlevel with \(h>0\), the top \(h\) points in \(W_0\) have mass at least
   \(\delta h\), so
   \[
      \delta h
      \le
      D_\eta^\theta(W_0,h)
      <
      A\Lambda .
   \]
   This is \((CWS3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Certified cohort-law superlevel reporter]
   \label{cor:certified-cohort-law-superlevel-reporter}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:cohort-law-weak-type-superlevel}.  For a
   cohort law \(\eta\), call
   \[
      (W_0,\theta,\delta,U,K,X)
   \]
   an \(\eta\)-superlevel report if
   \[
      U=\{p\in W_0:d_\eta^\theta(p)\ge\delta\},
      \qquad
      h=|U|>0,
      \tag{CWR0}
   \]
   the report gives one-sided certificates
   \[
      h\le K,
      \qquad
      0\le X\le \delta h,
      \tag{CWR1}
   \]
   and the retained record with update side \(U\), size certificate \(K\), and
   segment parameter \(\theta\) is affordable:
   \[
      (U,K,\theta)\in\mathcal R .
      \tag{CWR2}
   \]
   Here \(K\) may be a certified upper bound rather than the exact size; if the
   retained pool stores only exact-size records, take \(K=h\).

   Suppose that every cohort law \(\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}\)
   admits an \(\eta\)-superlevel report satisfying
   \[
      X\ge A\Lambda .
      \tag{CWR3}
   \]
   Then the averaged dominated-load certificate \((DPG3)\) holds.  More
   generally, it is enough that every \(\eta\) admits a finite probability law
   \(\zeta\) over \(\eta\)-superlevel reports with
   \[
      \E_{(W_0,\theta,\delta,U,K,X)\sim\zeta}X\ge A\Lambda ,
      \tag{CWR4}
   \]
   since some deterministic report in the support then satisfies \((CWR3)\).

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then there is a cohort law \(\eta\) for
   which every affordable \(\eta\)-superlevel report satisfies
   \[
      X<A\Lambda .
      \tag{CWR5}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let \((W_0,\theta,\delta,U,K,X)\) be an \(\eta\)-superlevel report satisfying
   \((CWR3)\).  Since every point of \(U\) has
   \(d_\eta^\theta(p)\ge\delta\),
   \[
      \sum_{p\in U}d_\eta^\theta(p)\ge\delta h\ge X\ge A\Lambda .
      \tag{CWR6}
   \]
   By \((CSP5)\), the affordable retained record \(R=(U,K,\theta)\) therefore
   satisfies the cohort capacity inequality \((CLS1)\).  If every cohort law has
   such a report, \cref{cor:exact-load-cohort-law-separator} gives \((DPG3)\).
   The randomized-report variant follows because a finite average at least
   \(A\Lambda\) has some support point with \(X\ge A\Lambda\).

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then
   \cref{cor:exact-load-cohort-law-separator} supplies a cohort law \(\eta\) for
   which every affordable retained record has cohort capacity strictly below
   \(A\Lambda\).  For any affordable \(\eta\)-superlevel report,
   \[
      X\le\delta h\le \sum_{p\in U}d_\eta^\theta(p)<A\Lambda ,
   \]
   which is \((CWR5)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Certified cohort-law mass reporter]
   \label{cor:certified-cohort-law-mass-reporter}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:certified-cohort-law-superlevel-reporter}.
   For a cohort law \(\eta\), call \((W_0,\theta,K,V,B)\) an
   \(\eta\)-mass report if \(K\ge1\), \(V>0\), \(B>0\), and it certifies
   \[
      |W_0|\le K,
      \qquad
      V\le\sum_{p\in W_0}d_\eta^\theta(p),
      \qquad
      d_\eta^\theta(p)\le B\quad(p\in W_0).
      \tag{CMR0}
   \]
   Define
   \[
      J_{B,K,V}
      =
      1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{2BK}{V}\right\rceil,
      \qquad
      \delta_j=B2^{-j}
      \quad(1\le j\le J_{B,K,V}),
      \tag{CMR1}
   \]
   and
   \[
      U_j=\{p\in W_0:d_\eta^\theta(p)\ge\delta_j\}.
      \tag{CMR2}
   \]
   Assume that every nonempty dyadic superlevel \(U_j\) from \((CMR2)\) can be
   retained with the same size certificate:
   \[
      (U_j,K,\theta)\in\mathcal R .
      \tag{CMR3}
   \]
   The certified yield of the mass report is
   \[
      Y(W_0,\theta,K,V,B)=\frac{V}{4J_{B,K,V}} .
      \tag{CMR4}
   \]
   If every cohort law \(\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}\) admits an
   \(\eta\)-mass report with
   \[
      Y(W_0,\theta,K,V,B)\ge A\Lambda ,
      \tag{CMR5}
   \]
   then the averaged dominated-load certificate \((DPG3)\) holds.  More
   generally, it is enough that every \(\eta\) admits a finite probability law
   \(\zeta\) over \(\eta\)-mass reports with
   \[
      \E_{(W_0,\theta,K,V,B)\sim\zeta}
      Y(W_0,\theta,K,V,B)
      \ge A\Lambda .
      \tag{CMR6}
   \]

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then there is a cohort law \(\eta\) for
   which every \(\eta\)-mass report satisfying \((CMR0)\)--\((CMR3)\) has
   \[
      Y(W_0,\theta,K,V,B)<A\Lambda .
      \tag{CMR7}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix an \(\eta\)-mass report and write \(J=J_{B,K,V}\),
   \(Y=V/(4J)\), and
   \[
      M=\sum_{p\in W_0}d_\eta^\theta(p).
   \]
   Since \(0\le d_\eta^\theta(p)\le B\) on \(W_0\), the dyadic layer-cake bound
   gives
   \[
      M
      \le
      B2^{-J}K
      +
      2\sum_{j=1}^J\delta_j|U_j| .
      \tag{CMR8}
   \]
   Indeed, for each \(x\in[0,B]\),
   \(x\le B2^{-J}+2\sum_{j=1}^J\delta_j{\bf 1}\{x\ge\delta_j\}\), and summing
   this inequality over \(x=d_\eta^\theta(p)\) gives \((CMR8)\).
   By the choice of \(J\), \(B2^{-J}K\le V/4\).  Since \(M\ge V\), we get
   \[
      \sum_{j=1}^J\delta_j|U_j|\ge\frac{3V}{8}.
   \]
   Hence some \(j\) satisfies
   \[
      \delta_j|U_j|>\frac{V}{4J}=Y.
      \tag{CMR9}
   \]
   For this \(j\), \(U_j\) is nonempty and affordable by \((CMR3)\), so
   \[
      (W_0,\theta,\delta_j,U_j,K,Y)
   \]
   is an \(\eta\)-superlevel report: its lower certificate obeys
   \(0\le Y\le \delta_j|U_j|\).  If \((CMR5)\) holds, then this report satisfies
   \((CWR3)\), and
   \cref{cor:certified-cohort-law-superlevel-reporter} gives \((DPG3)\).  If a
   finite law satisfies \((CMR6)\), one report in its support has yield at least
   \(A\Lambda\), so the same argument applies.

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then
   \cref{cor:certified-cohort-law-superlevel-reporter} gives a cohort law
   \(\eta\) for which every affordable \(\eta\)-superlevel report has
   certificate \(<A\Lambda\).  Applying the layer-cake construction above to any
   \(\eta\)-mass report produces an affordable superlevel report with
   certificate \(Y(W_0,\theta,K,V,B)\).  Therefore this yield must be
   \(<A\Lambda\), which is \((CMR7)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Explicit cohort-law mass envelope]
   \label{cor:explicit-cohort-law-mass-envelope}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:certified-cohort-law-mass-reporter}.  For
   \(B,K>0\), put
   \[
      L_{B,K}
      =
      1+\left\lceil
      \log_2\max\left\{2,\frac{2BK}{A\Lambda}\right\}
      \right\rceil .
      \tag{CME0}
   \]
   Suppose every cohort law \(\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}\) admits an
   \(\eta\)-mass report \((W_0,\theta,K,V,B)\) satisfying
   \[
      V\ge 4A\Lambda L_{B,K}.
      \tag{CME1}
   \]
   Then the averaged dominated-load certificate \((DPG3)\) holds.  More
   generally, it is enough that every \(\eta\) admits a finite probability law
   over \(\eta\)-mass reports with
   \[
      \E\frac{V}{4L_{B,K}}\ge A\Lambda .
      \tag{CME2}
   \]

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then there is a cohort law \(\eta\) for
   which every \(\eta\)-mass report satisfies the explicit logarithmic envelope
   \[
      V<4A\Lambda L_{B,K}.
      \tag{CME3}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If a report satisfies \((CME1)\), then \(V\ge A\Lambda\).  Since
   \((CMR0)\) implies \(V\le BK\), we have
   \[
      J_{B,K,V}
      =
      1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{2BK}{V}\right\rceil
      \le L_{B,K}.
   \]
   Therefore \(Y(W_0,\theta,K,V,B)=V/(4J_{B,K,V})\ge A\Lambda\), and
   \cref{cor:certified-cohort-law-mass-reporter} gives \((DPG3)\).  If the
   averaged condition \((CME2)\) holds, some report in the finite support has
   \(V/(4L_{B,K})\ge A\Lambda\), hence satisfies \((CME1)\).

   Conversely, suppose \((DPG3)\) fails, and take the cohort law from
   \cref{cor:certified-cohort-law-mass-reporter}.  For any mass report, if
   \(V<A\Lambda\), then \((CME3)\) is immediate because \(L_{B,K}\ge1\).  If
   \(V\ge A\Lambda\), then \(J_{B,K,V}\le L_{B,K}\), while \((CMR7)\) gives
   \(V/(4J_{B,K,V})<A\Lambda\).  Hence
   \(V<4A\Lambda J_{B,K,V}\le4A\Lambda L_{B,K}\), proving \((CME3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Capped marginal cohort-law mass reporter]
   \label{cor:capped-marginal-cohort-law-mass-reporter}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:explicit-cohort-law-mass-envelope}.  Fix a
   cohort law \(\eta\).  A reportable capped list law consists of a finite
   probability law \(\zeta\) over subsets \(W_s\subseteq P\), together with
   \(0\le\theta\le1\), an integer size certificate \(K\ge1\), and a height
   certificate \(B>0\), such that every \(s\) in the support satisfies
   \[
      |W_s|\le K,
      \qquad
      d_\eta^\theta(p)\le B\quad(p\in W_s),
      \tag{CMM0}
   \]
   and every nonempty dyadic degree superlevel of \(W_s\) can be retained with
   size certificate \(K\), as required in \((CMR3)\).  Let
   \[
      \pi_p=\Pr_{s\sim\zeta}[p\in W_s],
      \qquad
      V_\pi=\sum_p\pi_p\,d_\eta^\theta(p).
      \tag{CMM1}
   \]
   If every cohort law \(\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}\) admits a
   reportable capped list law satisfying
   \[
      V_\pi\ge4A\Lambda L_{B,K},
      \tag{CMM2}
   \]
   then the averaged dominated-load certificate \((DPG3)\) holds.  More
   generally, it is enough to have a finite outer probability law over
   reportable capped list laws with
   \[
      \E\frac{V_\pi}{4L_{B,K}}\ge A\Lambda .
      \tag{CMM3}
   \]

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then there is a cohort law \(\eta\) for
   which every reportable capped list law satisfies the marginal envelope
   \[
      V_\pi<4A\Lambda L_{B,K}.
      \tag{CMM4}
   \]

   In particular, suppose a retained parent container \(W\) is closed under
   all sublists of size at most \(K\) in the sense that every \(W_s\subseteq W\)
   with \(|W_s|\le K\) satisfies the reportability condition above.  Then it is
   enough to give soft responsibilities \(0\le\pi_p\le1\) on \(W\) with
   \[
      \sum_{p\in W}\pi_p\le K,
      \qquad
      d_\eta^\theta(p)\le B\quad(p\in W),
      \qquad
      \sum_{p\in W}\pi_p d_\eta^\theta(p)\ge4A\Lambda L_{B,K}.
      \tag{CMM5}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For an outcome \(s\), put
   \[
      V_s=\sum_{p\in W_s}d_\eta^\theta(p).
   \]
   Every outcome with \(V_s>0\) is an \(\eta\)-mass report
   \((W_s,\theta,K,V_s,B)\), and all outcomes have the same \(B,K\).  Moreover
   \[
      \E_{s\sim\zeta}V_s=V_\pi .
   \]
   If \((CMM2)\) holds, then the conditional law on the positive-\(V_s\)
   outcomes is a finite law over \(\eta\)-mass reports with
   \[
      \E\frac{V_s}{4L_{B,K}}\ge \frac{V_\pi}{4L_{B,K}}\ge A\Lambda .
   \]
   Applying \((CME2)\) gives \((DPG3)\).  The outer-law variant is the same
   averaging argument after first sampling the capped list law and then its
   list outcome.

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, take the cohort law from
   \cref{cor:explicit-cohort-law-mass-envelope}.  Each positive-\(V_s\) outcome
   is an \(\eta\)-mass report, so \((CME3)\) gives
   \(V_s<4A\Lambda L_{B,K}\); zero outcomes also satisfy this strict bound.
   Since the support is finite, averaging gives \((CMM4)\).

   For the final claim, use the standard integral decomposition of the capped
   hypersimplex.  The polytope
   \[
      \{x\in[0,1]^W:\sum_{p\in W}x_p\le K\}
   \]
   has only integral vertices: if two coordinates are fractional, one may
   perturb them in opposite directions; if exactly one coordinate is fractional,
   either the sum constraint is slack and that coordinate can be perturbed, or
   the sum is the integer \(K\), which is impossible with all other coordinates
   integral.  Thus any responsibility vector satisfying \(\sum_p\pi_p\le K\) is
   a convex combination of indicators of subsets of size at most \(K\).  The
   assumed sublist closure makes this a reportable capped list law with marginals
   \(\pi\), and \((CMM5)\) is exactly \((CMM2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite capped-marginal proposal oracle]
   \label{cor:finite-capped-marginal-cohort-oracle}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:capped-marginal-cohort-law-mass-reporter}.  For every cohort law
   \(\eta\), every \(0\le\theta\le1\), and every point \(p\),
   \[
      0\le d_\eta^\theta(p)\le1.
      \tag{FCM0}
   \]
   Let \(\mathcal B\) be a finite pool of reportable capped-marginal templates.
   A template \(B\in\mathcal B\) consists of a segment parameter
   \(\theta_B\), an integer size certificate \(K_B\ge1\), and inclusion
   marginals \(\pi_{B,p}\) that are realized by a reportable capped list law
   with height certificate \(1\).  Put
   \[
      L_B
      =
      1+\left\lceil
      \log_2\max\left\{2,\frac{2K_B}{A\Lambda}\right\}
      \right\rceil ,
      \tag{FCM1}
   \]
   and, for a cohort law \(\eta\),
   \[
      V_\eta(B)=\sum_p\pi_{B,p}d_\eta^{\theta_B}(p),
      \qquad
      G(B,\eta)=\frac{V_\eta(B)}{4L_B}-A\Lambda .
      \tag{FCM2}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \max_{\omega\in\Delta_{\mathcal B}}
      \min_{\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}}
      \sum_{B\in\mathcal B}\omega_BG(B,\eta)
      =
      \min_{\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}}
      \max_{B\in\mathcal B}G(B,\eta).
      \tag{FCM3}
   \]
   Consequently, if either side of \((FCM3)\) is nonnegative, then the averaged
   dominated-load certificate \((DPG3)\) holds.  Equivalently, it is enough that
   every cohort law \(\eta\) have some template \(B\in\mathcal B\) with
   \[
      V_\eta(B)\ge4A\Lambda L_B .
      \tag{FCM4}
   \]

   Conversely, if no randomized law on \(\mathcal B\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_B\omega_B\frac{V_\eta(B)}{4L_B}\ge A\Lambda
      \qquad(\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}),
      \tag{FCM5}
   \]
   then there is a cohort law \(\eta\) such that every template in the finite
   pool satisfies
   \[
      V_\eta(B)<4A\Lambda L_B .
      \tag{FCM6}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The unit-height bound follows from \(0\le e_q\le1\), \(0\le r_{p,q}\le1\),
   and \((GNR1)\):
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \sum_p d_\eta^\theta(p)
      &=
      \E_{(\Delta',e)\sim\eta}
      \sum_q e_q
      \sum_{\substack{p:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}}
      \bar\gamma^\theta_{p,q}r_{p,q}\\
      &\le
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\bar\gamma^\theta_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      =
      \mathsf M(\bar\gamma^\theta)
      =
      1 .
   \end{aligned}
   \]
   Hence each summand is in \([0,1]\), proving \((FCM0)\).

   Since \(\mathcal E_{\rm load}\) and \(\mathcal B\) are finite and
   \(G(B,\eta)\) is linear in \(\eta\) and \(\omega\), \((FCM3)\) is the finite
   matrix-game minimax theorem.  If the value is nonnegative, choose a
   maximizing law \(\omega\).  For every cohort law \(\eta\),
   \[
      \sum_B\omega_B\frac{V_\eta(B)}{4L_B}\ge A\Lambda .
   \]
   Sampling \(B\sim\omega\) and then sampling the capped list law realizing its
   marginals gives the finite outer law required in \((CMM3)\), with the common
   height certificate \(1\) for each sampled template.  Therefore
   \cref{cor:capped-marginal-cohort-law-mass-reporter} gives \((DPG3)\).  The
   pointwise condition \((FCM4)\) is exactly the statement that the right side of
   \((FCM3)\) is nonnegative.

   If no randomized law satisfies \((FCM5)\), the value in \((FCM3)\) is
   strictly negative.  A minimizing cohort law \(\eta\) then has
   \(\max_BG(B,\eta)<0\), which is exactly \((FCM6)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Logarithmic top-prefix cohort separator]
   \label{cor:logarithmic-top-prefix-cohort-separator}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:finite-capped-marginal-cohort-oracle}.  Let \(\mathcal T\) be a
   finite family of retained prefix templates \(T=(W_T,K_T,\theta_T)\), with
   \(1\le K_T\le |W_T|\), such that every sublist \(U\subseteq W_T\) with
   \(|U|\le K_T\) is reportable with size certificate \(K_T\).  Put
   \[
      L_T
      =
      1+\left\lceil
      \log_2\max\left\{2,\frac{2K_T}{A\Lambda}\right\}
      \right\rceil .
      \tag{LTP0}
   \]
   If every cohort law \(\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}\) admits a
   template \(T\in\mathcal T\) satisfying
   \[
      D_\eta^{\theta_T}(W_T,K_T)
      \ge
      4A\Lambda L_T,
      \tag{LTP1}
   \]
   then the averaged dominated-load certificate \((DPG3)\) holds.

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then there is a cohort law \(\eta\) such
   that every retained prefix template \(T\in\mathcal T\) satisfies
   \[
      D_\eta^{\theta_T}(W_T,K_T)
      <
      4A\Lambda L_T .
      \tag{LTP2}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix \(\eta\) and \(T=(W_T,K_T,\theta_T)\).  Let \(U_T\) be a maximizing
   \(K_T\)-point subset in the definition of \(D_\eta^{\theta_T}(W_T,K_T)\).
   Since \(K_T\le |W_T|\), this subset exists.  By the sublist-closure
   hypothesis, the point-mass capped list law on \(U_T\) is reportable with size
   certificate \(K_T\) and height certificate \(1\), using \((FCM0)\).  Its
   marginal mass is exactly
   \[
      V_\eta(T)=D_\eta^{\theta_T}(W_T,K_T).
   \]
   Therefore \((LTP1)\) is the capped-marginal condition \((CMM2)\) for this
   deterministic law, and
   \cref{cor:capped-marginal-cohort-law-mass-reporter} gives \((DPG3)\) when
   every cohort law has such a template.

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then
   \cref{cor:capped-marginal-cohort-law-mass-reporter} gives a cohort law
   \(\eta\) for which every reportable capped list law satisfies \((CMM4)\).
   Applying that envelope to the point-mass law on the maximizing prefix
   \(U_T\) gives \((LTP2)\) for every \(T\in\mathcal T\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Dyadic-depth cancellation in the cohort prefix threshold]
   \label{cor:cohort-prefix-depth-cancellation}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:logarithmic-top-prefix-cohort-separator}, and substitute the
   constants \(A,\Lambda\) from \((DLE1)\).  Define
   \[
      \Theta_C
      =
      4A\Lambda
      =
      \frac{(1-\xi)\beta_0C_\eta\pi_1\kappa}
      {2CJK_{|P|}} .
      \tag{CDC0}
   \]
   Then the sufficient prefix condition \((LTP1)\) is equivalently
   \[
      D_\eta^{\theta_T}(W_T,K_T)
      \ge
      \Theta_C
      \left(
         1+\left\lceil
         \log_2\max\left\{2,\frac{8K_T}{\Theta_C}\right\}
         \right\rceil
      \right).
      \tag{CDC1}
   \]
   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then there is a cohort law \(\eta\) such
   that every retained prefix template satisfies the strict reverse of
   \((CDC1)\).

   In particular, the number \(H_m(\Delta)\) of dyadic annular size levels does
   not appear in the final prefix threshold.  It cancels between the efficiency
   threshold \(A=2H_m(\Delta)/C\) and the exact-load cohort mass
   \(\Lambda\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Multiplying the definitions in \((DLE1)\) gives
   \[
      4A\Lambda
      =
      4\cdot\frac{2H_m(\Delta)}{C}\cdot
      \frac{(1-\xi)\beta_0C_\eta\pi_1\kappa}
      {16J K_{|P|}H_m(\Delta)}
      =
      \Theta_C .
   \]
   Also \(A\Lambda=\Theta_C/4\), hence
   \[
      \frac{2K_T}{A\Lambda}=\frac{8K_T}{\Theta_C}.
   \]
   Substituting these identities into \((LTP1)\) and \((LTP2)\) gives
   \((CDC1)\) and its strict reverse.  The cancellation statement is the same
   algebra read off from the displayed product.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cardinality-net cohort prefix envelope]
   \label{cor:cardinality-net-cohort-prefix-envelope}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:cohort-prefix-depth-cancellation}.  Let
   \(b\ge1\).  Suppose the retained prefix templates are organized by retained
   parent containers and segment parameters, with a finite cardinality net
   \(\mathcal K_{W,\theta}\) satisfying: for every
   \(1\le h\le |W|\) there is \(K\in\mathcal K_{W,\theta}\) such that
   \[
      h\le K\le b h,
      \tag{CNC0}
   \]
   and every sublist of \(W\) of size at most such a \(K\) is reportable with
   size certificate \(K\).  Put
   \[
      L_b(h)
      =
      1+\left\lceil
      \log_2\max\left\{2,\frac{8bh}{\Theta_C}\right\}
      \right\rceil .
      \tag{CNC1}
   \]
   If every cohort law \(\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}\) admits
   \(W,\theta,h\) with \(1\le h\le |W|\) such that
   \[
      D_\eta^\theta(W,h)\ge\Theta_C L_b(h),
      \tag{CNC2}
   \]
   then the averaged dominated-load certificate \((DPG3)\) holds.

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then there is a cohort law \(\eta\) such
   that every retained parent container \(W\), segment \(\theta\), and analytic
   prefix size \(1\le h\le |W|\) satisfies
   \[
      D_\eta^\theta(W,h)<\Theta_C L_b(h).
      \tag{CNC3}
   \]
   For dyadic cardinalities one may take \(b=2\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((CNC2)\) holds, choose \(K\in\mathcal K_{W,\theta}\) satisfying
   \((CNC0)\).  The top \(K\)-prefix contains at least as much cohort mass as
   the top \(h\)-prefix, so
   \[
      D_\eta^\theta(W,K)\ge D_\eta^\theta(W,h).
   \]
   Also \(K\le bh\), hence the logarithmic factor in \((CDC1)\) for \(K\) is at
   most \(L_b(h)\).  Therefore the retained template \((W,K,\theta)\) satisfies
   \((CDC1)\), and
   \cref{cor:cohort-prefix-depth-cancellation} gives \((DPG3)\).

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then
   \cref{cor:cohort-prefix-depth-cancellation} gives a cohort law \(\eta\) for
   which every retained net size \(K\in\mathcal K_{W,\theta}\) satisfies the
   strict reverse of \((CDC1)\).  Given any analytic \(h\), choose
   \(K\in\mathcal K_{W,\theta}\) with \(h\le K\le bh\).  Since
   \(D_\eta^\theta(W,h)\le D_\eta^\theta(W,K)\), and the \(K\)-threshold is at
   most \(\Theta_C L_b(h)\), we get \((CNC3)\).

   Powers of two are \(2\)-dense from above, giving the final claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite prefix-template separation game]
   \label{cor:finite-prefix-template-separation-game}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:cardinality-net-cohort-prefix-envelope}, and fix a finite retained
   prefix-record pool \(\mathcal P_b\).  A record
   \(T\in\mathcal P_b\) consists of
   \[
      T=(W_T,\theta_T,h_T,K_T,U_T),
      \qquad
      U_T\subseteq W_T,\quad |U_T|=h_T,
      \qquad
      h_T\le K_T\le b h_T,
      \tag{FPT0}
   \]
   where \(K_T\in\mathcal K_{W_T,\theta_T}\) and every sublist of \(W_T\) of
   size at most \(K_T\) is reportable with size certificate \(K_T\).  Define
   the cohort value and verified surplus
   \[
      V_\eta(T)=\sum_{p\in U_T}d_\eta^{\theta_T}(p),
      \qquad
      G(T,\eta)=V_\eta(T)-\Theta_C L_b(h_T).
      \tag{FPT1}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \max_{\omega\in\Delta_{\mathcal P_b}}
      \min_{\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}}
      \sum_{T\in\mathcal P_b}\omega_TG(T,\eta)
      =
      \min_{\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}}
      \max_{T\in\mathcal P_b}G(T,\eta).
      \tag{FPT2}
   \]
   If the common value in \((FPT2)\) is nonnegative, then the averaged
   dominated-load certificate \((DPG3)\) holds.

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then there is a cohort law \(\eta\) such
   that, for this pool and indeed for every retained prefix-record pool
   satisfying \((FPT0)\), the strict inequalities
   \[
      G(T,\eta)<0
      \qquad(T\in\mathcal P_b)
      \tag{FPT3}
   \]
   hold.
   This same \(\eta\) is independent of the chosen finite pool.

   In particular, when the pool contains all reportable \(h\)-subsets of each
   retained parent \(W\), optimizing over \(U_T\) for fixed \(W,\theta,h\) is
   exactly the top-prefix quantity \(D_\eta^\theta(W,h)\).  Thus the build-time
   separation objective is the verified score
   \[
      D_\eta^\theta(W,h)-\Theta_C L_b(h),
      \tag{FPT4}
   \]
   or equivalently the ratio \(D_\eta^\theta(W,h)/L_b(h)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The set \(\mathcal E_{\rm load}\) is finite, and \(G(T,\eta)\) is linear in
   \(\eta\) for each fixed retained record \(T\).  Hence \((FPT2)\) is the
   finite matrix-game minimax theorem.

   If the value is nonnegative, choose a maximizing law \(\omega\).  For every
   cohort law \(\eta\), the \(\omega\)-average of \(G(T,\eta)\) is nonnegative,
   so some support record has \(G(T,\eta)\ge0\).  For that record,
   \[
      D_\eta^{\theta_T}(W_T,h_T)\ge V_\eta(T)\ge\Theta_C L_b(h_T),
   \]
   because \(U_T\) is one feasible \(h_T\)-subset of \(W_T\).  Therefore
   \((CNC2)\) holds for every cohort law, and
   \cref{cor:cardinality-net-cohort-prefix-envelope} gives \((DPG3)\).

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then
   \cref{cor:cardinality-net-cohort-prefix-envelope} gives a cohort law
   \(\eta\) satisfying the strict envelope \((CNC3)\) for every retained
   \(W,\theta,h\).  For any record \(T\),
   \[
      V_\eta(T)
      \le
      D_\eta^{\theta_T}(W_T,h_T)
      <
      \Theta_C L_b(h_T),
   \]
   which is \((FPT3)\).

   The final statement is only the definition of
   \(D_\eta^\theta(W,h)\) as the maximum \(d_\eta^\theta\)-mass over
   \(h\)-subsets of \(W\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Prefix-template column generation]
   \label{cor:prefix-template-column-generation}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:finite-prefix-template-separation-game}.  Let
   \(\mathcal U_b\) be a finite full universe of retained prefix records
   satisfying \((FPT0)\).  Suppose that for every cohort law \(\eta\) one has
   a separation oracle that either returns a record \(T\in\mathcal U_b\) with
   \[
      G(T,\eta)\ge0
      \tag{PTC0}
   \]
   or certifies
   \[
      \max_{T\in\mathcal U_b}G(T,\eta)<0 .
      \tag{PTC1}
   \]
   Then the following column-generation procedure is complete for this
   universe.  Start with any nonempty finite pool
   \(\mathcal P\subseteq\mathcal U_b\).  Repeatedly solve the restricted game
   \[
      v(\mathcal P)
      =
      \min_{\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}}
      \max_{T\in\mathcal P}G(T,\eta).
      \tag{PTC2}
   \]
   If \(v(\mathcal P)\ge0\), then \((DPG3)\) holds.  If
   \(v(\mathcal P)<0\), let \(\eta_{\mathcal P}\) be a minimizer and call the
   separator on \(\eta_{\mathcal P}\).  If it returns \(T\), add \(T\) to the
   pool; if it certifies \((PTC1)\), then the full universe
   \(\mathcal U_b\) cannot satisfy the prefix-template sufficient condition.

   Consequently, if
   \[
      \min_{\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}}
      \max_{T\in\mathcal U_b}G(T,\eta)\ge0,
      \tag{PTC3}
   \]
   the procedure terminates after at most \(|\mathcal U_b|\) successful
   additions with a pool proving \((DPG3)\).  The cost of solving the games and
   running the separator is preprocessing only; the retained index pays only
   for the final verified pool.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(v(\mathcal P)\ge0\), then
   \cref{cor:finite-prefix-template-separation-game} applied to the current
   pool gives \((DPG3)\).

   Suppose \(v(\mathcal P)<0\) and let \(\eta_{\mathcal P}\) attain the
   minimum in \((PTC2)\).  Then
   \[
      G(T,\eta_{\mathcal P})<0
      \qquad(T\in\mathcal P),
      \tag{PTC4}
   \]
   because the maximum over the current pool is negative.  Hence any separator
   output satisfying \((PTC0)\) is not already in \(\mathcal P\), so a
   successful call strictly enlarges the pool.  Since \(\mathcal U_b\) is
   finite, there can be at most \(|\mathcal U_b|\) successful additions.

   If the separator certifies \((PTC1)\) at some minimizer, then the full
   universe has negative value at that cohort law, so \((PTC3)\) is false.  In
   particular, \(\mathcal U_b\) does not contain a prefix record satisfying
   \((CNC2)\) for that \(\eta\), and this prefix universe alone cannot close
   the dominated-load certificate through
   \cref{cor:cardinality-net-cohort-prefix-envelope}.

   Under \((PTC3)\), the certificate \((PTC1)\) can never be valid.  Therefore
   the finite enlargement process must eventually reach a pool with
   nonnegative restricted value, and the first paragraph gives \((DPG3)\).
   The last sentence is just the separation between build-time search and the
   retained verified records in the finite cover LP.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[One-sided prefix-value column generation]
   \label{cor:one-sided-prefix-value-column-generation}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:prefix-template-column-generation}.  For a cohort law \(\eta\),
   call \((T,X)\) a one-sided prefix-value report if \(T\in\mathcal U_b\) and
   \[
      0\le X\le V_\eta(T).
      \tag{OPV0}
   \]
   The report is separating if
   \[
      X\ge \Theta_C L_b(h_T).
      \tag{OPV1}
   \]
   Suppose that for every cohort law \(\eta\) a build-time oracle either
   returns a separating one-sided prefix-value report or certifies
   \[
      \max_{T\in\mathcal U_b}G(T,\eta)<0 .
      \tag{OPV2}
   \]
   Then the column-generation procedure of
   \cref{cor:prefix-template-column-generation} remains complete when the
   separator call is replaced by this one-sided oracle: on a successful call,
   add only the verified record \(T\) to the pool, and score it in all later
   restricted games by its exact payoff \(G(T,\cdot)\).

   Consequently, if the full universe satisfies \((PTC3)\), the procedure
   terminates after finitely many successful one-sided reports with a pool
   proving \((DPG3)\).  If the oracle returns \((OPV2)\), then the full universe
   cannot satisfy the prefix-template sufficient condition.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   A separating report satisfies
   \[
      G(T,\eta)
      =
      V_\eta(T)-\Theta_C L_b(h_T)
      \ge
      X-\Theta_C L_b(h_T)
      \ge0 .
      \tag{OPV3}
   \]
   Hence a successful one-sided oracle call is also a valid separator output
   satisfying \((PTC0)\).  If the current restricted value is negative at the
   minimizing law \(\eta_{\mathcal P}\), every current pool record has
   \(G(T,\eta_{\mathcal P})<0\); therefore any successful one-sided report has
   \(T\notin\mathcal P\) and strictly enlarges the pool.  The rest is exactly
   \cref{cor:prefix-template-column-generation}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[One-sided proposal-law prefix separator]
   \label{cor:one-sided-proposal-law-prefix-separator}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:one-sided-prefix-value-column-generation}, and fix a cohort law
   \(\eta\).  A finite \(\eta\)-proposal law is a finite probability law
   \(\zeta\) over pairs \(R=(T_R,X_R)\) such that
   \[
      T_R\in\mathcal U_b,
      \qquad
      0\le X_R\le V_\eta(T_R).
      \tag{OPL0}
   \]
   Define its certified surplus by
   \[
      \Psi_\eta(R)
      =
      X_R-\Theta_C L_b(h_{T_R}).
      \tag{OPL1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \E_{R\sim\zeta}\Psi_\eta(R)\ge0,
      \tag{OPL2}
   \]
   then the support of \(\zeta\) contains a separating one-sided prefix-value
   report.  Consequently the separator call in
   \cref{cor:one-sided-prefix-value-column-generation} may be implemented by
   any randomized, batched, or learned proposal generator whose realized finite
   support is verified by \((OPL0)\) and whose certified average surplus
   satisfies \((OPL2)\); only the exposed deterministic record \(T_R\) is added
   to the retained pool.

   Conversely, if the exact full-universe certificate \((OPV2)\) holds for
   \(\eta\), then every finite \(\eta\)-proposal law satisfies
   \[
      \E_{R\sim\zeta}\Psi_\eta(R)<0 .
      \tag{OPL3}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If every support point had \(\Psi_\eta(R)<0\), the finite average would be
   negative.  Hence \((OPL2)\) gives some \(R=(T_R,X_R)\) with
   \(\Psi_\eta(R)\ge0\), which is exactly \((OPV1)\) together with
   \((OPV0)\).

   Conversely, if \((OPV2)\) holds, then for every report in the support,
   \[
      \Psi_\eta(R)
      \le
      V_\eta(T_R)-\Theta_C L_b(h_{T_R})
      =
      G(T_R,\eta)
      <
      0 .
   \]
   Averaging gives \((OPL3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Sampled one-sided prefix separator]
   \label{cor:sampled-one-sided-prefix-separator}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:one-sided-prefix-value-column-generation}.  Fix a cohort law
   \(\eta\), and suppose preprocessing has a sampleable law \(\mathfrak P_\eta\)
   on one-sided prefix-value reports \(R=(T_R,X_R)\) satisfying \((OPV0)\).
   Let
   \[
      \Psi_\eta(R)=X_R-\Theta_C L_b(h_{T_R})
      \tag{SOP0}
   \]
   and assume \(\Psi_\eta\) is integrable and
   \[
      \E_{R\sim\mathfrak P_\eta}\Psi_\eta(R)\ge0.
      \tag{SOP1}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \Pr_{R\sim\mathfrak P_\eta}[\Psi_\eta(R)\ge0]>0.
      \tag{SOP2}
   \]
   Consequently, repeated independent sampling from \(\mathfrak P_\eta\), with
   exact verification of \((OPV0)\) and \(\Psi_\eta(R)\ge0\) after each sample,
   is a Las Vegas separator: it halts almost surely with a separating
   one-sided prefix-value report, and if the probability in \((SOP2)\) is
   \(\pi_\eta\), its expected number of samples is \(1/\pi_\eta\).

   Therefore the column-generation procedure remains complete with uncharged
   randomized preprocessing if, for every minimizing cohort law encountered by
   the restricted game, either an exact oracle certifies \((OPV2)\) or
   preprocessing supplies such a sampleable law.  The retained index still pays
   only for the deterministic verified records that are actually accepted.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(\Pr[\Psi_\eta(R)\ge0]=0\), then \(\Psi_\eta(R)<0\) almost surely.  Since
   \(\Psi_\eta\) is integrable, this implies
   \(\E\Psi_\eta(R)<0\) unless \(\Psi_\eta=0\) almost surely, which contradicts
   \(\Psi_\eta<0\) almost surely.  Hence \((SOP2)\) follows from \((SOP1)\).

   A sample with \(\Psi_\eta(R)\ge0\) satisfies \(X_R\ge\Theta_C L_b(h_{T_R})\),
   so it is separating by \((OPV1)\).  Independent repetitions hit this event
   almost surely, and the geometric waiting-time formula gives expectation
   \(1/\pi_\eta\).  The final statement is
   \cref{cor:one-sided-prefix-value-column-generation}: every successful
   sampled report is a valid separator output, while \((OPV2)\) is the exact
   no-column certificate.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Sampled soft-prefix proposal separator]
   \label{cor:sampled-soft-prefix-proposal-separator}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:sampled-one-sided-prefix-separator}.  A soft prefix proposal for a
   cohort law \(\eta\) is a tuple
   \[
      R=(W_R,\theta_R,h_R,K_R,\pi_R,X_R)
   \]
   such that \(1\le h_R\le |W_R|\) is an integer,
   \(h_R\le K_R\le b h_R\), \(K_R\in\mathcal K_{W_R,\theta_R}\), every sublist
   of \(W_R\) of size at most \(K_R\) is reportable with size certificate
   \(K_R\),
   \[
      0\le \pi_{R,p}\le1,\qquad
      \sum_{p\in W_R}\pi_{R,p}\le h_R,
      \tag{SFP0}
   \]
   and the proposal gives a one-sided value certificate
   \[
      0\le X_R\le
      \sum_{p\in W_R}\pi_{R,p}d_\eta^{\theta_R}(p).
      \tag{SFP1}
   \]
   Assume that whenever such a tuple is sampled, preprocessing can materialize an
   \(h_R\)-point maximizer
   \[
      U_R^*\in
      \arg\max_{\substack{U\subseteq W_R\\ |U|=h_R}}
      \sum_{p\in U}d_\eta^{\theta_R}(p),
      \tag{SFP2}
   \]
   and that the corresponding record
   \(T_R=(W_R,\theta_R,h_R,K_R,U_R^*)\) lies in \(\mathcal U_b\).  If
   preprocessing has a sampleable law on soft prefix proposals with integrable
   surplus and for which
   \[
      \E\bigl[X_R-\Theta_C L_b(h_R)\bigr]\ge0,
      \tag{SFP3}
   \]
   then repeated sampling, exact materialization of \(U_R^*\), and verification of
   \(X_R\ge\Theta_C L_b(h_R)\) form a Las Vegas separator for the current cohort
   law.

   Thus a randomized \(k\)-means++, additive-quantization, range-reporting, or
   learned panel may be analyzed only through soft inclusion responsibilities and
   a one-sided lower value certificate.  The retained index still stores only the
   deterministic prefix record \(T_R\), never the soft proposal itself.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For any admissible proposal, the top-\(h_R\) set \(U_R^*\) dominates the soft
   responsibility vector.  Indeed, the polytope
   \[
      \left\{x\in[0,1]^{W_R}:\sum_{p\in W_R}x_p\le h_R\right\}
   \]
   has integral vertices, and every such vertex is the indicator of a subset of
   size at most \(h_R\).  Since \(d_\eta^{\theta_R}(p)\ge0\), the maximum of the
   linear functional \(\sum_p x_p d_\eta^{\theta_R}(p)\) over this polytope is
   attained by an \(h_R\)-point top prefix.  Hence
   \[
      V_\eta(T_R)
      =
      \sum_{p\in U_R^*}d_\eta^{\theta_R}(p)
      \ge
      \sum_{p\in W_R}\pi_{R,p}d_\eta^{\theta_R}(p)
      \ge X_R .
      \tag{SFP4}
   \]
   Therefore \((T_R,X_R)\) is a one-sided prefix-value report in the sense of
   \((OPV0)\).  Its surplus is exactly
   \(X_R-\Theta_C L_b(h_R)\), so \((SFP3)\) is the expectation hypothesis
   \((SOP1)\) for the induced law on one-sided reports.  Applying
   \cref{cor:sampled-one-sided-prefix-separator} gives positive probability of a
   separating sample and the stated Las Vegas separator.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Cardinality-net cohort superlevel reporter]
   \label{cor:cardinality-net-cohort-superlevel-reporter}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:cardinality-net-cohort-prefix-envelope}.  For a cohort law
   \(\eta\), a retained parent container \(W\), a segment parameter \(\theta\),
   and a level \(\delta>0\), call
   \[
      (W,\theta,\delta,U,h,K,X)
   \]
   a certified cardinality-net superlevel report if
   \[
      U\subseteq W,\qquad |U|=h>0,\qquad
      d_\eta^\theta(p)\ge\delta\quad(p\in U),
      \tag{CNS0}
   \]
   \[
      K\in\mathcal K_{W,\theta},
      \qquad h\le K\le bh,
      \tag{CNS1}
   \]
   every sublist of \(W\) of size at most \(K\) is reportable with size
   certificate \(K\), and the report gives the one-sided certificate
   \[
      0\le X\le\delta h .
      \tag{CNS2}
   \]
   Its certified surplus is
   \[
      \Phi_\eta(W,\theta,\delta,U,h,K,X)
      =
      X-\Theta_C L_b(h).
      \tag{CNS3}
   \]
   If every cohort law \(\eta\in\Delta_{\mathcal E_{\rm load}}\) admits a
   certified cardinality-net superlevel report with
   \[
      \Phi_\eta(W,\theta,\delta,U,h,K,X)\ge0,
      \tag{CNS4}
   \]
   then the averaged dominated-load certificate \((DPG3)\) holds.  More
   generally, it is enough that every \(\eta\) admits a finite probability law
   over such reports with
   \[
      \E\Phi_\eta(W,\theta,\delta,U,h,K,X)\ge0,
      \tag{CNS5}
   \]
   because some deterministic report in the support has nonnegative certified
   surplus.

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then there is a cohort law \(\eta\) for
   which every certified cardinality-net superlevel report satisfies
   \[
      \Phi_\eta(W,\theta,\delta,U,h,K,X)<0.
      \tag{CNS6}
   \]
   In particular every such report has
   \[
      \delta h<\Theta_C L_b(h).
      \tag{CNS7}
   \]

   In the finite-universe setting of
   \cref{cor:prefix-template-column-generation}, any report satisfying
   \((CNS4)\) whose record
   \[
      T=(W,\theta,h,K,U)
   \]
   lies in the implicit universe \(\mathcal U_b\) is a valid separator output:
   it satisfies \(G(T,\eta)\ge0\).
   Equivalently, \((T,X)\) is a separating one-sided prefix-value report in the
   sense of \cref{cor:one-sided-prefix-value-column-generation}.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let \((W,\theta,\delta,U,h,K,X)\) be a report satisfying \((CNS4)\).  Since
   every point of \(U\) has \(d_\eta^\theta(p)\ge\delta\),
   \[
      \sum_{p\in U}d_\eta^\theta(p)\ge\delta h\ge X
      \ge\Theta_C L_b(h).
      \tag{CNS8}
   \]
   Hence the top \(h\)-prefix in \(W\) also has mass at least
   \(\Theta_C L_b(h)\), so \((CNC2)\) holds for this cohort law.  If every
   cohort law has such a report, then
   \cref{cor:cardinality-net-cohort-prefix-envelope} gives \((DPG3)\).  The
   randomized-report variant follows because a finite average of
   \(\Phi_\eta\) is nonnegative only if some support report has
   \(\Phi_\eta\ge0\).

   Conversely, if \((DPG3)\) fails, then
   \cref{cor:cardinality-net-cohort-prefix-envelope} gives a cohort law
   \(\eta\) satisfying \((CNC3)\) for every retained parent, segment, and
   analytic prefix size.  For any certified report, the reported list is one
   \(h\)-subset of \(W\), so
   \[
      X\le\delta h
      \le
      \sum_{p\in U}d_\eta^\theta(p)
      \le
      D_\eta^\theta(W,h)
      <
      \Theta_C L_b(h).
      \tag{CNS9}
   \]
   This proves \((CNS6)\), and \((CNS7)\) follows from the same displayed
   inequality without \(X\).

   Finally, in the finite prefix-template game the corresponding record has
   \[
      V_\eta(T)
      =
      \sum_{p\in U}d_\eta^\theta(p)
      \ge X\ge\Theta_C L_b(h),
   \]
   hence \(G(T,\eta)\ge0\).
\end{proof}

The lemma is the fractional version of the dominated-load endpoint.  It does not
claim the remaining geometric theorem.  Rather, after terminal low-load levels
and the \(A\)-boundary alternative have been dealt with by
\((DLE2)\)--\((DLE3)\), a finite proposal pool fails only if the dual can choose
level weights and one dominated query distribution per level so that every
affordable record has mean efficiency below \(A\).  By
\cref{cor:exact-load-dominated-proposal-obstruction}, the same obstruction is a
law over exact-load cohorts, each integral except for one boundary query.  Thus a
list-decoding, LP-range-reporting, additive-quantization, or seeded clustering
oracle should be analyzed against the single weighted cohort objective in
\((EDP2)\) or \((EDP3)\).  Equivalently,
\cref{cor:exact-load-cohort-law-separator} says that the remaining finite-pool
theorem is to beat every law over these cohorts by one affordable retained
record.  Finally,
\cref{cor:cohort-law-scalar-prefix-normal-form} rewrites that record search as a
scalar top-prefix problem for the cohort degree \(d_\eta^\theta\), not as a
choice of disjoint dense clusters.  In the weak-type form of
\cref{cor:cohort-law-weak-type-superlevel}, the remaining range-reporting target
is just to find one affordable scalar superlevel with \(\delta h\ge A\Lambda\).
\Cref{cor:certified-cohort-law-superlevel-reporter} is the build-facing version:
the decoder need only give a one-sided lower certificate \(X\le\delta h\) and a
certified size bound \(K\) for the exact retained superlevel; any finite
randomized panel whose expected certificate reaches \(A\Lambda\) exposes a
deterministic affordable record.  Thus \(k\)-means++ panels, additive
quantization, list recovery, or LP range reporting can be analyzed through
certified superlevel reports rather than exact dense-cluster choices.
\Cref{cor:certified-cohort-law-mass-reporter} removes the need to guess the
level directly: it is enough to certify total cohort degree \(V\) in a retained
container, a pointwise height bound \(B\), and a size bound \(K\).  A dyadic
layer-cake then finds a reportable superlevel with certified yield
\(V/O(\log(BK/V))\).
\Cref{cor:explicit-cohort-law-mass-envelope} removes the remaining implicit
