level dependence: failure leaves one cohort law for which every retained mass
certificate obeys \(V=O(A\Lambda\log(2BK/(A\Lambda)))\).  Thus the geometric
theorem can target a direct mass violation rather than optimizing over
thresholds.
\Cref{cor:capped-marginal-cohort-law-mass-reporter} is the soft proposal
interface: a \(k\)-means++, additive-quantization, or list-decoding panel may
output a finite law over capped hard lists and be analyzed only through its
inclusion marginals.  If the parent container is closed under sublists, even a
responsibility vector with total mass at most \(K\) is enough, by integral
decomposition of the capped hypersimplex.
\Cref{cor:finite-capped-marginal-cohort-oracle} packages the build step as a
finite matrix game over generated soft panels: either a randomized panel law
beats every cohort law at the explicit logarithmic mass threshold, or one cohort
law witnesses that every generated panel is below threshold.  Because the
cohort degrees have unit height under \((GNR1)\), the logarithmic factor depends
only on the size certificate \(K_B\).
\Cref{cor:logarithmic-top-prefix-cohort-separator} removes the last soft
artifact for sublist-closed retained containers: it is enough to find a
top-\(K\) prefix whose cohort-degree mass beats
\(4A\Lambda\bigl(1+\lceil\log_2\max\{2,2K/(A\Lambda)\}\rceil\bigr)\).  Failure
leaves the same explicit prefix envelope for every retained template.
\Cref{cor:cohort-prefix-depth-cancellation} substitutes the annular constants:
\(4A\Lambda=(1-\xi)\beta_0C_\eta\pi_1\kappa/(2CJK_{|P|})\), so the dyadic level
count \(H_m(\Delta)\) cancels out of the retained prefix threshold.
\Cref{cor:cardinality-net-cohort-prefix-envelope} removes exact-cardinality
search: a factor-\(b\) retained cardinality net, in particular dyadic sizes
with \(b=2\), leaves only the explicit envelope with \(K\) replaced by \(bh\).
\Cref{cor:finite-prefix-template-separation-game} is the final finite
column-generation form of this target: preprocessing may spend arbitrary time
proposing \(W,\theta,h\) and candidate sublists, but the retained column is
accepted only when the verified surplus
\(V_\eta(T)-\Theta_C L_b(h_T)\) is nonnegative against the current cohort law.
If the dominated-load certificate fails, one cohort law witnesses negative
surplus for every generated template.
\Cref{cor:prefix-template-column-generation} turns this into an exact
build-time algorithm for any finite implicit universe: solve the restricted
game, ask the separator for a nonnegative-surplus prefix against the minimizing
cohort law, and add only verified records.  If the full universe satisfies the
prefix condition, this terminates after finitely many additions; if the
separator proves no such prefix exists, the certificate identifies the actual
cohort-law obstruction for that universe.
\Cref{cor:one-sided-prefix-value-column-generation} weakens the required
separator output further: the build oracle may return any retained record with a
one-sided lower value certificate \(X\le V_\eta(T)\) beating
\(\Theta_C L_b(h_T)\); later games still use the exact verified payoff of the
record.
\Cref{cor:one-sided-proposal-law-prefix-separator} makes this compatible with
randomized proposal mechanisms: a finite \(k\)-means++, additive-quantization,
range-reporting, or list-decoding batch is useful exactly when its verified
average one-sided surplus is nonnegative, and then averaging exposes one
deterministic column.
\Cref{cor:sampled-one-sided-prefix-separator} removes even the finite-batch
enumeration requirement from the theorem target: a sampleable proposal law with
nonnegative expected verified surplus can be searched by unlimited
preprocessing until a separating report is found, and only that report is
retained.
\Cref{cor:sampled-soft-prefix-proposal-separator} gives the same interface for
soft responsibilities: a proposal may output fractional inclusion weights, after
which preprocessing materializes the exact top-degree prefix and retains only
that deterministic record.
\Cref{cor:cardinality-net-cohort-superlevel-reporter} removes the need for the
separator to optimize an exact top prefix: any certified threshold list with
one-sided value \(X\ge\Theta_C L_b(h)\) is already a valid column, and failure
leaves the strict weak-type cap \(\delta h<\Theta_C L_b(h)\) for every retained
threshold-list report.
Pools with different congestion guesses may be split into dyadic \(C\)-strata and
tested by the same game within each stratum.

\begin{corollary}[Load-quantile recycled obstruction profile]
   \label{cor:load-quantile-recycled-obstruction-profile}
   Work in the notation of
   \cref{lem:finite-prefix-recycled-threshold-screen}.  The threshold screen
   \((FPS1)\) fails if and only if
   \[
      L_\infty\ge\Lambda ,
      \tag{LQO1}
   \]
   the boundary alternative fails, namely
   \[
      A L_0-S_0>0
      \qquad\text{or}\qquad
      L_0>\Lambda ,
      \tag{LQO2}
   \]
   and, whenever \(L_0<\Lambda\), the first load-crossing index
   \[
      j=\min\{i\in\{1,\ldots,k\}:L_i\ge\Lambda\}
      \tag{LQO3}
   \]
   satisfies the strict quantile deficit
   \[
      a_jL_j-S_j>(a_j-A)\Lambda .
      \tag{LQO4}
   \]
   Thus every failed scan has either \(L_0\ge\Lambda\), where the \(A\)-boundary
   already blocks the screen, or one strict deficit at the weighted
   \(\Lambda\)-quantile breakpoint.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   This is the exact negation of
   \cref{lem:load-quantile-recycled-threshold-screen}.  Failure of \((LQS2)\) is
   \((LQO1)\).  Since \(A L_0-S_0\ge0\), failure of \((LQS1)\) is \((LQO2)\).  If
   \(L_0<\Lambda\), then \((LQO1)\) makes the index \(j\) in \((LQO3)\)
   well-defined, and failure of \((LQS3)\) is exactly \((LQO4)\).  If
   \(L_0\ge\Lambda\), the quantile alternative \((LQS3)\) is inapplicable, so no
   additional condition remains.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exact-load recycled obstruction profile]
   \label{cor:exact-load-recycled-obstruction-profile}
   Work in the notation of
   \cref{lem:finite-prefix-recycled-threshold-screen}.  The threshold screen
   \((FPS1)\) fails if and only if \(L_\infty\ge\Lambda\), the boundary
   alternative \((LQS1)\) fails, and, in the non-boundary case
   \(L_0<\Lambda\), the fractional \(\Lambda\)-load quantile capacity satisfies
   \[
      \widehat S_\Lambda<A\Lambda .
      \tag{ELO1}
   \]
   Thus, after excluding terminal low load and the \(A\)-boundary case, the
   entire residual obstruction is that the lowest-efficiency fractional prefix
   of exact load \(\Lambda\) has average capacity strictly below \(A\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   This is \cref{cor:load-quantile-recycled-obstruction-profile} with the
   quantile deficit \((LQO4)\) rewritten by
   \cref{lem:exact-load-recycled-quantile-screen}.  The exact-load rewrite is
   needed only when \(L_0<\Lambda\), which is precisely the non-boundary case in
   which the quantile breakpoint is active.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Variational exact-load recycled obstruction profile]
   \label{cor:variational-exact-load-recycled-obstruction-profile}
   Work in the notation of
   \cref{lem:finite-prefix-recycled-threshold-screen}.  The threshold screen
   \((FPS1)\) fails if and only if \(L_\infty\ge\Lambda\), the boundary
   alternative \((LQS1)\) fails, and, in the non-boundary case \(L_0<\Lambda\),
   there exists a fractional sublayer \(0\le y_q\le1\) of exact load
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q^+}y_q\ell_q=\Lambda
      \tag{VEO1}
   \]
   whose capacity is strictly deficient:
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q^+}y_qs_q<A\Lambda .
      \tag{VEO2}
   \]
   Moreover, the deficient sublayer may be chosen as the lowest-efficiency
   fractional prefix from \cref{lem:exact-load-recycled-quantile-screen}.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \cref{lem:variational-exact-load-recycled-screen}, the minimum capacity
   among exact-load fractional sublayers is \(\widehat S_\Lambda\).  Thus the
   exact-load obstruction \((ELO1)\) from
   \cref{cor:exact-load-recycled-obstruction-profile} is equivalent to the
   existence of a fractional sublayer satisfying \((VEO1)\)--\((VEO2)\), and an
   optimizer is the lowest-efficiency fractional prefix.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Dominated-load recycled obstruction profile]
   \label{cor:dominated-load-recycled-obstruction-profile}
   Work in the notation of
   \cref{lem:finite-prefix-recycled-threshold-screen}.  The threshold screen
   \((FPS1)\) fails if and only if \(L_\infty\ge\Lambda\), the boundary
   alternative \((LQS1)\) fails, and, in the non-boundary case \(L_0<\Lambda\),
   there exists a probability vector \(\nu\) satisfying
   \[
      0\le\nu_q\le\frac{\ell_q}{\Lambda},
      \qquad
      \sum_{q\in Q^+}\nu_q=1,
      \tag{DLO1}
   \]
   whose average efficiency is strictly deficient:
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q^+}\nu_q\sigma_q<A .
      \tag{DLO2}
   \]
   Moreover, the deficient \(\nu\) may be chosen by filling the lowest
   efficiencies up to the load cap \(\ell_q/\Lambda\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   This is \cref{cor:variational-exact-load-recycled-obstruction-profile} under
   the change of variables from \cref{lem:dominated-load-recycled-screen}.  The
   extremal choice follows from the lowest-efficiency prefix optimizer in
   \cref{lem:variational-exact-load-recycled-screen}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite-prefix recycled obstruction profile]
   \label{cor:finite-prefix-recycled-obstruction-profile}
   Work in the notation of
   \cref{lem:finite-prefix-recycled-threshold-screen}.  The threshold screen
   \((FPS1)\) fails if and only if
   \[
      L_\infty\ge\Lambda ,
      \tag{FPO1}
   \]
   \[
      a_iL_i-S_i>(a_i-A)\Lambda
      \qquad(1\le i\le k),
      \tag{FPO2}
   \]
   and
   \[
      A L_0-S_0>0
      \qquad\text{or}\qquad
      L_0>\Lambda .
      \tag{FPO3}
   \]
   Equivalently, every remaining failed finite-prefix scan has a strict
   positive breakpoint deficit profile
   \[
      a_i(L_i-\Lambda)-(S_i-A\Lambda)>0
      \qquad(1\le i\le k),
      \tag{FPO4}
   \]
   together with large total load and a nontrivial \(A\)-boundary obstruction.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   This is the exact negation of the three finite alternatives in
   \cref{lem:finite-prefix-recycled-threshold-screen}.  The only point to note
   is that \(A L_0-S_0\ge0\), because every query in the \(a_0=A\) prefix has
   \(\sigma_q\le A\).  Thus failure of \((FPS2)\) is exactly \((FPO3)\), while
   failure of \((FPS3)\) and \((FPS4)\) gives \((FPO2)\) and \((FPO1)\).
   The displayed form \((FPO4)\) is just \((FPO2)\) rearranged.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Integrated recycled-threshold obstruction]
   \label{lem:integrated-recycled-threshold-obstruction}
   Work in the notation of
   \cref{lem:finite-prefix-recycled-threshold-screen}.  Define
   the low-efficiency shortfall curve
   \[
      M(t)=
      \sum_{q\in Q^+}(t-\sigma_q)_+\ell_q
      =
      tL(t)-S(t)
      \qquad(t>A),
   \]
   and the excess-area curve
   \[
      E(t)=M(t)-(t-A)\Lambda .
      \tag{ITO1}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      E(t)=
      A L_0-S_0
      +
      \int_A^t (L(u)-\Lambda)\,du
      \qquad(t>A),
      \tag{ITO2}
   \]
   where \(L(u)=\sum_{\sigma_q\le u}\ell_q\).  Consequently the threshold
   screen \((FPS1)\) fails if and only if
   \[
      A L_0-S_0
      +
      \int_A^t (L(u)-\Lambda)\,du
      >
      0
      \qquad\text{for every }t>A.
      \tag{ITO3}
   \]
   In particular, a failed finite-prefix scan is equivalently a cumulative
   excess-load profile whose area never drops to zero.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   The equality \(M(t)=tL(t)-S(t)\) follows by grouping the terms with
   \(\sigma_q\le t\).  Extend \(M\) continuously to \(A\).  It is continuous and
   piecewise affine, and its derivative agrees with the step function \(L(u)\)
   away from the finitely many efficiency breakpoints.  Also
   \[
      M(A)=\sum_{\sigma_q\le A}(A-\sigma_q)\ell_q=A L_0-S_0.
   \]
   Integrating this step function from \(A\) to \(t\) gives
   \[
      M(t)=A L_0-S_0+\int_A^t L(u)\,du,
   \]
   and subtracting \((t-A)\Lambda\) gives \((ITO2)\).  The threshold screen is
   exactly the existence of \(t>A\) with \(E(t)\le0\), so its failure is
   \((ITO3)\).
\end{proof}

The transport formulation is useful because it cleanly separates the two
remaining tasks.  The annular witnesses are far points and still cannot be used
as cover columns.  A geometric or list-recovery argument must instead construct
a low-congestion transport from those annular incidences into actual
near-shadow mass.  If it does, \cref{lem:annular-shadow-transport-reporter}
turns that transport into the same verified scalar reporter as before.  If the
LP remains infeasible, \cref{cor:annular-shadow-transport-obstruction} and
\cref{cor:annular-shadow-congestion-lower-bound} say that every such transport
must have large congestion.  \Cref{lem:annular-shadow-cut-normal-form} and
\cref{cor:cut-certified-annular-reporter} make the same failure cut-based:
for every proposed retained container and target mass, some sublayer of the
annular queries has annular demand larger than its true near-shadow neighborhood
capacity plus the allowed unshipped tail.  Thus the current irreducible
obstruction can be stated as a purely geometric Hall failure: a query-price-heavy
annular layer exists, but no retained smaller-radius container receives a large
fraction of its incidences into the true near-shadow potential at
Renyi-affordable congestion.  \Cref{cor:half-mass-excess-cut-obstruction}
removes the last target-mass parameter: any container whose half-mass transport
would be affordable must have a sublayer \(Y\) with excess
\(\sum_{q\in Y}b_q-C D_W^\theta(Y)>B_{\rm tot}/2\).  The next geometric theorem
can therefore try to rule out these excess cuts directly, or else feed the
large-excess sublayer back into the spherical far-load analysis.
\Cref{lem:cut-recycled-annular-sublayer} makes that feedback canonical: every
such cut contains a dyadic cut-restricted annular layer that preserves a
logarithmic fraction of the annular load while the proposed retained core sees
only \(O(H_m(\Delta)/C)\) times that load as true near-shadow capacity.  Thus the
remaining obstruction can be searched as a weighted list-recovery/range-reporting
problem on these recycled sublayers, rather than as a choice of disjoint dense
clusters.  Equivalently,
\cref{cor:recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices} says that a separator only has
to rule out those recycled layers for one affordable retained container; doing so
closes the local fractional cover.
\Cref{lem:lagrange-recycled-sublayer-screen} and
\cref{cor:lagrange-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices} give the additive form
of the same target: for each dyadic annular size level, it is enough to find a
positive multiplier \(\lambda\) for which the total positive query deficit
\(\sum_q((2H/C+\lambda)\Delta'\bar\tau_q-s_{W,\theta}(q))_+\) is below the
Lagrange budget.  \Cref{lem:fractional-recycled-layer-dual-normal-form}
identifies this condition as the positive-multiplier dual certificate for a
fractional bad-sublayer knapsack.  Thus the remaining separator can be searched
as a one-dimensional dual screen over query-wise near-shadow masses, rather
than as an all-subsets Hall check.  \Cref{lem:threshold-recycled-bad-layers}
gives the matching primal search form: any fractional bad sublayer is witnessed
by a low-efficiency prefix in the ratios \(s_{W,\theta}(q)/(\Delta'\bar\tau_q)\),
with at most one fractional boundary level.
\Cref{cor:threshold-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices} packages this into a
build-facing certificate: for each dyadic annular size level it is enough to
sort queries by that efficiency and find one threshold whose low-efficiency
prefix passes the scalar inequality.
\Cref{lem:finite-prefix-recycled-threshold-screen} and
\cref{cor:finite-prefix-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices} make the search
finite: only the sorted prefix breakpoints, the right-limit at \(A\), and the
terminal low-total-load case can certify the threshold screen.
\Cref{lem:load-quantile-recycled-threshold-screen} and
\cref{cor:load-quantile-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices} sharpen this
further: because the excess curve is convex, all positive breakpoints collapse
to the first one whose cumulative load reaches \(\Lambda\).  The build-time
certificate is therefore a weighted-quantile test, not a full prefix scan.
\Cref{lem:exact-load-recycled-quantile-screen} and
\cref{cor:exact-load-recycled-sublayer-separator-suffices} remove the remaining
overshoot from that test in the non-boundary case: the reporter only has to
certify that the lowest-efficiency fractional prefix of exact load \(\Lambda\)
has capacity at least \(A\Lambda\).
\Cref{lem:variational-exact-load-recycled-screen} and
\cref{cor:variational-exact-load-recycled-separator-suffices} remove the sorting
language entirely: equivalently, every fractional sublayer of exact load
\(\Lambda\) must have near-shadow capacity at least \(A\Lambda\).
\Cref{lem:exact-load-margin-extension} shows why this exact-load condition is
not merely a boundary artifact: once it holds, every larger fractional layer has
strict positive margin because all additional load has efficiency \(>A\).
\Cref{lem:dominated-load-recycled-screen} and
\cref{cor:dominated-load-recycled-separator-suffices} normalize the exact-load
condition further: it is enough to prove that every probability distribution
dominated by the normalized query load has average near-shadow efficiency at
least \(A\).
\Cref{cor:dominated-load-recycled-local-cover-endpoint} packages this as the
current local theorem target: one affordable retained container must pass the
dominated-load mean-efficiency test at every dyadic annular level, and then the
local fractional cover is feasible.
\Cref{lem:finite-dominated-load-proposal-game} gives the corresponding fully
fractional finite-pool target: after terminal and boundary alternatives are
removed, either a proposal law over affordable retained records passes every
dominated-load test in the averaged sense, or a single level-weighted family of
dominated query distributions prices every affordable record below \(A\).  This
is the column-generation obstruction that a list-decoding, range-reporting, or
additive-quantization theorem should beat.
\Cref{cor:exact-load-dominated-proposal-obstruction} rewrites that obstruction as
a law over exact-load cohorts, each with at most one fractional query.  This is
the discrete cohort form needed for finite reporter or integer-materialization
arguments.
\Cref{cor:exact-load-cohort-law-separator} turns it into the sharp finite-pool
separator target: every law over those exact-load cohorts must be beaten by one
affordable retained record.
\Cref{cor:cohort-law-scalar-prefix-normal-form} then removes the last record
notation: a cohort law induces a scalar degree \(d_\eta^\theta\) on data points,
and the retained oracle only has to find an affordable top-\(K\) prefix with mass
at least \(A\Lambda\).
\Cref{cor:cohort-law-weak-type-superlevel} gives the equivalent weak-type
superlevel target: find a materializable affordable superlevel with
\(\delta h\ge A\Lambda\), or else every such superlevel obeys the strict cap
\(\delta h<A\Lambda\).
\Cref{cor:load-quantile-recycled-obstruction-profile} gives the matching
failure form: after the terminal and \(A\)-boundary cases are excluded, one
strict deficit at this weighted quantile is the entire obstruction.
\Cref{cor:exact-load-recycled-obstruction-profile} rewrites the same residual as
\(\widehat S_\Lambda<A\Lambda\), which is the clean exact-load form for the
remaining range-reporting/list-recovery theorem.
\Cref{cor:variational-exact-load-recycled-obstruction-profile} gives the
corresponding witness form: a failed non-boundary screen is exactly an
exact-load fractional query layer whose true near-shadow capacity is below the
allowed \(A\)-multiple.
\Cref{cor:dominated-load-recycled-obstruction-profile} gives the normalized
witness: a probability distribution dominated by the query-load measure whose
mean efficiency is below \(A\).
\Cref{cor:finite-prefix-recycled-obstruction-profile} gives the exact negation:
if the finite scan fails, total load is at least \(\Lambda\), every positive
breakpoint prefix has strict deficit, and the \(A\)-boundary already carries
either positive deficit or too much load.
\Cref{lem:integrated-recycled-threshold-obstruction} converts the same failed
scan into a cumulative excess-load profile:
\[
   A L_0-S_0+\int_A^t(L(u)-\Lambda)\,du>0
   \qquad(t>A).
\]
Thus the remaining range-reporting/list-recovery target can also be phrased as
forcing this excess-area curve to hit zero for one retained container and one
dyadic annular size level.

\begin{corollary}[Annular reporter closes the local cover]
   \label{cor:annular-reporter-local-cover}
   Work under the hypotheses of
   \cref{cor:relative-annular-active-collision-residual}, using relative
   threshold \(\beta_0\).  Choose \(J\ge1\) and \(0\le\xi<1\) so that
   \((DAR1)\) holds, and suppose the retained scalar prefix pool has the closure
   required in \cref{cor:certified-scalar-superlevel-reporter}.  If
   \cref{asm:weighted-annular-scalar-reporter} holds for every guarded
   normalized residual produced by local infeasibility, then the enlarged local
   filter-cover LP is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Suppose the enlarged local filter-cover LP were infeasible.  Then
   \cref{cor:dyadic-annular-residual-witness} produces a guarded normalized
   residual and a dyadic level \(\beta\in\mathcal B_J\) satisfying \((ASR1)\).
   By \cref{asm:weighted-annular-scalar-reporter}, this residual has a certified
   scalar reporter for some point on the normalized segment
   \(\bar\gamma^\theta\).

   The proof of \cref{cor:certified-scalar-superlevel-reporter} turns the
   reported one-sided quantities into a valid scalar average superlevel panel,
   hence into a positive reduced-gain retained prefix/core for the same price
   system.  This contradicts \((GNR3)\), which says that every retained core has
   nonpositive hinge gain for every \(\theta\) on the segment.  Therefore the
   assumed infeasible residual cannot exist, and the local filter-cover LP is
   feasible.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Primitive hit-kernel cover equivalence]
   \label{lem:primitive-hit-kernel-cover-equivalence}
   Work in the setting of \cref{asm:one-potential-core-separator}.  For each
   Pareto core \(U\in\mathcal U\) and query subset \(Q'\subseteq\mathcal Q\),
   form the Boolean core record
   \[
      R=(U,Q'),\qquad T_R=T_U,\qquad S_R=S_U,
   \]
   with incidence
   \[
      b_R(p,q)
      =
      \mathbf 1\{p\in U,\ \exists z\in\mathcal Z:\ p\in V_{z,q}\}
      \mathbf 1\{q\in Q'\}.
   \]
   Consider the fractional primitive hit-kernel cover
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \text{\rm find} & \lambda_R\ge0\\[0.4em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_R\lambda_R b_R(p,q)\ge r_{p,q}
        \qquad((p,q)\in\mathcal N),\\[0.8em]
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{R:q\in Q'_R}\lambda_R T_R\le \pi_1 L
        \qquad(q\in\mathcal Q),\\[0.8em]
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_R\lambda_R S_R\le \pi_1 S .
   \end{array}
   \tag{$\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U}$}
   \]
   Then \(\mathcal U\) is one-potential separating if and only if
   \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\) is feasible.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Apply Farkas' lemma exactly as in
   \cref{lem:finite-filter-cover-dual}.  Infeasibility of
   \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\) is equivalent to the existence of
   nonnegative prices \(\gamma_{p,q},\tau_q,\sigma\) such that
   \[
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      >
      \pi_1\left(L\sum_q\tau_q+\sigma S\right),
      \tag{HKC-D1}
   \]
   and every Boolean core record satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}b_R(p,q)
      \le
      T_R\sum_{q\in Q'_R}\tau_q+\sigma S_R .
      \tag{HKC-D2}
   \]
   For a fixed core \(U\), the left side of \((HKC\text{-}D2)\) is
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q'}a_U^\gamma(q),
   \]
   with \(a_U^\gamma\) as in \((CDH1)\).  Therefore the constraints
   \((HKC\text{-}D2)\) over all \(Q'\subseteq\mathcal Q\) are equivalent to
   \[
      \sum_q\bigl(a_U^\gamma(q)-T_U\tau_q\bigr)_+
      \le
      \sigma S_U
      \qquad(U\in\mathcal U).
   \]
   The strict surplus condition \((HKC\text{-}D1)\) is exactly \((OPC2)\).
   Thus infeasibility of the primitive hit-kernel cover is exactly failure of
   \cref{asm:one-potential-core-separator}.  Negating gives the equivalence.
\end{proof}

Consequently the one-potential theorem has a primal form: fractionally cover the
spherical primitive hit kernel \(r_{p,q}\), not a hand-picked set of dense
clusters.  Since \(r_{p,q}\ge\pi_1\) for every demanded pair under \((WS1)\),
scaling a feasible solution of \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\) by \(1/\pi_1\)
gives an ordinary near-pair core cover with query budget \(L\) and storage
budget \(S\).  The remaining geometric task can therefore be read either as the
normalized obstruction of
\cref{cor:normalized-one-potential-obstruction} or as the fully fractional
hit-kernel cover \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\); they are the same minimax
statement.
\Cref{cor:guarded-normalized-residual-segment} adds the low-guard spherical
information to this normalized obstruction: a surviving residual must carry
unit primitive captured mass, satisfy all core hinge envelopes, and still have
activation-weighted high-correlation guard mass \(>\pi_1\kappa/2\).  Thus the
remaining theorem can target this single normalized system rather than juggling
separate spherical and dense dual certificates.
\Cref{cor:guard-leakage-residual-dichotomy} further splits that obstruction:
under the budget-compatible low-guard choice, the part of \(H(q)\) inside the
resident \(cr\)-guard ball is too small to carry the required mass, so any
surviving residual must put constant normalized weight on the annular leakage
\(H(q)\setminus B(q,cr)\).
\Cref{cor:thresholded-annular-collision-residual} makes the leakage canonical:
take \(H(q)\) to be the resident guard ball plus exactly those annular points
whose primitive spherical collision is above the far threshold \(\pi_2\).  A
surviving residual must then charge many such threshold violators in the
activation-weighted sense.
\Cref{cor:annular-active-collision-residual} converts this to the scalar
quantity that a spherical or range-reporting argument can try to upper-bound:
the \(\bar\tau\)-weighted active collision mass with far annular points.
\Cref{cor:relative-annular-active-collision-residual} gives the sharper
activation-normalized version.  Thresholding by the conditional load
\(c_q(x)/a_q\) still satisfies the spherical far-budget condition with
\(\pi_2=\beta\max_q a_q\), but the resulting active-collision obstruction loses
only the chosen relative threshold \(\beta\).  This is the more useful target
when the activation budget permits constant \(\beta\).
\Cref{cor:far-active-load-spherical-fallback} records the direct
pseudo-random close: if the whole far active load of each query is already below
the \(\pi_1L\) budget scale, then no annular residual can survive.  Thus the
remaining dense/list-decoding theorem only has to handle failures of this
aggregate load bound, not failures of pointwise far collision.
\Cref{lem:dyadic-relative-load-superlevel} makes such a failure finite: after
discarding a \(2^{-J}\) tail, some dyadic relative threshold captures the far
load up to an \(O(J)\) loss.  Taking \(J=\lceil\log_2|P|\rceil\) turns the
overflow branch into an \(O(\log |P|)\)-level reporter problem.
\Cref{lem:weighted-dyadic-annular-load} and
\cref{cor:dyadic-annular-residual-witness} give the dual-weighted form actually
needed by the LP: if a guarded residual survives the aggregate spherical
fallback, then after a negligible tail there is a dyadic annular conditional
collision superlevel with large \(\bar\tau_q a_q\)-weighted size.  The remaining
geometric theorem may therefore search a finite panel of such annular
superlevels and either prove their total load impossible or convert one of them
into a paid scalar-reporter column.
\Cref{asm:weighted-annular-scalar-reporter} and
\cref{cor:annular-reporter-local-cover} isolate exactly this conversion.  The
annular sets \(A_\beta(q)\) are far false-positive witnesses, not cover columns
by themselves.  They close the LP only after a reporter converts their
dual-weighted abundance into one-sided scalar certificates for an actual
near-pair prefix/core.
\Cref{lem:primitive-annular-superlevel-lift} moves this target from query-level
superlevel sets to the primitive bucket panel \(B_{z,\beta}(q)\).  Thus the
remaining list-decoding or additive-quantization search can look for a concrete
seed whose active bucket has large dual-priced annular co-load; by
\cref{cor:primitive-annular-panel-reporter-suffices}, converting such a panel
to the certified scalar reporter is already enough to close the local LP.
\Cref{cor:single-seed-annular-query-layer} adds the last finite layer-cake
normal form: with finite primitive support, a surviving residual has one seed,
one collision level, and one dyadic size layer of queries carrying
dual-priced annular co-load.  This is the smallest current reporter object.

\begin{corollary}[Hit-kernel cover materialization]
   \label{cor:hit-kernel-cover-materialization}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{lem:primitive-hit-kernel-cover-equivalence}, and assume
   \(r_{p,q}\ge\pi_1\) for every demanded pair.  Suppose
   \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\) is feasible and that every Boolean core
   record obeys the atom bounds
   \[
      T_R\le L,\qquad S_R\le S .
      \tag{HKM1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      B\ge
      \max\left\{
         1,\log(4|\mathcal N|),\log(8(|\mathcal Q|+1))
      \right\},
      \tag{HKM2}
   \]
   then preprocessing can retain an integral multiset of Boolean core records
   \(\mathcal R\) such that every demanded pair is covered,
   \[
      \sum_{R\in\mathcal R}b_R(p,q)\ge1
      \qquad((p,q)\in\mathcal N),
      \tag{HKM3}
   \]
   while every query has active descendant price at most \(3BL\), and total
   storage is at most \(3BS\):
   \[
      \sum_{R\in\mathcal R:q\in Q'_R}T_R\le3BL
      \qquad(q\in\mathcal Q),
      \qquad
      \sum_{R\in\mathcal R}S_R\le3BS .
      \tag{HKM4}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let \(\lambda\) be feasible for \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\), and put
   \[
      \widehat\lambda_R=\lambda_R/\pi_1 .
   \]
   Since \(r_{p,q}\ge\pi_1\),
   \[
      \sum_R\widehat\lambda_Rb_R(p,q)
      \ge
      r_{p,q}/\pi_1
      \ge1
      \qquad((p,q)\in\mathcal N).
   \]
   The query and storage constraints of
   \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\) scale to
   \[
      \sum_{R:q\in Q'_R}\widehat\lambda_R T_R\le L,
      \qquad
      \sum_R\widehat\lambda_R S_R\le S .
   \]
   Thus \(\widehat\lambda\) is feasible for the ordinary filter-cover LP
   \((\mathsf{FC}_{\mathcal N})\) over the Boolean core records with uniform
   query budget \(L\) and storage budget \(S\).  Applying
   \cref{lem:poisson-filter-cover-materialization} with the atom bounds
   \((HKM1)\) gives the retained multiset and the displayed \(3B\)-inflated
   query and storage guarantees.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Primitive slice law as a hit-kernel cover]
   \label{lem:primitive-slice-law-hit-kernel-cover}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:high-correlation-dense-slice-separator}.
   Suppose the Pareto core family contains every nonempty primitive slice
   \(V_{z,q}\) as a core with certified prices \(T_{z,q},S_{z,q}\), and includes
   the singleton-query Boolean record \((V_{z,q},\{q\})\).  Empty slices
   contribute zero price.  If
   \[
      \E_{Z\sim\Pi}T_{Z,q}\le\pi_1L
      \qquad(q\in\mathcal Q),
      \tag{PSH1}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \E_{Z\sim\Pi}\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}S_{Z,q}\le\pi_1S,
      \tag{PSH2}
   \]
   then \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\) is feasible.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   For each \(z\in\mathcal Z\) and \(q\in\mathcal Q\), assign intensity
   \[
      \lambda_{z,q}=\Pi(z)
   \]
   to the record \((V_{z,q},\{q\})\), omitting empty slices.  For a demanded pair
   \((p,q)\),
   \[
      \sum_z\lambda_{z,q}\mathbf 1\{p\in V_{z,q}\}
      =
      \Pr_{Z\sim\Pi}[p\in V_{Z,q}]
      =
      r_{p,q},
   \]
   so the hit-kernel coverage constraints hold with equality.  For query \(q\),
   the active query price is
   \[
      \sum_z\Pi(z)T_{z,q}
      =
      \E_ZT_{Z,q}
      \le\pi_1L
   \]
   by \((PSH1)\), and total storage is
   \[
      \sum_q\sum_z\Pi(z)S_{z,q}
      =
      \E_Z\sum_qS_{Z,q}
      \le\pi_1S
   \]
   by \((PSH2)\).  These are exactly the constraints of
   \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\).
\end{proof}

Thus quotienting and core compression are needed only when the raw primitive
slice law has too much recursive moment.  In the favorable case
\((PSH1)\)--\((PSH2)\), the spherical bucket law itself already supplies the
fractional dense-overlap cover, and
\cref{cor:hit-kernel-cover-materialization} turns it into retained dense
filters.  The hard geometric theorem is precisely to replace the primitive
slice law by cheaper Pareto cores when \((PSH1)\) or \((PSH2)\) fails.

\begin{lemma}[Excess slice-moment repair]
   \label{lem:excess-slice-moment-repair}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{lem:primitive-slice-law-hit-kernel-cover}.  Let
   \(0\le\delta_{z,q}\le\Pi(z)\) be a fractional sublaw of primitive slices to
   delete.  Suppose there is a nonnegative measure \(\mu\) on Boolean Pareto
   core records \(R=(U_R,Q'_R,T_R,S_R)\) such that, for every demanded pair,
   \[
      \sum_R\mu_R b_R(p,q)
      \ge
      \sum_z\delta_{z,q}\mathbf 1\{p\in V_{z,q}\},
      \tag{ESR1}
   \]
   and the repaired query and storage loads obey
   \[
      \E_ZT_{Z,q}
      -
      \sum_z\delta_{z,q}T_{z,q}
      +
      \sum_{R:q\in Q'_R}\mu_R T_R
      \le
      \pi_1L
      \qquad(q\in\mathcal Q),
      \tag{ESR2}
   \]
   \[
      \E_Z\sum_qS_{Z,q}
      -
      \sum_{z,q}\delta_{z,q}S_{z,q}
      +
      \sum_R\mu_R S_R
      \le
      \pi_1S .
      \tag{ESR3}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\) is feasible.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Keep the undeleted primitive-slice intensity
   \[
      \lambda^{\rm keep}_{z,q}=\Pi(z)-\delta_{z,q}
   \]
   on the singleton-query record \((V_{z,q},\{q\})\), and add the repairing
   core measure \(\mu\).  For a demanded pair \((p,q)\), the resulting coverage
   is at least
   \[
      \sum_z(\Pi(z)-\delta_{z,q})\mathbf 1\{p\in V_{z,q}\}
      +
      \sum_z\delta_{z,q}\mathbf 1\{p\in V_{z,q}\}
      =
      r_{p,q},
   \]
   where the inequality uses \((ESR1)\).  Thus the hit-kernel coverage
   constraints hold.  The query load at \(q\) is exactly the left side of
   \((ESR2)\), and the storage load is exactly the left side of \((ESR3)\).
   Hence all constraints of \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\) are feasible.
\end{proof}

This is the budget-repair form of dense merging.  The algorithm need not
compress the whole spherical slice law.  It may retain every primitive slice
whose recursive moment is already affordable and ask the dense proposal oracle
only to replace a fractional overbudget sublaw.  The certificate is purely
local: \((ESR1)\) says the replacement cores dominate the deleted hit kernel,
while \((ESR2)\)--\((ESR3)\) say that the replacement saves enough query and
storage price to fit the \(\pi_1\)-scaled budgets.

\begin{lemma}[Finite repair dual]
   \label{lem:finite-repair-dual}
   Fix a deletion sublaw \(\delta\) as in
   \cref{lem:excess-slice-moment-repair}, and put
   \[
      d_\delta(p,q)=
      \sum_z\delta_{z,q}\mathbf 1\{p\in V_{z,q}\}.
   \]
   Define the residual query and storage budgets
   \[
      \bar L_q=
      \pi_1L-\E_ZT_{Z,q}+\sum_z\delta_{z,q}T_{z,q},
      \tag{FRD0}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \bar S=
      \pi_1S-\E_Z\sum_qS_{Z,q}+\sum_{z,q}\delta_{z,q}S_{z,q}.
      \tag{FRD1}
   \]
   Let \(\mathcal R\) be a finite family of Boolean Pareto core records.  The
   finite repair LP
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \text{\rm find} & \mu_R\ge0\\[0.4em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_R\mu_Rb_R(p,q)\ge d_\delta(p,q)
        \qquad((p,q)\in\mathcal N),\\[0.8em]
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{R:q\in Q'_R}\mu_R T_R\le\bar L_q
        \qquad(q\in\mathcal Q),\\[0.8em]
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_R\mu_R S_R\le\bar S
   \end{array}
   \tag{$\mathsf{Repair}_\delta$}
   \]
   is infeasible if and only if there are nonnegative prices
   \(\gamma_{p,q},\tau_q,\sigma\) such that
   \[
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}d_\delta(p,q)
      >
      \sum_q\tau_q\bar L_q+\sigma\bar S,
      \tag{FRD2}
   \]
   while every repair record satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}b_R(p,q)
      \le
      T_R\sum_{q\in Q'_R}\tau_q+\sigma S_R .
      \tag{FRD3}
   \]
   Equivalently, a column-generation repair routine succeeds over a finite
   universe \(\mathcal R_\star\) iff every price system satisfying
   \((FRD2)\) exposes some record \(R\in\mathcal R_\star\) with positive repair
   reduced gain
   \[
      \sum_{p,q}\gamma_{p,q}b_R(p,q)
      -
      T_R\sum_{q\in Q'_R}\tau_q
      -
      \sigma S_R .
      \tag{FRD4}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   This is Farkas' lemma applied to the finite repair system.  The coverage
   inequalities have right-hand sides \(d_\delta(p,q)\), while the query and
   storage budgets have right-hand sides \(\bar L_q\) and \(\bar S\).  A
   nonnegative multiplier system certifies infeasibility exactly when its
   coefficient on every variable \(\mu_R\) is nonnegative and its weighted
   right-hand side is negative.  Written with the coverage multipliers
   \(\gamma\) on the opposite side, these two conditions are precisely
   \((FRD3)\) and \((FRD2)\).  Negating the infeasibility certificate gives the
   column-generation statement: if all surplus repair duals have a positive
   reduced-gain record, no infeasible restricted optimum can be final; finiteness
   gives termination after at most \(|\mathcal R_\star|\) added records.
\end{proof}

Thus the overbudget repair problem has the same local form as the original
filter-cover LP, but with the deleted primitive hit kernel
\(d_\delta\) as demand and the saved primitive slice costs as residual budgets.
This is useful algorithmically: preprocessing may choose a deletion sublaw,
solve the finite repair LP, inspect its dual, and search only for a positive
repair-gain core.  Successful repair plus
\cref{lem:excess-slice-moment-repair} gives the hit-kernel cover.

\begin{lemma}[Joint deletion-repair dual]
   \label{lem:joint-deletion-repair-dual}
   In the setting of \cref{lem:finite-repair-dual}, assume the primitive law has
   finite support and let \(\mathcal R\) be a finite family of Boolean Pareto
   core records.  Consider the joint repair feasibility problem
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \text{\rm find} & \mu_R\ge0,\qquad 0\le\delta_{z,q}\le\Pi(z)\\[0.4em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_R\mu_Rb_R(p,q)
        \ge
        \sum_z\delta_{z,q}\mathbf 1\{p\in V_{z,q}\}
        \qquad((p,q)\in\mathcal N),\\[0.8em]
      & \displaystyle
        \E_ZT_{Z,q}
        -
        \sum_z\delta_{z,q}T_{z,q}
        +
        \sum_{R:q\in Q'_R}\mu_R T_R
        \le \pi_1L
        \qquad(q\in\mathcal Q),\\[0.8em]
      & \displaystyle
        \E_Z\sum_qS_{Z,q}
        -
        \sum_{z,q}\delta_{z,q}S_{z,q}
        +
        \sum_R\mu_R S_R
        \le \pi_1S .
   \end{array}
   \tag{$\mathsf{JointRepair}$}
   \]
   For nonnegative prices \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\), write
   \[
      A_{z,q}^\gamma
      =
      \sum_{\substack{p:(p,q)\in\mathcal N\\ p\in V_{z,q}}}
      \gamma_{p,q},
      \qquad
      P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma}
      =
      \tau_qT_{z,q}+\sigma S_{z,q}.
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{JointRepair})\) is infeasible if and only if there are
   nonnegative prices \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) such that every repair record
   satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}b_R(p,q)
      \le
      T_R\sum_{q\in Q'_R}\tau_q+\sigma S_R ,
      \tag{JDR1}
   \]
   while
   \[
      \sum_q\tau_q\bigl(\E_ZT_{Z,q}-\pi_1L\bigr)
      +
      \sigma\left(\E_Z\sum_qS_{Z,q}-\pi_1S\right)
      >
      \sum_{z,q}\Pi(z)
      \bigl(P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma}-A_{z,q}^\gamma\bigr)_+ .
      \tag{JDR2}
   \]
   Equivalently, under fixed dual prices the deletion sublaw that is most
   favorable to feasibility saturates exactly the primitive slices with
   \(P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma}>A_{z,q}^\gamma\), deletes none of the slices with
   \(P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma}<A_{z,q}^\gamma\), and is arbitrary on ties.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Put
   \[
      B_q=\pi_1L-\E_ZT_{Z,q},
      \qquad
      B_S=\pi_1S-\E_Z\sum_qS_{Z,q}.
   \]
   Write the coverage constraints in the form
   \[
      \sum_z\delta_{z,q}\mathbf 1\{p\in V_{z,q}\}
      -
      \sum_R\mu_Rb_R(p,q)
      \le0,
   \]
   the query and storage constraints as
   \[
      \sum_{R:q\in Q'_R}\mu_RT_R-\sum_z\delta_{z,q}T_{z,q}\le B_q,
      \qquad
      \sum_R\mu_RS_R-\sum_{z,q}\delta_{z,q}S_{z,q}\le B_S,
   \]
   and the upper bounds as \(\delta_{z,q}\le\Pi(z)\).

   By Farkas' lemma, infeasibility is equivalent to nonnegative multipliers
   \(\gamma_{p,q},\tau_q,\sigma,\xi_{z,q}\) whose coefficient on every
   nonnegative variable is nonnegative and whose weighted right-hand side is
   negative.  The coefficient condition for a repair variable \(\mu_R\) is
   exactly \((JDR1)\).  The coefficient condition for \(\delta_{z,q}\) is
   \[
      A_{z,q}^\gamma-P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma}+\xi_{z,q}\ge0 .
      \tag{JDR3}
   \]
   For fixed \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\), the smallest admissible upper-bound
   multiplier is therefore
   \[
      \xi_{z,q}=
      \bigl(P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma}-A_{z,q}^\gamma\bigr)_+ .
   \]
   Substituting this choice into the weighted right-hand side gives
   \[
      \sum_q\tau_qB_q+\sigma B_S
      +
      \sum_{z,q}\Pi(z)
      \bigl(P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma}-A_{z,q}^\gamma\bigr)_+
      <0,
   \]
   which is \((JDR2)\) after moving the first two terms to the other side.

   The final statement is the primal form of the same hinge.  For fixed prices,
   the deletion-dependent part of the priced margin is
   \[
      \sum_{z,q}\delta_{z,q}
      \bigl(A_{z,q}^\gamma-P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma}\bigr),
   \]
   minimized over \(0\le\delta_{z,q}\le\Pi(z)\) by setting
   \(\delta_{z,q}=\Pi(z)\) when
   \(P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma}>A_{z,q}^\gamma\) and
   \(\delta_{z,q}=0\) when
   \(P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma}<A_{z,q}^\gamma\).
\end{proof}

\Cref{lem:joint-deletion-repair-dual} removes another artificial choice from
the repair picture.  The build stage does not have to guess a special family of
overbudget dense slices.  Given dual prices, the fractional deletion step is a
canonical hinge: delete the primitive records whose saved recursive
query/storage price exceeds their exposed near-pair value, then ask the
repair-core oracle to compress what remains.  Thus the dense side is now a
single reduced-cost search over repaired primitive moments rather than a
separate greedy selection rule.

\begin{corollary}[Joint repair separator implies hit-kernel cover]
   \label{cor:joint-repair-hit-kernel-cover}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:primitive-slice-law-hit-kernel-cover}, with
   finite primitive support, and let \(\mathcal R\) be a finite family of
   Boolean Pareto core records drawn from \(\mathcal U\).  Suppose that every
   nonnegative price system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying \((JDR1)\) for
   all \(R\in\mathcal R\) also satisfies the joint hinge bound
   \[
      \sum_q\tau_q\bigl(\E_ZT_{Z,q}-\pi_1L\bigr)
      +
      \sigma\left(\E_Z\sum_qS_{Z,q}-\pi_1S\right)
      \le
      \sum_{z,q}\Pi(z)
      \bigl(P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma}-A_{z,q}^\gamma\bigr)_+ ,
      \tag{JRS1}
   \]
   with \(A_{z,q}^\gamma\) and \(P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma}\) as in
   \cref{lem:joint-deletion-repair-dual}.  Then
   \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\) is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \((JRS1)\), no nonnegative price system can satisfy both \((JDR1)\) and
   the strict obstruction \((JDR2)\).  Hence
   \((\mathsf{JointRepair})\) is feasible by
   \cref{lem:joint-deletion-repair-dual}.  Let \((\delta,\mu)\) be a feasible
   solution.  Its three constraints are exactly \((ESR1)\), \((ESR2)\), and
   \((ESR3)\), with the repair measure supported on \(\mathcal R\).  Applying
   \cref{lem:excess-slice-moment-repair} gives feasibility of
   \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\).
\end{proof}

\Cref{cor:joint-repair-hit-kernel-cover} is the current compact finite target.
The primitive spherical slice law supplies the original hit kernel; the hinge
term is the maximal cost that can be deleted without leaving more exposed value
than it saves; and the repair records are ordinary Pareto cores.  Ruling out
\((JDR1)\)--\((JDR2)\) for a sufficiently rich core universe is therefore
already enough for the fractional dense-overlap cover.

\begin{lemma}[Capped primitive-moment normal form]
   \label{lem:capped-primitive-moment-normal-form}
   In the setting of \cref{cor:joint-repair-hit-kernel-cover}, the hinge bound
   \((JRS1)\) is equivalent to
   \[
      \sum_{z,q}\Pi(z)
      \min\left\{
         P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma},
         A_{z,q}^{\gamma}
      \right\}
      \le
      \pi_1\left(L\sum_q\tau_q+\sigma S\right).
      \tag{CPM1}
   \]
   Consequently, if every nonnegative price system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\)
   satisfying \((JDR1)\) for all records \(R\in\mathcal R\) obeys
   \((CPM1)\), then \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\) is feasible.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Since
   \[
      \sum_{z,q}\Pi(z)P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma}
      =
      \sum_q\tau_q\E_ZT_{Z,q}
      +
      \sigma\E_Z\sum_qS_{Z,q},
   \]
   the left side of \((JRS1)\) can be rewritten as
   \[
      \sum_{z,q}\Pi(z)P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma}
      -
      \pi_1\left(L\sum_q\tau_q+\sigma S\right).
   \]
   Moving the hinge term in \((JRS1)\) to the left therefore gives
   \[
      \sum_{z,q}\Pi(z)
      \left(
         P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma}
         -
         \bigl(P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma}-A_{z,q}^\gamma\bigr)_+
      \right)
      \le
      \pi_1\left(L\sum_q\tau_q+\sigma S\right).
   \]
   For nonnegative \(P\) and \(A\),
   \(P-(P-A)_+=\min\{P,A\}\), which is exactly \((CPM1)\).  The final statement
   is \cref{cor:joint-repair-hit-kernel-cover} with \((JRS1)\) replaced by its
   equivalent capped-moment form.
\end{proof}

\Cref{lem:capped-primitive-moment-normal-form} is the cleanest way to read the
joint deletion repair.  The raw primitive recursive moment
\(\sum\Pi P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma}\) may be far above the budget; cost-dominated
primitive records are simply deleted.  What remains to prove is only a capped
moment inequality: under any dual prices for which no Pareto core has positive
reduced gain, the primitive law cannot place more than the scaled budget on
records whose exposed near-pair value pays for their recursive price.

\begin{lemma}[Paid primitive-sublaw normal form]
   \label{lem:paid-primitive-sublaw-normal-form}
   Fix nonnegative prices \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\).  For each primitive record
   \((z,q)\) with \(P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma}>0\), define
   \[
      \omega_{z,q}
      =
      \Pi(z)
      \min\left\{
         1,\frac{A_{z,q}^{\gamma}}{P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma}}
      \right\},
      \tag{PPS1}
   \]
   and set \(\omega_{z,q}=0\) when \(P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma}=0\).  Then
   \(0\le\omega_{z,q}\le\Pi(z)\), and
   \[
      \sum_{z,q}\omega_{z,q}P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma}
      =
      \sum_{z,q}\Pi(z)
      \min\left\{
         P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma},
         A_{z,q}^{\gamma}
      \right\}.
      \tag{PPS2}
   \]
   Moreover each retained amount is paid pointwise by exposed demand:
   \[
      \omega_{z,q}P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma}
      \le
      \Pi(z)A_{z,q}^{\gamma}
      =
      \Pi(z)
      \sum_{\substack{p:(p,q)\in\mathcal N\\ p\in V_{z,q}}}
      \gamma_{p,q}.
      \tag{PPS3}
   \]
   Hence failure of \((CPM1)\) is equivalent to the canonical paid sublaw
   \(\omega\) having priced recursive moment larger than
   \(\pi_1(L\sum_q\tau_q+\sigma S)\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   The bounds \(0\le\omega_{z,q}\le\Pi(z)\) are immediate from \((PPS1)\).
   If \(P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma}>0\), then multiplying \((PPS1)\) by
   \(P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma}\) gives
   \[
      \omega_{z,q}P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma}
      =
      \Pi(z)
      \min\left\{
         P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma},
         A_{z,q}^{\gamma}
      \right\}.
   \]
   If \(P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma}=0\), both sides are zero.  Summing proves
   \((PPS2)\).  Since
   \(\min\{P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma},A_{z,q}^{\gamma}\}\le
   A_{z,q}^{\gamma}\), \((PPS3)\) follows.  The final sentence is exactly
   \((PPS2)\) compared with \((CPM1)\).
\end{proof}

Thus the residual dense theorem can be phrased without the raw primitive
moment.  An obstruction must produce a paid fractional sublaw of primitive
slices whose recursive price exceeds the scaled budget, while every paid unit
is backed by exposed near-pair value and no proposed Pareto core has positive
reduced gain.  The geometric separator only has to show that such a paid
overbudget sublaw contains a compressing core.

\begin{corollary}[Singleton-saturated paid law]
   \label{cor:singleton-saturated-paid-law}
   In the setting of \cref{lem:paid-primitive-sublaw-normal-form}, suppose that
   \(\mathcal R\) contains every nonempty primitive singleton record
   \(R_{z,q}=(V_{z,q},\{q\})\) with prices \(T_{z,q},S_{z,q}\).  If a price
   system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfies \((JDR1)\) for all records in
   \(\mathcal R\), then
   \[
      A_{z,q}^{\gamma}\le P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma}
      \qquad(z,q),
      \tag{SSP1}
   \]
   and the paid sublaw from \cref{lem:paid-primitive-sublaw-normal-form}
   satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{z,q}\omega_{z,q}P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma}
      =
      \sum_{z,q}\Pi(z)A_{z,q}^{\gamma}
      =
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
      \tag{SSP2}
   \]
   Consequently, under singleton saturation, any surplus primitive-hit dual
   \[
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      >
      \pi_1\left(L\sum_q\tau_q+\sigma S\right)
      \tag{SSP3}
   \]
   produces an overbudget paid primitive sublaw unless some non-singleton
   repair record has positive reduced gain.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \((JDR1)\) to the singleton record \(R_{z,q}\).  Its left side is
   \(A_{z,q}^{\gamma}\), and its right side is
   \(P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma}\), proving \((SSP1)\).  Hence
   \[
      \min\{P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma},A_{z,q}^{\gamma}\}
      =
      A_{z,q}^{\gamma}.
   \]
   Combining this with \((PPS2)\) gives the first equality in \((SSP2)\).  For
   the second equality, expand \(A_{z,q}^{\gamma}\) and exchange sums:
   \[
      \sum_{z,q}\Pi(z)A_{z,q}^{\gamma}
      =
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}
      \gamma_{p,q}
      \sum_z\Pi(z)\mathbf 1\{p\in V_{z,q}\}
      =
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
   \]
   If \((SSP3)\) holds and no non-singleton record has positive reduced gain,
   then \((JDR1)\) holds for all records in the saturated family, so
   \((SSP2)\) makes the paid sublaw overbudget.
\end{proof}

\Cref{cor:singleton-saturated-paid-law} explains why primitive slices should
remain in the build-time proposal universe even when they are too expensive to
store as the final cover.  They normalize the dual: after they fail to have
positive gain, the obstruction is no longer an arbitrary cap of the raw moment
but the value-proportional paid law
\(\omega_{z,q}=\Pi(z)A_{z,q}^{\gamma}/P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma}\) on slices with
positive price.  The only useful remaining columns are compressions of that
paid law into cheaper Pareto cores.

\begin{lemma}[Paid quotient reduced-gain criterion]
   \label{lem:paid-quotient-reduced-gain}
   Work with prices \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) and primitive slices \(V_{z,q}\).
   Let \(R=(U_R,Q'_R,T_R,S_R)\) be a Boolean Pareto core record, and suppose it
   is assigned a finite set of primitive records
   \[
      \mathcal I_R\subseteq\mathcal Z\times\mathcal Q
   \]
   such that, for every \((z,q)\in\mathcal I_R\),
   \[
      V_{z,q}\subseteq U_R,\qquad q\in Q'_R .
      \tag{PQR1}
   \]
   Define its probability-weighted paid primitive value by
   \[
      \mathsf V_R^{\gamma}
      =
      \sum_{(z,q)\in\mathcal I_R}\Pi(z)A_{z,q}^{\gamma}.
      \tag{PQR2}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \mathsf V_R^{\gamma}
      \le
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}b_R(p,q).
      \tag{PQR3}
   \]
   Consequently, if
   \[
      \mathsf V_R^{\gamma}
      >
      T_R\sum_{q\in Q'_R}\tau_q+\sigma S_R,
      \tag{PQR4}
   \]
   then \(R\) has positive repair reduced gain.  More generally, if a
   nonnegative finite intensity vector \(\lambda_R\) over such records satisfies
   \[
      \sum_R\lambda_R\mathsf V_R^{\gamma}
      >
      \sum_R\lambda_R
      \left(
         T_R\sum_{q\in Q'_R}\tau_q+\sigma S_R
      \right),
      \tag{PQR5}
   \]
   then at least one record in its support has positive repair reduced gain.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Expanding \((PQR2)\) gives
   \[
      \mathsf V_R^{\gamma}
      =
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}
      \gamma_{p,q}
      \sum_{\substack{z:(z,q)\in\mathcal I_R\\ p\in V_{z,q}}}\Pi(z).
   \]
   By \((PQR1)\), every primitive incidence counted in the inner sum satisfies
   \(p\in U_R\) and \(q\in Q'_R\).  Also
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{z:(z,q)\in\mathcal I_R\\ p\in V_{z,q}}}\Pi(z)
      \le
      \sum_z\Pi(z)
      =
      1 .
   \]
   Thus each demand pair contributes at most
   \(\gamma_{p,q}\mathbf 1\{p\in U_R\}\mathbf 1\{q\in Q'_R\}\), which is exactly
   \((PQR3)\).  If \((PQR4)\) holds, \((PQR3)\) implies
   \[
      \sum_{p,q}\gamma_{p,q}b_R(p,q)
      -
      T_R\sum_{q\in Q'_R}\tau_q
      -
      \sigma S_R
      >0,
   \]
   the positive repair reduced gain \((FRD4)\).  Finally, if every record in
   the support of \(\lambda\) had nonpositive reduced gain, then \((PQR3)\)
   would make the left side of \((PQR5)\) no larger than the right side.  Hence
   \((PQR5)\) exposes at least one positive-gain record.
\end{proof}

\Cref{lem:paid-quotient-reduced-gain} is the paid-law analogue of
\cref{lem:dense-slice-quotient-separation}, but the probability weight
\(\Pi(z)\) removes the duplicate-incidence factor.  The remaining dense
separator may therefore search for cores that capture a large amount of
probability-weighted paid primitive value, rather than de-duplicating raw
singleton slices by hand.

\begin{corollary}[Paid compression implies hit-kernel cover]
   \label{cor:paid-compression-hit-kernel-cover}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{lem:primitive-slice-law-hit-kernel-cover}, with finite primitive
   support, and suppose the Boolean core universe contains every primitive
   singleton record \(R_{z,q}=(V_{z,q},\{q\},T_{z,q},S_{z,q})\).
   Let \(\mathcal C\) be a finite family of assigned Boolean Pareto core
   records \(C=(R_C,\mathcal I_C)\), where
   \(R_C=(U_C,Q'_C,T_C,S_C)\) is in the Boolean core universe and
   \(\mathcal I_C\subseteq\mathcal Z\times\mathcal Q\) satisfies
   \[
      V_{z,q}\subseteq U_C,\qquad q\in Q'_C
      \qquad((z,q)\in\mathcal I_C).
      \tag{PCOV1}
   \]
   Assume the following paid-compression separator: for every nonnegative
   price system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) such that
   \[
      A_{z,q}^{\gamma}\le P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma}
      \qquad(z,q),
      \tag{PCOV2}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      >
      \pi_1\left(L\sum_q\tau_q+\sigma S\right),
      \tag{PCOV3}
   \]
   there is a nonnegative finite intensity vector \(\lambda_C\) on
   \(\mathcal C\) such that
   \[
      \sum_C\lambda_C
      \sum_{(z,q)\in\mathcal I_C}\Pi(z)A_{z,q}^{\gamma}
      >
      \sum_C\lambda_C
      \left(
         T_C\sum_{q\in Q'_C}\tau_q+\sigma S_C
      \right).
      \tag{PCOV4}
   \]
   Then the primitive hit-kernel cover
   \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\) is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Suppose \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\) were infeasible.  By
   \cref{lem:primitive-hit-kernel-cover-equivalence}, there are nonnegative
   prices \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying the surplus inequality
   \((HKC\text{-}D1)\) while every Boolean core record has nonpositive reduced
   gain \((HKC\text{-}D2)\).  Applied to the primitive singleton record
   \(R_{z,q}\), this nonpositive-gain condition gives exactly
   \[
      A_{z,q}^{\gamma}
      \le
      T_{z,q}\tau_q+\sigma S_{z,q}
      =
      P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma},
   \]
   so \((PCOV2)\) holds.  The surplus inequality \((HKC\text{-}D1)\) is
   \((PCOV3)\).

   The paid-compression separator therefore gives a conic certificate
   \((PCOV4)\).  Applying
   \cref{lem:paid-quotient-reduced-gain} to the assigned records in the support
   of \(\lambda\) exposes at least one underlying Boolean core record with
   positive reduced gain.  This contradicts \((HKC\text{-}D2)\).  Hence
   \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\) is feasible.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Canonical paid-core hinge normal form]
   \label{lem:canonical-paid-core-hinge}
   Work with nonnegative prices \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\).  Let
   \(U\) be a Pareto core with prices \(T_U,S_U\), and assume the Boolean core
   universe contains \((U,Q',T_U,S_U)\) for every \(Q'\subseteq\mathcal Q\).
   Define the canonical paid whole-slice support of \(U\) at query \(q\) by
   \[
      h_U^\gamma(q)
      =
      \sum_{z:V_{z,q}\subseteq U}\Pi(z)A_{z,q}^{\gamma}.
      \tag{CPH1}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \max_{Q'\subseteq\mathcal Q}
      \left[
         \sum_{q\in Q'}h_U^\gamma(q)
         -
         T_U\sum_{q\in Q'}\tau_q
         -
         \sigma S_U
      \right]
      =
      \sum_q\bigl(h_U^\gamma(q)-T_U\tau_q\bigr)_+
      -
      \sigma S_U .
      \tag{CPH2}
   \]
   The maximum is attained by
   \[
      Q_\gamma^+(U)=\{q:h_U^\gamma(q)>T_U\tau_q\}.
      \tag{CPH3}
   \]
   Consequently, if
   \[
      \sum_q\bigl(h_U^\gamma(q)-T_U\tau_q\bigr)_+
      >
      \sigma S_U,
      \tag{CPH4}
   \]
   then the Boolean record \((U,Q_\gamma^+(U),T_U,S_U)\), assigned all primitive
   records \((z,q)\) with \(q\in Q_\gamma^+(U)\) and \(V_{z,q}\subseteq U\), has
   positive repair reduced gain.  Conversely, if any assignment
   \(\mathcal I\) to any record \((U,Q',T_U,S_U)\) satisfying
   \[
      V_{z,q}\subseteq U,\qquad q\in Q'
      \qquad((z,q)\in\mathcal I)
   \]
   has paid value larger than its query/storage price, then \((CPH4)\) holds.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   For a fixed query set \(Q'\), the largest paid value obtainable by assigning
   primitive records to \((U,Q')\) is achieved by assigning every visible
   primitive record:
   \[
      \mathcal I^\star(U,Q')
      =
      \{(z,q):q\in Q',\ V_{z,q}\subseteq U\},
   \]
   because all coefficients \(\Pi(z)A_{z,q}^{\gamma}\) are nonnegative.  Its
   value is \(\sum_{q\in Q'}h_U^\gamma(q)\).  Hence optimizing the paid surplus
   over assignments and query sets is exactly
   \[
      \max_{Q'\subseteq\mathcal Q}
      \sum_{q\in Q'}\bigl(h_U^\gamma(q)-T_U\tau_q\bigr)-\sigma S_U .
   \]
   The maximum keeps exactly the positive-margin queries, giving
   \((CPH2)\)--\((CPH3)\).  If \((CPH4)\) holds, this canonical assignment has
   paid value above price, so
   \cref{lem:paid-quotient-reduced-gain} gives positive repair reduced gain.
   The converse follows because any noncanonical assignment to any \(Q'\) has
   value at most the canonical value for that \(Q'\), which is bounded by the
   positive-part maximum in \((CPH2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Canonical paid-core separator implies hit-kernel cover]
   \label{cor:canonical-paid-core-hit-kernel-cover}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:paid-compression-hit-kernel-cover}.  Suppose the assigned core
   family is closed under the canonical assignment from
   \cref{lem:canonical-paid-core-hinge}.  If every nonnegative price system
   \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying \((PCOV2)\)--\((PCOV3)\) admits a Pareto
   core \(U\) satisfying \((CPH4)\), then
   \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\) is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Given prices satisfying \((PCOV2)\)--\((PCOV3)\), choose the core \(U\) from
   the hypothesis and use the canonical query side \(Q_\gamma^+(U)\) and
   canonical assignment from \cref{lem:canonical-paid-core-hinge}.  By
   \((CPH4)\), the single assigned record has paid value above price, which is
   \((PCOV4)\) with one nonzero intensity.  Therefore the paid-compression
   separator hypothesis of \cref{cor:paid-compression-hit-kernel-cover} holds,
   and that corollary gives the primitive hit-kernel cover.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Atomized paid-core hinge normal form]
   \label{lem:atomized-paid-core-hinge}
   Work with nonnegative prices \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\), primitive slices
   \(V_{z,q}\), and primitive hit kernel
   \[
      r_{p,q}=\sum_z\Pi(z)\mathbf 1\{p\in V_{z,q}\}.
   \]
   Let \(U\) be a Pareto core with prices \(T_U,S_U\), and assume the Boolean
   core universe contains \((U,Q',T_U,S_U)\) for every \(Q'\subseteq\mathcal Q\).
   Define the atomized paid support of \(U\) at query \(q\) by
   \[
      \bar h_U^\gamma(q)
      =
      \sum_{\substack{p:(p,q)\in\mathcal N\\ p\in U}}
      \gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
      \tag{APH1}
   \]
   Then the maximum paid atom surplus over all query sides and all atom
   assignments inside \(U\) is
   \[
      \max_{Q'\subseteq\mathcal Q}
      \left[
         \sum_{q\in Q'}\bar h_U^\gamma(q)
         -
         T_U\sum_{q\in Q'}\tau_q
         -
         \sigma S_U
      \right]
      =
      \sum_q\bigl(\bar h_U^\gamma(q)-T_U\tau_q\bigr)_+
      -
      \sigma S_U .
      \tag{APH2}
   \]
   The maximum is attained by
   \[
      \bar Q_\gamma^+(U)=\{q:\bar h_U^\gamma(q)>T_U\tau_q\}.
      \tag{APH3}
   \]
   Consequently, if
   \[
      \sum_q\bigl(\bar h_U^\gamma(q)-T_U\tau_q\bigr)_+
      >
      \sigma S_U,
      \tag{APH4}
   \]
   then the Boolean record \((U,\bar Q_\gamma^+(U),T_U,S_U)\) has positive
   repair reduced gain.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   For a fixed query side \(Q'\), the largest atomized paid value inside \(U\)
   is obtained by assigning all primitive atoms
   \[
      (z,p,q)
      \quad\text{with}\quad
      q\in Q',\ (p,q)\in\mathcal N,\ p\in U\cap V_{z,q}.
   \]
   Its value is
   \[
      \sum_{q\in Q'}
      \sum_{\substack{p:(p,q)\in\mathcal N\\ p\in U}}
      \gamma_{p,q}
      \sum_{z:p\in V_{z,q}}\Pi(z)
      =
      \sum_{q\in Q'}\bar h_U^\gamma(q).
   \]
   Thus the assignment has disappeared, and optimizing over \(Q'\) is the
   coordinatewise positive-part maximization in \((APH2)\), attained by
   \((APH3)\).

   If \((APH4)\) holds, the atomized paid value of the record
   \(R=(U,\bar Q_\gamma^+(U),T_U,S_U)\) is larger than its query/storage price.
   For every fixed near pair \((p,q)\), the total primitive probability of
   assigned atoms with that pair is at most
   \(r_{p,q}\le1\).  Hence the atomized value is at most
   \[
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}b_R(p,q),
   \]
   the same de-duplication argument as in
   \cref{lem:paid-quotient-reduced-gain}.  Therefore \(R\) has positive repair
   reduced gain.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Atomized paid-core separator implies hit-kernel cover]
   \label{cor:atomized-paid-core-hit-kernel-cover}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{lem:primitive-slice-law-hit-kernel-cover}, with finite primitive
   support, and suppose the Boolean core universe contains every primitive
   singleton record and all query-side threshold activations of a Pareto core
   family \(\mathcal U_{\rm at}\).  If every nonnegative price system
   \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying
   \[
      A_{z,q}^{\gamma}\le P_{z,q}^{\tau,\sigma}\qquad(z,q),
      \tag{APC1}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \sum_{(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
      >
      \pi_1\left(L\sum_q\tau_q+\sigma S\right)
      \tag{APC2}
   \]
   admits a core \(U\in\mathcal U_{\rm at}\) satisfying \((APH4)\), then
   \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\) is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\) were infeasible, the proof of
   \cref{cor:paid-compression-hit-kernel-cover} gives a nonnegative dual price
   system satisfying \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\) and having nonpositive reduced gain
   on every Boolean core record.  By hypothesis, some core \(U\) satisfies
   \((APH4)\).  Then \cref{lem:atomized-paid-core-hinge} exposes a Boolean
   threshold activation of \(U\) with positive repair reduced gain, a
   contradiction.  Hence the primitive hit-kernel cover is feasible.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Weighted atomized-prefix normal form]
   \label{lem:weighted-atomized-prefix-normal-form}
   Work with the atomized paid weights
   \[
      w_{p,q}^\gamma=\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
   \]
   Fix a certified container \(W\subseteq P\), a price factor \(\psi>0\), an
   exponent \(0\le\rho\le1\), and a cardinality \(k\le |W|\).  For a fractional
   query weighting \(0\le y_q\le1\), define the paid weighted degree
   \[
      d_y^\gamma(p)
      =
      \sum_{q:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}y_qw_{p,q}^\gamma,
      \tag{WAP1}
   \]
   and let \(D_y^\gamma(k)\) be the sum of the largest \(k\) values of
   \(d_y^\gamma(p)\) over \(p\in W\).  Put
   \[
      T(k)=\psi k^\rho,\qquad S(k)=\psi k^{1+\rho}.
   \]
   Then
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      &\max_{\substack{U\subseteq W\\ |U|=k}}
      \left[
         \sum_q
         \left(
            \sum_{p\in U:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}w_{p,q}^\gamma
            -
            T(k)\tau_q
         \right)_+
         -
         \sigma S(k)
      \right]
      \\
      &\qquad =
      \max_{0\le y\le1}
      \left[
         D_y^\gamma(k)
         -
         T(k)\sum_q\tau_qy_q
         -
         \sigma S(k)
      \right].
   \end{aligned}
      \tag{WAP2}
   \]
   Consequently, if the left side of \((WAP2)\) is positive, it is witnessed by
   an integral query set \(Q'\subseteq\mathcal Q\).  The top-\(k\) prefix of
   \(W\) sorted by
   \[
      d_{Q'}^\gamma(p)=
      \sum_{q\in Q':(p,q)\in\mathcal N}w_{p,q}^\gamma
   \]
   then satisfies \((APH4)\) with query side \(Q'\) and prices \(T(k),S(k)\),
   hence has positive repair reduced gain.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   For a fixed \(U\), use \((x)_+=\max_{0\le y\le1}yx\) independently for every
   query:
   \[
      \sum_q
      \left(
         \sum_{p\in U}w_{p,q}^\gamma
         -
         T(k)\tau_q
      \right)_+
      =
      \max_{0\le y\le1}
      \left[
         \sum_{p\in U}d_y^\gamma(p)
         -
         T(k)\sum_q\tau_qy_q
      \right].
   \]
   The sets are finite, so the maxima over \(U\) and \(y\) commute.  For fixed
   \(y\), the maximizing \(k\)-point set is the top-\(k\) paid-degree prefix,
   whose value is \(D_y^\gamma(k)\).  This proves \((WAP2)\).

   The function
   \[
      y\mapsto
      D_y^\gamma(k)-T(k)\sum_q\tau_qy_q-\sigma S(k)
   \]
   is convex, since \(D_y^\gamma(k)\) is a maximum of finitely many linear
   functions.  A convex function on the cube \([0,1]^{\mathcal Q}\) has a
   maximizer at an extreme point, so any positive maximum is witnessed by an
   integral vector \(y=\mathbf 1_{Q'}\).  For that \(Q'\), the top-\(k\) prefix
   satisfies \((APH4)\), and \cref{lem:atomized-paid-core-hinge} gives positive
   repair reduced gain.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Weighted atomized-prefix envelope]
   \label{cor:weighted-atomized-prefix-envelope}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:weighted-atomized-prefix-normal-form}, and
   assume that every \(k\)-point paid-degree prefix in \(W\) is an available
   Boolean core with prices \(T(k)=\psi k^\rho\) and
   \(S(k)=\psi k^{1+\rho}\).  If no such prefix has positive repair reduced
   gain, then for every fractional query weighting \(0\le y\le1\) and every
   available cardinality \(k\),
   \[
      D_y^\gamma(k)
      \le
      \psi\left(k^\rho\sum_q\tau_qy_q+\sigma k^{1+\rho}\right).
      \tag{WAE1}
   \]
   Consequently, if
   \[
      h_\delta(y)=|\{p\in W:d_y^\gamma(p)\ge\delta\}|
   \]
   is an available cardinality and is nonzero, then
   \[
      \delta
      \le
      \psi\left(
         \left(\sum_q\tau_qy_q\right)h_\delta(y)^{\rho-1}
         +
         \sigma h_\delta(y)^\rho
      \right).
      \tag{WAE2}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((WAE1)\) failed for some \(y,k\), then the right side of \((WAP2)\)
   would be positive.  By
   \cref{lem:weighted-atomized-prefix-normal-form}, an integral query set and
   the corresponding top-\(k\) paid-degree prefix would have positive repair
   reduced gain, contradicting the hypothesis.

   For the degree-superlevel form, put \(h=h_\delta(y)\).  The top \(h\) points
   have paid degree at least \(\delta\), so \(D_y^\gamma(h)\ge\delta h\).
   Applying \((WAE1)\) at cardinality \(h\) and dividing by \(h\) gives
   \((WAE2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{assumption}[Paid atomized-prefix separator]
   \label{asm:paid-atomized-prefix-separator}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:atomized-paid-core-hit-kernel-cover}.  Let
   \(\mathcal W\) be a finite family of certified containers.  Each
   \(W\in\mathcal W\) comes with a price factor \(\psi_W>0\), an exponent
   \(0\le\rho_W\le1\), and a finite set of available cardinalities
   \(\mathcal K_W\subseteq\{1,\ldots,|W|\}\).  For \(k\in\mathcal K_W\), write
   \[
      T_W(k)=\psi_Wk^{\rho_W},
      \qquad
      S_W(k)=\psi_Wk^{1+\rho_W}.
   \]
   The required build-time closure is the following: for every price system
   considered below and every integral query set \(Q'\subseteq\mathcal Q\), the
   top-\(k\) prefix of \(W\) sorted by
   \[
      p\mapsto
      \sum_{q\in Q':(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}
   \]
   is an available Boolean Pareto core with prices \(T_W(k),S_W(k)\).  This
   closure is finite; in the worst case preprocessing may include all
   \(k\)-subsets of each \(W\), while the prefix rule only identifies the
   subset used by the separator proof.

   The container family is paid atomized-prefix separating if, for every
   nonnegative price system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying
   \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\), there are \(W\in\mathcal W\),
   \(k\in\mathcal K_W\), and fractional query weights \(0\le y_q\le1\) such
   that, with \(D_{W,y}^\gamma(k)\) denoting the top-\(k\) paid-degree sum
   inside \(W\),
   \[
      D_{W,y}^\gamma(k)
      >
      \psi_W\left(
         k^{\rho_W}\sum_q\tau_qy_q+\sigma k^{1+\rho_W}
      \right).
      \tag{PAPS1}
   \]
\end{assumption}

\begin{corollary}[Paid prefixes imply the hit-kernel cover]
   \label{cor:paid-prefix-hit-kernel-cover}
   In the setting of \cref{asm:paid-atomized-prefix-separator}, if
   \(\mathcal W\) is paid atomized-prefix separating, then
   \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\) is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \cref{cor:atomized-paid-core-hit-kernel-cover}, it is enough to show that
   every price system satisfying \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\) admits an available core
   satisfying \((APH4)\).  Apply
   \cref{asm:paid-atomized-prefix-separator} to such a price system.  The
   strict inequality \((PAPS1)\) makes the right side of \((WAP2)\) positive
   for the fixed container \(W\), cardinality \(k\), price factor \(\psi_W\),
   and exponent \(\rho_W\).  Hence
   \cref{lem:weighted-atomized-prefix-normal-form} gives an integral query set
   \(Q'\) whose top-\(k\) paid prefix satisfies \((APH4)\) with prices
   \(T_W(k),S_W(k)\).  This prefix is an available Pareto core by the closure
   built into \cref{asm:paid-atomized-prefix-separator}, so the hypothesis of
   \cref{cor:atomized-paid-core-hit-kernel-cover} holds.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Paid prefix residual envelope]
   \label{cor:paid-prefix-residual-envelope}
   Work in the setting of \cref{asm:paid-atomized-prefix-separator}.  Let
   \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) be a residual price system satisfying
   \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\) and having nonpositive repair reduced gain on every
   available paid prefix from \(\mathcal W\).  Then for every
   \(W\in\mathcal W\), every \(k\in\mathcal K_W\), and every fractional query
   weighting \(0\le y\le1\),
   \[
      D_{W,y}^\gamma(k)
      \le
      \psi_W\left(
         k^{\rho_W}\sum_q\tau_qy_q+\sigma k^{1+\rho_W}
      \right).
      \tag{PPRE1}
   \]
   Consequently, if
   \[
      h_{W,\delta}(y)=|\{p\in W:d_y^\gamma(p)\ge\delta\}|
   \]
   lies in \(\mathcal K_W\) and is nonzero, then
   \[
      \delta
      \le
      \psi_W\left(
         \left(\sum_q\tau_qy_q\right)h_{W,\delta}(y)^{\rho_W-1}
         +
         \sigma h_{W,\delta}(y)^{\rho_W}
      \right).
      \tag{PPRE2}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \cref{cor:weighted-atomized-prefix-envelope} separately inside each
   certified container \(W\), with \(\psi=\psi_W\), \(\rho=\rho_W\), and the
   available cardinalities \(\mathcal K_W\).  The hypothesis that no paid prefix
   has positive repair reduced gain is exactly the hypothesis of that
   corollary.  The two displayed inequalities are \((WAE1)\) and \((WAE2)\) in
   this container-indexed notation.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Weak-type form of the paid prefix envelope]
   \label{lem:paid-prefix-weak-type}
   Work in the residual setting of
   \cref{cor:paid-prefix-residual-envelope}.  Fix a container \(W\), a
   fractional query weighting \(0\le y\le1\), and write
   \[
      A_y=\sum_q\tau_qy_q,\qquad \rho=\rho_W,\qquad \psi=\psi_W.
   \]
   Assume \(0<\rho<1\).  Let
   \[
      h_\delta=h_{W,\delta}(y)
      =
      |\{p\in W:d_y^\gamma(p)\ge\delta\}|
   \]
   be nonzero and available, and let \(\delta>0\).  If \(\sigma=0\), then
   \[
      h_\delta
      \le
      \left(\frac{\psi A_y}{\delta}\right)^{1/(1-\rho)}.
      \tag{PWT1}
   \]
   If \(\sigma>0\), then at least one of the two alternatives holds:
   \[
      h_\delta
      \le
      \left(\frac{2\psi A_y}{\delta}\right)^{1/(1-\rho)}
      \tag{PWT2}
   \]
   or
   \[
      h_\delta
      \ge
      \left(\frac{\delta}{2\psi\sigma}\right)^{1/\rho}.
      \tag{PWT3}
   \]
   Moreover, if \(A_y>0\), \(\sigma>0\), and
   \[
      k_\star=\frac{(1-\rho)A_y}{\rho\sigma},
   \]
   then for every \(a\ge1\), every available nonzero superlevel with
   \(a^{-1}k_\star\le h_\delta\le ak_\star\) satisfies
   \[
      \delta
      \le
      a\,C_\rho\,\psi A_y^\rho\sigma^{1-\rho},
      \qquad
      C_\rho=\rho^{-\rho}(1-\rho)^{-(1-\rho)}.
      \tag{PWT4}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   The superlevel envelope \((PPRE2)\) gives
   \[
      \delta
      \le
      \psi\left(A_yh_\delta^{\rho-1}+\sigma h_\delta^\rho\right).
      \tag{PWT5}
   \]
   When \(\sigma=0\), rearranging \((PWT5)\) gives \((PWT1)\).

   Now assume \(\sigma>0\).  Since the two summands on the right of
   \((PWT5)\) are nonnegative, at least one is at least \(\delta/2\).  The
   query-price case
   \[
      \psi A_yh_\delta^{\rho-1}\ge\delta/2
   \]
   is exactly \((PWT2)\), while the storage-price case
   \[
      \psi\sigma h_\delta^\rho\ge\delta/2
   \]
   is exactly \((PWT3)\).

   For the balanced-scale statement, minimize
   \(A_yh^{\rho-1}+\sigma h^\rho\) over \(h>0\).  The stationary point is
   \(k_\star=(1-\rho)A_y/(\rho\sigma)\), and
   \[
      A_yk_\star^{\rho-1}+\sigma k_\star^\rho
      =
      C_\rho A_y^\rho\sigma^{1-\rho}.
   \]
   If \(h_\delta=\lambda k_\star\) with \(\lambda\in[a^{-1},a]\), then
   \[
      A_yh_\delta^{\rho-1}+\sigma h_\delta^\rho
      =
      \lambda^{\rho-1}A_yk_\star^{\rho-1}
      +
      \lambda^\rho\sigma k_\star^\rho
      \le
      a\left(A_yk_\star^{\rho-1}+\sigma k_\star^\rho\right).
   \]
   Combining this estimate with \((PWT5)\) proves \((PWT4)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Forbidden weak-type superlevel exposes a prefix]
   \label{lem:forbidden-weak-type-superlevel}
   Work in the setting of \cref{asm:paid-atomized-prefix-separator}, and fix a
   nonnegative price system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying
   \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\).  Suppose there are a certified container
   \(W\in\mathcal W\), fractional query weights \(0\le y_q\le1\), and a level
   \(\delta>0\) such that
   \[
      h=h_{W,\delta}(y)=|\{p\in W:d_y^\gamma(p)\ge\delta\}|
   \]
   is nonzero and belongs to \(\mathcal K_W\).  Put
   \[
      A_y=\sum_q\tau_qy_q,
      \qquad
      \rho=\rho_W,
      \qquad
      \psi=\psi_W .
   \]
   Assume \(0<\rho<1\).  If \(\sigma=0\) and
   \[
      h>
      \left(\frac{\psi A_y}{\delta}\right)^{1/(1-\rho)},
      \tag{FWS1}
   \]
   then an available paid prefix has positive repair reduced gain.
   If \(\sigma>0\) and
   \[
      h>
      \left(\frac{2\psi A_y}{\delta}\right)^{1/(1-\rho)}
      \quad\text{and}\quad
      h<
      \left(\frac{\delta}{2\psi\sigma}\right)^{1/\rho},
      \tag{FWS2}
   \]
   then an available paid prefix has positive repair reduced gain.
   Finally, if \(A_y>0\), \(\sigma>0\), and for some \(a\ge1\),
   \[
      a^{-1}\frac{(1-\rho)A_y}{\rho\sigma}
      \le h\le
      a\frac{(1-\rho)A_y}{\rho\sigma},
      \qquad
      \delta>
      a\,C_\rho\,\psi A_y^\rho\sigma^{1-\rho},
      \tag{FWS3}
   \]
   where \(C_\rho=\rho^{-\rho}(1-\rho)^{-(1-\rho)}\), then an available paid
   prefix has positive repair reduced gain.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Suppose, toward a contradiction, that no available paid prefix has positive
   repair reduced gain.  Then
   \cref{cor:paid-prefix-residual-envelope} applies to
   \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\), and hence
   \cref{lem:paid-prefix-weak-type} applies inside \(W\) at the level
   \(\delta\).  If \(\sigma=0\), \((PWT1)\) contradicts \((FWS1)\).  If
   \(\sigma>0\), the two alternatives \((PWT2)\)--\((PWT3)\) contradict
   \((FWS2)\).  In the balanced case, \((PWT4)\) contradicts \((FWS3)\).
   Therefore some available paid prefix has positive repair reduced gain.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Weak-type separator implies the hit-kernel cover]
   \label{cor:weak-type-prefix-hit-kernel-cover}
   Work in the setting of \cref{asm:paid-atomized-prefix-separator}, and assume
   every container has exponent \(0<\rho_W<1\).  Suppose that every nonnegative
   price system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\)
   admits a certified container, fractional query weighting, and available
   superlevel satisfying one of \((FWS1)\), \((FWS2)\), or \((FWS3)\).  Then
   \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\) is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Suppose \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\) were infeasible.  As in the proof of
   \cref{cor:atomized-paid-core-hit-kernel-cover}, there is a nonnegative price
   system satisfying \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\) and having nonpositive repair
   reduced gain on every available Boolean core record.  By the weak-type
   separator hypothesis and
   \cref{lem:forbidden-weak-type-superlevel}, the same price system exposes an
   available paid prefix with positive repair reduced gain.  This prefix is one
   of the available Boolean core records, a contradiction.  Hence
   \((\mathsf{HKC}_{\mathcal U})\) is feasible.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Cardinality-net weak-type separator]
   \label{lem:cardinality-net-weak-type-superlevel}
   Work in the setting of \cref{asm:paid-atomized-prefix-separator}, and fix a
   nonnegative price system \((\gamma,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying
   \((APC1)\)--\((APC2)\).  Fix a container \(W\in\mathcal W\) with
   \(0<\rho_W<1\), and suppose its available cardinalities are
   \(b\)-dense from below: for every integer \(1\le h\le |W|\), some
   \(k\in\mathcal K_W\) satisfies
   \[
      h/b\le k\le h .
      \tag{CNW0}
   \]
   Let \(0\le y_q\le1\), let
   \[
      h=|\{p\in W:d_y^\gamma(p)\ge\delta\}|
   \]
   be nonzero, and put
   \[
      A_y=\sum_q\tau_qy_q,\qquad
      \rho=\rho_W,\qquad
      \psi=\psi_W,\qquad
      \widehat A_y=b^{1-\rho}A_y .
   \]
   If
   \[
      \delta>
      \psi\left(\widehat A_yh^{\rho-1}+\sigma h^\rho\right),
      \tag{CNW1}
   \]
