\cref{cor:weak-type-prefix-hit-kernel-cover} make this operational: a proposed
geometric separator only has to return one certified superlevel in the
forbidden middle regime, after which the finite cover duality supplies the
positive column and the hit-kernel cover.
\Cref{lem:cardinality-net-weak-type-superlevel} removes the exact-cardinality
artifact from this target.  If the available prefix sizes form a constant-net,
for example the powers of two, then a list-decoding or range-reporting
separator may return an arbitrary heavy superlevel with only the displayed
constant slack; the verifier rounds its cardinality down to an available prefix
and the final retained column is still an ordinary paid prefix.
\Cref{lem:layer-cake-weak-type-separator} gives the averaged version needed for
list-size arguments: it is enough to prove that a weighted collection of levels,
or a truncated Lorentz moment of the paid-degree sequence, has positive surplus
over the recursive query/storage envelope.  A positive average cannot hide; one
level is already a forbidden weak-type superlevel after cardinality rounding.
\Cref{lem:aggregate-list-moment-weak-type-separator} is the list-size form of
the same statement.  The query side needs only the aggregate list mass \(M_1\)
through the concave power \(M_0^{1-\rho}M_1^\rho\); the storage side is the
\((1+\rho)\)-moment \(M_{1+\rho}\), or the cruder cap \(H^\rho M_1\).  Thus a
spherical or lattice list-decoding theorem can aim to lower-bound the captured
paid mass \(B\) while upper-bounding only these average list-size quantities.
\Cref{def:success-normalized-aggregate-list-panel} makes this the same
success-normalized potential as in the compressed-bucket picture: the useful
quantity is not raw list size, but list query/storage cost divided by captured
hit mass.  \Cref{asm:balanced-aggregate-list-size-separator} is therefore the
plug-in theorem target for tensorized spherical filters, range-reporting
violator search, lattice decoders, or any other proposal mechanism.  A proposed
geometric proof only has to output one balanced aggregate panel; the LP
materialization then turns that averaged certificate into ordinary retained
filters.
\Cref{lem:average-list-size-panel-criterion} gives the normalized probability
form of the same target.  After choosing a finite law over levels, the geometric
proof only has to show
\[
   \E[\text{captured paid list mass}]
   >
   \psi\left(
      \widehat A_y(\E[\text{list size}])^\rho
      +
      \sigma\E[\text{list size}^{1+\rho}]
   \right),
\]
or the capped analogue.  This is the exact average Renyi list-size statement
suggested by the compressed-bucket route; large lists are allowed if their
\((1+\rho)\)-moment is paid by the captured hit mass.
\Cref{lem:random-list-proposal-criterion} removes the remaining threshold-list
artifact.  A build-time routine may output any random list \(\mathcal L\) inside
a certified container.  If its expected paid value beats the same query and
storage moments of \(K=|\mathcal L|\), the exact verifier replaces it by an
available top-degree prefix with positive reduced gain.  Thus \(k\)-means++,
facility search, AQ buckets, LP range reporting, or list/lattice decoders only
need to generate high value-per-moment lists; they do not need to align their
raw output with the final retained prefix.
\Cref{lem:query-layer-random-list-proposal} removes the remaining fractional
query-weight artifact from this interface: any successful fractional-query list
certificate has an ordinary threshold query layer with the same surplus.
\Cref{cor:seeded-list-proposal-criterion} and
\cref{cor:marginal-list-proposal-criterion} are the two forms most useful for
implementation and for geometry.  A seeded decoder only has to prove an average
value-per-moment inequality over its seed law; one good seed then exists and is
verified exactly.  A soft or randomized decoder can instead certify only the
inclusion marginals and a second moment of the emitted list.
\Cref{cor:query-layer-seeded-marginal-proposals} combines these two reductions:
seeded and marginal certificates may also be materialized on an ordinary
threshold query layer.  Thus fractional query weights are only an analysis
device; the retained filters are still Boolean query-side activations.  This
turns the remaining separator into a concrete moment problem for geometric
neighborhoods, facility cells, additive-code buckets, or list-decoding output
sets.
\Cref{cor:query-free-marginal-proposal-separator} removes the query side from
the proposal mechanism as well.  A soft bucket only has to specify update
marginals and a realizable second moment; the canonical positive-margin query
layer is chosen after the dual prices are known, and the final retained object
is still the exact top-degree Boolean prefix.  This is the fractional analogue
of dense-overlap column generation: preprocessing may search over soft
facilities, additive-quantization codes, or list-decoder panels, but the LP pays
only for the verified column it keeps.
\Cref{cor:independent-soft-proposal-separator} is the simplest operational
version: independent thinning turns a responsibility vector of mass \(\mu\) into
a valid proposal with second moment at most \(\mu+\mu^2\), hence with the usual
\(\mu^{1+\rho}\) storage charge once \(\mu\ge1\).
\Cref{cor:finite-soft-bucket-separation} turns this into an exact finite
column-generation oracle: for any generated pool of soft buckets, the only
build-time optimization objective is the scalar reduced gain \((FSB1)\), and
positive gain is both necessary and sufficient for that pool to defeat the
current surplus dual.
\Cref{cor:aggregate-list-moment-residual-envelope} is the matching obstruction:
if the hit-kernel cover fails, every finite list-size panel obeys \((ALR1)\).
Thus a proof of the polylog endpoint can now target a single averaged
inequality, rather than locating a profitable dense cluster or superlevel by
hand.

\Cref{cor:paid-compression-hit-kernel-cover} is the fractional dense-filter
cover in its paid form.  The separator does not choose disjoint dense clusters.
It only has to prove that any overbudget value-proportional primitive law can be
compressed, fractionally and with arbitrary overlap, into cheaper Pareto cores.
Query overlap is charged by
\(\sum_C\lambda_CT_C\mathbf 1\{q\in Q'_C\}\), storage by
\(\sum_C\lambda_CS_C\), and coverage is inherited from the primitive hit
kernel.  Thus ordinary spherical slices, singleton dense slices, quotient
cores, \(k\)-means-style facilities, additive-quantization buckets, and
list-decoding outputs are all merely proposal mechanisms for the same paid
reduced-cost inequality \((PCOV4)\).  When the family is closed under canonical
assignment, \cref{lem:canonical-paid-core-hinge} removes the assignment and
query-side choices too: preprocessing only has to search for an update core
whose paid whole-slice support violates the hinge inequality \((CPH4)\).
\Cref{lem:atomized-paid-core-hinge} is sharper still.  It allows a core to
capture only the paid primitive atoms that actually lie in its update side, so
the support term becomes the hit-kernel-weighted quantity
\[
   \bar h_U^\gamma(q)
   =
   \sum_{p\in U:(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\gamma_{p,q}r_{p,q}.
\]
The remaining dense theorem can therefore be stated without choosing primitive
slice assignments at all: every surplus singleton-saturated paid dual must
contain a radius-contracting core whose atomized support violates \((APH4)\).
\Cref{lem:weighted-atomized-prefix-normal-form} pushes this to the prefix level:
inside a certified container, every fractional query weighting induces paid
degrees \(d_y^\gamma(p)\), and the best \(k\)-point core is simply the top-\(k\)
prefix.  Thus failure of all paid prefixes is equivalent to the explicit
degree envelope \((WAE1)\)--\((WAE2)\), which is the concrete residual packing
condition left for geometry.
\Cref{asm:paid-atomized-prefix-separator} and
\cref{cor:paid-prefix-hit-kernel-cover} make this a complete dense-side
criterion: every surplus paid dual only has to violate one certified
container-prefix envelope.  If it does not, then
\cref{cor:paid-prefix-residual-envelope} gives the exact counterexample format
that the spherical residual or the next geometric separator must rule out.
\Cref{lem:paid-prefix-weak-type} converts that counterexample into an explicit
level-set dichotomy: residual paid mass is either query-price small, storage
massive, or below the balanced density \(C_\rho\psi A_y^\rho\sigma^{1-\rho}\).
\Cref{cor:weak-type-prefix-hit-kernel-cover} is the corresponding acceptance
criterion: any geometric, range-reporting, or list-decoding routine that always
finds a forbidden weak-type superlevel proves the primitive hit-kernel cover.

\begin{assumption}[Compression-dual separator]
   \label{asm:compression-dual-separator}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:residual-separator-local-cover}.  Fix a
   finite family \(\mathcal R\) of query-weighted Pareto-core records as in
   \cref{lem:slice-core-compression-dual}, and enlarge the finite filter
   universe by all threshold activations of the underlying cores appearing in
   those records.  The family \(\mathcal R\) is compression-dual separating if,
   for every surplus dual price system
   \((\alpha,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying \((RS1)\) and having nonpositive reduced
   gain on the spherical buckets, whole high-correlation dense slices, and
   atom-safe primitive dense prefixes, the associated compression dual
   \((SCD\text{-}D)\) has no feasible \(\beta\) satisfying \((SCDD1)\).
\end{assumption}

\begin{corollary}[Compression-dual separation implies local cover]
   \label{cor:compression-dual-local-cover}
   In the setting of \cref{asm:compression-dual-separator}, if
   \(\mathcal R\) is compression-dual separating, then the finite filter-cover
   LP \((\mathsf{FC}_{\mathcal N})\) is feasible with query budget \(L\) and
   storage budget \(S\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Suppose the filter-cover LP were infeasible.  By
   \cref{lem:finite-filter-cover-dual}, there is a surplus dual price system
   with nonpositive reduced gain on every retained column.  In particular it has
   nonpositive gain on the spherical buckets, whole high-correlation dense
   slices, and atom-safe primitive prefixes.  Compression-dual separation rules
   out alternative \textup{(ii)} of
   \cref{lem:slice-core-compression-dual}, so alternative \textup{(i)} holds:
   there is a slice-to-core domination certificate of price
   \(<\mathsf A_{\rm hc}\).  By \cref{lem:slice-to-core-domination}, some
   threshold activation of an underlying core represented in \(\mathcal R\) has
   positive reduced gain.  This activation is a retained column of the enlarged
   universe, contradicting the dual certificate.  Hence the cover LP is
   feasible.
\end{proof}

\Cref{asm:compression-dual-separator} is the exact finite form of the remaining
dense-versus-pseudo-random theorem.  One must rule out a simultaneous pair of
certificates: a filter-cover dual \((\alpha,\tau,\sigma)\) that defeats
spherical buckets and primitive dense slices, and a compression dual \(\beta\)
under which every proposed radius-contracting core is no better than its
Pareto price.  A proof may do this by a geometric argument, by adding richer
core records, or by showing that such a \(\beta\)-spread residual already
violates the spherical reduced-gain test.

The exact weighted form is stronger than the dyadic core screen above.  The
dyadic objective \(\theta_jc_U(q)\) lower-bounds \(a_U(q)\) on one price layer
and is useful when the proposal generator wants an unweighted counting problem.
But the filter-cover proof itself does not need to pay that dyadic loss: an
offline separator with access to the dual prices can optimize \((WPC2)\)
directly, and the retained column is still the same ordinary query activation
\((U,Q_\alpha^+(U))\).  Thus demand-layering is a build-time simplification, not
an inherent overhead in the fractional dense-cover theorem.

\begin{assumption}[Layer quotient separator]
   \label{asm:layer-quotient-separator}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:residual-separator-local-cover}.  Suppose a
   surplus dual price system \((\alpha,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfies \((RS1)\) and
   has nonpositive reduced gain on the spherical buckets, whole
   high-correlation dense slices, and atom-safe dense prefixes.  Partition the
   positive demand prices \(\alpha_{p,q}\) into dyadic classes
   \(\mathcal N_j\) as in \cref{lem:dyadic-quotient-packing}.

   The quotient family \(\mathcal G\) is layer separating if, for every such
   residual dual, there is a dyadic class \(j\) and a quotient
   \(G\in\mathcal G\) such that
   \[
      \theta_j C_j(G)>P(G),
      \tag{LQS1}
   \]
   with \(C_j(G)\) and \(P(G)\) defined in
   \cref{cor:unweighted-quotient-coverage-screen}.
\end{assumption}

\begin{corollary}[Layer separation implies local cover]
   \label{cor:layer-separation-local-cover}
   In the setting of \cref{cor:residual-separator-local-cover}, if the quotient
   family is layer separating in the sense of
   \cref{asm:layer-quotient-separator}, then the finite filter-cover LP
   \((\mathsf{FC}_{\mathcal N})\) is feasible with query budget \(L\) and
   storage budget \(S\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Suppose the LP were infeasible.  By \cref{lem:finite-filter-cover-dual} there
   is a surplus dual system with nonpositive reduced gain on every column in the
   finite universe.  In particular, the spherical buckets, whole dense slices,
   and atom-safe prefixes do not have positive gain.  The layer separator
   therefore returns \(j\) and \(G\) satisfying \((LQS1)\).  By
   \cref{cor:unweighted-quotient-coverage-screen}, this quotient has positive
   reduced gain, contradicting the dual certificate.  Hence the LP is feasible.
\end{proof}

\Cref{asm:layer-quotient-separator} is the most concrete form of the remaining
fractional dense-overlap theorem.  It asks only for an unweighted coverage
separator on one dyadic price layer, while the final acceptance test remains the
original weighted reduced-gain inequality.  Thus \(k\)-means++, additive vector
quantization, cap nets, range-reporting violator search, or lattice/list
decoders are all proposal mechanisms for the same certificate; none is assumed
correct until it produces a quotient satisfying \((LQS1)\) and hence the exact
dual inequality.

\begin{corollary}[Quotient-packing local cover criterion]
   \label{cor:quotient-packing-local-cover}
   In the setting of \cref{cor:residual-separator-local-cover}, suppose that for
   every surplus dual price system \((\alpha,\tau,\sigma)\) satisfying \((RS1)\),
   at least one of the following holds:
   a spherical bucket has positive reduced gain; a whole high-correlation dense
   slice has positive reduced gain; an atom-safe dense prefix has positive
   reduced gain; or there is a quotient-packing law \(\Gamma\) on \(\mathcal G\)
   satisfying \((QP3)\).  Then the finite filter-cover LP is feasible with query
   budget \(L\) and storage budget \(S\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If the LP were infeasible, \cref{lem:finite-filter-cover-dual} would give a
   surplus dual price system with nonpositive reduced gain on every column in the
   finite universe.  The first three alternatives are then impossible because the
   universe contains the spherical buckets, whole dense slices, and atom-safe
   dense prefixes.  The last alternative is impossible by
   \cref{lem:quotient-packing-reduced-gain}, since \((QP3)\) would expose a
   positive-gain quotient column.  This contradicts the assumed alternative for
   every surplus dual.
\end{proof}

Thus the remaining geometric task can be stated in an algorithmic column-generation
form: against every residual dual, construct a quotient-packing law \(\Gamma\)
with \(\mathsf A_\Gamma>\mathsf P_\Gamma\).  Expensive preprocessing may search
for this law by clustering, cap nets, additive quantization, or learned seeds,
but the retained proof object is only the verified quotient family and the
inequality \((QP3)\).

\begin{lemma}[Finite-signature filter-cover compiler]
   \label{lem:finite-signature-filter-cover}
   Let $\Omega$ be a query domain for one resident node \(P\), and let
   $\mathcal F$ be a finite priced-filter universe.  Suppose preprocessing
   supplies a finite signature set \(\Sigma\), a decoder
   \(\sigma:\Omega\to\Sigma\), active bits \(a_A(\sigma_0)\in\{0,1\}\), and
   witness supersets \(W_{\sigma_0}\subseteq P\) such that, for every
   \(q\in\Omega\) with \(\sigma(q)=\sigma_0\),
   \[
      a_A(q)=a_A(\sigma_0)\qquad(A\in\mathcal F),
      \qquad
      \{p\in P:\|p-q\|\le r\}\subseteq W_{\sigma_0}.
      \tag{FS1}
   \]
   Each filter \(A\) has update side \(U_A\), certified query price \(T_A\),
   and certified storage price \(S_A\).  Assume the finite signature LP
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \text{\rm find} & \lambda_A\ge0\\[0.4em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{A:p\in U_A}a_A(\sigma_0)\lambda_A\ge1
        \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma,\ p\in W_{\sigma_0}),\\[0.8em]
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_Aa_A(\sigma_0)T_A\lambda_A\le L_{\sigma_0}
        \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma),\\[0.8em]
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_AS_A\lambda_A\le S
   \end{array}
   \tag{$\mathsf{SFC}_\Sigma$}
   \]
   is feasible, and that the atom bounds
   \[
      a_A(\sigma_0)T_A\le L_{\sigma_0}
      \qquad(A\in\mathcal F,\ \sigma_0\in\Sigma),
      \qquad
      S_A\le S
      \tag{FS2}
   \]
   hold.  Put
   \[
      M_\Sigma=\sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma}|W_{\sigma_0}|,
      \qquad
      B\ge
      \max\left\{
         1,\log(4(M_\Sigma+1)),\log(8(|\Sigma|+1))
      \right\}.
   \]
   Then preprocessing can retain an integral multiset of filters \(\mathcal R\)
   such that every query \(q\in\Omega\) has certified active cost
   \[
      \sum_{A\in\mathcal R}a_A(q)T_A
      \le
      3B\,L_{\sigma(q)},
   \]
   total storage
   \[
      \sum_{A\in\mathcal R}S_A\le3BS,
   \]
   and routing correctness for all near pairs: if \(p\in P\) and
   \(\|p-q\|\le r\), then some retained active filter \(A\in\mathcal R\)
   satisfies \(p\in U_A\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \cref{lem:poisson-filter-cover-materialization} with query constraint
   set \(\Sigma\) and demand set
   \[
      \mathcal N_\Sigma
      =
      \{(p,\sigma_0):\sigma_0\in\Sigma,\ p\in W_{\sigma_0}\}.
   \]
   The coverage coefficient is
   \[
      c_A(p,\sigma_0)=\mathbf 1\{p\in U_A\}a_A(\sigma_0),
   \]
   and the LP \((\mathsf{SFC}_\Sigma)\) is exactly
   \((\mathsf{FC}_{\mathcal N_\Sigma})\).  The materialization lemma gives a
   retained multiset whose signature loads and storage are bounded by the
   displayed factors and whose every finite demand is covered.

   Now fix an actual query \(q\), let \(\sigma_0=\sigma(q)\), and let
   \(p\in P\) satisfy \(\|p-q\|\le r\).  By \((FS1)\), \(p\in W_{\sigma_0}\).
   The retained finite cover contains some \(A\) with \(p\in U_A\) and
   \(a_A(\sigma_0)=1\).  Again by \((FS1)\), \(a_A(q)=1\).  Thus the query probes
   a retained child containing the near point.  The active-cost bound for the
   actual query is the signature-load bound for \(\sigma_0\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Exact-near-set finite-signature compiler]
   \label{lem:exact-near-set-filter-cover}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:finite-signature-filter-cover}, but suppose
   the signature records the exact unresolved near set.  Thus preprocessing
   supplies sets \(N_{\sigma_0}\subseteq P\) such that, for every
   \(q\in\Omega\) with \(\sigma(q)=\sigma_0\),
   \[
      a_A(q)=a_A(\sigma_0)\qquad(A\in\mathcal F),
      \qquad
      \{p\in P:\|p-q\|\le r\}=N_{\sigma_0}.
      \tag{EN1}
   \]
   Write \(\Sigma^+=\{\sigma_0\in\Sigma:N_{\sigma_0}\ne\emptyset\}\) and
   \[
      e_A(\sigma_0)
      =
      a_A(\sigma_0)\mathbf 1\{U_A\cap N_{\sigma_0}\ne\emptyset\}.
   \]
   Assume the weaker existential signature LP
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \text{\rm find} & \lambda_A\ge0\\[0.4em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_Ae_A(\sigma_0)\lambda_A\ge1
        \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+),\\[0.8em]
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_Aa_A(\sigma_0)T_A\lambda_A\le L_{\sigma_0}
        \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma),\\[0.8em]
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_AS_A\lambda_A\le S
   \end{array}
   \tag{$\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma$}
   \]
   is feasible, and that the atom bounds \((FS2)\) hold.  Put
   \[
      M_\Sigma^{\exists}=|\Sigma^+|,
      \qquad
      B\ge
      \max\left\{
         1,\log(4(M_\Sigma^{\exists}+1)),\log(8(|\Sigma|+1))
      \right\}.
   \]
   Then preprocessing can retain an integral multiset of filters \(\mathcal R\)
   with active cost at most \(3B\,L_{\sigma(q)}\) for every query, total storage
   at most \(3BS\), and ANN routing correctness: if \(N_{\sigma(q)}\ne\emptyset\),
   then some retained active filter contains a point within distance \(r\) of
   \(q\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Use the same Poisson rounding as in
   \cref{lem:poisson-filter-cover-materialization}.  Independently draw
   \(M_A\sim{\rm Pois}(B\lambda_A)\) and retain \(M_A\) copies of \(A\).  For
   a nonempty signature \(\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+\), feasibility gives
   \(\Lambda_{\sigma_0}=\sum_Ae_A(\sigma_0)\lambda_A\ge1\), hence
   \[
      \Pr[\sigma_0\text{ is not existentially covered}]
      =
      \Pr\left[\sum_Ae_A(\sigma_0)M_A=0\right]
      =
      e^{-B\Lambda_{\sigma_0}}
      \le e^{-B}.
   \]
   The choice of \(B\) makes the probability that some nonempty signature is
   uncovered at most \(1/4\).

   For each signature with \(L_{\sigma_0}>0\), put
   \[
      X_{\sigma_0}=
      \sum_A M_A\,\frac{a_A(\sigma_0)T_A}{L_{\sigma_0}}.
   \]
   The atom bound in \((FS2)\) gives weights in \([0,1]\), and LP feasibility
   gives \(\E X_{\sigma_0}\le B\).  The Chernoff argument in
   \cref{lem:poisson-filter-cover-materialization} therefore gives
   \(\Pr[X_{\sigma_0}>3B]\le e^{-B}\).  If \(L_{\sigma_0}=0\), then \((FS2)\)
   forces \(a_A(\sigma_0)T_A=0\) for every \(A\), so the signature-load bound is
   deterministic.  The same bound holds for total storage after normalizing by
   \(S\); if \(S=0\), then \((FS2)\) forces every \(S_A=0\).  A union bound over
   all signatures and the storage constraint has failure probability at most
   \(1/4\).  With positive probability all existential coverage, signature-load,
   and storage events hold, so fix such an outcome.

   Now take an actual query \(q\) with \(\sigma(q)=\sigma_0\) and
   \(N_{\sigma_0}\ne\emptyset\).  Existential coverage gives a retained filter
   \(A\) with \(a_A(\sigma_0)=1\) and \(U_A\cap N_{\sigma_0}\ne\emptyset\).
   By \((EN1)\), \(a_A(q)=1\), and every point of \(N_{\sigma_0}\) is within
   distance \(r\) of \(q\).  Thus the active child contains at least one valid
   ANN witness, which final metric verification can accept.  The cost and
   storage bounds are the materialized signature bounds.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Exact-near-set signature dual]
   \label{lem:exact-near-set-signature-dual}
   In the setting of \cref{lem:exact-near-set-filter-cover}, the LP
   \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is infeasible if and only if there are signature
   demand prices \(\beta_{\sigma_0}\ge0\) for \(\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+\), query
   prices \(\tau_{\sigma_0}\ge0\) for \(\sigma_0\in\Sigma\), and a storage price
   \(\theta\ge0\) such that
   \[
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}\beta_{\sigma_0}
      >
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma}\tau_{\sigma_0}L_{\sigma_0}
      +\theta S,
      \tag{EN-D1}
   \]
   while every filter satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}
      \beta_{\sigma_0}
      a_A(\sigma_0)\mathbf 1\{U_A\cap N_{\sigma_0}\ne\emptyset\}
      \le
      \theta S_A
      +
      T_A\sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma}\tau_{\sigma_0}a_A(\sigma_0).
      \tag{EN-D2}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Apply Farkas' lemma exactly as in
   \cref{lem:finite-filter-cover-dual}, using one lower-bound coverage
   constraint for each nonempty exact signature and the coefficient
   \(e_A(\sigma_0)\) above.  The nonnegative multipliers of these coverage
   constraints are \(\beta_{\sigma_0}\), the query-budget multipliers are
   \(\tau_{\sigma_0}\), and the storage-budget multiplier is \(\theta\).
   Nonnegativity of the coefficient of every variable \(\lambda_A\) is
   \((EN\text{-}D2)\), and strict negativity of the combined right-hand side is
   \((EN\text{-}D1)\).  The converse is the same certificate read backward.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exact-signature column generation]
   \label{cor:exact-signature-column-generation}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:exact-near-set-signature-dual}.  For a
   price system \((\beta,\tau,\theta)\), define the exact-signature reduced
   gain of a filter \(A\in\mathcal F\) by
   \[
      \mathsf{EG}_{\beta,\tau,\theta}(A)
      =
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}
      \beta_{\sigma_0}a_A(\sigma_0)
      \mathbf 1\{U_A\cap N_{\sigma_0}\ne\emptyset\}
      -
      T_A\sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma}\tau_{\sigma_0}a_A(\sigma_0)
      -
      \theta S_A .
      \tag{ESC1}
   \]
   The existential signature LP \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible if and
   only if every nonnegative price system satisfying \((EN\text{-}D1)\) has
   some filter \(A\in\mathcal F\) with
   \[
      \mathsf{EG}_{\beta,\tau,\theta}(A)>0 .
      \tag{ESC2}
   \]
   Consequently, over any finite full universe \(\mathcal F_\star\), unbounded
   preprocessing may solve a restricted LP, read its exact-signature dual, add
   any filter with positive \(\mathsf{EG}\), and terminate with a feasible
   existential cover whenever the full universe satisfies \((ESC2)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \cref{lem:exact-near-set-signature-dual}, infeasibility is exactly the
   existence of a surplus price system satisfying \((EN\text{-}D1)\) and
   \(\mathsf{EG}_{\beta,\tau,\theta}(A)\le0\) for every filter \(A\).  Negating
   this statement gives the equivalence.  The column-generation statement is the
   same finite-pool argument as in \cref{cor:filter-cover-column-generation}:
   each positive-gain column invalidates the current dual certificate, and a
   finite universe can be exhausted only after feasibility has been reached.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Exact-signature coverage-list oracle]
   \label{lem:exact-signature-coverage-list-oracle}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:exact-signature-column-generation}.  Let
   \(\mathcal C\) be a finite build-time family of certified list templates.  A
   template \(C\in\mathcal C\) consists of a container \(W_C\subseteq P\), a
   cardinality \(1\le K_C\le |W_C|\), and certified prices \(T_C,S_C\).  Assume
   the filter universe contains, for every \(C\), every \(K_C\)-point list
   \(L\subseteq W_C\), and every query-signature layer
   \(Q'\subseteq\Sigma\), the filter
   \[
      A(C,L,Q')=(L,Q'),
      \qquad
      U_A=L,
      \qquad
      a_A(\sigma_0)=\mathbf 1\{\sigma_0\in Q'\},
      \qquad
      T_A=T_C,\quad S_A=S_C .
      \tag{ECL0}
   \]
   For a price system \((\beta,\tau,\theta)\), define the positive signature
   weight at template \(C\) by
   \[
      w_C(\sigma_0)=
      \bigl(\beta_{\sigma_0}-T_C\tau_{\sigma_0}\bigr)_+
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+),
      \tag{ECL1}
   \]
   and the exact-signature max-coverage value
   \[
      \mathsf{EC}_{\beta,\tau,\theta}(C)
      =
      \max_{\substack{L\subseteq W_C\\ |L|=K_C}}
      \sum_{\substack{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+\\ L\cap N_{\sigma_0}\ne\emptyset}}
      w_C(\sigma_0)
      -
      \theta S_C .
      \tag{ECL2}
   \]
   If every nonnegative price system satisfying \((EN\text{-}D1)\) has
   \[
      \max_{C\in\mathcal C}\mathsf{EC}_{\beta,\tau,\theta}(C)>0,
      \tag{ECL3}
   \]
   then the existential signature LP \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Fix a surplus price system and choose \(C\) and \(L\subseteq W_C\) attaining
   positive value in \((ECL2)\).  Let
   \[
      Q^+(C,L)=
      \left\{
         \sigma_0\in\Sigma^+:
         L\cap N_{\sigma_0}\ne\emptyset,
         \beta_{\sigma_0}>T_C\tau_{\sigma_0}
      \right\}.
      \tag{ECL4}
   \]
   For \(A=A(C,L,Q^+(C,L))\), the exact-signature gain is
   \[
      \mathsf{EG}_{\beta,\tau,\theta}(A)
      =
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in Q^+(C,L)}
      \left(\beta_{\sigma_0}-T_C\tau_{\sigma_0}\right)
      -
      \theta S_C
      =
      \mathsf{EC}_{\beta,\tau,\theta}(C)>0 .
   \]
   Thus every surplus exact-signature dual has a positive-gain filter, and
   \cref{cor:exact-signature-column-generation} gives feasibility.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Seeded exact-signature list proposal]
   \label{cor:seeded-exact-signature-list-proposal}
   In the setting of \cref{lem:exact-signature-coverage-list-oracle}, it is
   enough to prove the following averaged proposal statement.  For every
   nonnegative price system satisfying \((EN\text{-}D1)\), there is a finite
   seed law \(s\sim\nu\) such that seed \(s\) chooses a template \(C_s\in
   \mathcal C\) and a list \(L_s\subseteq W_{C_s}\), \(|L_s|=K_{C_s}\), with
   \[
      \E_s
      \left[
         \sum_{\substack{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+\\
                         L_s\cap N_{\sigma_0}\ne\emptyset}}
         \bigl(\beta_{\sigma_0}-T_{C_s}\tau_{\sigma_0}\bigr)_+
         -
         \theta S_{C_s}
      \right]
      >0 .
      \tag{ESL1}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If the expectation in \((ESL1)\) is positive, some deterministic seed has
   positive bracketed value.  Its template therefore has positive
   \(\mathsf{EC}\), and \cref{lem:exact-signature-coverage-list-oracle} applies.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Hit-probability exact-signature proposal]
   \label{cor:hit-probability-exact-signature-proposal}
   In the setting of \cref{lem:exact-signature-coverage-list-oracle}, the
   seeded proposal condition may be proved through hit probabilities.  For every
   nonnegative price system satisfying \((EN\text{-}D1)\), suppose there is a
   finite seed law \(s\sim\nu\) such that seed \(s\) chooses a template
   \(C_s\in\mathcal C\) and a randomized list
   \(\mathcal L_s\subseteq W_{C_s}\), always of size \(K_{C_s}\).  Put
   \[
      h_s(\sigma_0)=
      \Pr[\mathcal L_s\cap N_{\sigma_0}\ne\emptyset]
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+).
      \tag{EHP1}
   \]
   If
   \[
      \E_s
      \left[
         \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}
         h_s(\sigma_0)
         \bigl(\beta_{\sigma_0}-T_{C_s}\tau_{\sigma_0}\bigr)_+
         -
         \theta S_{C_s}
      \right]
      >0,
      \tag{EHP2}
   \]
   then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   More generally, it is enough to provide certified lower bounds
   \(\underline h_s(\sigma_0)\le h_s(\sigma_0)\) satisfying \((EHP2)\) with
   \(h_s\) replaced by \(\underline h_s\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Expand the seed by also drawing the randomized list
   \(L_s\sim\mathcal L_s\).  Conditional on \(s\), the expected bracket in
   \((ESL1)\) is exactly the bracket in \((EHP2)\), because
   \[
      \E_{\mathcal L_s}
      \mathbf 1\{\mathcal L_s\cap N_{\sigma_0}\ne\emptyset\}
      =
      h_s(\sigma_0).
   \]
   Thus \((EHP2)\) gives a finite seed law over deterministic lists satisfying
   \((ESL1)\), and \cref{cor:seeded-exact-signature-list-proposal} applies.
   Replacing \(h_s\) by smaller certified lower bounds only decreases the left
   side, so the same argument applies.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Variable-size exact-signature proposal]
   \label{cor:variable-size-exact-signature-proposal}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:exact-signature-column-generation}.  Let a
   finite proposal seed \(s\) choose a container \(W_s\subseteq P\), a finite set
   of available cardinalities \(\mathcal K_s\subseteq\{0,\ldots,|W_s|\}\), and
   certified prices \(T_{s,k},S_{s,k}\) for each \(k\in\mathcal K_s\).  Assume
   the filter universe contains, for every \(s\), every list \(L\subseteq W_s\)
   with \(|L|=k\in\mathcal K_s\), and every query-signature layer
   \(Q'\subseteq\Sigma\), the corresponding filter with update side \(L\),
   activation \(a_A(\sigma_0)=\mathbf 1\{\sigma_0\in Q'\}\), and prices
   \(T_{s,k},S_{s,k}\).

   Suppose that for every nonnegative price system satisfying \((EN\text{-}D1)\)
   there is a finite seed law \(s\sim\nu\), and for each seed a randomized list
   \(\mathcal L_s\subseteq W_s\) with \(|\mathcal L_s|\in\mathcal K_s\), such
   that
   \[
      \E_{s,\mathcal L_s}
      \left[
         \sum_{\substack{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+\\
                         \mathcal L_s\cap N_{\sigma_0}\ne\emptyset}}
         \bigl(\beta_{\sigma_0}
               -T_{s,|\mathcal L_s|}\tau_{\sigma_0}\bigr)_+
         -
         \theta S_{s,|\mathcal L_s|}
      \right]
      >0 .
      \tag{EVS1}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   Equivalently, it is enough to certify size-stratified lower bounds
   \[
      \underline h_{s,k}(\sigma_0)
      \le
      \Pr[
         |\mathcal L_s|=k,
         \mathcal L_s\cap N_{\sigma_0}\ne\emptyset
      ],
      \tag{EVS2}
   \]
   and upper bounds \(\overline p_{s,k}\ge\Pr[|\mathcal L_s|=k]\), satisfying
   \[
      \E_s
      \left[
         \sum_{k\in\mathcal K_s}
         \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}
         \underline h_{s,k}(\sigma_0)
         \bigl(\beta_{\sigma_0}-T_{s,k}\tau_{\sigma_0}\bigr)_+
         -
         \theta\sum_{k\in\mathcal K_s}\overline p_{s,k}S_{s,k}
      \right]
      >0 .
      \tag{EVS3}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((EVS1)\) holds, then some deterministic seed and some deterministic
   list \(L\) in the support have positive realized bracket.  With
   \(k=|L|\), use the corresponding filter template \(C=(W_s,k,T_{s,k},S_{s,k})\)
   and the positive-margin signature layer
   \[
      Q^+(L)=
      \{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+:
        L\cap N_{\sigma_0}\ne\emptyset,
        \beta_{\sigma_0}>T_{s,k}\tau_{\sigma_0}\}.
   \]
   The resulting filter has positive exact-signature gain \((ESC1)\).  Hence
   every surplus exact-signature dual exposes a positive-gain column, and
   \cref{cor:exact-signature-column-generation} gives feasibility.

   The stratified condition \((EVS3)\) lower-bounds the expectation in
   \((EVS1)\): the coverage terms are decreased by replacing true joint
   probabilities by \(\underline h\), while the storage charge is increased by
   replacing true size probabilities by \(\overline p\).  Therefore \((EVS3)\)
   implies \((EVS1)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Bernoulli exact-signature soft bucket]
   \label{cor:bernoulli-exact-signature-soft-bucket}
   In \cref{cor:variable-size-exact-signature-proposal}, the randomized list
   may be generated by independent responsibilities.  A seed \(s\) chooses a
   container \(W_s\), probabilities \(0\le\pi_{s,p}\le1\), available
   cardinalities \(\mathcal K_s\), and prices \(T_{s,k},S_{s,k}\).  Let
   \(\mathcal L_s\) include each \(p\in W_s\) independently with probability
   \(\pi_{s,p}\), conditioned or truncated so that
   \(|\mathcal L_s|\in\mathcal K_s\).  If the resulting size-stratified hit
   probabilities satisfy \((EVS3)\), then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is
   feasible.

   In the unconditioned case with \(\mathcal K_s=\{0,\ldots,|W_s|\}\), and
   with \(T_{s,0}=S_{s,0}=0\) for the empty no-op list, these probabilities are
   coefficients of explicit generating polynomials:
   \[
      \Pr[|\mathcal L_s|=k]
      =
      [z^k]\prod_{p\in W_s}(1-\pi_{s,p}+\pi_{s,p}z),
      \tag{EBS1}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \Pr[|\mathcal L_s|=k,\ \mathcal L_s\cap N_{\sigma_0}\ne\emptyset]
      =
      [z^k]\left(
         \prod_{p\in W_s}(1-\pi_{s,p}+\pi_{s,p}z)
         -
         \prod_{p\in W_s\setminus N_{\sigma_0}}
            (1-\pi_{s,p}+\pi_{s,p}z)
         \prod_{p\in W_s\cap N_{\sigma_0}}(1-\pi_{s,p})
      \right).
      \tag{EBS2}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The first claim is exactly
   \cref{cor:variable-size-exact-signature-proposal} applied to the Bernoulli
   law after any advertised conditioning or truncation.  For the unconditioned
   identities, \((EBS1)\) is the ordinary probability generating function for
   the Bernoulli sum.  The second product in \((EBS2)\) is the generating
   function of lists that avoid \(N_{\sigma_0}\): points outside the near set
   are sampled normally, while every point in \(W_s\cap N_{\sigma_0}\) is forced
   absent.  Subtracting avoiders from all lists gives the coefficient for
   hitting \(N_{\sigma_0}\) at size \(k\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Capped Bernoulli exact-signature mass certificate]
   \label{cor:capped-bernoulli-exact-signature-mass}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:exact-signature-coverage-list-oracle}.  A
   seed \(s\) chooses a fixed-size template \(C_s\in\mathcal C\), written
   \(C_s=(W_s,H_s,T_s,S_s)\), where \(1\le H_s\le |W_s|\), and independent
   responsibilities \(0\le\pi_{s,p}\le1\) on \(W_s\).  Let
   \(B_s\subseteq W_s\) include each \(p\) independently with probability
   \(\pi_{s,p}\), and let \(\varepsilon_s\) be any certified upper bound on
   \[
      \Pr[|B_s|>H_s].
      \tag{ECB1}
   \]
   Define the exact-near-set hit mass and its mass-only lower bound by
   \[
      m_s(\sigma_0)=
      \sum_{p\in W_s\cap N_{\sigma_0}}\pi_{s,p},
      \qquad
      \underline h_s(\sigma_0)=
      \bigl(1-e^{-m_s(\sigma_0)}-\varepsilon_s\bigr)_+ .
      \tag{ECB2}
   \]
   If every nonnegative price system satisfying \((EN\text{-}D1)\) admits a
   finite seed law such that
   \[
      \E_s
      \left[
         \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}
         \underline h_s(\sigma_0)
         \bigl(\beta_{\sigma_0}-T_s\tau_{\sigma_0}\bigr)_+
         -
         \theta S_s
      \right]
      >0,
      \tag{ECB3}
   \]
   then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   In particular, if \(\mu_s=\sum_{p\in W_s}\pi_{s,p}\), then the elementary
   bound
   \[
      \varepsilon_s=\frac{\mu_s}{H_s+1}
      \tag{ECB4}
   \]
   is always valid; sharper Chernoff or exact Poisson-binomial tail bounds may
   be substituted whenever useful.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Convert the soft bucket into a random \(H_s\)-point list.  Sample \(B_s\).
   If \(|B_s|\le H_s\), pad \(B_s\) arbitrarily to an \(H_s\)-point subset
   \(L_s\subseteq W_s\).  If \(|B_s|>H_s\), output any fixed \(H_s\)-point
   subset of \(W_s\).  For every nonempty exact signature,
   \[
      \Pr[L_s\cap N_{\sigma_0}\ne\emptyset]
      \ge
      \Pr[B_s\cap N_{\sigma_0}\ne\emptyset]-\Pr[|B_s|>H_s].
      \tag{ECB5}
   \]
   Independence gives
   \[
      \Pr[B_s\cap N_{\sigma_0}\ne\emptyset]
      =
      1-\prod_{p\in W_s\cap N_{\sigma_0}}(1-\pi_{s,p})
      \ge
      1-e^{-m_s(\sigma_0)}.
      \tag{ECB6}
   \]
   Hence \(\underline h_s(\sigma_0)\) is a certified lower bound on the hit
   probability of the padded fixed-size list.  Applying
   \cref{cor:hit-probability-exact-signature-proposal} to these lower bounds
   gives feasibility from \((ECB3)\).  Finally, \((ECB4)\) is Markov's
   inequality, since \(|B_s|>H_s\) implies \(|B_s|\ge H_s+1\) and
   \(\E|B_s|=\mu_s\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Normalized exact-signature coverage obstruction]
   \label{cor:normalized-exact-signature-coverage-obstruction}
   Work in the setting of \cref{lem:exact-signature-coverage-list-oracle} with
   a fixed finite list-template family \(\mathcal C\).  Failure of the
   list-separation condition \((ECL3)\) is equivalent to the existence of
   nonnegative prices \(\beta,\tau,\theta\) such that
   \[
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}\beta_{\sigma_0}=1,
      \qquad
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma}\tau_{\sigma_0}L_{\sigma_0}
      +\theta S<1,
      \tag{ESNO1}
   \]
   and every template \(C\in\mathcal C\) satisfies
   \[
      \max_{\substack{L\subseteq W_C\\ |L|=K_C}}
      \sum_{\substack{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+\\
                      L\cap N_{\sigma_0}\ne\emptyset}}
      \bigl(\beta_{\sigma_0}-T_C\tau_{\sigma_0}\bigr)_+
      \le
      \theta S_C .
      \tag{ESNO2}
   \]
   Equivalently, every finite randomized proposal over template/list pairs has
   nonpositive expected exact-signature reduced gain against the normalized
   witness \((\beta,\tau,\theta)\).

   In the variable-size setting of
   \cref{cor:variable-size-exact-signature-proposal}, the same obstruction is
   obtained by treating every available pair \((s,k)\) as a separate template
   with container \(W_s\), cardinality \(k\), and prices \(T_{s,k},S_{s,k}\).
   Consequently every Bernoulli or soft-bucket proposal whose true
   size-stratified hit probabilities are used in \((EVS3)\) has nonpositive
   left-hand side under this witness.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Failure of \((ECL3)\) means that some nonnegative price system satisfies the
   surplus inequality \((EN\text{-}D1)\), but
   \(\mathsf{EC}_{\beta,\tau,\theta}(C)\le0\) for every \(C\in\mathcal C\).
   The surplus inequality forces
   \(M=\sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}\beta_{\sigma_0}>0\).  Divide
   \(\beta,\tau,\theta\) by \(M\).  The strict surplus becomes \((ESNO1)\), and
   the positive part in \((ESNO2)\) is homogeneous, so
   \(\mathsf{EC}\le0\) becomes exactly \((ESNO2)\).

   Conversely, multiplying any normalized witness by an arbitrary positive
   scalar gives a surplus price system satisfying \((EN\text{-}D1)\) and
   \(\mathsf{EC}_{\beta,\tau,\theta}(C)\le0\) for every \(C\), so \((ECL3)\)
   fails.  The randomized-proposal formulation is just averaging: if every
   deterministic template/list pair has nonpositive gain, then every finite
   law over such pairs has nonpositive expected gain, and a positive expected
   gain would expose a deterministic positive-gain pair.

   The variable-size claim is a relabeling of templates by the pair \((s,k)\).
   Applying the first part after this relabeling gives nonpositive expectation
   for the true size-stratified hit probabilities in \((EVS3)\); certified
   lower hit bounds and upper size-probability bounds only decrease that left
   side further.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Normalized capped-mass obstruction]
   \label{cor:normalized-capped-mass-obstruction}
   Fix a build-time class \(\mathcal B\) of capped responsibility buckets.  An
   element \(B\in\mathcal B\) consists of a certified template
   \(C_B=(W_B,H_B,T_B,S_B)\in\mathcal C\), responsibilities
   \(0\le\pi_{B,p}\le1\), and a certified overflow bound
   \(\varepsilon_B\ge\Pr[|L^{\rm raw}_B|>H_B]\), where
   \(L^{\rm raw}_B\) is the independent Bernoulli subset generated from
   \(\pi_B\).  Put
   \[
      m_B(\sigma_0)=
      \sum_{p\in W_B\cap N_{\sigma_0}}\pi_{B,p},
      \qquad
      \underline h_B(\sigma_0)=
      \bigl(1-e^{-m_B(\sigma_0)}-\varepsilon_B\bigr)_+ ,
      \tag{ECBO1}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \mathsf{MB}_{\beta,\tau,\theta}(B)
      =
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}
      \underline h_B(\sigma_0)
      \bigl(\beta_{\sigma_0}-T_B\tau_{\sigma_0}\bigr)_+
      -
      \theta S_B .
      \tag{ECBO2}
   \]
   If every nonnegative price system satisfying \((EN\text{-}D1)\) has some
   \(B\in\mathcal B\) with
   \[
      \mathsf{MB}_{\beta,\tau,\theta}(B)>0,
      \tag{ECBO3}
   \]
   then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   Failure of this capped-mass screen is equivalent to the existence of
   nonnegative prices \(\beta,\tau,\theta\) satisfying the normalized surplus
   condition \((ESNO1)\) and
   \[
      \mathsf{MB}_{\beta,\tau,\theta}(B)\le0
      \qquad(B\in\mathcal B).
      \tag{ECBO4}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The first claim is \cref{cor:capped-bernoulli-exact-signature-mass} applied
   with the point-mass seed law on the positive bucket \(B\).  For the
   obstruction statement, failure of \((ECBO3)\) means that some surplus price
   system satisfying \((EN\text{-}D1)\) has
   \(\mathsf{MB}_{\beta,\tau,\theta}(B)\le0\) for every \(B\in\mathcal B\).
   Let \(M=\sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}\beta_{\sigma_0}\).  The surplus
   inequality forces \(M>0\).  Dividing \(\beta,\tau,\theta\) by \(M\) gives
   \((ESNO1)\), and \((ECBO4)\) is preserved because both the hinge term and
   the storage term are homogeneous in the prices.  Conversely, multiplying a
   normalized witness by any positive scalar gives a surplus price system
   satisfying \((EN\text{-}D1)\) and still obeying \((ECBO4)\), so the
   capped-mass screen fails.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Saturated-mass exact-signature screen]
   \label{cor:saturated-mass-exact-signature-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:normalized-capped-mass-obstruction}.  For a price system
   \((\beta,\tau,\theta)\), a capped responsibility bucket \(B\in\mathcal B\),
   and a threshold \(a>0\), define
   \[
      w_B(\sigma_0)=
      \bigl(\beta_{\sigma_0}-T_B\tau_{\sigma_0}\bigr)_+
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+),
      \tag{ESM0}
   \]
   and the saturated-mass reduced gain
   \[
      \mathsf{SM}_{\beta,\tau,\theta}(B,a)
      =
      (1-e^{-a})
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}
      w_B(\sigma_0)\min\left\{\frac{m_B(\sigma_0)}{a},1\right\}
      -
      \varepsilon_B\sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}w_B(\sigma_0)
      -
      \theta S_B .
      \tag{ESM1}
   \]
   If every nonnegative price system satisfying \((EN\text{-}D1)\) admits
   \(B\in\mathcal B\) and \(a>0\) with
   \[
      \mathsf{SM}_{\beta,\tau,\theta}(B,a)>0,
      \tag{ESM2}
   \]
   then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   Equivalently, if the saturated-mass screen fails, then there is a normalized
   witness satisfying \((ESNO1)\) such that, for every \(B\in\mathcal B\) and
   every \(a>0\),
   \[
      (1-e^{-a})
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}
      w_B(\sigma_0)\min\left\{\frac{m_B(\sigma_0)}{a},1\right\}
      \le
      \theta S_B
      +
      \varepsilon_B\sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}w_B(\sigma_0).
      \tag{ESM3}
   \]
   In particular, the single threshold \(a=1\) gives the simpler sufficient
   test
   \[
      (1-e^{-1})
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}
      w_B(\sigma_0)\min\{m_B(\sigma_0),1\}
      >
      \theta S_B
      +
      \varepsilon_B\sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}w_B(\sigma_0).
      \tag{ESM4}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For every \(u\ge0\) and \(a>0\),
   \[
      1-e^{-u}
      \ge
      (1-e^{-a})\min\{u/a,1\}.
      \tag{ESM5}
   \]
   Indeed, for \(0\le u\le a\) this is the chord lower bound for the concave
   function \(1-e^{-u}\) on \([0,a]\), and for \(u\ge a\) it follows from
   monotonicity.  Therefore
   \[
      \bigl(1-e^{-m_B(\sigma_0)}-\varepsilon_B\bigr)_+
      \ge
      (1-e^{-a})\min\left\{\frac{m_B(\sigma_0)}{a},1\right\}
      -
      \varepsilon_B .
      \tag{ESM6}
   \]
   Multiplying by \(w_B(\sigma_0)\), summing over signatures, and subtracting
   \(\theta S_B\) gives
   \[
      \mathsf{MB}_{\beta,\tau,\theta}(B)
      \ge
      \mathsf{SM}_{\beta,\tau,\theta}(B,a).
   \]
   Hence a positive saturated-mass gain is a positive capped-mass gain, and
   \cref{cor:normalized-capped-mass-obstruction} gives feasibility.

   The normalized residual statement follows by the same homogeneity argument
   as in \cref{cor:normalized-capped-mass-obstruction}: failure of the
   saturated-mass screen exposes a surplus dual with all saturated gains
   nonpositive; normalizing by
   \(\sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}\beta_{\sigma_0}\) gives \((ESNO1)\) and
   \((ESM3)\).  Conversely, any normalized witness satisfying \((ESM3)\) can be
   scaled to a surplus price system with no positive saturated-mass certificate.
   The displayed \(a=1\) test is the special case of \((ESM2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Layer-cake saturated-mass screen]
   \label{cor:layer-cake-saturated-mass-screen}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:saturated-mass-exact-signature-screen}.  For a bucket
   \(B\in\mathcal B\), threshold \(a>0\), and price system
   \((\beta,\tau,\theta)\), put
   \[
      W_B(t)=
      \sum_{\substack{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+\\ m_B(\sigma_0)\ge t}}
      w_B(\sigma_0),
      \qquad
      W_B^{\rm tot}=\sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}w_B(\sigma_0),
      \tag{ELC1}
   \]
   where \(w_B\) is defined in \((ESM0)\).  Then
   \[
      \mathsf{SM}_{\beta,\tau,\theta}(B,a)
      =
      \frac{1-e^{-a}}{a}\int_0^a W_B(t)\,dt
      -
      \varepsilon_B W_B^{\rm tot}
      -
      \theta S_B .
      \tag{ELC2}
   \]
   Consequently, \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible if every surplus price
   system satisfying \((EN\text{-}D1)\) admits \(B\in\mathcal B\), \(a>0\), and
   a finite nonnegative level weighting \((\lambda_i,t_i)_i\) supported on
   \(0<t_i\le a\), such that
   \[
      \frac{1-e^{-a}}{a}
      \sum_i\lambda_i t_i W_B(t_i)
      >
      \left(\sum_i\lambda_i\right)
      \left(\theta S_B+\varepsilon_BW_B^{\rm tot}\right).
      \tag{ELC3}
   \]
   In particular, it is enough to find one level \(0<t\le a\) with
   \[
      (1-e^{-a})\frac{t}{a}W_B(t)
      >
      \theta S_B+\varepsilon_BW_B^{\rm tot}.
      \tag{ELC4}
   \]

   If the saturated-mass screen fails, then there is a normalized witness
   satisfying \((ESNO1)\) such that, for every \(B\in\mathcal B\),
   every \(a>0\), and every \(0<t\le a\),
   \[
      (1-e^{-a})\frac{t}{a}W_B(t)
      \le
      \theta S_B+\varepsilon_BW_B^{\rm tot}.
      \tag{ELC5}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For each signature,
   \[
      \min\left\{\frac{m_B(\sigma_0)}{a},1\right\}
      =
      \frac1a\int_0^a
      \mathbf 1\{m_B(\sigma_0)\ge t\}\,dt,
   \]
   changing only a null set if equality occurs.  Summing against \(w_B\) gives
   \((ELC2)\).

   If a level weighting satisfies \((ELC3)\), then some level in its finite
   support satisfies \((ELC4)\).  Since \(W_B\) is nonincreasing,
   \[
      \int_0^a W_B(s)\,ds
      \ge
      t_iW_B(t_i),
   \]
   so \((ELC4)\) implies that the right side of \((ELC2)\) is positive.
   Therefore \(\mathsf{SM}_{\beta,\tau,\theta}(B,a)>0\), and
   \cref{cor:saturated-mass-exact-signature-screen} gives feasibility.

   Finally, if the saturated-mass screen fails, then by
   \cref{cor:saturated-mass-exact-signature-screen} there is a normalized
   witness satisfying the integral envelope \((ESM3)\).  Combining \((ESM3)\)
   with the monotonicity lower bound
   \[
      \int_0^aW_B(s)\,ds\ge tW_B(t)
      \qquad(0<t\le a)
   \]
   gives \((ELC5)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Unit-mass weak-type residual]
   \label{cor:unit-mass-weak-type-residual}
   In the normalized residual of
   \cref{cor:layer-cake-saturated-mass-screen}, every bucket satisfies
   \[
      W_B^{\rm tot}\le1 .
      \tag{EWT1}
   \]
   Consequently, if the saturated-mass screen fails, then there is a normalized
   witness satisfying \((ESNO1)\) such that, for every \(B\in\mathcal B\) and
   every \(t>0\),
   \[
      (1-e^{-t})W_B(t)
      \le
      \theta S_B+\varepsilon_B,
      \tag{EWT2}
   \]
   and hence
   \[
      W_B(t)
      \le
      \frac{\theta S_B+\varepsilon_B}{1-e^{-t}}
      \le
      \frac{2(\theta S_B+\varepsilon_B)}{\min\{t,1\}} .
      \tag{EWT3}
   \]
   Therefore, to rule out the residual it is enough to prove that every
   normalized witness satisfying \((ESNO1)\) admits a bucket \(B\) and a level
   \(t>0\) with
   \[
      (1-e^{-t})W_B(t)>\theta S_B+\varepsilon_B .
      \tag{EWT4}
   \]
   Under this condition \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   In a normalized witness,
   \[
      w_B(\sigma_0)
      =
      \bigl(\beta_{\sigma_0}-T_B\tau_{\sigma_0}\bigr)_+
      \le
      \beta_{\sigma_0},
   \]
   because \(T_B,\tau_{\sigma_0}\ge0\).  Summing over
   \(\Sigma^+\) and using \((ESNO1)\) gives \((EWT1)\).

   Apply \((ELC5)\) with \(a=t\).  Since \(W_B^{\rm tot}\le1\), the overflow
   term is at most \(\varepsilon_B\), giving \((EWT2)\).  The last display uses
   \(1-e^{-t}\ge t/2\) for \(0<t\le1\) and
   \(1-e^{-t}\ge1-e^{-1}\ge1/2\) for \(t\ge1\).

   If \((EWT4)\) holds for every normalized witness, then no normalized
   residual satisfying \((EWT2)\) exists.  Hence the saturated-mass screen
   cannot fail; feasibility follows from
   \cref{cor:saturated-mass-exact-signature-screen}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite exact-signature superlevel separator]
   \label{cor:finite-exact-signature-superlevel-separator}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:unit-mass-weak-type-residual}, and assume the bucket family
   \(\mathcal B\) is finite.  For \(B\in\mathcal B\), define the finite level
   set
   \[
      \mathcal T_B=
      \{m_B(\sigma_0):\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+,\ m_B(\sigma_0)>0\}.
      \tag{EFS1}
   \]
   Suppose that every normalized price system satisfying \((ESNO1)\) admits a
   bucket \(B\in\mathcal B\) and a level \(t\in\mathcal T_B\) such that
   \[
      (1-e^{-t})
      \sum_{\substack{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+\\ m_B(\sigma_0)\ge t}}
      \bigl(\beta_{\sigma_0}-T_B\tau_{\sigma_0}\bigr)_+
      >
      \theta S_B+\varepsilon_B .
      \tag{EFS2}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   Conversely, if the saturated-mass screen fails, then there is a normalized
   witness satisfying \((ESNO1)\) for which every \(B\in\mathcal B\) and every
   \(t\in\mathcal T_B\) satisfy the reverse weak-type inequality
   \[
      (1-e^{-t})
      \sum_{\substack{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+\\ m_B(\sigma_0)\ge t}}
      \bigl(\beta_{\sigma_0}-T_B\tau_{\sigma_0}\bigr)_+
      \le
      \theta S_B+\varepsilon_B .
      \tag{EFS3}
   \]
   Thus the remaining soft-bucket theorem is exactly a finite weighted
   superlevel-search problem over the pairs \((B,t)\) with
   \(t\in\mathcal T_B\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The sufficient direction is exactly \((EWT4)\), restricted to the finite
   level sets \(\mathcal T_B\), followed by
   \cref{cor:unit-mass-weak-type-residual}.

   For the converse, \cref{cor:unit-mass-weak-type-residual} gives a normalized
   witness satisfying \((EWT2)\) for every real level \(t>0\).  In particular it
   holds for every \(t\in\mathcal T_B\), which is \((EFS3)\).

   Finally, no levels outside \(\mathcal T_B\) are needed for the separator.  If
   a real \(t>0\) satisfies \(W_B(t)>0\), let
   \[
      t^+=\min\{u\in\mathcal T_B:u\ge t\}.
   \]
   Then the set of signatures with \(m_B(\sigma_0)\ge t^+\) is the same as the
   set with \(m_B(\sigma_0)\ge t\), while \(1-e^{-t^+}\ge1-e^{-t}\).  Hence any
   real-level violation is also witnessed at \(t^+\in\mathcal T_B\).  If
   \(W_B(t)=0\), there is no violation.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Randomized superlevel proposal]
   \label{cor:randomized-superlevel-proposal}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:finite-exact-signature-superlevel-separator}.  It is enough to
   prove the separator by an averaged build-time proposal.  Namely, suppose
   that for every normalized price system satisfying \((ESNO1)\) there is a
   finite seed law \(s\sim\nu\) such that seed \(s\) chooses
   \(B_s\in\mathcal B\) and \(t_s\in\mathcal T_{B_s}\), and
   \[
      \E_s\left[
         (1-e^{-t_s})
         \sum_{\substack{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+\\
                         m_{B_s}(\sigma_0)\ge t_s}}
         \bigl(\beta_{\sigma_0}-T_{B_s}\tau_{\sigma_0}\bigr)_+
         -
         \theta S_{B_s}
         -
         \varepsilon_{B_s}
      \right]>0 .
      \tag{ERP1}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   More generally, it is enough to provide certified quantities
   \[
      \underline W_s
      \le
      \sum_{\substack{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+\\
                      m_{B_s}(\sigma_0)\ge t_s}}
      \bigl(\beta_{\sigma_0}-T_{B_s}\tau_{\sigma_0}\bigr)_+,
      \qquad
      \overline S_s\ge S_{B_s},
      \qquad
      \overline\varepsilon_s\ge\varepsilon_{B_s},
      \tag{ERP2}
   \]
   satisfying
   \[
      \E_s\left[
         (1-e^{-t_s})\underline W_s
         -
         \theta\overline S_s
         -
         \overline\varepsilon_s
      \right]>0 .
      \tag{ERP3}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \((ERP1)\) holds, then some seed \(s\) has positive realized surplus.
   That seed gives a deterministic pair \((B_s,t_s)\) satisfying \((EFS2)\), so
   \cref{cor:finite-exact-signature-superlevel-separator} applies.  The
   certified version only decreases the displayed surplus, because
   \(\theta\ge0\).  Thus \((ERP3)\) implies \((ERP1)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Multiplicative level-net separator]
   \label{cor:multiplicative-level-net-separator}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:finite-exact-signature-superlevel-separator}.  For each
   \(B\in\mathcal B\), let \(\mathcal G_B\subset(0,\infty)\) be a finite level
   net, and let \(b\ge1\).  Assume \(\mathcal G_B\) is \(b\)-dense from below
   for \(\mathcal T_B\): for every \(t\in\mathcal T_B\) there is
   \(g\in\mathcal G_B\) with
   \[
      t/b\le g\le t .
      \tag{EMN1}
   \]
   If every normalized price system satisfying \((ESNO1)\) admits
   \(B\in\mathcal B\) and \(t\in\mathcal T_B\) such that
   \[
      (1-e^{-t})W_B(t)
      >
      b\bigl(\theta S_B+\varepsilon_B\bigr),
      \tag{EMN2}
   \]
   then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   Equivalently, it is enough to search only the net levels: under \((EMN2)\)
   some \(g\in\mathcal G_B\) satisfies
   \[
      (1-e^{-g})W_B(g)
      >
      \theta S_B+\varepsilon_B .
      \tag{EMN3}
   \]
   In particular, the dyadic lower grid
   \[
      \mathcal G_B^{\rm dyad}
      =
      \{2^{\lfloor\log_2 t\rfloor}:t\in\mathcal T_B\}
      \tag{EMN4}
   \]
   is \(2\)-dense from below, so it loses only a factor \(2\) in the surplus
   test.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let \(B,t\) satisfy \((EMN2)\), and choose \(g\in\mathcal G_B\) satisfying
   \((EMN1)\).  Since \(g\le t\), monotonicity gives \(W_B(g)\ge W_B(t)\).  The
   function \(x\mapsto1-e^{-x}\) is concave and vanishes at \(0\), hence
   \[
      1-e^{-g}
      \ge
      1-e^{-t/b}
      \ge
      \frac1b(1-e^{-t}).
   \]
   Combining the last two inequalities with \((EMN2)\) gives \((EMN3)\).  Then
   \cref{cor:unit-mass-weak-type-residual} gives feasibility.  The dyadic
   statement is the special case in which
   \(2^{\lfloor\log_2 t\rfloor}\le t<2\cdot2^{\lfloor\log_2t\rfloor}\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Output-sensitive reported superlevel separator]
   \label{cor:reported-superlevel-separator}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:multiplicative-level-net-separator}.  For a normalized price
   system satisfying \((ESNO1)\), put
   \[
      \Delta(B,g)
      =
      (1-e^{-g})W_B(g)-\theta S_B-\varepsilon_B,
      \qquad
      B\in\mathcal B,\ g\in\mathcal G_B .
      \tag{ERS1}
   \]
   Suppose a finite reporter, given the price system, outputs a set
   \(\mathcal R\subseteq\{(B,g):B\in\mathcal B,\ g\in\mathcal G_B\}\).
   For every reported pair it also outputs certificates
   \[
      \underline W_{B,g}\le W_B(g),\qquad
      \overline S_{B,g}\ge S_B,\qquad
      \overline\varepsilon_{B,g}\ge\varepsilon_B ,
      \tag{ERS2}
   \]
   and define the certified surplus
   \[
      \widehat\Delta(B,g)
      =
      (1-e^{-g})\underline W_{B,g}
      -\theta\overline S_{B,g}
      -\overline\varepsilon_{B,g}.
      \tag{ERS3}
   \]
   We use the convention that the maximum over an empty reported panel is
   \(-\infty\).  If every normalized price system satisfying \((ESNO1)\) has a
   reported pair
   with
   \[
      \max_{(B,g)\in\mathcal R}\widehat\Delta(B,g)>0 ,
      \tag{ERS4}
   \]
   then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   The same conclusion holds for a randomized reporter if
   \[
      \E_s\max_{(B,g)\in\mathcal R_s}\widehat\Delta_s(B,g)>0 .
      \tag{ERS5}
   \]
   More generally, let
   \[
      \Delta_{\mathcal G}^*
      =
      \max_{\substack{B\in\mathcal B\\ g\in\mathcal G_B}}\Delta(B,g).
   \]
   If, for some \(\xi>\delta\ge0\), every normalized price system has
   \(\Delta_{\mathcal G}^*\ge\xi\), and the reporter always returns certified
   values satisfying
   \[
      \max_{(B,g)\in\mathcal R}\widehat\Delta(B,g)
      \ge
      \Delta_{\mathcal G}^*-\delta ,
      \tag{ERS6}
   \]
   then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   In particular, if the nets are \(b\)-dense from below and every normalized
   price system has some \(B\in\mathcal B\) and exact level
   \(t\in\mathcal T_B\) with
   \[
      (1-e^{-t})W_B(t)
      >
      b\bigl(\theta S_B+\varepsilon_B\bigr)+\xi ,
      \tag{ERS7}
   \]
   then the net optimum satisfies
   \(\Delta_{\mathcal G}^*\ge\xi/b\).  Thus any reporter with additive
   certified loss \(<\xi/b\) is sufficient.

   If the reporter outputs at most \(M\) pairs and evaluates the certificates in
   work \(C_{\rm rep}\), the separation search costs \(C_{\rm rep}+O(M)\).  This
   is only preprocessing work: the retained filter-cover LP keeps the single
   positive-surplus column, not the reporter transcript.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The certificates imply
   \(\widehat\Delta(B,g)\le\Delta(B,g)\) for every reported pair, because
   \(\theta\ge0\).  Hence \((ERS4)\) exposes a deterministic pair satisfying
   \((EMN3)\), and \cref{cor:multiplicative-level-net-separator} gives
   feasibility.  If the reporter is randomized and \((ERS5)\) holds, some seed
   has positive realized maximum certified surplus, reducing to the deterministic
   case.

   The approximate version is immediate from \((ERS6)\): if
   \(\Delta_{\mathcal G}^*\ge\xi>\delta\), then the reported certified maximum
   is positive.  Finally, under \((ERS7)\), choose
   \(g\in\mathcal G_B\) with \(t/b\le g\le t\).  As in the proof of
   \cref{cor:multiplicative-level-net-separator},
   \[
      (1-e^{-g})W_B(g)
      \ge
      \frac1b(1-e^{-t})W_B(t)
      >
      \theta S_B+\varepsilon_B+\xi/b .
   \]
   Thus \(\Delta_{\mathcal G}^*\ge\xi/b\).  The work statement is just the
   finite scan of the reported panel after the certificates have been computed.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Success-normalized superlevel law]
   \label{cor:success-normalized-superlevel-law}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:reported-superlevel-separator}.  For a
   reported pair \((B,g)\), write
   \[
      s_g=1-e^{-g},
      \qquad
      \kappa(B,g)=
      \frac{\theta\overline S_{B,g}+\overline\varepsilon_{B,g}}{s_g}.
      \tag{ESN1}
   \]
   Thus \(\kappa(B,g)\) is the certified query/storage price per unit
   superlevel hit probability.  If every normalized price system satisfying
   \((ESNO1)\) admits a finite law \(\nu\) over reported pairs for which
   \[
      \E_{(B,g)\sim\nu}
      s_g\bigl(\underline W_{B,g}-\kappa(B,g)\bigr)>0,
      \tag{ESN2}
   \]
   then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.  Equivalently, putting
   \[
      \mathsf H(\nu)=
      \E_\nu s_g\underline W_{B,g},
      \qquad
      \mathsf C(\nu)=
      \E_\nu\bigl(\theta\overline S_{B,g}
                  +\overline\varepsilon_{B,g}\bigr),
      \tag{ESN3}
   \]
   it is enough to prove
   \[
      \mathsf H(\nu)>\mathsf C(\nu).
      \tag{ESN4}
   \]
   In homogeneous form, any law with \(\mathsf H(\nu)>0\) and
   \[
      \frac{\mathsf C(\nu)}{\mathsf H(\nu)}<1
      \tag{ESN5}
   \]
   supplies a separator.

   Consequently, the remaining exact-signature soft-bucket theorem may be
   stated as a success-normalized moment problem: produce bucket-level
   proposals whose recursive query/storage price per certified exact-near-set
   hit mass is less than the priced mass they capture.  Large reported buckets
   are harmless when their certified hit probability \(s_g\) is proportionally
   large.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Since \(g>0\), \(s_g>0\), and
   \[
      s_g\bigl(\underline W_{B,g}-\kappa(B,g)\bigr)
      =
      (1-e^{-g})\underline W_{B,g}
      -\theta\overline S_{B,g}
      -\overline\varepsilon_{B,g}
      =
      \widehat\Delta(B,g).
   \]
   Thus \((ESN2)\) is exactly positive expected certified surplus for the law
   \(\nu\).  Some pair in the finite support has positive certified surplus,
   and \cref{cor:reported-superlevel-separator} applies.  The equivalence with
   \((ESN4)\) and the ratio form \((ESN5)\) is immediate from the definitions
   in \((ESN3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exact-signature moment separator]
   \label{cor:exact-signature-moment-separator}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:success-normalized-superlevel-law}.  For a
   reported pair \((B,g)\), define the active signature layer
   \[
      \mathcal A(B,g)=
      \{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+:m_B(\sigma_0)\ge g\},
      \tag{EMOM1}
   \]
   and its captured price and query-price load
   \[
      X(B,g)=\sum_{\sigma_0\in\mathcal A(B,g)}\beta_{\sigma_0},
      \qquad
      Y(B,g)=\sum_{\sigma_0\in\mathcal A(B,g)}\tau_{\sigma_0}.
      \tag{EMOM2}
   \]
   Suppose that the reporter also supplies certified query and storage price
   envelopes
   \[
      \widehat T(B,g)\ge T_B,\qquad
      \widehat S(B,g)\ge S_B,\qquad
      \widehat\varepsilon(B,g)\ge\varepsilon_B .
      \tag{EMOM3}
   \]
   If every normalized price system satisfying \((ESNO1)\) admits a finite law
   \(\nu\) over reported pairs such that
   \[
      \E_\nu
      \left[
         (1-e^{-g})
         \bigl(X(B,g)-\widehat T(B,g)Y(B,g)\bigr)
         -
         \theta\widehat S(B,g)
         -
         \widehat\varepsilon(B,g)
      \right]>0 ,
      \tag{EMOM4}
   \]
   then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   In particular, suppose the reporter supplies a size or compressed-net
   parameter \(K(B,g)\ge0\), an exponent \(0\le\rho\le1\), and a price factor
   \(\psi(B,g)\ge0\) with
   \[
      T_B\le\psi(B,g)K(B,g)^\rho,\qquad
      S_B\le\psi(B,g)K(B,g)^{1+\rho}.
      \tag{EMOM5}
   \]
   Then it is enough to prove the Renyi moment inequality
   \[
      \E_\nu(1-e^{-g})X(B,g)
      >
      \E_\nu\!\left[
         (1-e^{-g})\psi(B,g)K(B,g)^\rho Y(B,g)
         +
         \theta\psi(B,g)K(B,g)^{1+\rho}
         +
         \widehat\varepsilon(B,g)
      \right].
      \tag{EMOM6}
   \]
   This is the exact-signature version of the average list-size target:
   captured signature mass is charged against the success-weighted recursive
   query moment and the storage moment of the reported bucket or compressed
   net.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For every reported pair,
   \[
      W_B(g)
      =
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\mathcal A(B,g)}
      \bigl(\beta_{\sigma_0}-T_B\tau_{\sigma_0}\bigr)_+
      \ge
      X(B,g)-T_BY(B,g)
      \ge
      X(B,g)-\widehat T(B,g)Y(B,g).
      \tag{EMOM7}
   \]
   Therefore
   \[
      \underline W_{B,g}
      =
      X(B,g)-\widehat T(B,g)Y(B,g),
      \qquad
      \overline S_{B,g}=\widehat S(B,g),
      \qquad
      \overline\varepsilon_{B,g}=\widehat\varepsilon(B,g)
   \]
   are valid certificates in \((ERS2)\).  The positivity condition
   \((EMOM4)\) is exactly positive expected certified surplus \((ERS5)\), so
   \cref{cor:reported-superlevel-separator} gives feasibility.

   The Renyi form is the special case
   \[
      \widehat T(B,g)=\psi(B,g)K(B,g)^\rho,\qquad
      \widehat S(B,g)=\psi(B,g)K(B,g)^{1+\rho},
   \]
   using \((EMOM5)\).  Substituting these envelopes into \((EMOM4)\) gives
   \((EMOM6)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Exact-signature Renyi residual envelope]
   \label{cor:exact-signature-renyi-residual}
   Fix a finite reported universe
   \(\mathcal U\subseteq\{(B,g):B\in\mathcal B,\ g\in\mathcal G_B\}\) with
   certified envelopes as in \cref{cor:exact-signature-moment-separator}.
   Suppose the moment separator fails on \(\mathcal U\): there is a normalized
   price system satisfying \((ESNO1)\) for which no finite law on
   \(\mathcal U\) satisfies \((EMOM4)\).  Then every reported pair
   \((B,g)\in\mathcal U\) obeys
   \[
      (1-e^{-g})X(B,g)
      \le
      (1-e^{-g})\widehat T(B,g)Y(B,g)
      +
      \theta\widehat S(B,g)
      +
      \widehat\varepsilon(B,g).
      \tag{EMRE1}
   \]
   Equivalently, every finite law \(\nu\) on \(\mathcal U\) obeys
   \[
      \E_\nu(1-e^{-g})X(B,g)
      \le
      \E_\nu\!\left[
         (1-e^{-g})\widehat T(B,g)Y(B,g)
         +
         \theta\widehat S(B,g)
         +
         \widehat\varepsilon(B,g)
      \right].
      \tag{EMRE2}
   \]

   In the compressed-size case \((EMOM5)\), the residual envelope becomes
   \[
      \E_\nu(1-e^{-g})X(B,g)
      \le
      \E_\nu\!\left[
         (1-e^{-g})\psi(B,g)K(B,g)^\rho Y(B,g)
         +
         \theta\psi(B,g)K(B,g)^{1+\rho}
         +
         \widehat\varepsilon(B,g)
      \right]
      \tag{EMRE3}
   \]
   for every finite law \(\nu\) on \(\mathcal U\).
   Thus the remaining geometric theorem may be stated as ruling out a
   normalized exact-signature price system for which all proposed bucket or
   compressed-net panels satisfy \((EMRE3)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If some deterministic pair \((B,g)\in\mathcal U\) violated \((EMRE1)\), the
   point mass on that pair would satisfy \((EMOM4)\), contradicting the failed
   separator.  Hence every deterministic pair obeys \((EMRE1)\), and averaging
   gives \((EMRE2)\).  Conversely, \((EMRE2)\) applied to point masses gives
   \((EMRE1)\), so the deterministic and averaged forms are equivalent.  The
   compressed-size statement is obtained by substituting the envelopes from
   \((EMOM5)\) into \((EMRE2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Observable exact-signature Renyi profile]
   \label{def:observable-exact-signature-renyi-profile}
   Work in the compressed-size setting \((EMOM5)\).  A finite law \(\nu\) over
   reported pairs \((B,g)\) induces the observable profile
   \[
      h_\nu(\sigma_0)
      =
      \E_\nu
      (1-e^{-g})\mathbf 1\{\sigma_0\in\mathcal A(B,g)\}
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+),
      \tag{ORP1}
   \]
   \[
      \ell_\nu(\sigma_0)
      =
      \E_\nu
      (1-e^{-g})\psi(B,g)K(B,g)^\rho
      \mathbf 1\{\sigma_0\in\mathcal A(B,g)\}
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma),
      \tag{ORP2}
   \]
   where the indicator is zero for
   \(\sigma_0\notin\Sigma^+\), and the scalar storage and error moments
   \[
      u_\nu=\E_\nu\psi(B,g)K(B,g)^{1+\rho},
      \qquad
      e_\nu=\E_\nu\widehat\varepsilon(B,g).
      \tag{ORP3}
   \]
   Thus \(h_\nu\) is the certified exact-near-set hit vector, \(\ell_\nu\) is
   the success-weighted recursive query-load vector, and \(u_\nu\) is the
   recursive storage moment of the panel.
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Observable Renyi profile separator]
   \label{cor:observable-renyi-profile-separator}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{def:observable-exact-signature-renyi-profile}.  If every normalized
   price system satisfying \((ESNO1)\) admits a finite reported-pair law \(\nu\)
   whose profile satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}\beta_{\sigma_0}h_\nu(\sigma_0)
      >
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma}\tau_{\sigma_0}\ell_\nu(\sigma_0)
      +\theta u_\nu+e_\nu ,
      \tag{ORPS1}
   \]
   then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   More generally, it is enough to certify profile envelopes
   \[
      \underline h_\nu(\sigma_0)\le h_\nu(\sigma_0),\qquad
      \overline\ell_\nu(\sigma_0)\ge\ell_\nu(\sigma_0),\qquad
      \overline u_\nu\ge u_\nu,\qquad
      \overline e_\nu\ge e_\nu
      \tag{ORPS2}
   \]
   such that
   \[
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}
      \beta_{\sigma_0}\underline h_\nu(\sigma_0)
      >
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma}
      \tau_{\sigma_0}\overline\ell_\nu(\sigma_0)
      +\theta\overline u_\nu+\overline e_\nu .
      \tag{ORPS3}
   \]

   Conversely, if a finite reported universe \(\mathcal U\) cannot separate a
   normalized price system, then every profile generated by a finite law on
   \(\mathcal U\) obeys the reverse inequality
   \[
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}\beta_{\sigma_0}h_\nu(\sigma_0)
      \le
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma}\tau_{\sigma_0}\ell_\nu(\sigma_0)
      +\theta u_\nu+e_\nu .
      \tag{ORPS4}
   \]
   Hence the remaining geometric/list-decoding theorem can be stated without
   the LP variables: every normalized dual obstruction must admit an observable
   panel whose certified hit vector has larger price than its Renyi query,
   storage, and error profile.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Expanding \((ORP1)\)--\((ORP3)\) gives
   \[
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}\beta_{\sigma_0}h_\nu(\sigma_0)
      =
      \E_\nu(1-e^{-g})X(B,g),
   \]
   and
   \[
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma}\tau_{\sigma_0}\ell_\nu(\sigma_0)
      +\theta u_\nu+e_\nu
      =
      \E_\nu\!\left[
         (1-e^{-g})\psi(B,g)K(B,g)^\rho Y(B,g)
         +\theta\psi(B,g)K(B,g)^{1+\rho}
         +\widehat\varepsilon(B,g)
      \right].
   \]
   Thus \((ORPS1)\) is exactly \((EMOM6)\), and
   \cref{cor:exact-signature-moment-separator} gives feasibility.  The
   certified-envelope version only decreases the left side and increases the
   right side, so \((ORPS3)\) implies \((ORPS1)\).  Finally, \((ORPS4)\) is
   \((EMRE3)\) rewritten with the profile notation.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Observable Renyi profile-cover LP]
   \label{cor:observable-renyi-profile-cover}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:observable-renyi-profile-separator}.  Let \(\mathcal P\) be a
   finite family of certified observable profiles
   \[
      \Pi=(H_\Pi,L_\Pi,U_\Pi,E_\Pi),
   \]
   meaning that \(H_\Pi(\sigma_0)\) is a certified lower hit vector,
   \(L_\Pi(\sigma_0)\) is a certified upper query-load vector, and
   \(U_\Pi,E_\Pi\) are certified upper storage and error moments as in
   \((ORPS2)\).  Consider the error-discounted profile-cover LP
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \text{\rm find} & \lambda_\Pi\ge0\\[0.4em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{\Pi\in\mathcal P}\lambda_\Pi
        \bigl(H_\Pi(\sigma_0)-E_\Pi\bigr)\ge1
        \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+),\\[0.9em]
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{\Pi\in\mathcal P}\lambda_\Pi L_\Pi(\sigma_0)
        \le L_{\sigma_0}
        \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma),\\[0.9em]
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{\Pi\in\mathcal P}\lambda_\Pi U_\Pi\le S .
   \end{array}
   \tag{\(\mathsf{ORPC}_\Sigma\)}
   \]
   If \((\mathsf{ORPC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible, then
   \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   Conversely, if \((\mathsf{ORPC}_\Sigma)\) is infeasible, then there is a
   normalized price system satisfying \((ESNO1)\) such that every certified
   profile \(\Pi\in\mathcal P\) obeys
   \[
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}\beta_{\sigma_0}H_\Pi(\sigma_0)
      \le
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma}\tau_{\sigma_0}L_\Pi(\sigma_0)
      +\theta U_\Pi+E_\Pi .
      \tag{ORPC1}
   \]
   Thus the observable residual is exactly failure of a fractional
   error-discounted cover by panel profiles.  Dense buckets, spherical buckets,
   additive-quantization panels, and list-decoder outputs are all columns of
   the same profile LP once their hit, query, storage, and error moments are
   certified.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Suppose first that \((\mathsf{ORPC}_\Sigma)\) has a feasible solution
   \(\lambda\), and fix any normalized price system satisfying \((ESNO1)\).
   Using \(\sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}\beta_{\sigma_0}=1\),
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      &\sum_{\Pi\in\mathcal P}\lambda_\Pi
      \left[
         \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}\beta_{\sigma_0}H_\Pi(\sigma_0)
         -
         \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma}\tau_{\sigma_0}L_\Pi(\sigma_0)
         -
         \theta U_\Pi-E_\Pi
      \right]  \\
      &\qquad =
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}\beta_{\sigma_0}
      \sum_{\Pi}\lambda_\Pi\bigl(H_\Pi(\sigma_0)-E_\Pi\bigr)
      -
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma}\tau_{\sigma_0}
      \sum_{\Pi}\lambda_\Pi L_\Pi(\sigma_0)
      -
      \theta\sum_{\Pi}\lambda_\Pi U_\Pi  \\
      &\qquad \ge
      1-\sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma}\tau_{\sigma_0}L_{\sigma_0}-\theta S
      >0 .
   \end{aligned}
   \]
   Therefore some profile in \(\mathcal P\) has positive certified margin
   \((ORPS3)\).  By
   \cref{cor:observable-renyi-profile-separator}, this gives
   \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\).

   For the converse, apply Farkas' lemma to
   \((\mathsf{ORPC}_\Sigma)\).  Infeasibility gives multipliers
   \(\beta_{\sigma_0}\ge0\), \(\tau_{\sigma_0}\ge0\), and \(\theta\ge0\) such
   that
   \[
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}\beta_{\sigma_0}
      >
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma}\tau_{\sigma_0}L_{\sigma_0}+\theta S,
   \]
   while every profile satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}
      \beta_{\sigma_0}\bigl(H_\Pi(\sigma_0)-E_\Pi\bigr)
      \le
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma}\tau_{\sigma_0}L_\Pi(\sigma_0)
      +\theta U_\Pi .
   \]
   The strict inequality forces
   \(M=\sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}\beta_{\sigma_0}>0\).  Dividing all prices by
   \(M\) gives \((ESNO1)\), and since the normalized \(\beta\)-mass is one, the
   last display becomes \((ORPC1)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Local-error observable profile-cover LP]
   \label{cor:local-error-observable-profile-cover}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:observable-renyi-profile-separator}.  Let \(\mathcal P\) be a
   finite family of certified local-error profiles
   \[
      \Pi=(H_\Pi,L_\Pi,U_\Pi,E_\Pi(\cdot)),
   \]
   where \(H_\Pi(\sigma_0)\) is a certified lower hit vector,
   \(L_\Pi(\sigma_0)\) is a certified upper query-load vector,
   \(U_\Pi\) is a certified upper storage moment, and
   \(E_\Pi(\sigma_0)\) is a certified upper error contribution for the
   individual exact signature \(\sigma_0\), truncated so that
   \(0\le E_\Pi(\sigma_0)\le H_\Pi(\sigma_0)\).  Assume the discounted hit vector
   \[
      \widetilde H_\Pi(\sigma_0)
      =
      H_\Pi(\sigma_0)-E_\Pi(\sigma_0)
      \tag{LEPC0}
   \]
   is a certified lower useful-hit vector.  Consider the local-error profile
   cover
   \[
   \begin{array}{ll}
   \text{\rm find} & \lambda_\Pi\ge0\\[0.4em]
   \text{\rm subject to}
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{\Pi\in\mathcal P}\lambda_\Pi
        \widetilde H_\Pi(\sigma_0)\ge1
        \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+),\\[0.9em]
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{\Pi\in\mathcal P}\lambda_\Pi L_\Pi(\sigma_0)
        \le L_{\sigma_0}
        \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma),\\[0.9em]
      & \displaystyle
        \sum_{\Pi\in\mathcal P}\lambda_\Pi U_\Pi\le S .
   \end{array}
   \tag{\(\mathsf{LORPC}_\Sigma\)}
   \]
   If \((\mathsf{LORPC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible, then
   \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   Conversely, if \((\mathsf{LORPC}_\Sigma)\) is infeasible, then there is a
   normalized price system satisfying \((ESNO1)\) such that every certified
   local-error profile obeys
   \[
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}\beta_{\sigma_0}H_\Pi(\sigma_0)
      \le
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma}\tau_{\sigma_0}L_\Pi(\sigma_0)
      +\theta U_\Pi
      +\sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}\beta_{\sigma_0}E_\Pi(\sigma_0).
      \tag{LEPC1}
   \]

   In particular, if finitely supported weights \(\omega_\Pi\) have aggregate
   quantities
   \[
      H(\sigma_0)=\sum_\Pi\omega_\Pi H_\Pi(\sigma_0),\quad
      E(\sigma_0)=\sum_\Pi\omega_\Pi E_\Pi(\sigma_0),\quad
      L(\sigma_0)=\sum_\Pi\omega_\Pi L_\Pi(\sigma_0),\quad
      U=\sum_\Pi\omega_\Pi U_\Pi ,
   \]
   and there is \(a>0\) such that
   \[
      H(\sigma_0)-E(\sigma_0)\ge a
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+),
      \tag{LEPC2}
   \]
   \[
      L(\sigma_0)\le aL_{\sigma_0}
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma),
      \qquad
      U\le aS,
      \tag{LEPC3}
   \]
   then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For the first claim, apply
   \cref{cor:observable-renyi-profile-cover} to the ordinary certified profiles
   \[
      \widetilde\Pi=(\widetilde H_\Pi,L_\Pi,U_\Pi,0).
   \]
   The LP \((\mathsf{ORPC}_\Sigma)\) for these profiles is exactly
   \((\mathsf{LORPC}_\Sigma)\), so feasibility implies
   \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\).

   The converse is Farkas' lemma applied to
   \((\mathsf{LORPC}_\Sigma)\), followed by the same normalization as in the
   proof of \cref{cor:observable-renyi-profile-cover}.  Infeasibility gives
   nonnegative multipliers \(\beta,\tau,\theta\) with
   \[
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}\beta_{\sigma_0}
      >
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma}\tau_{\sigma_0}L_{\sigma_0}+\theta S
   \]
   and, for every \(\Pi\),
   \[
      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}
      \beta_{\sigma_0}\bigl(H_\Pi(\sigma_0)-E_\Pi(\sigma_0)\bigr)
      \le
