      \sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma}\tau_{\sigma_0}L_\Pi(\sigma_0)+\theta U_\Pi .
   \]
   Dividing by \(M=\sum_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}\beta_{\sigma_0}>0\) gives
   \((ESNO1)\), and rearranging gives \((LEPC1)\).

   For the aggregate certificate, set \(\lambda_\Pi=\omega_\Pi/a\).  Conditions
   \((LEPC2)\)--\((LEPC3)\) are precisely the three constraints of
   \((\mathsf{LORPC}_\Sigma)\) for this \(\lambda\), so the first claim applies.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Single-panel success-normalized profile certificate]
   \label{cor:single-panel-success-normalized-profile}
   In the setting of \cref{cor:observable-renyi-profile-cover}, suppose
   there are nonnegative weights \(\omega_\Pi\), finitely supported on
   \(\mathcal P\), with aggregate quantities
   \[
      H(\sigma_0)=\sum_{\Pi}\omega_\Pi H_\Pi(\sigma_0),\quad
      L(\sigma_0)=\sum_{\Pi}\omega_\Pi L_\Pi(\sigma_0),\quad
      U=\sum_{\Pi}\omega_\Pi U_\Pi,\quad
      E=\sum_{\Pi}\omega_\Pi E_\Pi .
   \]
   If there is \(a>0\) such that
   \[
      H(\sigma_0)\ge a+E\qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+),
      \tag{OSN1}
   \]
   \[
      L(\sigma_0)\le aL_{\sigma_0}\qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma),
      \qquad
      U\le aS,
      \tag{OSN2}
   \]
   then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   In particular, a single randomized spherical, tensor, AQ, or list-decoding
   panel with uniform exact-signature hit probability at least \(a+E\), Renyi
   query-load at most \(aL_{\sigma_0}\) for every query signature, and storage
   moment at most \(aS\), already supplies the local fractional dense-filter
   cover.  This is the profile form of the success-normalized invariant:
   recursive query and storage costs are charged after division by the
   certified hit probability \(a\), not by raw bucket size.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Set \(\lambda_\Pi=\omega_\Pi/a\).  Conditions \((OSN1)\)--\((OSN2)\) are
   exactly the three constraints of \((\mathsf{ORPC}_\Sigma)\) for this
   \(\lambda\).  Apply \cref{cor:observable-renyi-profile-cover}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Decoded bucket-panel profile certificate]
   \label{cor:decoded-bucket-panel-profile}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:observable-renyi-profile-cover}.  Let a
   finite build-time seed law \(s\sim\nu\) produce a finite multiset of decoded
   bucket records \(\mathcal B_s\).  Each record \(b\in\mathcal B_s\) is
   certified as an observable profile
   \[
      \Pi_{s,b}=(H_{s,b},L_{s,b},U_{s,b},E_{s,b})\in\mathcal P .
   \]
   Define the panel aggregates
   \[
      H_{\rm pan}(\sigma_0)
      =
      \E_s\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_s}H_{s,b}(\sigma_0),
      \qquad
      L_{\rm pan}(\sigma_0)
      =
      \E_s\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_s}L_{s,b}(\sigma_0),
      \tag{DBP1}
   \]
   and
   \[
      U_{\rm pan}=\E_s\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_s}U_{s,b},
      \qquad
      E_{\rm pan}=\E_s\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_s}E_{s,b}.
      \tag{DBP2}
   \]
   If there is \(a>0\) such that
   \[
      H_{\rm pan}(\sigma_0)\ge a+E_{\rm pan}
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+),
      \tag{DBP3}
   \]
   and
   \[
      L_{\rm pan}(\sigma_0)\le aL_{\sigma_0}
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma),
      \qquad
      U_{\rm pan}\le aS,
      \tag{DBP4}
   \]
   then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   In the superlevel form of \cref{cor:exact-signature-moment-separator}, a
   record \(b=(B,g)\) with compressed size \(K_b\), price factor \(\psi_b\), and
   overflow certificate \(\varepsilon_b\) has the concrete profile
   \[
      H_b(\sigma_0)
      =
      (1-e^{-g})\mathbf 1\{m_B(\sigma_0)\ge g\},
      \tag{DBP5}
   \]
   \[
      L_b(\sigma_0)
      =
      (1-e^{-g})\psi_bK_b^\rho
      \mathbf 1\{m_B(\sigma_0)\ge g\},
      \qquad
      U_b=\psi_bK_b^{1+\rho},
      \qquad
      E_b=\varepsilon_b .
      \tag{DBP6}
   \]
   Therefore a decoded spherical, tensor, AQ, or list-decoding panel is
   sufficient whenever its averaged superlevel hit spectrum dominates
   \(a+E_{\rm pan}\), while its success-weighted Renyi query spectrum and
   storage spectrum are at most \(a\) times the local budgets.  The panel may
   contain many overlapping buckets; overlap is charged only through the
   aggregate \(L_{\rm pan}\) and \(U_{\rm pan}\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Group identical certified profiles and define
   \[
      \omega_\Pi=
      \E_s\bigl|\{b\in\mathcal B_s:\Pi_{s,b}=\Pi\}\bigr|.
   \]
   The aggregate quantities in
   \cref{cor:single-panel-success-normalized-profile} are exactly
   \(H_{\rm pan},L_{\rm pan},U_{\rm pan},E_{\rm pan}\).  Conditions
   \((DBP3)\)--\((DBP4)\) are therefore \((OSN1)\)--\((OSN2)\), and
   \cref{cor:single-panel-success-normalized-profile} gives feasibility.

   The superlevel formulas \((DBP5)\)--\((DBP6)\) are the profile components
   \((ORP1)\)--\((ORP3)\) for the point-mass law on \((B,g)\), with the Renyi
   envelopes from \((EMOM5)\).  Substituting these record profiles into
   \((DBP1)\)--\((DBP2)\) gives the stated spectrum criterion.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Local-error decoded bucket-panel profile]
   \label{cor:local-error-decoded-bucket-panel-profile}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:local-error-observable-profile-cover}.  Let a finite build-time
   seed law \(s\sim\nu\) produce a finite multiset of decoded bucket records
   \(\mathcal B_s\).  Each record \(b\in\mathcal B_s\) is certified as a
   local-error observable profile
   \[
      \Pi_{s,b}=(H_{s,b},L_{s,b},U_{s,b},E_{s,b}(\cdot)),
   \]
   with \(0\le E_{s,b}(\sigma_0)\le H_{s,b}(\sigma_0)\).  Define
   \[
      H_{\rm loc}(\sigma_0)
      =
      \E_s\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_s}H_{s,b}(\sigma_0),
      \qquad
      L_{\rm loc}(\sigma_0)
      =
      \E_s\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_s}L_{s,b}(\sigma_0),
      \tag{LDBP1}
   \]
   and
   \[
      E_{\rm loc}(\sigma_0)
      =
      \E_s\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_s}E_{s,b}(\sigma_0),
      \qquad
      U_{\rm loc}=\E_s\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_s}U_{s,b}.
      \tag{LDBP2}
   \]
   If there is \(a>0\) such that
   \[
      H_{\rm loc}(\sigma_0)-E_{\rm loc}(\sigma_0)\ge a
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+),
      \tag{LDBP3}
   \]
   and
   \[
      L_{\rm loc}(\sigma_0)\le aL_{\sigma_0}
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma),
      \qquad
      U_{\rm loc}\le aS,
      \tag{LDBP4}
   \]
   then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   Thus a decoded panel need not pay one global overflow or certification error
   against every exact signature.  It may certify the signatures on which each
   bucket record can fail, and the profile cover subtracts only that local
   error vector.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Group identical local-error profiles and define
   \[
      \omega_\Pi=
      \E_s\bigl|\{b\in\mathcal B_s:\Pi_{s,b}=\Pi\}\bigr|.
   \]
   The aggregate quantities in the final part of
   \cref{cor:local-error-observable-profile-cover} are exactly
   \(H_{\rm loc},E_{\rm loc},L_{\rm loc},U_{\rm loc}\).  Conditions
   \((LDBP3)\)--\((LDBP4)\) are therefore \((LEPC2)\)--\((LEPC3)\), and
   \cref{cor:local-error-observable-profile-cover} gives feasibility.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Recursive compressed-net panel criterion]
   \label{cor:recursive-compressed-net-panel}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:decoded-bucket-panel-profile}.  Let a seed
   \(z\sim\nu\) produce a finite multiset of recursive bucket records
   \(\mathcal B_z\).  A record \(b\in\mathcal B_z\) comes with an active
   query-signature set \(\mathcal Q_{z,b}\subseteq\Sigma\), a captured
   exact-signature set \(\mathcal H_{z,b}\subseteq\Sigma^+\), a certified hit
   weight \(0\le s_{z,b}\le1\), a compressed child size \(K_{z,b}\), a child
   exponent \(0\le\rho_{z,b}\le1\), a price factor \(\psi_{z,b}\), and an error
   certificate \(\varepsilon_{z,b}\).  Interpret this as the profile
   \[
      H_{z,b}(\sigma_0)
      =
      s_{z,b}\mathbf 1\{\sigma_0\in\mathcal H_{z,b}\},
      \tag{RCN1}
   \]
   \[
      L_{z,b}(\sigma_0)
      =
      s_{z,b}\psi_{z,b}K_{z,b}^{\rho_{z,b}}
      \mathbf 1\{\sigma_0\in\mathcal Q_{z,b}\},
      \qquad
      U_{z,b}=\psi_{z,b}K_{z,b}^{1+\rho_{z,b}},
      \qquad
      E_{z,b}=\varepsilon_{z,b}.
      \tag{RCN2}
   \]
   Define the aggregate spectra
   \[
      H_{\rm net}(\sigma_0)
      =
      \E_z\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_z}H_{z,b}(\sigma_0),
      \qquad
      L_{\rm net}(\sigma_0)
      =
      \E_z\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_z}L_{z,b}(\sigma_0),
      \tag{RCN3}
   \]
   and
   \[
      U_{\rm net}=\E_z\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_z}U_{z,b},
      \qquad
      E_{\rm net}=\E_z\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_z}E_{z,b}.
      \tag{RCN4}
   \]
   If there is \(a>0\) such that
   \[
      H_{\rm net}(\sigma_0)\ge a+E_{\rm net}
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+),
      \tag{RCN5}
   \]
   and
   \[
      L_{\rm net}(\sigma_0)\le aL_{\sigma_0}
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma),
      \qquad
      U_{\rm net}\le aS,
      \tag{RCN6}
   \]
   then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   Thus a bucket \(b\) may have a large compressed child, but its query charge
   is multiplied by its certified hit weight \(s_{z,b}\) only after all
   query-active signatures in \(\mathcal Q_{z,b}\) have been charged.  In the
   bucket-net recursion, \(K_{z,b}\) is the size of the canonical separated net
   retained for that bucket, \(\rho_{z,b}\) is the exponent of the
   smaller-radius child, and \(\psi_{z,b}\) is the already certified
   polylogarithmic child overhead.  The local query invariant is exactly the
   success-normalized moment bound \(s_{z,b}K_{z,b}^{\rho_{z,b}}\) on the
   active query layer, while the global space invariant is the Renyi list-size
   moment \(K_{z,b}^{1+\rho_{z,b}}\).  False active buckets are not free: they
   belong to \(\mathcal Q_{z,b}\) and contribute to \(L_{\rm net}\), even when
   they do not belong to the captured layer \(\mathcal H_{z,b}\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   The profiles in \((RCN1)\)--\((RCN2)\) are certified observable profiles of
   the kind allowed in \cref{cor:decoded-bucket-panel-profile}; the exponent and
   price factor are part of the record's child-price certificate.  With these
   profiles, the panel aggregates \((DBP1)\)--\((DBP2)\) are precisely
   \(H_{\rm net},L_{\rm net},U_{\rm net},E_{\rm net}\).  Conditions
   \((RCN5)\)--\((RCN6)\) are therefore \((DBP3)\)--\((DBP4)\), so
   \cref{cor:decoded-bucket-panel-profile} gives feasibility of
   \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Success-normalized bucket-net ratio form]
   \label{cor:bucket-net-ratio-form}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:recursive-compressed-net-panel}.  If
   \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible by the
   zero solution.  Otherwise put
   \[
      a_*=\inf_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}
      \bigl(H_{\rm net}(\sigma_0)-E_{\rm net}\bigr).
      \tag{BNR1}
   \]
   If \(a_*>0\) and
   \[
      \sup_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma}
      \frac{L_{\rm net}(\sigma_0)}{a_*L_{\sigma_0}}\le1,
      \qquad
      \frac{U_{\rm net}}{a_*S}\le1,
      \tag{BNR2}
   \]
   with the convention that a zero denominator requires the corresponding
   numerator to be zero, then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   Equivalently, a decoded recursive panel may be checked by the three
   observable quantities
   \[
      \text{hit mass }H_{\rm net}-E_{\rm net},\qquad
      \text{query Renyi moment }L_{\rm net},\qquad
      \text{storage Renyi moment }U_{\rm net}.
   \]
   The required theorem is a uniform ratio bound: query and storage moments per
   certified hit mass fit the local budgets.  In a spherical bucket-net
   construction this is precisely the pair of average list-decoding estimates
   \[
      \frac{
      \E\sum_{b:\sigma_0\in\mathcal Q_{z,b}}
      s_{z,b}\psi_{z,b}K_{z,b}^{\rho_{z,b}}
      }{
      \inf_{\sigma\in\Sigma^+}(H_{\rm net}(\sigma)-E_{\rm net})
      }
      \le L_{\sigma_0},
      \tag{BNR3}
   \]
   and
   \[
      \frac{
      \E\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_z}
      \psi_{z,b}K_{z,b}^{1+\rho_{z,b}}
      }{
      \inf_{\sigma\in\Sigma^+}(H_{\rm net}(\sigma)-E_{\rm net})
      }
      \le S .
      \tag{BNR4}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), the zero vector \(\lambda=0\) satisfies all
   coverage constraints of \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\), and the query/storage
   constraints are immediate.  Hence assume \(\Sigma^+\ne\emptyset\).
   Set \(a=a_*\).  By \((BNR1)\),
   \(H_{\rm net}(\sigma_0)\ge a+E_{\rm net}\) for every nonempty signature.
   The two inequalities in \((BNR2)\) are exactly \((RCN6)\).  Hence
   \cref{cor:recursive-compressed-net-panel} applies.  The displayed
   \((BNR3)\)--\((BNR4)\) are just \((BNR2)\) with \(L_{\rm net}\) and
   \(U_{\rm net}\) expanded from \((RCN3)\)--\((RCN4)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Local-error recursive bucket-net ratio form]
   \label{cor:local-error-bucket-net-ratio}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:recursive-compressed-net-panel}, but replace
   each scalar record error \(\varepsilon_{z,b}\) by a certified local error
   vector \(\varepsilon_{z,b}(\sigma_0)\) satisfying
   \[
      0\le \varepsilon_{z,b}(\sigma_0)
      \le
      s_{z,b}\mathbf 1\{\sigma_0\in\mathcal H_{z,b}\}
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+).
      \tag{LBNR0}
   \]
   Define \(H_{\rm net},L_{\rm net},U_{\rm net}\) as in
   \((RCN3)\)--\((RCN4)\), omitting the scalar \(E_{\rm net}\), and put
   \[
      E_{\rm net}(\sigma_0)
      =
      \E_z\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_z}\varepsilon_{z,b}(\sigma_0).
      \tag{LBNR1}
   \]
   If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.
   Otherwise let
   \[
      a_{\rm loc}
      =
      \inf_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+}
      \bigl(H_{\rm net}(\sigma_0)-E_{\rm net}(\sigma_0)\bigr).
      \tag{LBNR2}
   \]
   If \(a_{\rm loc}>0\) and
   \[
      \sup_{\sigma_0\in\Sigma}
      \frac{L_{\rm net}(\sigma_0)}{a_{\rm loc}L_{\sigma_0}}\le1,
      \qquad
      \frac{U_{\rm net}}{a_{\rm loc}S}\le1,
      \tag{LBNR3}
   \]
   with the same zero-denominator convention as in \((BNR2)\), then
   \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   This is the strictly sharper bucket-net invariant: the denominator is the
   minimum useful hit mass
   \(H_{\rm net}(\sigma_0)-E_{\rm net}(\sigma_0)\), where the error term is
   local to the signature.  The scalar-error ratio
   \(\inf_{\sigma}(H_{\rm net}(\sigma)-E_{\rm net})\) is recovered by taking
   \(\varepsilon_{z,b}(\sigma_0)=\varepsilon_{z,b}\) after truncation for every
   captured signature.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), use the zero cover.  Otherwise set
   \(a=a_{\rm loc}\).  Each record is a local-error profile with
   \[
      H_{z,b}(\sigma_0)=s_{z,b}\mathbf 1\{\sigma_0\in\mathcal H_{z,b}\},
   \]
   \[
      L_{z,b}(\sigma_0)=
      s_{z,b}\psi_{z,b}K_{z,b}^{\rho_{z,b}}
      \mathbf 1\{\sigma_0\in\mathcal Q_{z,b}\},
      \qquad
      U_{z,b}=\psi_{z,b}K_{z,b}^{1+\rho_{z,b}},
   \]
   and error vector \(E_{z,b}=\varepsilon_{z,b}\).  The aggregates of
   \cref{cor:local-error-decoded-bucket-panel-profile} are exactly
   \(H_{\rm net},E_{\rm net},L_{\rm net},U_{\rm net}\).  The definition
   \((LBNR2)\) gives \((LDBP3)\), and \((LBNR3)\) gives \((LDBP4)\).  Hence
   \cref{cor:local-error-decoded-bucket-panel-profile} applies.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[First-moment active-load query certificate]
   \label{cor:first-moment-active-load-query}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:bucket-net-ratio-form}, and assume
   \(K_{z,b}\) is an integer child size, with the convention that records with
   \(K_{z,b}=0\) have zero query and storage price.  If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\),
   the cover is feasible.  Otherwise let \(a_*\) be as in \((BNR1)\).  Suppose
   \(a_*>0\), and suppose the active first moments satisfy
   \[
      \E_z\sum_{b:\sigma_0\in\mathcal Q_{z,b}}
      s_{z,b}\psi_{z,b}K_{z,b}
      \le
      a_*L_{\sigma_0}
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma),
      \tag{FAL1}
   \]
   while the storage Renyi moment satisfies
   \[
      \E_z\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_z}
      \psi_{z,b}K_{z,b}^{1+\rho_{z,b}}
      \le
      a_*S .
      \tag{FAL2}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   In particular, if each compressed net is contained in an active raw bucket
   of size \(M_{z,b}\), it is enough to replace \(K_{z,b}\) by \(M_{z,b}\) in
   \((FAL1)\).  Thus the query half of the bucket-net ratio theorem is the
   ordinary success-normalized active candidate-load estimate, with all false
   active buckets included through \(\mathcal Q_{z,b}\).  The genuinely new
   worst-case geometric content is the storage estimate \((FAL2)\), or a
   sharper distinct-canonical-net version of it.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), use the zero cover as in
   \cref{cor:bucket-net-ratio-form}.  Otherwise \(a_*>0\).  For every nonzero
   record, \(K_{z,b}\ge1\) and \(0\le\rho_{z,b}\le1\), hence
   \(K_{z,b}^{\rho_{z,b}}\le K_{z,b}\).  Therefore \((FAL1)\) implies
   \(L_{\rm net}(\sigma_0)\le a_*L_{\sigma_0}\) for every signature, while
   \((FAL2)\) is exactly \(U_{\rm net}\le a_*S\).  The hit condition is the
   definition of \(a_*\), so \cref{cor:bucket-net-ratio-form} applies.  If
   \(K_{z,b}\le M_{z,b}\), the same argument uses
   \(K_{z,b}^{\rho_{z,b}}\le K_{z,b}\le M_{z,b}\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Local-error first-moment active-load certificate]
   \label{cor:local-error-first-moment-active-load}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:local-error-bucket-net-ratio}, and assume
   \(K_{z,b}\) is an integer child size, with zero-size records interpreted as
   no-op records of zero query and storage price.  If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\),
   the cover is feasible.  Otherwise let \(a_{\rm loc}\) be as in \((LBNR2)\).
   Suppose \(a_{\rm loc}>0\), and suppose the active first moments satisfy
   \[
      \E_z\sum_{b:\sigma_0\in\mathcal Q_{z,b}}
      s_{z,b}\psi_{z,b}K_{z,b}
      \le
      a_{\rm loc}L_{\sigma_0}
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma),
      \tag{LFAL1}
   \]
   while the storage Renyi moment satisfies
   \[
      \E_z\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_z}
      \psi_{z,b}K_{z,b}^{1+\rho_{z,b}}
      \le
      a_{\rm loc}S .
      \tag{LFAL2}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   Thus localizing the error vector does not reintroduce a query-side Renyi
   burden.  Since \(K^\rho\le K\), the query condition remains the ordinary
   success-normalized active-load estimate; the useful hit mass in the
   denominator is simply the sharper local-error quantity \(a_{\rm loc}\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), use the zero cover.  Otherwise \(a_{\rm loc}>0\).
   For every nonzero record, \(K_{z,b}\ge1\) and \(0\le\rho_{z,b}\le1\), so
   \(K_{z,b}^{\rho_{z,b}}\le K_{z,b}\).  Hence \((LFAL1)\) implies
   \(L_{\rm net}(\sigma_0)\le a_{\rm loc}L_{\sigma_0}\) for every signature,
   and \((LFAL2)\) is \(U_{\rm net}\le a_{\rm loc}S\).  The useful-hit condition
   is the definition of \(a_{\rm loc}\).  Apply
   \cref{cor:local-error-bucket-net-ratio}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Shared-canonical panel storage certificate]
   \label{cor:shared-canonical-panel-storage}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:observable-renyi-profile-cover}.  Let a
   finite seed \(z\sim\nu\) produce a finite decoded panel
   \(\mathcal B_z\).  Each record \(b\in\mathcal B_z\) has certified hit,
   query-load, and error components
   \(H_{z,b}(\sigma_0)\), \(L_{z,b}(\sigma_0)\), and \(E_{z,b}\).  Records also
   point to canonical child identifiers
   \[
      \kappa_{z,b}\in\mathcal C_z ,
   \]
   where every child \(\kappa\in\mathcal C_z\) has a certified storage price
   \(U_{z,\kappa}\).  Let \(\Gamma_z\ge0\) be any additional metadata price for
   the panel records and pointers, and define
   \[
      H_{\rm can}(\sigma_0)
      =
      \E_z\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_z}H_{z,b}(\sigma_0),
      \qquad
      L_{\rm can}(\sigma_0)
      =
      \E_z\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_z}L_{z,b}(\sigma_0),
      \tag{SCS1}
   \]
   \[
      E_{\rm can}
      =
      \E_z\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_z}E_{z,b},
      \qquad
      U_{\rm can}
      =
      \E_z\left[
         \Gamma_z+
         \sum_{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)}U_{z,\kappa}
      \right],
      \tag{SCS2}
   \]
   where \(\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)=\{\kappa_{z,b}:b\in\mathcal B_z\}\).
   Suppose these seedwise aggregate panels are certified observable profiles:
   retaining one seed panel stores each canonical child once, pays the record
   metadata \(\Gamma_z\), and has hit/query/error profile bounded by the sums in
   \((SCS1)\)--\((SCS2)\).  If there is \(a>0\) such that
   \[
      H_{\rm can}(\sigma_0)\ge a+E_{\rm can}
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+),
      \tag{SCS3}
   \]
   and
   \[
      L_{\rm can}(\sigma_0)\le aL_{\sigma_0}
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma),
      \qquad
      U_{\rm can}\le aS,
      \tag{SCS4}
   \]
   then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   Thus child storage is charged to distinct canonical identifiers inside the
   retained panel, while occurrence multiplicity remains visible only through
   query load, hit/error accounting, and the explicit metadata term
   \(\Gamma_z\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For each seed \(z\), let
   \(\Pi_z=(H_z,L_z,U_z^{\rm prof},E_z^{\rm prof})\) be the certified
   aggregate observable profile with
   \[
      H_z=\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_z}H_{z,b},\qquad
      L_z=\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_z}L_{z,b},\qquad
      E_z^{\rm prof}=\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_z}E_{z,b},
   \]
   and
   \[
      U_z^{\rm prof}=
      \Gamma_z+
      \sum_{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)}U_{z,\kappa}.
   \]
   Use the probabilities of the finite seed law as the weights
   \(\omega_{\Pi_z}\) in
   \cref{cor:single-panel-success-normalized-profile}, grouping identical
   aggregate profiles if desired.  The aggregate quantities in that corollary
   are precisely \(H_{\rm can},L_{\rm can},U_{\rm can},E_{\rm can}\).  Hence
   \((SCS3)\)--\((SCS4)\) imply feasibility.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Local-error shared-canonical panel storage certificate]
   \label{cor:local-error-shared-canonical-panel-storage}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:local-error-observable-profile-cover}.  Let a finite seed
   \(z\sim\nu\) produce a finite decoded panel \(\mathcal B_z\).  Each record
   \(b\in\mathcal B_z\) has certified hit and query-load components
   \(H_{z,b}(\sigma_0)\) and \(L_{z,b}(\sigma_0)\), and a certified local error
   vector \(E_{z,b}(\sigma_0)\) with
   \(0\le E_{z,b}(\sigma_0)\le H_{z,b}(\sigma_0)\).  Records also point to
   canonical child identifiers \(\kappa_{z,b}\in\mathcal C_z\), where every
   child \(\kappa\in\mathcal C_z\) has certified storage price
   \(U_{z,\kappa}\).  Let \(\Gamma_z\ge0\) be any additional metadata price, and
   define
   \[
      H_{\rm lcan}(\sigma_0)
      =
      \E_z\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_z}H_{z,b}(\sigma_0),
      \qquad
      L_{\rm lcan}(\sigma_0)
      =
      \E_z\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_z}L_{z,b}(\sigma_0),
      \tag{LSCS1}
   \]
   \[
      E_{\rm lcan}(\sigma_0)
      =
      \E_z\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_z}E_{z,b}(\sigma_0),
      \qquad
      U_{\rm lcan}
      =
      \E_z\left[
         \Gamma_z+
         \sum_{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)}U_{z,\kappa}
      \right].
      \tag{LSCS2}
   \]
   Suppose these seedwise aggregate panels are certified local-error profiles:
   retaining one seed panel stores each canonical child once, pays
   \(\Gamma_z\), and has hit/query/local-error profile bounded by the sums in
   \((LSCS1)\)--\((LSCS2)\).  If there is \(a>0\) such that
   \[
      H_{\rm lcan}(\sigma_0)-E_{\rm lcan}(\sigma_0)\ge a
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma^+),
      \tag{LSCS3}
   \]
   and
   \[
      L_{\rm lcan}(\sigma_0)\le aL_{\sigma_0}
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma),
      \qquad
      U_{\rm lcan}\le aS,
      \tag{LSCS4}
   \]
   then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   Thus the shared-DAG storage accounting can use the same local-error
   denominator as the decoded-panel cover: repeated occurrences affect query
   load and local error, while each canonical child is stored once.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For each seed \(z\), let
   \(\Pi_z=(H_z,L_z,U_z^{\rm prof},E_z^{\rm prof}(\cdot))\) be the certified
   aggregate local-error profile with
   \[
      H_z=\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_z}H_{z,b},\qquad
      L_z=\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_z}L_{z,b},\qquad
      E_z^{\rm prof}(\sigma_0)=
      \sum_{b\in\mathcal B_z}E_{z,b}(\sigma_0),
   \]
   and
   \[
      U_z^{\rm prof}=
      \Gamma_z+
      \sum_{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)}U_{z,\kappa}.
   \]
   Use the probabilities of the finite seed law as the weights in the aggregate
   part of \cref{cor:local-error-observable-profile-cover}.  The resulting
   aggregates are exactly
   \(H_{\rm lcan},E_{\rm lcan},L_{\rm lcan},U_{\rm lcan}\).  Conditions
   \((LSCS3)\)--\((LSCS4)\) are \((LEPC2)\)--\((LEPC3)\), so feasibility
   follows.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Distinct-canonical bucket-net certificate]
   \label{cor:distinct-canonical-bucket-net}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:bucket-net-ratio-form}.  In addition to the
   record data of \cref{cor:recursive-compressed-net-panel}, suppose every
   record \(b\in\mathcal B_z\) points to a canonical child identifier
   \(\kappa_{z,b}\).  The child identifier \(\kappa\) has integer size
   \(K_{z,\kappa}\), exponent \(0\le\rho_{z,\kappa}\le1\), and price factor
   \(\psi_{z,\kappa}\), and record \(b\) uses the corresponding values
   \(K_{z,b}=K_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}\),
   \(\rho_{z,b}=\rho_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}\), and
   \(\psi_{z,b}=\psi_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}\).  Let \(\Gamma_z\ge0\) bound all
   nonrecursive panel metadata and occurrence-pointer storage, and put
   \[
      U_{\rm can}
      =
      \E_z\left[
         \Gamma_z+
         \sum_{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)}
         \psi_{z,\kappa}K_{z,\kappa}^{1+\rho_{z,\kappa}}
      \right].
      \tag{DCB1}
   \]
   If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), the cover is feasible.  Otherwise let \(a_*\) be
   as in \((BNR1)\).  Suppose \(a_*>0\), the active first moments satisfy
   \[
      \E_z\sum_{b:\sigma_0\in\mathcal Q_{z,b}}
      s_{z,b}\psi_{z,b}K_{z,b}
      \le
      a_*L_{\sigma_0}
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma),
      \tag{DCB2}
   \]
   and the distinct-canonical storage satisfies
   \[
      U_{\rm can}\le a_*S .
      \tag{DCB3}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   In particular, the storage theorem needed for a bucket-net/list-decoding
   implementation is not the occurrence moment
   \(\E_z\sum_b\psi_{z,b}K_{z,b}^{1+\rho_{z,b}}\).  It is the distinct
   canonical child bound \((DCB1)\), plus the explicit metadata budget
   \(\E_z\Gamma_z\).  Multiple decoded records may point to the same recursive
   child at no additional child-index storage cost.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), use the zero cover.  Otherwise \(a_*>0\).
   For each record, \(K_{z,b}^{\rho_{z,b}}\le K_{z,b}\), with zero-price
   records interpreted as in
   \cref{cor:first-moment-active-load-query}.  Hence \((DCB2)\) implies the
   query inequality \(L_{\rm net}(\sigma_0)\le a_*L_{\sigma_0}\).  The hit
   inequality is the definition of \(a_*\), and \((DCB3)\) is the shared
   storage inequality \((SCS4)\) for the aggregate panel profile whose record
   hit/query/error components are \((RCN1)\)--\((RCN2)\) and whose child storage
   is charged by \((DCB1)\).  Applying
   \cref{cor:shared-canonical-panel-storage} gives feasibility.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Local-error distinct-canonical bucket-net certificate]
   \label{cor:local-error-distinct-canonical-bucket-net}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:local-error-bucket-net-ratio}.  In addition
   to the record data there, suppose every record \(b\in\mathcal B_z\) points to
   a canonical child identifier \(\kappa_{z,b}\).  The child identifier
   \(\kappa\) has integer size \(K_{z,\kappa}\), exponent
   \(0\le\rho_{z,\kappa}\le1\), and price factor \(\psi_{z,\kappa}\), and
   record \(b\) uses the corresponding values
   \(K_{z,b}=K_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}\),
   \(\rho_{z,b}=\rho_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}\), and
   \(\psi_{z,b}=\psi_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}\).  Let \(\Gamma_z\ge0\) bound all
   nonrecursive panel metadata and occurrence-pointer storage, and put
   \[
      U_{\rm lcan}
      =
      \E_z\left[
         \Gamma_z+
         \sum_{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)}
         \psi_{z,\kappa}K_{z,\kappa}^{1+\rho_{z,\kappa}}
      \right].
      \tag{LDCB1}
   \]
   If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), the cover is feasible.  Otherwise let
   \(a_{\rm loc}\) be as in \((LBNR2)\).  Suppose \(a_{\rm loc}>0\), the active
   first moments satisfy
   \[
      \E_z\sum_{b:\sigma_0\in\mathcal Q_{z,b}}
      s_{z,b}\psi_{z,b}K_{z,b}
      \le
      a_{\rm loc}L_{\sigma_0}
      \qquad(\sigma_0\in\Sigma),
      \tag{LDCB2}
   \]
   and the distinct-canonical storage satisfies
   \[
      U_{\rm lcan}\le a_{\rm loc}S .
      \tag{LDCB3}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   This is the local-error storage target for decoded bucket nets: the useful
   hit denominator is \(a_{\rm loc}\), but recursive child storage is still paid
   only once per distinct canonical child.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), use the zero cover.  Otherwise \(a_{\rm loc}>0\).
   For each record, \(K_{z,b}^{\rho_{z,b}}\le K_{z,b}\), with zero-price
   records interpreted as in
   \cref{cor:local-error-first-moment-active-load}.  Hence \((LDCB2)\) implies
   the query inequality \(L_{\rm net}(\sigma_0)\le a_{\rm loc}L_{\sigma_0}\).
   The useful-hit inequality is the definition of \(a_{\rm loc}\).  The storage
   inequality \((LDCB3)\) is \((LSCS4)\) for the aggregate local-error panel
   profile whose record hit/query/local-error components are those of
   \cref{cor:local-error-bucket-net-ratio} and whose child storage is charged by
   \((LDCB1)\).  Applying
   \cref{cor:local-error-shared-canonical-panel-storage} gives feasibility.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Dyadic tail certificate for distinct child storage]
   \label{lem:dyadic-tail-distinct-child-storage}
   Work with one seed \(z\) in the setting of
   \cref{cor:distinct-canonical-bucket-net}, and write the certified storage
   price of a distinct canonical child as
   \[
      u_{z,\kappa}=
      \psi_{z,\kappa}K_{z,\kappa}^{1+\rho_{z,\kappa}} .
   \]
   For \(i\in\mathbb Z\), let
   \[
      C_z(i)=
      \left|\{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z):
      2^i\le u_{z,\kappa}<2^{i+1}\}\right|.
      \tag{DTS1}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      \sum_{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)}u_{z,\kappa}
      \le
      2\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z}2^iC_z(i),
      \tag{DTS2}
   \]
   with only finitely many nonzero terms.  Equivalently, for the tail counts
   \[
      N_z(t)=
      \left|\{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z):u_{z,\kappa}\ge t\}\right|,
      \tag{DTS3}
   \]
   one has the exact layer-cake identity
   \[
      \sum_{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)}u_{z,\kappa}
      =
      \int_0^\infty N_z(t)\,dt .
      \tag{DTS4}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   The dyadic classes in \((DTS1)\) partition the positive-price children.  A
   child in class \(i\) has price less than \(2^{i+1}\), so summing over classes
   gives \((DTS2)\).  Zero-price children contribute neither side.

   For the layer-cake form, use
   \[
      u_{z,\kappa}=\int_0^\infty \mathbf 1\{t\le u_{z,\kappa}\}\,dt
   \]
   for each finite child price and interchange the finite sum and the integral.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Layer-cake distinct-storage bucket-net certificate]
   \label{cor:layer-cake-distinct-storage-bucket-net}
   Work in either of the following two settings:
   the scalar distinct-storage setting of
   \cref{cor:distinct-canonical-bucket-net}, with \(a=a_*\) and active
   first-moment condition \((DCB2)\), or the local-error setting of
   \cref{cor:local-error-distinct-canonical-bucket-net}, with
   \(a=a_{\rm loc}\) and active first-moment condition \((LDCB2)\).  For each
   seed \(z\), define \(u_{z,\kappa}\) and \(N_z(t)\) as in
   \cref{lem:dyadic-tail-distinct-child-storage}.  If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\),
   the cover is feasible.  Otherwise suppose \(a>0\), the corresponding active
   first-moment condition holds, and
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+
      \E_z\int_0^\infty N_z(t)\,dt
      \le
      aS .
      \tag{LCDS1}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   Thus the dyadic large-child formulation is only a convenient discretization.
   The exact storage theorem is an integrated tail bound for the number of
   distinct canonical children whose recursive price exceeds \(t\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By the layer-cake identity \((DTS4)\),
   \[
      \E_z\int_0^\infty N_z(t)\,dt
      =
      \E_z\sum_{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)}u_{z,\kappa}.
   \]
   Hence \((LCDS1)\) is exactly the storage condition \((DCB3)\) in the scalar
   setting and \((LDCB3)\) in the local-error setting.  The conclusion follows
   from \cref{cor:distinct-canonical-bucket-net} and
   \cref{cor:local-error-distinct-canonical-bucket-net}, respectively.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Dyadic distinct-storage bucket-net certificate]
   \label{cor:dyadic-distinct-storage-bucket-net}
   Work in the setting of \cref{cor:distinct-canonical-bucket-net}.  For each
   seed \(z\), define \(u_{z,\kappa}\) and \(C_z(i)\) as in
   \cref{lem:dyadic-tail-distinct-child-storage}.  If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\),
   the cover is feasible.  Otherwise let \(a_*\) be as in \((BNR1)\).  Suppose
   \(a_*>0\), the active first moments satisfy \((DCB2)\), and the dyadic
   distinct-child tail bound
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+
      2\E_z\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z}2^iC_z(i)
      \le
      a_*S
      \tag{DDS1}
   \]
   holds.  Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   Thus the remaining storage geometry may be stated as a large-child counting
   theorem: at each recursive price scale \(2^i\), bound the number of distinct
   canonical bucket nets with price in that dyadic class.  This is strictly the
   shared-DAG quantity; repeated decoded occurrences of the same canonical net
   do not increase \(C_z(i)\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \cref{lem:dyadic-tail-distinct-child-storage}, the left side of
   \((DCB1)\) is at most the left side of \((DDS1)\).  Hence \((DDS1)\) implies
   \((DCB3)\), and \cref{cor:distinct-canonical-bucket-net} applies.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Local-error dyadic distinct-storage bucket-net certificate]
   \label{cor:local-error-dyadic-distinct-storage-bucket-net}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:local-error-distinct-canonical-bucket-net}.  For each seed \(z\),
   define \(u_{z,\kappa}\) and \(C_z(i)\) as in
   \cref{lem:dyadic-tail-distinct-child-storage}.  If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\),
   the cover is feasible.  Otherwise let \(a_{\rm loc}\) be as in \((LBNR2)\).
   Suppose \(a_{\rm loc}>0\), the active first moments satisfy \((LDCB2)\), and
   the dyadic distinct-child tail bound
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+
      2\E_z\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z}2^iC_z(i)
      \le
      a_{\rm loc}S
      \tag{LDDS1}
   \]
   holds.  Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   Thus local-error accounting and shared-DAG storage commute: local errors
   improve the hit denominator, while dyadic large-child counting remains the
   same storage theorem.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \cref{lem:dyadic-tail-distinct-child-storage}, the left side of
   \((LDCB1)\) is at most the left side of \((LDDS1)\).  Hence \((LDDS1)\)
   implies \((LDCB3)\), and
   \cref{cor:local-error-distinct-canonical-bucket-net} applies.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Tuple witnesses for distinct child tails]
   \label{lem:tuple-witness-distinct-child-tail}
   Work at one resident node \(P\), fix a separation scale \(\delta>0\), and
   let \(\mathcal T_k(P,\delta)\) be as in
   \cref{lem:packing-list-tuple-moment}.  In the setting of
   \cref{lem:dyadic-tail-distinct-child-storage}, suppose that for every
   dyadic price class \(i\) we choose an integer \(k_i\ge1\) and a number
   \(R_i>0\).  Each distinct canonical child \(\kappa\) in class \(i\) has an
   associated separated net \(A_{z,\kappa}\subseteq P\), and satisfies the
   witness lower bound
   \[
      \left|
      \{(x_1,\ldots,x_{k_i})\in\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta):
      x_j\in A_{z,\kappa}\ \forall j\}
      \right|
      \ge R_i .
      \tag{TWT1}
   \]
   For a tuple \(\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)\), let
   \[
      M_z(i,\mathbf x)
      =
      \left|
      \{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z):
      2^i\le u_{z,\kappa}<2^{i+1},
      \ x_j\in A_{z,\kappa}\ \forall j\}
      \right|.
      \tag{TWT2}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      C_z(i)
      \le
      \frac1{R_i}
      \sum_{\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)}
      M_z(i,\mathbf x).
      \tag{TWT3}
   \]

   In particular, if every child in class \(i\) has
   \(|A_{z,\kappa}|\ge K_i\), then one may take \(R_i=K_i^{k_i}\), since
   repetitions are allowed in \(\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   Sum the witness lower bound \((TWT1)\) over all distinct canonical children
   in the dyadic class \(i\):
   \[
      R_iC_z(i)
      \le
      \sum_{\substack{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z):\\
                      2^i\le u_{z,\kappa}<2^{i+1}}}
      \sum_{\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)}
      \mathbf 1\{x_j\in A_{z,\kappa}\ \forall j\}.
   \]
   Interchanging the two finite sums gives
   \(\sum_{\mathbf x}M_z(i,\mathbf x)\), and division by \(R_i\) proves
   \((TWT3)\).  If \(|A_{z,\kappa}|\ge K_i\), then every ordered \(k_i\)-tuple
   from \(A_{z,\kappa}\), with repetitions, belongs to
   \(\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)\) because the distinct entries of
   \(A_{z,\kappa}\) are \(\delta\)-separated.  Hence there are at least
   \(K_i^{k_i}\) witnesses.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Multiplicity-discounted tuple witnesses]
   \label{lem:multiplicity-discounted-tuple-witness}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{lem:tuple-witness-distinct-child-tail}, and suppose the decoded panel
   contains occurrence records \(b\in\mathcal B_z\) pointing to the same
   canonical child identifiers \(\kappa_{z,b}\).  For a distinct child
   \(\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)\), let
   \[
      m_z(\kappa)
      =
      \left|\{b\in\mathcal B_z:\kappa_{z,b}=\kappa\}\right|
      \tag{MDT0}
   \]
   be its occurrence multiplicity.  For
   \(\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)\), define the
   multiplicity-discounted tuple incidence
   \[
      \widetilde M_z(i,\mathbf x)
      =
      \sum_{\substack{b\in\mathcal B_z:\\
         2^i\le u_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}<2^{i+1}\\
         x_j\in A_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}\ \forall j}}
      \frac1{m_z(\kappa_{z,b})}.
      \tag{MDT1}
   \]
   Then
   \[
      C_z(i)
      \le
      \frac1{R_i}
      \sum_{\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)}
      \widetilde M_z(i,\mathbf x).
      \tag{MDT2}
   \]

   In particular, if every distinct child \(\kappa\) in class \(i\) has
   occurrence multiplicity at least \(M_i\ge1\), and
   \[
      M_z^{\rm occ}(i,\mathbf x)
      =
      \left|
      \{b\in\mathcal B_z:
      2^i\le u_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}<2^{i+1},\
      x_j\in A_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}\ \forall j\}
      \right|,
      \tag{MDT3}
   \]
   then
   \[
      C_z(i)
      \le
      \frac1{R_iM_i}
      \sum_{\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)}
      M_z^{\rm occ}(i,\mathbf x).
      \tag{MDT4}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   For a fixed tuple \(\mathbf x\), group the sum in \((MDT1)\) by canonical
   child identifier.  Each child \(\kappa\) contributes either zero, if not all
   entries of \(\mathbf x\) lie in \(A_{z,\kappa}\), or
   \(m_z(\kappa)\cdot m_z(\kappa)^{-1}=1\), if
   all entries of \(\mathbf x\) lie in \(A_{z,\kappa}\).  Hence
   \[
      \widetilde M_z(i,\mathbf x)
      =
      M_z(i,\mathbf x),
   \]
   where \(M_z(i,\mathbf x)\) is the distinct-child tuple incidence in
   \((TWT2)\).  Therefore \((MDT2)\) is exactly \((TWT3)\).

   If every child in the dyadic class has multiplicity at least \(M_i\), then
   each occurrence term satisfies
   \(m_z(\kappa_{z,b})^{-1}\le M_i^{-1}\).  Thus
   \(\widetilde M_z(i,\mathbf x)\le M_i^{-1}M_z^{\rm occ}(i,\mathbf x)\), and
   substituting this into \((MDT2)\) gives \((MDT4)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Integrated tuple-tail distinct-storage certificate]
   \label{cor:integrated-tuple-tail-distinct-storage}
   Work in either of the two settings of
   \cref{cor:layer-cake-distinct-storage-bucket-net}, with the corresponding
   value of \(a\).  Fix a separation scale \(\delta>0\).  For every \(t>0\),
   suppose that an integer \(k(t)\ge1\), a number \(R(t)>0\), and certified
   measurable envelopes \(J_t(\mathbf x)\ge0\) are chosen so that every distinct
   child \(\kappa\) with \(u_{z,\kappa}\ge t\) has an associated separated net
   \(A_{z,\kappa}\subseteq P\) satisfying
   \[
      \left|
      \{(x_1,\ldots,x_{k(t)})\in\mathcal T_{k(t)}(P,\delta):
      x_j\in A_{z,\kappa}\ \forall j\}
      \right|
      \ge R(t),
      \tag{ITD1}
   \]
   and, with
   \[
      M_z(t,\mathbf x)
      =
      \left|
      \{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z):
      u_{z,\kappa}\ge t,\
      x_j\in A_{z,\kappa}\ \forall j\}
      \right|,
      \tag{ITD2}
   \]
   one has
   \[
      \E_zM_z(t,\mathbf x)\le J_t(\mathbf x).
      \tag{ITD3}
   \]
   If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), the cover is feasible.  Otherwise suppose \(a>0\),
   the corresponding active first-moment condition holds, and
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+
      \int_0^\infty
      \frac1{R(t)}
      \sum_{\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_{k(t)}(P,\delta)}
      J_t(\mathbf x)\,dt
      \le
      aS .
      \tag{ITD4}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   Equivalently, if for each \(t\) the tuple set is partitioned into profile
   classes \(\Pi_t\), every tuple in profile \(\pi\in\Pi_t\) has
   \(J_t(\mathbf x)\le e^{-I_{t,\pi}}\), and the profile has size
   \(N_{t,\pi}\), it is enough to replace the inner tuple sum in \((ITD4)\) by
   \[
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi_t}N_{t,\pi}e^{-I_{t,\pi}} .
      \tag{ITD5}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Fix \(t>0\).  Summing the witness bound \((ITD1)\) over all children with
   \(u_{z,\kappa}\ge t\) and interchanging finite sums gives
   \[
      N_z(t)
      \le
      \frac1{R(t)}
      \sum_{\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_{k(t)}(P,\delta)}
      M_z(t,\mathbf x).
      \tag{ITD6}
   \]
   Taking expectation and using \((ITD3)\),
   \[
      \E_zN_z(t)
      \le
      \frac1{R(t)}
      \sum_{\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_{k(t)}(P,\delta)}
      J_t(\mathbf x).
   \]
   Integrating this inequality over \(t\) and applying \((ITD4)\) gives
   \((LCDS1)\).  Therefore
   \cref{cor:layer-cake-distinct-storage-bucket-net} proves feasibility.  The
   profile form is just summation of the pointwise envelope over each profile
   class.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Price-weighted witness-packing storage certificate]
   \label{cor:price-weighted-witness-packing-storage}
   Work in either of the two settings of
   \cref{cor:layer-cake-distinct-storage-bucket-net}, with the corresponding
   value of \(a\).  Let \(\Omega\) be a finite witness universe.  For every seed
   \(z\) and every distinct canonical child
   \(\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)\), suppose preprocessing certifies a
   probability law \(\pi_{z,\kappa}\) on \(\Omega\).  Let \(u_{z,\kappa}\) be the
   child storage price from \((DTS4)\).  Suppose there are certified envelopes
   \(J(\omega)\ge0\) such that
   \[
      \E_z
      \sum_{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)}
      u_{z,\kappa}\pi_{z,\kappa}(\omega)
      \le
      J(\omega)
      \qquad(\omega\in\Omega).
      \tag{PWP1}
   \]
   If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), the cover is feasible.  Otherwise suppose \(a>0\),
   the corresponding active first-moment condition holds, and
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}J(\omega)\le aS .
      \tag{PWP2}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   In the tuple specialization, \(\Omega\) may be a finite union of separated
   tuple sets \(\mathcal T_k(P,\delta)\), and \(\pi_{z,\kappa}\) is supported on
   tuple witnesses lying inside the separated net \(A_{z,\kappa}\).  Then the
   remaining storage theorem is a price-weighted tuple-congestion bound: every
   distinct child pays its full recursive storage price once, and the geometric
   proof only has to show that no tuple or tuple profile receives too much total
   paid child price.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For each seed \(z\),
   \[
   \begin{aligned}
      \sum_{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)}u_{z,\kappa}
      &=
      \sum_{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)}
      u_{z,\kappa}
      \sum_{\omega\in\Omega}\pi_{z,\kappa}(\omega) \\
      &=
      \sum_{\omega\in\Omega}
      \sum_{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)}
      u_{z,\kappa}\pi_{z,\kappa}(\omega).
   \end{aligned}
   \]
   Taking expectation over \(z\) and applying \((PWP1)\) gives
   \[
      \E_z\sum_{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)}u_{z,\kappa}
      \le
      \sum_{\omega\in\Omega}J(\omega).
   \]
   Therefore \((PWP2)\) implies the layer-cake storage condition \((LCDS1)\), and
   \cref{cor:layer-cake-distinct-storage-bucket-net} gives feasibility.  The
   tuple specialization is the same argument with a witness universe whose atoms
   are certified tuples.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Uniform tuple witness-packing certificate]
   \label{cor:uniform-tuple-witness-packing-storage}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:price-weighted-witness-packing-storage}.  Fix a separation scale
   \(\delta>0\) and a finite set of tuple orders \(\mathcal K\subset\mathbb N\).
   For every distinct child \(\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z)\), suppose there
   is a certified separated net \(A_{z,\kappa}\subseteq P\) and a chosen order
   \(k_{z,\kappa}\in\mathcal K\) such that
   \[
      |A_{z,\kappa}|\ge1,
      \qquad
      A_{z,\kappa}\text{ is }\delta\text{-separated}.
      \tag{UTW0}
   \]
   For \(k\in\mathcal K\) and
   \(\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_k(P,\delta)\), define the price-weighted tuple
   congestion
   \[
      W_z(k,\mathbf x)
      =
      \sum_{\substack{\kappa\in\kappa_z(\mathcal B_z):\\
         k_{z,\kappa}=k,\ x_j\in A_{z,\kappa}\ \forall j}}
      \frac{u_{z,\kappa}}{|A_{z,\kappa}|^k}.
      \tag{UTW1}
   \]
   Suppose there are certified envelopes \(J_k(\mathbf x)\ge0\) with
   \[
      \E_z W_z(k,\mathbf x)\le J_k(\mathbf x)
      \qquad(k\in\mathcal K,\ \mathbf x\in\mathcal T_k(P,\delta)).
      \tag{UTW2}
   \]
   If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), the cover is feasible.  Otherwise suppose \(a>0\),
   the corresponding active first-moment condition holds, and
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+
      \sum_{k\in\mathcal K}
      \sum_{\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_k(P,\delta)}J_k(\mathbf x)
      \le aS .
      \tag{UTW3}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   In particular, if
   \(u_{z,\kappa}=\psi_{z,\kappa}|A_{z,\kappa}|^{1+\rho_{z,\kappa}}\) with
   \(0\le\rho_{z,\kappa}\le1\) and one takes \(k_{z,\kappa}=2\), then each
   tuple-incidence is weighted by
   \[
      \psi_{z,\kappa}|A_{z,\kappa}|^{\rho_{z,\kappa}-1}\le\psi_{z,\kappa}.
      \tag{UTW4}
   \]
   Thus, up to the child price factor \(\psi\), the storage theorem can be
   attacked as an ordinary pair-congestion bound for distinct canonical nets.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Let
   \[
      \Omega=\bigcup_{k\in\mathcal K}\{k\}\times\mathcal T_k(P,\delta).
   \]
   For a child \(\kappa\), define \(\pi_{z,\kappa}\) to be the uniform law on
   ordered \(k_{z,\kappa}\)-tuples from \(A_{z,\kappa}\), embedded in the
   corresponding component of \(\Omega\).  Because \(A_{z,\kappa}\) is
   \(\delta\)-separated and repetitions are allowed in
   \(\mathcal T_k(P,\delta)\), this is a probability law on \(\Omega\).  For an
   atom \((k,\mathbf x)\),
   \[
      \sum_{\kappa}u_{z,\kappa}\pi_{z,\kappa}(k,\mathbf x)
      =
      W_z(k,\mathbf x).
   \]
   Hence \((UTW2)\) is exactly \((PWP1)\) for the witness universe \(\Omega\), and
   \((UTW3)\) is \((PWP2)\).  Applying
   \cref{cor:price-weighted-witness-packing-storage} proves feasibility.

   The final statement is the identity
   \[
      \frac{u_{z,\kappa}}{|A_{z,\kappa}|^2}
      =
      \psi_{z,\kappa}|A_{z,\kappa}|^{\rho_{z,\kappa}-1},
   \]
   and the inequality follows from \(|A_{z,\kappa}|\ge1\) and
   \(\rho_{z,\kappa}\le1\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Occurrence-discounted tuple storage congestion]
   \label{cor:occurrence-discounted-tuple-storage}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:uniform-tuple-witness-packing-storage}, and suppose the decoded
   panel contains occurrence records \(b\in\mathcal B_z\) pointing to the same
   canonical child identifiers \(\kappa_{z,b}\).  Let
   \[
      m_z(\kappa)=|\{b\in\mathcal B_z:\kappa_{z,b}=\kappa\}|
      \tag{ODT0}
   \]
   be the occurrence multiplicity of a distinct child.  For
   \(k\in\mathcal K\) and \(\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_k(P,\delta)\), define
   \[
      \widehat W_z(k,\mathbf x)
      =
      \sum_{\substack{b\in\mathcal B_z:\\
         k_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}=k,\
         x_j\in A_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}\ \forall j}}
      \frac{
         u_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}
      }{
         m_z(\kappa_{z,b})\,|A_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}|^k
      } .
      \tag{ODT1}
   \]
   Suppose there are certified envelopes \(\widehat J_k(\mathbf x)\ge0\) with
   \[
      \E_z\widehat W_z(k,\mathbf x)\le\widehat J_k(\mathbf x)
      \qquad(k\in\mathcal K,\ \mathbf x\in\mathcal T_k(P,\delta)).
      \tag{ODT2}
   \]
   If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), the cover is feasible.  Otherwise suppose \(a>0\),
   the corresponding active first-moment condition holds, and
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+
      \sum_{k\in\mathcal K}
      \sum_{\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_k(P,\delta)}\widehat J_k(\mathbf x)
      \le aS .
      \tag{ODT3}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   In particular, for the pair specialization \(k=2\) and
   \(u_{z,\kappa}=\psi_{z,\kappa}|A_{z,\kappa}|^{1+\rho_{z,\kappa}}\), it is
   enough to bound, for each \((x,y)\in\mathcal T_2(P,\delta)\), the expected
   occurrence sum
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{b\in\mathcal B_z:\\ x,y\in A_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}}}
      \frac{
         \psi_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}|A_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}|^{\rho_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}-1}
      }{
         m_z(\kappa_{z,b})
      },
      \tag{ODT4}
   \]
   which is at most the same sum with the numerator
   \(\psi_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}\).  Thus an occurrence-based decoder may prove the
   shared-DAG storage bound by reciprocal-multiplicity-weighted pair congestion.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For a fixed tuple \((k,\mathbf x)\), group the occurrence sum \((ODT1)\) by
   canonical child identifier.  A child \(\kappa\) with
   \(k_{z,\kappa}=k\) and \(x_j\in A_{z,\kappa}\) for all \(j\) contributes
   \[
      m_z(\kappa)\cdot
      \frac{u_{z,\kappa}}{m_z(\kappa)|A_{z,\kappa}|^k}
      =
      \frac{u_{z,\kappa}}{|A_{z,\kappa}|^k},
   \]
   and otherwise contributes zero.  Hence
   \[
      \widehat W_z(k,\mathbf x)=W_z(k,\mathbf x).
      \tag{ODT5}
   \]
   Conditions \((ODT2)\)--\((ODT3)\) are therefore exactly the hypotheses
   \((UTW2)\)--\((UTW3)\), and
   \cref{cor:uniform-tuple-witness-packing-storage} gives feasibility.

   The displayed pair specialization is \((ODT1)\) with \(k=2\) and the stated
   storage price.  Since \(|A_{z,\kappa}|\ge1\) and
   \(\rho_{z,\kappa}\le1\), each factor
   \(|A_{z,\kappa}|^{\rho_{z,\kappa}-1}\) is at most one.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Pair-profile occurrence-discounted storage certificate]
   \label{cor:pair-profile-occurrence-discounted-storage}
   Work in the pair specialization \(k=2\) of
   \cref{cor:occurrence-discounted-tuple-storage}.  Partition
   \(\mathcal T_2(P,\delta)\) into finite profile classes \(\Pi\).  For each
   profile \(\pi\in\Pi\), let \(N_\pi\) be its cardinality, and suppose there is
   a certified envelope \(B_\pi\ge0\) such that
   \[
      \E_z\widehat W_z(2,x,y)\le B_\pi
      \qquad((x,y)\in\pi).
      \tag{POD1}
   \]
   If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), the cover is feasible.  Otherwise suppose \(a>0\),
   the corresponding active first-moment condition holds, and
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+\sum_{\pi\in\Pi}N_\pi B_\pi\le aS .
      \tag{POD2}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   In particular, if a geometric or list-decoding analysis gives
   \[
      B_\pi\le C_\pi e^{-I_\pi},
      \tag{POD3}
   \]
   where \(I_\pi\) is a cap-intersection or decoder energy and \(C_\pi\) is the
   largest certified price factor for occurrences in that profile, then it is
   enough to prove the entropy-energy inequality
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}N_\pi C_\pi e^{-I_\pi}
      \le aS .
      \tag{POD4}
   \]
   This is the profile form of the remaining shared-DAG storage theorem.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Define \(\widehat J_2(x,y)=B_\pi\) for \((x,y)\in\pi\).  Then \((POD1)\) is
   exactly the envelope condition \((ODT2)\), and
   \[
      \sum_{(x,y)\in\mathcal T_2(P,\delta)}\widehat J_2(x,y)
      =
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}N_\pi B_\pi .
   \]
   Hence \((POD2)\) is \((ODT3)\), and
   \cref{cor:occurrence-discounted-tuple-storage} gives feasibility.  The final
   statement is obtained by substituting \((POD3)\) into \((POD2)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Multiplicity-layer pair-profile certificate]
   \label{cor:multiplicity-layer-pair-profile-storage}
   Work in the pair specialization of
   \cref{cor:occurrence-discounted-tuple-storage}, with
   \(u_{z,\kappa}=\psi_{z,\kappa}|A_{z,\kappa}|^{1+\rho_{z,\kappa}}\).
   Partition \(\mathcal T_2(P,\delta)\) into finite profile classes \(\Pi\).
   For \(\pi\in\Pi\), let \(N_\pi\) be its cardinality.
   For \((x,y)\in\pi\) and \(\ell\ge0\), define the undiscounted occurrence
   congestion in multiplicity layer \(\ell\) by
   \[
      V_z(\pi,\ell;x,y)
      =
      \sum_{\substack{b\in\mathcal B_z:\ x,y\in A_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}\\
            2^\ell\le m_z(\kappa_{z,b})<2^{\ell+1}}}
      \psi_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}
      |A_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}|^{\rho_{z,\kappa_{z,b}}-1}.
      \tag{MLP1}
   \]
   Suppose there are envelopes \(A_{\pi,\ell}\ge0\) such that
   \[
      \E_z V_z(\pi,\ell;x,y)\le A_{\pi,\ell}
      \qquad((x,y)\in\pi,\ \ell\ge0).
      \tag{MLP2}
   \]
   If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), the cover is feasible.  Otherwise suppose \(a>0\),
   the corresponding active first-moment condition holds, and
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}N_\pi
      \sum_{\ell\ge0}2^{-\ell}A_{\pi,\ell}
      \le aS .
      \tag{MLP3}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   In particular, if a profile analysis gives
   \[
      A_{\pi,\ell}\le C_{\pi,\ell}e^{-I_{\pi,\ell}},
      \tag{MLP4}
   \]
   then it is enough to prove the discounted entropy-energy inequality
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}N_\pi
      \sum_{\ell\ge0}
      2^{-\ell}C_{\pi,\ell}e^{-I_{\pi,\ell}}
      \le aS .
      \tag{MLP5}
   \]
   Thus high occurrence multiplicity appears as a literal \(2^{-\ell}\)
   storage discount.  Low-multiplicity profiles must be paid by cap-intersection
   or decoder energy; high-multiplicity profiles may be paid by quotienting many
   decoded records to one canonical child.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For \((x,y)\in\pi\), decompose the discounted occurrence sum \((ODT4)\) by
   the dyadic layer containing \(m_z(\kappa_{z,b})\).  Every record in layer
   \(\ell\) has reciprocal multiplicity at most \(2^{-\ell}\), so
   \[
      \widehat W_z(2,x,y)
      \le
      \sum_{\ell\ge0}2^{-\ell}V_z(\pi,\ell;x,y).
   \]
   Taking expectations and using \((MLP2)\) gives the pair-profile envelope
   \[
      B_\pi=\sum_{\ell\ge0}2^{-\ell}A_{\pi,\ell}.
   \]
   Condition \((MLP3)\) is therefore \((POD2)\) for this envelope, and
   \cref{cor:pair-profile-occurrence-discounted-storage} gives feasibility.
   Substituting \((MLP4)\) gives \((MLP5)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Aggregate multiplicity-profile storage certificate]
   \label{cor:aggregate-multiplicity-profile-storage}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:multiplicity-layer-pair-profile-storage}.  For each profile
   \(\pi\in\Pi\) and layer \(\ell\ge0\), define the aggregate undiscounted
   layer congestion
   \[
      \mathcal V_z(\pi,\ell)
      =
      \sum_{(x,y)\in\pi}V_z(\pi,\ell;x,y).
      \tag{AMP1}
   \]
   Suppose there are certified aggregate envelopes
   \(\mathcal A_{\pi,\ell}\ge0\) such that
   \[
      \E_z\mathcal V_z(\pi,\ell)\le\mathcal A_{\pi,\ell}
      \qquad(\pi\in\Pi,\ \ell\ge0).
      \tag{AMP2}
   \]
   If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), the cover is feasible.  Otherwise suppose \(a>0\),
   the corresponding active first-moment condition holds, and
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi}\sum_{\ell\ge0}
      2^{-\ell}\mathcal A_{\pi,\ell}
      \le aS .
      \tag{AMP3}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   In particular, it is enough to prove an aggregate entropy-energy estimate
   \[
      \mathcal A_{\pi,\ell}
      \le
      C_{\pi,\ell}\exp(H_{\pi,\ell}-I_{\pi,\ell}),
      \tag{AMP4}
   \]
   where \(H_{\pi,\ell}\) is the logarithmic number or mass of pair occurrences
   in the profile layer and \(I_{\pi,\ell}\) is the corresponding
   cap-intersection or decoder energy, together with
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+
      \sum_{\pi,\ell}
      2^{-\ell}C_{\pi,\ell}\exp(H_{\pi,\ell}-I_{\pi,\ell})
      \le aS .
      \tag{AMP5}
   \]
   Thus the storage proof does not need a uniform worst-pair bound inside a
   profile.  It may bound the whole profile-layer mass directly.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   For each separated pair \((x,y)\), set
   \[
      \widehat J_2(x,y)=\E_z\widehat W_z(2,x,y).
   \]
   This is a valid envelope for \((ODT2)\) with equality.  If \((x,y)\in\pi\),
   the proof of \cref{cor:multiplicity-layer-pair-profile-storage} gives
   pointwise in \(z\)
   \[
      \widehat W_z(2,x,y)
      \le
      \sum_{\ell\ge0}2^{-\ell}V_z(\pi,\ell;x,y).
   \]
   Summing over \((x,y)\in\pi\), taking expectations, and using \((AMP2)\)
   gives
   \[
      \sum_{(x,y)\in\pi}\widehat J_2(x,y)
      \le
      \sum_{\ell\ge0}2^{-\ell}\mathcal A_{\pi,\ell}.
   \]
   Summing over profiles and applying \((AMP3)\) yields \((ODT3)\), so
   \cref{cor:occurrence-discounted-tuple-storage} gives feasibility.  The final
   claim follows by substituting \((AMP4)\) into \((AMP3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Gaussian aggregate profile-layer storage test]
   \label{cor:gaussian-aggregate-profile-layer-storage}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:aggregate-multiplicity-profile-storage}.  Fix a profile
   \(\pi\) and multiplicity layer \(\ell\).  Suppose the undiscounted layer
   congestion admits the following certified expansion before the Gaussian cap
   tests are evaluated:
   \[
      \mathcal V_z(\pi,\ell)
      \le
      \sum_{r\in\mathcal R_{\pi,\ell}}
      w_r
      \sum_{(x,y)\in E_r}
      \mathbf 1\{x,y\in U_{G_r}\},
      \tag{GAP1}
   \]
   where \(w_r\ge0\), \(E_r\subseteq\pi\), and
   \(U_{G_r}=\{u:\ip{G_r}{u}\ge T_r\}\) with
   \(G_r\sim N(\mu_r,I)\).  Assume that for every \(r\) and every
   \((x,y)\in E_r\),
   \[
      -1<\theta_{\pi,\ell}<1,
      \qquad
      \ip{x}{y}\le\theta_{\pi,\ell},
      \qquad
      T_r-\ip{\mu_r}{x}\ge\beta_{\pi,\ell},
      \qquad
      T_r-\ip{\mu_r}{y}\ge\beta_{\pi,\ell},
      \tag{GAP2}
   \]
   with \(\beta_{\pi,\ell}\ge0\).  Put
   \[
      W_{\pi,\ell}
      =
      \sum_{r\in\mathcal R_{\pi,\ell}}w_r|E_r|.
      \tag{GAP3}
   \]
   Then \((AMP2)\) holds with
   \[
      \mathcal A_{\pi,\ell}
      =
      W_{\pi,\ell}
      \exp\left(
         -\frac{\beta_{\pi,\ell}^2}{1+\theta_{\pi,\ell}}
      \right).
      \tag{GAP4}
   \]
   Consequently, if
   \[
      W_{\pi,\ell}\le C_{\pi,\ell}e^{H_{\pi,\ell}},
      \tag{GAP5}
   \]
   then \((AMP4)\) holds with
   \[
      I_{\pi,\ell}
      =
      \frac{\beta_{\pi,\ell}^2}{1+\theta_{\pi,\ell}} .
      \tag{GAP6}
   \]
   Thus a Gaussian cap or list-decoding implementation only has to certify
   three profile-layer quantities: weighted incidence entropy \(H_{\pi,\ell}\),
   threshold margin \(\beta_{\pi,\ell}\), and maximum pair correlation
   \(\theta_{\pi,\ell}\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \cref{lem:two-point-gaussian-cap-energy}, every summand in \((GAP1)\)
   satisfies
   \[
      \Pr[x,y\in U_{G_r}]
      \le
      \exp\left(
         -\frac{\beta_{\pi,\ell}^2}{1+\theta_{\pi,\ell}}
      \right).
   \]
   Linearity of expectation in \((GAP1)\) gives \((GAP4)\).  If \((GAP5)\)
   holds, substitute \(W_{\pi,\ell}\le C_{\pi,\ell}e^{H_{\pi,\ell}}\) into
   \((GAP4)\) to obtain \((AMP4)\) with \((GAP6)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[High-correlation pair-star reporter]
   \label{lem:high-correlation-pair-star-reporter}
   Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb S^{D-1}\), let \(\mathcal R\) be finite, and for
   each \(r\in\mathcal R\) let \(w_r\ge0\) and
   \(E_r\subseteq P\times P\).  Suppose every retained edge is
   \(\underline\theta\)-correlated:
   \[
      (x,y)\in E_r
      \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
      \ip{x}{y}\ge\underline\theta
      \qquad(-1<\underline\theta<1).
      \tag{HPS1}
   \]
   Define the weighted star multiplicities
   \[
      M_x(y)=\sum_{r:\ (x,y)\in E_r}w_r,
      \qquad
      W=\sum_{x,y\in P}M_x(y)=\sum_{r\in\mathcal R}w_r|E_r|.
      \tag{HPS2}
   \]
   For \(t>0\), put
   \[
      U_{x,t}=\{y\in P:M_x(y)\ge t\}.
      \tag{HPS3}
   \]
   Then every \(U_{x,t}\) is contained in the smaller Euclidean ball
   \[
      U_{x,t}\subseteq P\cap B\!\left(x,\sqrt{2(1-\underline\theta)}\right),
      \tag{HPS4}
   \]
   and the exact layer-cake identity
   \[
      W=\sum_{x\in P}\int_0^\infty |U_{x,t}|\,dt
      \tag{HPS5}
   \]
   holds.

   In particular, suppose all positive multiplicities \(M_x(y)\) lie in
   \([M_{\min},M_{\max}]\), where \(0<M_{\min}\le M_{\max}\), and let
   \[
      J=1+\left\lceil\log_2\frac{M_{\max}}{M_{\min}}\right\rceil .
      \tag{HPS6}
   \]
   Then there are \(x\in P\) and a dyadic level
   \(t\in\{2^jM_{\min}:0\le j<J\}\) such that
   \[
      t\,|U_{x,t}|
      \ge
      \frac{W}{2|P|J}.
      \tag{HPS7}
   \]
   Thus any profile layer with large weighted high-correlation incidence either
   has small total incidence \(W\), or exposes a certified smaller-radius
   superlevel \(U_{x,t}\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   If \(y\in U_{x,t}\), then \(M_x(y)>0\), so \((x,y)\in E_r\) for some \(r\)
   with \(w_r>0\).  By \((HPS1)\),
   \[
      \|x-y\|^2=2-2\ip{x}{y}\le2(1-\underline\theta),
   \]
   proving \((HPS4)\).

   For every fixed ordered pair \((x,y)\),
   \[
      M_x(y)=\int_0^\infty \mathbf 1\{M_x(y)\ge t\}\,dt .
   \]
   Summing over ordered pairs gives \((HPS5)\).

   Choose \(x\) with
   \[
      \sum_yM_x(y)\ge W/|P|.
   \]
   For a positive number \(m\in[M_{\min},M_{\max}]\),
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{0\le j<J:\\ 2^jM_{\min}\le m}}2^jM_{\min}
      \ge \frac m2 .
   \]
   Therefore
   \[
      \sum_{j=0}^{J-1}2^jM_{\min}|U_{x,2^jM_{\min}}|
      \ge
      \frac12\sum_yM_x(y)
      \ge
      \frac{W}{2|P|}.
   \]
   One of the \(J\) dyadic levels satisfies \((HPS7)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Dense-star alternative for Gaussian profile layers]
   \label{cor:dense-star-gaussian-profile-layer}
   In the setting of
   \cref{cor:gaussian-aggregate-profile-layer-storage}, suppose in addition
   that every edge in every \(E_r\) satisfies
   \[
      \ip{x}{y}\ge\underline\theta_{\pi,\ell}
      \qquad(-1<\underline\theta_{\pi,\ell}<1),
      \tag{DSG1}
   \]
   and that the positive weighted star multiplicities from \((HPS2)\) lie in a
   certified range \([M_{\min},M_{\max}]\).  If \(J\) is as in \((HPS6)\) and
   \(W_{\pi,\ell}\) is the incidence weight in \((GAP3)\), then either
   \(W_{\pi,\ell}=0\), or there are a center \(x\in P\), a dyadic level \(t\),
   and a certified smaller-radius superlevel
   \[
      U_{x,t}\subseteq
      P\cap B\!\left(x,\sqrt{2(1-\underline\theta_{\pi,\ell})}\right)
      \tag{DSG2}
   \]
   with
   \[
      t|U_{x,t}|
      \ge
      \frac{W_{\pi,\ell}}{2|P|J}.
      \tag{DSG3}
   \]
   Consequently, failure of the Gaussian entropy-energy inequality in a
   high-correlation profile layer can be routed to the dense-cover separator:
   a range reporter only has to search these star superlevels and submit the
   deterministic candidate to the finite filter-cover verifier.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \cref{lem:high-correlation-pair-star-reporter} to the weighted edge
   family \((\mathcal R_{\pi,\ell},w_r,E_r)\).  The total incidence \(W\) in
   \((HPS2)\) is \(W_{\pi,\ell}\) by \((GAP3)\), and the radius claim is
   \((HPS4)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Star-superlevel column verifier]
   \label{lem:star-superlevel-column-verifier}
   Work in a finite filter-cover instance
   \((P,\mathcal Q,\mathcal N)\) as in
   \cref{lem:finite-filter-cover-dual}, where every demand
   \((p,q)\in\mathcal N\) satisfies \(\|p-q\|\le r\).  Let
   \(U\subseteq P\) be certified inside a ball \(B(x,R_U)\), and define the
   ball-thickened query activation
   \[
      a_U(q)=\mathbf 1\{\|q-x\|\le R_U+r\}
      \qquad(q\in\mathcal Q).
      \tag{SVC1}
   \]
   Let \(T_U,S_U\) be certified query and storage prices for the child on
   \(U\).  Then
   \[
      A_U=(U,a_U,T_U,S_U)
      \tag{SVC2}
   \]
   is a valid dense-filter column: if \(p\in U\) and \(\|p-q\|\le r\), then
   \(a_U(q)=1\).

   For any filter-cover dual prices \((\alpha,\tau,\sigma)\), its reduced gain
   is exactly
   \[
      \mathsf G(U)
      =
      \sum_{\substack{(p,q)\in\mathcal N:\\ p\in U}}
         \alpha_{p,q}a_U(q)
      -
      T_U\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}\tau_qa_U(q)
      -
      \sigma S_U .
      \tag{SVC3}
   \]
   If \(\mathsf G(U)>0\), then \(A_U\) is a positive reduced-gain column and
   the finite column-generation step of
   \cref{cor:filter-cover-column-generation} may add it.  Conversely, if a
   finite star family \(\mathcal U_\star\) contains no positive column, then
   every \(U\in\mathcal U_\star\) satisfies the explicit residual inequality
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{(p,q)\in\mathcal N:\\ p\in U}}
         \alpha_{p,q}a_U(q)
      \le
      T_U\sum_q\tau_qa_U(q)+\sigma S_U .
      \tag{SVC4}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   If \(p\in U\subseteq B(x,R_U)\) and \(\|p-q\|\le r\), then
   \[
      \|q-x\|\le\|q-p\|+\|p-x\|\le r+R_U,
   \]
   so \(a_U(q)=1\).  Thus \((SVC2)\) satisfies the filter correctness condition
   used in \cref{def:fractional-dense-filter-cover}.  Formula \((SVC3)\) is
   \cref{cor:filter-cover-column-generation}'s reduced-gain definition applied
   to this column.  Positive gain is therefore an admissible column-generation
   certificate, and nonpositive gain for every member of a finite star family is
   exactly \((SVC4)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Pair-star reporter as dense-column generator]
   \label{cor:pair-star-dense-column-generator}
   In the setting of
   \cref{lem:high-correlation-pair-star-reporter}, also fix a finite
   filter-cover instance \((P,\mathcal Q,\mathcal N)\) with near radius \(r\).
   For each nonempty reported superlevel \(U_{x,t}\), put
   \[
      R_\star=\sqrt{2(1-\underline\theta)}
      \tag{PSG1}
   \]
   and equip \(U_{x,t}\) with the activation
   \[
      a_{x,t}(q)=\mathbf 1\{\|q-x\|\le R_\star+r\}.
      \tag{PSG2}
   \]
   Let \(T_{x,t},S_{x,t}\) be any certified descendant prices for this
   smaller-radius child.  For dual prices \((\alpha,\tau,\sigma)\), define
   \[
      \mathsf G(x,t)
      =
      \sum_{\substack{(p,q)\in\mathcal N:\\ p\in U_{x,t}}}
         \alpha_{p,q}a_{x,t}(q)
      -
      T_{x,t}\sum_q\tau_qa_{x,t}(q)
      -
      \sigma S_{x,t}.
      \tag{PSG3}
   \]
   If some dyadic reporter level has \(\mathsf G(x,t)>0\), then the fractional
   dense-filter cover has a valid positive-gain dense column.  If no dyadic
   reporter level has positive gain, then the residual dual satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{\substack{(p,q)\in\mathcal N:\\ p\in U_{x,t}}}
         \alpha_{p,q}a_{x,t}(q)
      \le
      T_{x,t}\sum_q\tau_qa_{x,t}(q)+\sigma S_{x,t}
      \tag{PSG4}
   \]
   for every reported star.  Thus the high-correlation pair-star construction
   is a safe build-time proposal mechanism: it may generate many overlapping
   candidates, but only the exact reduced-gain test \((PSG3)\) can retain one,
   and \((PSG4)\) is the precise no-star condition left for the diffuse
   spherical/list-decoding analysis.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   By \((HPS4)\), every nonempty \(U_{x,t}\) lies in \(B(x,R_\star)\).  Apply
   \cref{lem:star-superlevel-column-verifier} with \(U=U_{x,t}\) and
   \(R_U=R_\star\).  The displayed gain and residual inequalities are exactly
   \((SVC3)\) and \((SVC4)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Star-prefix weak-type residual]
   \label{lem:star-prefix-weak-type-residual}
   Work in a finite filter-cover instance as in
   \cref{lem:finite-filter-cover-dual}.  Let \(\mathcal X\) be a finite set of
   certified star centers.  For \(x\in\mathcal X\), let
   \(W_x\subseteq P\cap B(x,R_x)\) be a certified container, let
   \[
      a_x(q)=\mathbf 1\{\|q-x\|\le R_x+r\},
      \tag{SPW0}
   \]
   and let the child price for a \(K\)-point prefix of \(W_x\) be
   \[
      T_{x,K}=\psi_xK^{\rho_x},
      \qquad
      S_{x,K}=\psi_xK^{1+\rho_x},
      \qquad 0<\rho_x<1 .
      \tag{SPW1}
   \]
   For dual prices \((\alpha,\tau,\sigma)\), define the star paid degrees and
   query price
   \[
      d_x(p)=
      \sum_{q:\,(p,q)\in\mathcal N}\alpha_{p,q}a_x(q),
      \qquad
      A_x=\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}\tau_qa_x(q).
      \tag{SPW2}
   \]
   Order \(W_x=\{p_1,p_2,\ldots\}\) so that
   \(d_x(p_1)\ge d_x(p_2)\ge\cdots\).  Suppose that, after the current dual
   prices are known, the column generator may add, for every available
   cardinality \(K\in\mathcal K_x\), the star prefix
   \(U_{x,K}=\{p_1,\ldots,p_K\}\) with activation \(a_x\) and prices
   \((SPW1)\).  Equivalently, the finite universe may contain all
   \(K\)-subsets of \(W_x\), with the verifier selecting the best one.  If no
   such star prefix has positive reduced gain, then
   \[
      \sum_{i\le K}d_x(p_i)
      \le
      \psi_x\left(A_xK^{\rho_x}+\sigma K^{1+\rho_x}\right)
      \qquad(x\in\mathcal X,\ K\in\mathcal K_x).
      \tag{SPW3}
   \]
   Consequently every \(U\subseteq W_x\) with \(|U|=K\in\mathcal K_x\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{p\in U}d_x(p)
      \le
      \psi_x\left(A_xK^{\rho_x}+\sigma K^{1+\rho_x}\right).
      \tag{SPW4}
   \]

   If \(\mathcal K_x\) is \(b\)-dense from below, meaning that every
   \(1\le h\le |W_x|\) has some \(K\in\mathcal K_x\) with \(h/b\le K\le h\),
   then every nonempty paid-degree superlevel
   \[
      H_{x,\delta}=\{p\in W_x:d_x(p)\ge\delta\},
      \qquad h=|H_{x,\delta}|,
      \tag{SPW5}
   \]
   obeys the weak-type cap
   \[
      \delta
      \le
      \psi_x\left(
         b^{1-\rho_x}A_xh^{\rho_x-1}
         +\sigma h^{\rho_x}
      \right).
      \tag{SPW6}
   \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
   The reduced gain of \(U_{x,K}\) is
   \[
      \sum_{i\le K}d_x(p_i)
      -
      \psi_xK^{\rho_x}A_x
      -
      \sigma\psi_xK^{1+\rho_x}.
   \]
   Nonpositive gain for every available prefix is exactly \((SPW3)\).  Since
   the top \(K\) prefix maximizes \(\sum_{p\in U}d_x(p)\) among \(K\)-subsets of
   \(W_x\), \((SPW4)\) follows.

   For the weak-type statement, choose \(K\in\mathcal K_x\) with
   \(h/b\le K\le h\).  The top \(K\) points all have degree at least \(\delta\),
   so \(\delta K\le\sum_{i\le K}d_x(p_i)\).  Dividing \((SPW3)\) by \(K\) gives
   \[
      \delta
      \le
      \psi_x\left(A_xK^{\rho_x-1}+\sigma K^{\rho_x}\right).
   \]
   Because \(\rho_x-1<0\), \(K\ge h/b\) gives
   \(K^{\rho_x-1}\le b^{1-\rho_x}h^{\rho_x-1}\), while \(K\le h\) gives
   \(K^{\rho_x}\le h^{\rho_x}\).  This proves \((SPW6)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Pair-star weak-type normal form]
   \label{cor:pair-star-weak-type-normal-form}
   In the setting of
   \cref{cor:pair-star-dense-column-generator}, let
   \(\mathcal X_\star\) be the finite set of centers produced by the reporter,
   and put
   \[
      W_x=P\cap B(x,R_\star),
      \qquad
      a_x(q)=\mathbf 1\{\|q-x\|\le R_\star+r\}.
      \tag{PWN1}
   \]
   Suppose the dense-filter column generator may add the best paid prefix of
   each \(W_x\) at every cardinality, priced as
   \[
      T_{x,K}=\psi_\star K^{\rho_\star},
      \qquad
      S_{x,K}=\psi_\star K^{1+\rho_\star}.
      \tag{PWN2}
   \]
   If no reported center yields a positive-gain prefix, then every reported
   pair-star superlevel \(U_{x,t}\) satisfies
   \[
      \sum_{p\in U_{x,t}}
      \sum_{q:\,(p,q)\in\mathcal N}
         \alpha_{p,q}a_x(q)
      \le
      \psi_\star\left(
         A_x|U_{x,t}|^{\rho_\star}
         +\sigma |U_{x,t}|^{1+\rho_\star}
      \right),
      \tag{PWN3}
   \]
   where \(A_x=\sum_q\tau_qa_x(q)\).  Equivalently, a high-correlation
   pair-star reporter is useful only through a paid-degree violation of
   \((PWN3)\): geometric incidence alone proposes the center and smaller radius,
   while the exact finite-cover verifier chooses the best paid prefix.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Apply \cref{lem:star-prefix-weak-type-residual} with
   \(R_x=R_\star\), \(\psi_x=\psi_\star\), \(\rho_x=\rho_\star\), and
   \(\mathcal K_x=\{1,\ldots,|W_x|\}\).  Since \(U_{x,t}\subseteq W_x\) by
   \((HPS4)\), \((SPW4)\) gives \((PWN3)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Tuple-profile distinct-storage certificate]
   \label{cor:tuple-profile-distinct-storage}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:dyadic-distinct-storage-bucket-net} and
   \cref{lem:tuple-witness-distinct-child-tail}.  Suppose that for every price
   class \(i\) there are certified tuple-incidence envelopes
   \(J_i(\mathbf x)\ge0\) such that
   \[
      \E_z M_z(i,\mathbf x)\le J_i(\mathbf x)
      \qquad
      (\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)).
      \tag{TST1}
   \]
   If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), the cover is feasible.  Otherwise let \(a_*\) be
   as in \((BNR1)\).  Suppose \(a_*>0\), the active first moments satisfy
   \((DCB2)\), and
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+
      2\sum_i2^iR_i^{-1}
      \sum_{\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)}J_i(\mathbf x)
      \le
      a_*S .
      \tag{TST2}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   Equivalently, if \(\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)\) is partitioned into profile
   classes \(\Pi_i\), each profile \(\pi\in\Pi_i\) has cardinality
   \(N_{i,\pi}\), and every tuple in \(\pi\) has
   \(J_i(\mathbf x)\le e^{-I_{i,\pi}}\), then it is enough to replace the inner
   tuple sum in \((TST2)\) by
   \[
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi_i}N_{i,\pi}e^{-I_{i,\pi}} .
      \tag{TST3}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Taking expectations in \((TWT3)\) and using \((TST1)\) gives
   \[
      \E_zC_z(i)
      \le
      R_i^{-1}
      \sum_{\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)}J_i(\mathbf x).
   \]
   Substituting this into \((DDS1)\) shows that \((TST2)\) implies the dyadic
   distinct-child tail bound of
   \cref{cor:dyadic-distinct-storage-bucket-net}.  That corollary gives
   feasibility.  The profile form \((TST3)\) is just summation of the envelope
   \(J_i(\mathbf x)\le e^{-I_{i,\pi}}\) over each profile class.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Local-error tuple-profile distinct-storage certificate]
   \label{cor:local-error-tuple-profile-distinct-storage}
   Work in the setting of
   \cref{cor:local-error-dyadic-distinct-storage-bucket-net} and
   \cref{lem:tuple-witness-distinct-child-tail}.  Suppose that for every price
   class \(i\) there are certified tuple-incidence envelopes
   \(J_i(\mathbf x)\ge0\) such that
   \[
      \E_z M_z(i,\mathbf x)\le J_i(\mathbf x)
      \qquad
      (\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)).
      \tag{LTST1}
   \]
   If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), the cover is feasible.  Otherwise let
   \(a_{\rm loc}\) be as in \((LBNR2)\).  Suppose \(a_{\rm loc}>0\), the active
   first moments satisfy \((LDCB2)\), and
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+
      2\sum_i2^iR_i^{-1}
      \sum_{\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)}J_i(\mathbf x)
      \le
      a_{\rm loc}S .
      \tag{LTST2}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   Equivalently, if \(\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)\) is partitioned into profile
   classes \(\Pi_i\), each profile \(\pi\in\Pi_i\) has cardinality
   \(N_{i,\pi}\), and every tuple in \(\pi\) has
   \(J_i(\mathbf x)\le e^{-I_{i,\pi}}\), then it is enough to replace the inner
   tuple sum in \((LTST2)\) by
   \[
      \sum_{\pi\in\Pi_i}N_{i,\pi}e^{-I_{i,\pi}} .
      \tag{LTST3}
   \]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Taking expectations in \((TWT3)\) and using \((LTST1)\) gives
   \[
      \E_zC_z(i)
      \le
      R_i^{-1}
      \sum_{\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)}J_i(\mathbf x).
   \]
   Substituting this into \((LDDS1)\) shows that \((LTST2)\) implies the
   local-error dyadic distinct-child tail bound.  Hence
   \cref{cor:local-error-dyadic-distinct-storage-bucket-net} gives
   feasibility.  The profile form \((LTST3)\) is just summation over the profile
   partition.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Multiplicity-discounted distinct-storage certificate]
   \label{cor:multiplicity-discounted-distinct-storage}
   Work in either of the following two settings:
   the scalar distinct-storage setting of
   \cref{cor:dyadic-distinct-storage-bucket-net}, with
   \(a=a_*\) and active first-moment condition \((DCB2)\), or the local-error
   setting of
   \cref{cor:local-error-dyadic-distinct-storage-bucket-net}, with
   \(a=a_{\rm loc}\) and active first-moment condition \((LDCB2)\).  In both
   cases use the multiplicity-discounted tuple incidences
   \(\widetilde M_z(i,\mathbf x)\) from
   \cref{lem:multiplicity-discounted-tuple-witness}.  Suppose that for every
   price class \(i\) there are certified envelopes
   \(\widetilde J_i(\mathbf x)\ge0\) such that
   \[
      \E_z\widetilde M_z(i,\mathbf x)
      \le
      \widetilde J_i(\mathbf x)
      \qquad
      (\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)).
      \tag{MDS1}
   \]
   If \(\Sigma^+=\emptyset\), the cover is feasible.  Otherwise suppose
   \(a>0\), the corresponding active first-moment condition holds, and
   \[
      \E_z\Gamma_z+
      2\sum_i2^iR_i^{-1}
      \sum_{\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)}
      \widetilde J_i(\mathbf x)
      \le
      aS .
      \tag{MDS2}
   \]
   Then \((\mathsf{ESFC}_\Sigma)\) is feasible.

   Thus an occurrence-based list-decoding or range-reporting analysis may be
   used after quotienting by canonical child identity: each occurrence is
   weighted by the reciprocal of the number of occurrences that induce the same
   stored child.  In regimes where many caps, residues, or decoder transcripts
   collapse to one net, this is the quantity that matches shared-DAG storage.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
   Taking expectations in \((MDT2)\) and using \((MDS1)\) gives
   \[
      \E_zC_z(i)
      \le
      R_i^{-1}
      \sum_{\mathbf x\in\mathcal T_{k_i}(P,\delta)}
      \widetilde J_i(\mathbf x).
   \]
   Hence \((MDS2)\) implies the dyadic distinct-child tail bound \((DDS1)\) in
   the scalar setting, and \((LDDS1)\) in the local-error setting.  The
   corresponding conclusion follows from
   \cref{cor:dyadic-distinct-storage-bucket-net} or
   \cref{cor:local-error-dyadic-distinct-storage-bucket-net}, respectively.
\end{proof}

\Cref{lem:exact-near-set-filter-cover} is strictly weaker than
\cref{lem:finite-signature-filter-cover} when the exact near set is part of the
signature.  The all-pair LP covers every \(p\in N_{\sigma_0}\); the existential
LP covers only the event \(U_A\cap N_{\sigma_0}\ne\emptyset\), which is all ANN
needs.
This does not make exact near-set signatures free, but it separates the two
issues: pairwise robustness is no longer baked into the dense-overlap LP, and
any remaining cost of exact signatures is explicit metadata or decoder entropy.
\Cref{lem:exact-near-set-signature-dual} is the corresponding separation
statement: a failed existential signature cover prices signatures, not all near
pairs, and a proposed dense or spherical filter is accepted precisely when its
