fractional-delivery ports.  \Cref{lem:port-skeleton-saturated-comparison} and
\cref{cor:skeleton-cut-conductance} give the exact skeleton-level sufficient
condition: every cut of that port skeleton must carry inverse-polylogarithmic
activation mass, and the only additional loss is the sum of contracted
unit-region depths along a skeleton route.
\Cref{cor:existential-antichain-fano} composes this with the Fano decoder in
the ANN-correct existential form: if the union of valid terminal routes has the
same antichain charge bound and every such route has \(O_c(\log\log n)\) raw
reliability margin, then one deterministic biased stack decoder lists a valid
route with polylogarithmic overhead.  The remaining geometric theorem can
therefore be stated as an antichain charge bound plus a raw-margin/list-moment
bound for the successful-route trie, rather than as a separate allocation,
sampling, or cohort-materialization problem.
\Cref{lem:finite-convex-minimax} and
\cref{lem:robust-waterfilled-minimax} upgrade this from one route law to a
finite witness family: a single query allocation is optimal exactly when tested
against mixtures of the witness occupation profiles, so the remaining near-set
problem is a robust water-filled defect bound rather than a separate profile
for each possible near point.
\Cref{lem:waterfilled-layercake} and
\cref{cor:robust-waterfilled-tail} restate that robust defect as a tail
condition on high charge-to-occupation ratios above the water level.  The next
geometric proof target is therefore a uniform summable tail estimate for those
ratios over all finite mixtures of unresolved near-route laws.
\Cref{lem:waterfilled-moment-certificate} and
\cref{cor:robust-waterfilled-moment} give a more compact sufficient target:
it is enough to bound a small positive moment
\(\sum \ell^\alpha((a/(t_\alpha\ell^\alpha))^p-1)_+\) uniformly over
mixtures, with \(M/p=O_c(\log\log n)\).  Thus the remaining estimate can be
attacked as a low-temperature energy bound for the charge/occupation ratios,
rather than by proving every dyadic tail separately.
\Cref{lem:waterfilled-raw-moment-certificate} and
\cref{cor:robust-waterfilled-raw-moment} remove the implicit water level from
that target: if every mixture has total occupation at most \(H_0\), then
\(\tau=1/H_0\) is a valid lower bound on the water level, and it is enough to
bound the raw logarithmic defect
\[
   \sum_e\ell^\alpha_e
   \log_+\frac{H_0a_e}{\ell^\alpha_e},
\]
or more strongly the raw positive moment
\[
   \sum_e\ell^\alpha_e
   \left(
   \left(\frac{H_0a_e}{\ell^\alpha_e}\right)^p-1
   \right)_+
\]
with \(M/p=O_c(\log\log n)\).  A particularly concrete sufficient condition
is bounded charge density \(H_0a_e\le C\ell^\alpha_e\) on occupied unstable
opportunities, together with \(H_0=O_c(\log\log n)\); then the defect is at
most \(H_0\log C\).  For \(H_0=\log^{O_c(1)}n\), taking
\(p\asymp1/\log\log n\) still keeps the moment normalization \(H_0^p\)
constant, so the remaining theorem can be stated without solving for
\(t_\alpha\).
The guard refinement
\cref{lem:low-guard-shadow} further removes points whose entire near-query
neighborhood is already high-density: the finite dual now prices only the
low-guard shadow, so the remaining score-cover theorem is about sparse exposed
regions rather than dense clusters that resident sampling already solves.
\Cref{cor:shadow-finite-pool-dual} makes this formal in the LP: proposals are
intersected with the exposed shadow before their storage and active weights are
computed, and point prices vanish outside that shadow.
\Cref{lem:shadow-price-density-compiler} packages the exact remaining
score-cover theorem: every surplus shadow dual must expose a certified parent
proposal whose highest-price exposed prefix has positive reduced gain.  If this
separation holds for a finite low-guard pattern universe, column generation and
pattern-complete materialization produce the stored cover required by
\cref{asm:weak-offline-score-cover}.

\paragraph{Structured posterior route.}
\Cref{lem:posterior-superlevel-compiler} records the negative-moment identity suggested by the latest notes. \Cref{lem:explicit-enumeration-barrier} makes the coarse-child obstruction precise: the scale $\xi=m^{-1/(2c^2)}$ is the price of explicitly enumerating $B\simeq\xi^{-1}$ outcomes, not a geometric limit. \Cref{lem:oblivious-sparsification-barrier} adds the complementary warning that the moment bounds alone still permit $\Omega(\xi^{-1})$ disjoint possible witnesses, so direct random sparsification cannot replace structured decoding without an additional sensitivity theorem. \Cref{lem:scale-window-compiler} and \cref{lem:dyadic-structured-amplification} isolate the important arithmetic: if mass windows can be decoded output-sensitively, then $\xi^{-\rho}$ repetitions at each dyadic scale convert negative-moment value into constant hit probability, and summing all scales down to $1/m$ still fits the $m^\rho$ query budget. This scale-aware amplification is essential; a raw negative-moment diagnostic alone does not imply that the near point is actually listed with inverse-polylogarithmic probability. \Cref{cor:dyadic-affinity-boost} adds the skeleton-value refinement: multiplying the local repetitions by \(O(\log H)\) makes the outgoing-affinity deficit \(O(H^{-2})\), so the affinity-proportional toll is summable over a polylogarithmic-depth port skeleton rather than paid as a per-level recall loss.

The continuous likelihood-ball family now proves both analytic sides of the desired posterior decoder: \cref{thm:continuous-likelihood-balls} gives the guard-or-pure-child value, and \cref{lem:ideal-likelihood-scale-profile} gives the scale-normalized query and storage moments. \Cref{lem:likelihood-rank-prefix} further collapses the threshold continuum to rank gaps of a random score order. \Cref{cor:likelihood-prefix-leader} removes another artificial materialization cost: for ANN, every pure prefix may report the same score leader, so the decoder can aggregate prefix mass by leader buckets instead of storing one representative per prefix. \Cref{lem:dyadic-leader-quotient} records the full amplification in this hidden-label form and contributes no per-prefix storage term. \Cref{cor:dyadic-leader-affinity-boost} adds the skeleton-value refinement for the quotient itself: after the \(O(\log H)\)-boosted repetitions, the actual merged leader ports have total useful outgoing affinity \(1-O(H^{-2})\). \Cref{cor:boosted-leader-skeleton-toll} then composes this with affinity-proportional routing: quotienting prefixes by leader gives only constant total square toll over a depth-\(H\) port skeleton, not a hidden per-level recall loss. \Cref{cor:likelihood-leader-intensity} identifies the exact quotient law as the rank-gap weighted measure over score leaders. \Cref{lem:ideal-likelihood-leader-law} further proves that this quotient law has constant total intensity per scale and constant scale-weighted valid intensity under guard failure. \Cref{lem:poissonized-normalized-leader-sampler} removes the remaining all-listing requirement from a sampled implementation: computing the total intensity and sampling from the normalized tilted law gives the exact Poisson leader process. Finally, \cref{lem:scale-amplified-alpha-leader} shows that the dyadic repetitions cancel the rank powers, collapsing the whole amplified posterior to the max-tilted leader law \((AL2)\), with constant total mass and constant valid mass for every near pair. The clean measure target is therefore \cref{asm:alpha-leader-sampler}; conditional on it, \cref{prop:alpha-leader-polylog} gives the desired polylogarithmic ANN bounds. \Cref{lem:alpha-leader-voronoi-capture} gives an equivalent geometric normal form for that same target: the max-tilted intensity of \(x\) is a Gaussian Voronoi-cell capture probability for the interpolated center \((1-\alpha)q+\alpha x\), multiplied by the explicit distance tilt \(\exp(-\alpha(1-\alpha)t\|x-q\|^2/2)\). \Cref{cor:query-centered-cell-reweighting} and \cref{cor:truncated-nearest-cell-compiler} then reduce max-tilted sampling to query-centered nearest-cell decoding plus scalar rejection. The weakest current algorithmic posterior target is \cref{asm:smoothed-witness-list}: list the true near witness with constant tilted mass and scan the verified list. Conditional on it, \cref{prop:witness-list-polylog} gives the same polylogarithmic ANN bound. The facility form \cref{cor:facility-bucket-witness} is the version most directly connected to \(k\)-means++ or other build-time bucket proposals. \Cref{lem:poisson-rate-coverage}, \cref{lem:finite-signature-rate-coverage}, \cref{lem:finite-poisson-rate-coverage-realization}, \cref{cor:finite-signature-retained-buckets}, \cref{cor:finite-transcript-rate-coverage}, \cref{cor:compressed-decoder-dag-rate-coverage}, \cref{cor:output-sensitive-decoder-dag-rate-coverage}, \cref{lem:scalar-redundancy-waterfill}, and \cref{asm:rate-coverage-panel} sharpen this further into the redundancy theorem object: point-label intensities, query label sets, finite coefficient envelopes, one fixed retained Poisson realization, transcript-level and state-DAG decoder work, responsibility-weighted enumerator coverage, the marginal replication water level, the tilted miss bound, and the scan-load bound. \Cref{lem:finite-rate-coverage-convex} gives the finite convex feasibility test and dual obstruction for proposed panels. Conditional on that finite rate-coverage panel, \cref{prop:rate-coverage-polylog} gives the same endpoint. The scale-resolved sampler \cref{asm:ideal-likelihood-leader-law-sampler}, the hidden-label sampler \cref{asm:normalized-likelihood-leader-sampler}, the structured nearest-cell decoder \cref{asm:smoothed-nearest-cell}, and the older all-listing \cref{asm:multiscale-structured-likelihood} remain stronger sufficient implementation forms.

\Cref{lem:seeded-reduced-gain-search} is the build-time bridge from this
finite certificate to list-decoding and lattice-decoding proposals: the
proposal mechanism only has to expose a positive reduced-gain label against
the current dual obstruction, because the retained panel is accepted by the
same exact convex verifier.  \Cref{lem:implicit-reduced-gain-separation}
turns this into a true separation-oracle statement for implicit quotient
families: if a code, lattice, trellis, or facility universe cannot expose
positive gain, the dual obstruction rules out every finite-support panel from
that universe.  \Cref{lem:reduced-gain-variational-separation} gives the
search form of the oracle: after choosing tentative point intensities, the
label generator only solves a signed weighted coverage problem, and exact
verification converts any positive surplus into a valid column.
\Cref{lem:layer-cake-reduced-gain-separation} removes the remaining continuous
profile from that search, replacing it by a single point subset and scalar
layer, with a dyadic scalar grid whenever the retained intensities are capped.
\Cref{cor:pointwise-reduced-cost-separation} sharpens the final separator:
to certify completeness it is enough to find one point and one implicit label
whose residual tilted coverage exceeds its query-load and storage price.
\Cref{cor:soft-list-decoding-reduced-cost-separator} converts this into the
standard soft-decoding interface when the score is coordinatewise additive:
threshold-list codewords, lattice residues, or trellis paths by the dual-priced
reliability score, then exactly filter the returned candidates.
\Cref{cor:threshold-event-reduced-cost} records the corresponding exact target
for ordinary threshold reporters: solve a signed weighted coverage problem over
the satisfied threshold tests.
\Cref{cor:positive-coverage-screen} reduces candidate generation to the
nonnegative part of that coverage objective; signed terms are checked only
after a candidate label is returned.
\Cref{cor:dyadic-positive-list-recovery} then converts arbitrary nonnegative
dual weights into dyadic unweighted list-recovery calls, with the exact
weighted reduced cost checked only at the filter step.
\Cref{cor:ordinary-list-recovery-positive-coverage} identifies those calls
with ordinary list recovery on repeated coordinates for code, trellis, or
lattice-residue membership tests.
\Cref{cor:unified-soft-decoded-rate-coverage} is the corresponding full panel
contract: offline separation is a build-time concern, while online decoder
output, candidate incidence load, and stored replication are charged as three
separate resources.

\Cref{lem:smoothed-max-score-margin} gives a still simpler non-channel target: a query-centered Gaussian score direction separates every invalid point from the true near point by an additive $\Theta_c(tr^2)$ score margin, with high probability. The softest resulting primitive is \cref{asm:smoothed-gibbs}: with inverse-polylogarithmic probability, report a list carrying inverse-polylogarithmic mass under the Gaussian Gibbs kernel on data points. Sampling from the kernel restricted to that list gives a pointwise dominated output law by \cref{lem:captured-gibbs-domination}, and \cref{lem:smoothed-gibbs-suffices} then returns a valid answer because invalid points have negligible Gibbs mass and cannot be oversampled too much. A more exact sampling route is certified additive Gumbel-MIPS: \cref{lem:gumbel-additive-domination} shows that an $O(\log\log m)$ additive optimizer for the Gumbel-perturbed scores gives precisely the required one-sided Gibbs domination, yielding \cref{prop:gumbel-mips-polylog}. A stronger but different implementation route is smoothed additive nearest-neighbor search for the perturbed center $Y/t$ with additive squared-distance error $\Theta_c(r^2)$, exactly equivalent to additive score maximization by \cref{lem:score-max-additive-nn}. These oracles would bypass dyadic scales and representatives entirely, as recorded in \cref{prop:smoothed-gibbs-polylog}, \cref{prop:gumbel-mips-polylog}, and \cref{prop:smoothed-score-max-polylog}. They are targets, not implemented theorems; \cref{rem:gumbel-mips-not-ann} explains why black-box multiplicative ANN does not supply the Gumbel primitive. The older finite restricted-channel compiler \cref{asm:finite-restricted-channel} and \cref{prop:finite-channel-polylog} remain as a coarse explicit-enumeration special case and as a useful diagnostic framework.

\paragraph{Cohort-or-leaf.}
\Cref{asm:cohort-or-leaf} is the original full-child route-level condition for the broader posterior-cohort endpoint, but \cref{lem:prefix-slice-accounting} shows that a prefix-conditioned formulation is cleaner. Work accounting for opened children is no longer the hard part: \cref{lem:vote-budget} pays opened recursive calls from realized detector votes. The preferred remaining target for that more general route is \cref{asm:prefix-slice-survival}: prove that one cumulative near-pair score path either reaches a cap-free residual scan or receives enough detector votes to follow prefix-conditioned certified slices to a resident scan. \Cref{lem:detector-inflation} and \cref{lem:off-spine-inflation} reduce the detector-shadowing part of this target to early activation prefixes with large enough continuation mass $H(v)$ and logarithmic spine-ratio sum $\sum H(u^+)/H(u)$; \cref{rem:linear-spine-ratio} explains why long score routes need an aggregate detector-mass argument instead. This should be tested against the hard cases: an isolated near point next to a massive far cluster, a near point on a cluster boundary, a tiny child that becomes heavy only late, and symmetric far shells. The proof must show a whole-lineage inverse-polylogarithmic event, not merely an inverse-polylogarithmic event at each level.

\section{Conclusion}

The algorithmic target is a cumulative score-and-ball tree with query time
\[
   d\,n^{1/(2c^2-1)}\log^{O_c(1)}n
\]
and space
\[
   dn+n^{1+1/(2c^2-1)}\log^{O_c(1)}n.
\]
The exact pieces now aligned for the randomized cap-thinning route are: continuation-mass pruning gives optimal expected spherical work, adaptive continuation gives whole-lineage near survival, thinned cap splitting gives radius-potential contraction, and cap-free terminal scans are paid by low-correlation collisions.

The compressed-bucket route from \cref{prop:success-normalized-bucket-dag} is
now separated just as cleanly.  The recursion accounting is finished: a finite
approximation ladder gives \(n^{\rho_c}\polylog n\) query time once each rung
has a cost-normalized fractional probing law and a shared-DAG storage moment.
\Cref{cor:fractional-probe-compressed-bucket} folds the old near-hit lower bound
and query Renyi moment into one invariant: recursive one-probe price divided by
near-witness coverage.  The query moment is therefore no longer a separate
list-decoding problem; by \cref{lem:first-moment-query-compression}, the usual
success-normalized expected bucket load implies the Renyi child-work bound, and
\cref{cor:first-moment-active-load-query} is the exact finite-profile version
with false active buckets included in the active layer.
\Cref{cor:distinct-canonical-bucket-net} further sharpens the storage target:
the recursive child index is charged once per distinct canonical bucket net, not
once per decoded occurrence, with only occurrence pointers left in the metadata
budget.  \Cref{cor:dyadic-distinct-storage-bucket-net} rewrites that target as a
dyadic large-child counting problem: for every recursive price scale, bound the
number of distinct canonical bucket nets whose shared child index has that
price.  \Cref{cor:layer-cake-distinct-storage-bucket-net} and
\cref{cor:integrated-tuple-tail-distinct-storage} remove this dyadic
discretization when a geometric proof can bound the integrated tail directly.
\Cref{cor:price-weighted-witness-packing-storage} removes the tail parameter
altogether: each distinct child may choose a randomized tuple witness, and the
storage theorem becomes a bound on price-weighted witness congestion.
\Cref{cor:uniform-tuple-witness-packing-storage} gives the canonical choice for
bucket nets: sample a uniform tuple from the child itself.  In the pair case this
reduces the remaining theorem to bounding distinct-child pair congestion weighted
by \(\psi |A|^{\rho-1}\le\psi\).
\Cref{cor:occurrence-discounted-tuple-storage} converts this to the natural
decoder statistic: reciprocal-multiplicity-weighted pair congestion over decoded
occurrences.
\Cref{cor:pair-profile-occurrence-discounted-storage} is the finite
entropy-energy check for that statistic; it is now enough to show that each pair
profile has small discounted congestion \(B_\pi\), with
\(\sum_\pi N_\pi B_\pi\) inside the storage budget.
\Cref{cor:multiplicity-layer-pair-profile-storage} refines this into a
high-multiplicity-or-high-energy target: after dyadic multiplicity
stratification, layer \(\ell\) receives a \(2^{-\ell}\) quotient discount.
\Cref{cor:aggregate-multiplicity-profile-storage} is the sharpest current
storage certificate: prove the discounted aggregate entropy-energy sum over
profile layers, without first proving a uniform bound for every pair in the
profile.
\Cref{cor:gaussian-aggregate-profile-layer-storage} turns the Gaussian-cap
instance of this target into the explicit inequality
\[
   \sum_{\pi,\ell}2^{-\ell}
   C_{\pi,\ell}\exp\!\left(
      H_{\pi,\ell}
      -\frac{\beta_{\pi,\ell}^2}{1+\theta_{\pi,\ell}}
   \right)
   \le aS
\]
up to metadata, where \(H\) is weighted incidence entropy, \(\beta\) is the
shifted-threshold margin, and \(\theta\) is the worst pair correlation.
\Cref{lem:high-correlation-pair-star-reporter} adds the matching dense
alternative: if a profile layer has large weighted incidence on pairs with
correlation at least \(\underline\theta\), then some dyadic star superlevel lies
inside a ball of radius \(\sqrt{2(1-\underline\theta)}\) and carries incidence
at least the average layer mass up to a logarithmic dynamic-range factor.
\Cref{lem:star-superlevel-column-verifier} and
\cref{cor:pair-star-dense-column-generator} turn such a superlevel into an
ordinary fractional-cover column by using the certified query activation
\(\|q-x\|\le\sqrt{2(1-\underline\theta)}+r\); failure of every such column is
the explicit no-star reduced-gain inequality \((PSG4)\).
\Cref{lem:star-prefix-weak-type-residual} and
\cref{cor:pair-star-weak-type-normal-form} replace exact reported stars by the
best dual-price prefix in the same certified ball; if no prefix is profitable,
every reported star has paid near-pair mass bounded by the query/storage
Renyi envelope \((PWN3)\).
\Cref{lem:tuple-witness-distinct-child-tail} and
\cref{cor:tuple-profile-distinct-storage} reduce each dyadic count to tuple
incidence: a large separated child contains many ordered witness tuples, so the
storage proof can be stated as an entropy-energy bound on how often a tuple
profile can appear in distinct canonical children.  The storage side is
therefore a distinct-net geometric target.
\Cref{lem:multiplicity-discounted-tuple-witness} adds the quotient
normalization needed for occurrence-style analyses: if many decoded records
induce the same canonical child, each record contributes only the reciprocal of
that child's multiplicity to the tuple incidence.  Thus a list-decoding or
range-reporting proof may bound multiplicity-discounted occurrence energy,
which is exactly the shared-DAG storage quantity.
\Cref{lem:occurrence-moments-dominate-dag},
\cref{lem:packing-list-tuple-moment},
\cref{lem:gaussian-cap-intersection-energy}, and
\cref{cor:tuple-profile-renyi-certificate} give a sufficient occurrence
co-load route: count separated tuples in a bucket and subtract their Gaussian
cap-intersection energy.  The actual shared-DAG theorem is weaker still,
because it charges each distinct canonical bucket net once and charges
occurrence multiplicity only as metadata.  Thus the remaining theorem for this
route is a distinct-net entropy-energy inequality for separated spherical
buckets.  \Cref{lem:positive-correlation-occurrence-obstruction} shows that
occurrence co-load is only a sufficient certificate and is false as a final
worst-case target in positive-correlation tangent caps.

For the randomized cap-thinning route, one remaining task is the branching first-split work estimate in \cref{asm:mixed-continuation-operator}: prove that the thinned geometric child potentials contract over random cap-discovery frontiers without replacing the branching decoder by a normalized path law. The newer budget-thinned variant proves the expected work bound from a canonical prefix supermartingale and packages the remaining near-side issue as \cref{asm:aggregate-value-delivery}: prove that the saturated value, or equivalently every route-cut prefix mass, is inverse-polylogarithmic rather than tracking a product along one distinguished path. For laminar route tries, \cref{lem:lca-value-flow} turns the second-moment version into the concrete LCA target
\[
   V(\varnothing)\ge\log^{-O_c(1)}n,
   \qquad
   \sum_uA(u)V(u)^2
   \le
   \log^{O_c(1)}n\,V(\varnothing)^2 .
\]
\Cref{lem:local-lca-energy} further reduces this to a local Bellman multiplier, and \cref{cor:square-nonexpansive-routes} shows that square-nonexpansive value branching costs only the polylogarithmic route depth. Equivalently, \cref{lem:energy-spine-toll} says that it is enough to prove only $O_c(\log\log n)$ positive square-energy toll along the energy-biased route spine. The capped-flow certificate \cref{lem:unit-capped-value-flow}, the Bellman recursion \cref{lem:saturated-value-recursion}, and the min-cut dual \cref{lem:saturated-value-mincut} give a still simpler sufficient formulation: prove that every route cut has inverse-polylogarithmic prefix-success mass. The equivalent dominated-law form in \cref{lem:dominated-route-law} says to construct a tilted law on tame routes whose prefix probabilities are dominated by activation prefix masses up to a polylogarithmic factor; by \cref{cor:typical-route-law-toll}, it is enough to prove only $O_c(\log\log n)$ expected positive domination toll under that route law and prune the bad tail. The cut-energy form \cref{lem:cut-energy-route-law} is closer to stopping-time proofs: it asks only for polylogarithmic $\sum_{u\in\mathcal C}\Lambda(u)^2/A(u)$ on each route cut $\mathcal C$. By \cref{lem:frontier-square-toll}, this is equivalent to bounding the positive square toll of the square-biased route spine up to each stopped frontier, with no all-prefix depth summation. The stronger all-prefix bound in \cref{cor:route-law-prefix-energy} remains an LCA-compatible sufficient condition. \Cref{lem:unit-success-skeleton-contraction} contracts ordinary score-only regions into additive harmonic resistance, so the remaining value theorem can be stated on the skeleton of genuinely thinned opportunities. Conditional on either aggregate value statement, \cref{prop:budget-thinned-polylog} gives the desired polylogarithmic ANN theorem. This is a fully non-channel route; the smooth product terminal filter can be used after localization and no longer contributes an inverse-polylogarithmic table-recall penalty. The structured posterior route replaces the cap-frontier obstacle by the tilted witness-list target \cref{asm:smoothed-witness-list}: prove a compact reporter whose verified candidate list contains the true near point with constant mass under the query-centered tilted Gaussian law. The rate-coverage panel \cref{asm:rate-coverage-panel} is the most concrete facility version of this target: a multi-assignment scheme is certified by the closed-form miss term \(\exp(-a_p\mu_p(B))\), the reported-load bound, and the total replication budget. The stronger max-tilted sampler \cref{asm:alpha-leader-sampler} and nearest-cell decoder \cref{asm:smoothed-nearest-cell} remain clean implementation normal forms, but k-means++-style or lattice/code buckets only need the rate-coverage certificates. The smoothed sampling route replaces both by \cref{asm:smoothed-gibbs} or \cref{asm:gumbel-mips}: prove either an optimal-exponent reporter that captures inverse-polylogarithmic Gaussian Gibbs mass, or a certified $O(\log\log n)$-additive Gumbel-MIPS primitive. Smoothed additive nearest neighbor is another stronger sufficient primitive. The detector-vote cohort-or-leaf route is a separate possible generalization to arbitrary certified child hierarchies, where the remaining issue is near-lineage coupling between ordinary continuation paths and detector activations.
\Cref{cor:affinity-proportional-route-law} gives the cleanest current
list-decoding interpretation of the posterior handoff: once the reporter
decodes an outgoing port list, branch by local affinity and pay only the
cumulative deficit in the list's total affinity.  Thus the score-tree/lattice
analogy has become a concrete theorem target: prove that the decoded port
lists have inverse-polylogarithmic affinity across every skeleton cut.

\appendix

\section{More detail on the spherical exponent calculation}

For completeness, we verify the algebra leading to $\rho(a,b)$. Let $B$ be the branching factor and $\ell_B=\log B$. With
\[
   t^2=(1+a)\ell_B
\]
and
\[
   k=
   \frac{2(1+b)\log m}
   {(1+a)(1-b)\ell_B}
   +O(1),
\]
the expected number of accepting leaves for one point has logarithm
\begin{align*}
   k\ell_B-\frac{kt^2}{2}+O(\log k)
                                                                                                                  &=
                                                                                                                  \frac{k\ell_B(1-a)}{2}+O(\log k)\\
                                                                                                                                                                                                 &=
                                                                                                                                                                                                 \frac{(1-a)(1+b)}{(1+a)(1-b)}\log m+O(\log\log m).
\end{align*}
Thus it equals
\[
   m^{\rho(a,b)}\log^{O(1)}m.
\]

For a pair of correlation at most $b$, the expected number of common accepting leaves has logarithm at most
\begin{align*}
   k\ell_B-\frac{kt^2}{1+b}
                                                                                                                  &=
                                                                                                                  k\ell_B\left(1-\frac{1+a}{1+b}\right)\\
                                                                                                                                                                                                 &=-\frac{k\ell_B(a-b)}{1+b}\\
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           &=-\frac{2(a-b)}{(1+a)(1-b)}\log m+O(1).
\end{align*}
A direct calculation shows
\[
   1-\rho(a,b)
   =
   \frac{2(a-b)}{(1+a)(1-b)}.
\]
Hence one ordinary far point contributes at most
\[
   m^{-(1-\rho(a,b))}\log^{O(1)}m
\]
common leaves, and all $m$ ordinary far points contribute at most
\[
   m^{\rho(a,b)}\log^{O(1)}m.
\]

\section{Bellman cancellation algebra}

We record the cancellation with no surrounding notation. Let $s=1-\rho$, let a parent contain $m$ points in radius $R$, and let a child have relative size $\alpha$ and relative radius $\lambda$. With
\[
   F(m,R)=m^\rho\left(\frac Rr\right)^{2s}
\]
and activation threshold $\tau=\lambda^2$, the first-hit bound charges at most $(\alpha/\lambda^2)^s$ query mass to the child. The recursive charge is therefore
\begin{align*}
   \left(\frac{\alpha}{\lambda^2}\right)^s
   F(\alpha m,\lambda R)
   &=
   \alpha^s\lambda^{-2s}
   \alpha^\rho m^\rho
   \lambda^{2s}\left(\frac Rr\right)^{2s}\\
   &=
   \alpha F(m,R).
\end{align*}
Thus the radius improvement pays exactly for the posterior threshold, and disjoint children sum to at most the parent potential.

\section{Bibliographic note}

The one-sided spherical proof is motivated by the Ahle--Knudsen manuscript supplied with this project, but it uses continuation mass and an analytical upper barrier instead of the two-sided tube proof there. The score-and-ball tree follows the geometric ideas of Andoni and Razenshteyn while replacing dense-cap restart accounting by randomized cap thinning inside one cumulative score process. The local Bellman-game viewpoint is inspired by the robust learned hashing framework of Andoni and Beaglehole. The posterior-cohort route is retained as a possible extension to more general certified child hierarchies.
